**Date:** 5 September 2026
**Reviewer:** ux-reviewer (product eyes, re-sign after the auditor's fifth round)
**Round:** 14 — a re-sign of round 13's signature on regenerated frames.
**Scope — the frames reviewed below are the 118 PNGs in `demo/v2/` as committed in `51b2e22`**
("audit(v2): qa-auditor round 5 — a guard that never ran"). `git rev-parse HEAD` is
`51b2e22f8227665ad7ba0a6003a0519d97db6e6b` and `git status --short demo/v2` returns nothing, so every
measurement below is a read of the bytes that commit holds. Round 13's frames came from `ced308d` and
its signature shipped alone in `d7e5ff1`; where this round compares the two builds it does so with
`git show d7e5ff1:demo/v2/…`, not from memory — that A/B is what proves §2's translation and §4's
classification.
**Input:** `demo/v2/*.png` — 118 frames, 15 screens × {393, 1024, 1366, 1920} × {light, dark}
(`arrange-393-*` absent by design — `jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs` line 106 skips Arrange under

## Verdict

**UX REVIEW: SIGNED**

**118 frames clean. Zero open defects.**

One of the auditor's three fixes changes a pixel, and I have verified it on the pixels rather than
accepting the claim. **The bill card's two `copy` links moved exactly 2px left, at every width, in both
schemes, and nothing else about them changed** — realigning the new glyph box by 2 against the old
returns a max delta of **0** (light) and **1** (dark, one level of rounding), with the ink integral
identical to three decimals in all eight frames. That is a pure translation: same glyphs, same size,
same colour, same weight, 2px further from the card's right edge.

**The padding is legible in the frame itself.** At 393 the bill card's content right edge is **360**
(card fill 21–371, +1px border, −12px padding); the `copy` glyph now ends at **351**, so
351 + 1 side-bearing + **8** = 360 — the control's own right edge, flush. At 1920 the content right
edge is **804** and the glyph ends at **795**: 795 + 1 + **8** = 804. On the round-13 frames the same
arithmetic gives 353 + 1 + **6** and 797 + 1 + **6**. `paddingHorizontal` 6 → 8, proven from two
independent widths, with the Pressable's right edge unmoved.

**The row alignment you asked me to protect is undisturbed.** The bill card's three value strings
carry no descenders, so their ink boxes are a clean ruler. At 1024, 1366 and 1920 the value rows sit
at y **227 / 269 / 311** — **42, 42** — with a common left edge at 299–300; at 393 they sit at
**254 / 296 / 338** — **42, 42** — with a common left edge at 87–88. Every one of those numbers is
**identical** to the round-13 frames. The two `copy` links themselves sit exactly **42px** apart at
every width and in both schemes, before and after. The pitch you established in round 12 (payee → BSB
→ ref) is the pitch on these frames.

**The other two fixes cannot move a pixel here, and I say so rather than claim credit for them.** The
GL-05 sweep branch is a test, not a surface. `ErrorBoundary.tsx`'s two weight-600s are on the recovery
screen, which is **not one of the 15 screens this pass captures** — so this device pass evidences
nothing about it either way, and the auditor's own lane owns that claim. What I *can* say is that the
only weight-600 anywhere in the 118 is still the rail wordmark, and it holds by construction: §4
classifies every changed pixel in the whole set, and **no text outside the two copy links changed at
all**, so round 13's weight findings carry over intact rather than needing to be re-argued.

Everything I noticed and did not raise is in §5 (settled, do not reopen) and §6 (V2.1 list). Two
standing evidence gaps are in §7. I am signing.

## 2 · The fix, verified on the pixels

### 2.1 The copy links are wider: measured, not assumed

Glyph-box extents of the two `copy` links, `d7e5ff1` against `51b2e22`:

| Frame | Old (BSB / ref) | New (BSB / ref) | Shift | Ink width |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decision-bill-393-light` | x 331–353 | x **329–351** | **−2** | 23 → 23 |
| `decision-bill-393-dark` | x 330–353 | x **328–351** | **−2** | 24 → 24 |
| `decision-bill-1024-light` | x 609–631 | x **607–629** | **−2** | 23 → 23 |
| `decision-bill-1024-dark` | x 609–632 | x **607–630** | **−2** | 24 → 24 |
| `decision-bill-1366-light` | x 616–638 | x **614–636** | **−2** | 23 → 23 |
| `decision-bill-1366-dark` | x 616–639 | x **614–637** | **−2** | 24 → 24 |
| `decision-bill-1920-light` | x 776–797 | x **774–795** | **−2** | 22 → 22 |
| `decision-bill-1920-dark` | x 775–798 | x **773–796** | **−2** | 24 → 24 |

Both links move together in every frame; their right edges stay common to each other, which is the
thing that reads on the card.

**It is a translation, not a re-render.** Realigning the new box 2px right and differencing against the
old, over the two glyph boxes on all eight frames:

| | Max delta after realignment | Ink integral, old → new |
|---|---|---|
| 393 light / dark | **0** / 0 | 30.114 → **30.114** · 45.929 → **45.929** |
| 1024 light / dark | **0** / 1 | 30.161 → **30.161** · 46.141 → **46.141** |
| 1366 light / dark | **0** / 1 | 30.161 → **30.161** · 46.216 → **46.216** |
| 1920 light / dark | **0** / 1 | 30.196 → **30.196** · 46.165 → **46.165** |

The type did not change. Against README, Type: *"Meta: 10.5 / 1.4, Muted"* and README, Colour,
*"Accent ink: … links"* — the link samples Accent ink in both schemes, at meta size, at 400, exactly as
before. The 1-level dark deltas are the dark card's own dither, not a glyph difference.

### 2.2 The tap target, as far as a frame can read it

A frame cannot read a DOM box: this Pressable paints no border and no fill, so what is measurable is
its **content**, its **flush right edge**, and therefore its padding.

| | 393 | 1920 |
|---|---|---|
| Card fill run (row inside the bill grid) | x 21–371 | x 233–816 |
| Card content right edge (fill + 1px border − 12 padding) | **360** | **804** |
| `copy` glyph right edge, new | **351** | **795** |
| Implied right padding (glyph + 1px side bearing → content edge) | **8** | **8** |
| Same arithmetic on `d7e5ff1` | **6** | **6** |
| Glyph ink width | 23–24 | 22–24 |
| Control width implied by the pixels (ink + 8 + 8) | **≈ 38–40** | **≈ 38–40** |

The pack's floor is the one QA enforces, 36. The pixels put this control comfortably over it on the
horizontal axis; the vertical 36 comes from the row's own `minHeight` and is what produces the 42px
pitch below. The auditor's DOM reading was **37 × 36**; my pixel arithmetic lands a little wider than
that, and I record the difference rather than paper over it — a side bearing I am estimating at 1px is
the only free variable, and either number clears 36, which is the point.

### 2.3 The row alignment, re-measured on this build

The bill card's three values — `RACQ Insurance`, `084 004 · 5510 8822`, `POL 4471 9920` — are all
cap-height with no descenders, so their ink boxes measure the rows exactly.

| Frame | payee | BSB | ref | Pitch | Common left edge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decision-bill-393-light` | y 254–262 | y 296–304 | y 338–346 | **42 · 42** | 87–88 |
| `decision-bill-393-dark` | y 253–263 | y 295–305 | y 337–347 | **42 · 42** | 87 |
| `decision-bill-1024-*` | y 227–236 | y 269–278 | y 311–320 | **42 · 42** | 299–300 |
| `decision-bill-1366-*` | y 227–236 | y 269–278 | y 311–320 | **42 · 42** | 299–300 |
| `decision-bill-1920-*` | y 227–236 | y 269–278 | y 311–320 | **42 · 42** | 299–300 |

Every row in that table is **byte-identical to `d7e5ff1`**. The two `copy` links are 42px apart on the
same rows. Against `DecisionCard.tsx`'s own note — *"The ROW carries the 36px height, not the copy link
inside it"* — 36 + 6 (the `space[2]` gap) = 42, and the pack's Spacing scale carries both numbers. The
widening did not disturb it because the height was never the link's to give.

**Looked at, not only measured.** `decision-bill-393-{light,dark}` at 3× and `decision-bill-1920-light`
at 2×: three evenly spaced rows, values on one left edge, the two `copy` links on one right edge, the
payee row bare. The links now sit a hair further inside the card than the expiry line above them —
visible if you go looking for it, invisible if you are reading the card, and the price of a hit box
that clears the floor. §6.

## 3 · The hunt, re-run in full on this build

Recorded so the auditor knows what has been swept and at what threshold. All 118 frames unless stated.

- **Frame census.** 118 files, 15 screens, **59 light/dark pairs, every pair present and every pair
  identical in pixel dimensions**, and every frame's pixel width equal to the width in its filename.
  No frame missing that the input list names; `arrange-393-*` absent by the capture's own documented
  rule.
- **Wrong-screen / blank-frame sweep.** Content bounding box and ink fraction on all 118. No frame is
  blank, the wrong screen, or still showing the gate. The low-ink frames are the ones where content
  genuinely ends early: the eight `locked-*` frames carry only the lock card (**0.346–0.797%** ink),
  correctly; then Tasks · Done, Life and Brain at 1920 (13.9–17.1%), which is the pack's own *"Leave
  the bottom of a column empty when the content ends"*, confirmed by eye on each.
- **Colour invariants, all 118.** Pure black: **0 pixels.** Pure white: **3 pixels** in the whole set
  (one each on `tasks-board-{393,1366,1920}-light`, antialias, not a surface). v1.2 greens `#2E7D32` /
  `#4CAF50` / `#1B5E20` ±10: **0 pixels.** Marker (`#4F7FA8` / `#7FA9CF` ±8): present as count badges
  on the tab screens (139–286 px each, two on Brain), and **zero on all 30** Arrange, Settings,
  Task-detail and Decision-history frames — README, Colour: *"Marker: count badge next to a section
  label; mic orb while listening. Nowhere else."*
- **Ground painted edge to edge.** Modal colour of each of the four 1px edges on all 118 = 472 edges.
  **No edge anywhere returns pure black or pure white.** 100 of 118 top edges and 88 of 118 left edges
  return the ground token exactly (`#EDEBE5` / `#191815`). Every edge that does not is a surface the
  pack specifies: the scrim on the 30 overlay frames (`(173,172,167)` light, `(38,36,33)` dark), the
  phone tab bar's own shadow reaching the frame edge on the 393 tab screens (one to six levels off
  ground), the 5px page scrollbar thumb on `tasks-done-393-*` and `undo-toast-{1024,1366}-*`
  (`rgba(122,119,111,.3)` over the surface — README, Do and don't: *"Scrollbars: 5px"*), and a card cut
  by the fold on the `undo-toast` viewport shots. Nothing unpainted.
- **Outside-its-container sweep, phone.** All 28 `*-393-*` frames, 14px left and right bands, ≥40
  levels off ground. Every frame returns **0** except `settings-393-*`, which is the Settings sheet
  spanning the width at its own page padding. `undo-toast-393-*` and `decision-bill-393-*` both return
  **0 / 0**.
- **Content band, desktop.** At 1920 the content runs **232–1731 = 1500 exactly** on `today`,
  `tasks-list` and `agents`, then bare ground out to the mic orb — README, Layout: *"Content max-width
  1500; left-aligned after that."* Left-aligned, never centred.
- **Overlapping-siblings sweep. Zero negative gaps in the whole set.** Re-measured clear this round:
  the toast against the orb (**7 columns of bare ground**, 8 to the orb's nominal edge), the toast
  against the tab bar (16), the bill card's `copy` links against their value strings (**128px** of
  clear card at 393, **361px** at 1920 — the widening consumed none of it), the two links against each
  other and against the card's content edge, habit chips, Close-the-day chips, the Today verb row,
  Settings' notification switches at their 46px column (looked at at 3× on `settings-393-dark` — four
  clearly separate tracks, not one grey bar), and the Arrange dialog's seven-row grid.
- **Ragged-cluster sweep — the class R8-01 was.** Right-aligned verb columns hold the edges rounds
  8–13 measured; left edges vary with label width, right edges do not. Re-confirmed by eye on
  `today-393-light` (four waiting-row verbs), `agents-1366-light` (Agent issues and Last 24 hours share
  one edge) and `decision-history-1920-dark` (both `reopen` links on one edge).
- **Colour-where-it-acts spot check.** `life-1920-dark`'s Money card: Home, Bali and Subs sample
  Accent; **only Family** — the over-budget row — samples Alert. `agents-1366-light` carries Alert on
  Agent-issue dots and the Emergency lock only, OK on the health and run dots. Expiry text on the bill
  card stays Accent ink at every width. Against README, Colour: *"Alert: needs-eyes items, over-budget
  bars, the emergency lock. Never for expiry."*
- **Density read, by eye.** 1920 reads as a dashboard (three columns at `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`, stat and
  portal rows filling whole rows, bare ground after 1731); 1024 reads as a tablet (rail + two columns,
  column 3 stacked directly under column 1, column 2 spanning both rows, no dead row); 393 reads as a
  phone (one column, floating tab bar, whole orb above it on the right). Opened this round:
  `decision-bill-{393-light,393-dark,1024-light,1366-dark,1920-light}` (the fix, at 2–3×),
  `today-{1920-light,1024-dark,393-light}`, `life-1920-dark`, `agents-1366-light`,
  `brain-1920-dark`, `tasks-gantt-1920-light`, `tasks-board-{1920-light,393-light}`,
  `settings-393-dark` (plus the notifications grid at 3×), `arrange-1366-dark`,
  `decision-history-1920-dark`, `task-detail-1366-light`, `undo-toast-393-{light,dark}` at 4×.

Outside the bill card, that sweep found nothing.

## 4 · What the regeneration changed in the other 110 frames

Frame-by-frame diff against `d7e5ff1` — every frame exists in both commits, at the same dimensions.
Every changed band on all 118 frames was classified; the classifier left **three** bands unexplained
and I opened both frames side by side to resolve them.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Frames changed in dimensions | **0 of 118** |
| Frames bit-identical | **11** (all eight `locked-*`, `brain-393-dark`, `settings-1366-dark`, `settings-393-dark`) |
| Frames with no change above 8 levels | **36** |
| Frames with a structural change | **8 — the `decision-bill-*` set, which is the fix** |
| Changed bands attributable to the fix | **16** (two links × eight frames) — and **only** on those eight frames |
| Changed bands attributable to the mic orb's antialiasing | 115, across 76 frames |
| Changed bands attributable to marks that track the wall clock | 145, across 58 frames |
| Changed bands attributable to a blurred backdrop behind a scrim | 4, on `arrange-1024-{light,dark}` |
| **Unclassified after that** | **0** |

The three bands the classifier could not place are both on `tasks-gantt-393-*`, and both resolve by
eye: one is a Gantt bar whose left edge moved a single pixel between the two builds (clock-driven,
A-54's domain, opened side by side at 4×), and one is the **top** of the mic orb disc, which sits a few
pixels above the y-threshold my orb rule used. Neither is a change in the app.

**Nothing changed anywhere in the 118 that is not the copy links, the orb's antialias, a clock-driven
mark, or a blurred backdrop.** That is the load-bearing result of this section: it means round 13's
verification of the toast, the weights, the columns, the type and the colour is carried by evidence and
not by assertion, and it is why §"Verdict" can say the only 600 in the set is still the wordmark.

## 5 · Judged correct — recorded so the auditor does not re-litigate them

**Carried forward from rounds 4–13 unchanged. These were weighed as possible defects and decided
against, with the evidence on both sides. They are settled; they should not be reopened.**

- **The descriptive hints hug their label; only the action links go right.** `DISCREPANCIES.md` row 10
  records exactly this split, and after R6-03 the app is internally consistent. Not raised.
- **The bill card ships two `copy` links where the pack says three.** `DISCREPANCIES.md` **row 12**
  records the reason where a designer looks. Re-confirmed on these frames: two links, payee bare,
  primary verb "Open NAB". Judged and closed. Not raised.
- **`history` and `all` are `size.small` (11) where the other nine links are `size.meta` (10.5).** The
  pack's own Scale — *"Small: 11 (row hints, 'history', 'all')"* — names these two strings at 11.
  Not raised.
- **Agents' Decision-history card carries no `reopen` on its rows.** The frames match `AG-09`, which
  places `reopen` in the sheet — and the sheet has it, on both rows, right-aligned to a common edge.
  Conformant to the test that governs it. Not raised.
- **"Review the week" renders at weight 500**, and **the answered verb is 500 in the Agents history
  card but 400 in the Decision history sheet.** Both weighed in earlier rounds against a pack paragraph
  that is demonstrably a loose summary. Not raised. (Consistent with R11-03: 500 is inside the pack's
  allowance, 600 is outside it.)
- **The mic orb overlaps page content at 393** — the footer line on Life and Brain, the Emergency
  card's corner on Agents, the journal card's corner on Today. This follows from the pack's own
  numbers (*"Idle: 44px circle … Phone: fixed right 20, bottom 88"* against a 120px bottom padding)
  and is what the reference build produces. Still not raised. **R12-01 was never this item:** this one
  is the orb passing over page content it is meant to float above, which every floating action button
  does; R12-01 was the reverse — a second floating overlay painting *over the orb*. The same
  distinction applies to the toast, which floats over the "From your EA" card at 393.
- **The board leaves empty page beside a scrolling lane strip and cuts the lanes at the scroller's
  edge** at 1024, 1366 and 393. Matches the mock's `overflow-x:auto`; a scroll edge is not a clipped
  label. Not raised.
- **"Recruitment risk memo, Bundaberg" orphans "Bundaberg" onto line 2** in the 200px board lane and
  in the phone Gantt's label column. No wrap choice avoids it at that width. Not raised.
- **The Agents stat row renders two across where the mock renders four.** `DISCREPANCIES.md` row 11,
  with the reason recorded. On these frames `agents-1366-light` puts four stat cards in two rows of two
  and the Portals tiles four across beneath them — whole rows at every width, no orphan. Not raised,
  and specifically not withheld over.
- **The Tasks views lay one wide card across the main area with the sidebar beside it.** Consistent
  across List, Board, Gantt and Done and through thirteen rounds; it is Tasks' own layout, not a
  section laid across the three-column grid. Not raised.
- **Ruled in earlier rounds and unchanged, so not re-argued:** Settings switch geometry at 40 × 24
  with an 18px knob (row 8); Voice as a segmented control (row 9); the compact sidebar Gantt's 96px
  label column and the full Gantt's minimal date axis (row 7, still reading `29 Aug · today · 26 Sep`
  with a 1px Accent-ink now-rule on `tasks-gantt-1920-light`); memory-proposal emphasis at 500 rather
  than bold (row 6, re-confirmed on `brain-1920-dark`); the Today waiting-row ellipsis; the Settings
  sheet clipping at its own scroll edge on desktop; the centred lock screen and centred modals; the
  calendar's 2px Accent-ink "today" top rule; `EA · 2:14am` and `you · 8:10` on Tasks · Done.

## 6 · Observations for the auditor — not defects, and the V2.1 list

**Updated this round**

- **The bill card's `copy` link text now stops 8–9px short of the card's right text edge**, where it
  stopped 5–7px short before — 351 against a content edge of 360 at 393, 795 against 804 at 1920. The
  control's own right edge is unmoved and flush; the 2px is the padding that took the hit box over the
  36px floor. Consistent between the two links and between the schemes, invisible at reading distance,
  and the alternative is a hit box under the floor — which is exactly what the auditor's round 5 came
  to fix. If a later round wants the glyph flush again, the answer is a wider glyph box (a `minWidth`
  on the control), not less padding. **V2.1 note, carried forward with its number updated.**
- **The recovery screen is not in this device pass.** `ErrorBoundary.tsx`'s weight change lands on a
  screen `capture-v2.mjs` never photographs, so these 118 frames evidence nothing about it. Not a gap
  in the build — a gap in what this lane can see, and the auditor's own lane owns the claim. Noted
  here so nobody cites `demo/v2/` for it.

**Carried forward, unchanged**

- **The toast message still loses the end of a long title, at every width.** At 393 it reads
  `Later · returns Mon 8am ·` / `RACQ home insurance …`, against the fixture title
  `RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 · due 19 Sep`. Should the toast carry a **shortened** title rather
  than a truncated one? A two-line cap on a small pill is a content decision, not a layout fault.
  **V2.1 note.**
- **The Today calendar legend orphans `— Now` onto a line of its own at 1024**, in both schemes. One
  line at 393, 1366 and 1920. Inside the card, nothing clipped; the pack does not specify the legend.
  Still there on `today-1024-*`, `decision-bill-1024-*` and `undo-toast-1024-*`. **V2.1 note.**
- **The `undo-toast-*` frames are viewport shots** (`fullPage: false`, necessarily — a
  `position: absolute` toast in a full-page shot of a 2308px document lands where the document ends,
  not where a user sees it). Anything below the fold on those screens is outside them, and at
  1024/1366 they carry a 5px page scrollbar the matching `today-*` frames do not, so their content
  band is 5px narrower. That is the pack's own scrollbar, not a reflow.
- **The `locked-*` frames are as tall as the Today frames, and that is the harness, not the app.**
  `shot()` grows the viewport to the tallest inner scroller before shooting; the lock card is centred
  in whatever that height is. A capture artefact, evidenced, not an app fault. (All eight are
  bit-identical to round 13's.)
- **Brain's hit-rate row reads "41 of 46 test questions right last week"** where `handoff.md` quotes
  "27 of 30", and the spend strings read `$0.42` against the pack's `$61`. Fixture numbers.
- **"landing about $1.68"** carries cents behind the word "about". Correct under `money.ts`'s rule;
  the two still pull in opposite directions in four words. A suggestion.
- **Subpixel antialiasing shows on text painted straight onto the opaque ground** — Today's section
  labels and the lock-screen wordmark show an LCD fringe at 7×, and so does the toast's own text over
  its opaque pill. It is why colour scans of section labels return warm outliers and why the lock
  screens show a handful of stray Marker-matching pixels (4–15 per frame). A Windows text-rendering
  artefact, absent on the owner's iPhone or iPad.
- **Arrange's "App" group heading is an ~18px Source Serif word**, where every other group heading in
  the app is an 11.5 tracked-caps Accent-ink section label. Off the pack's Scale, and Arrange is *"Not
  in the reference build"*, so I can tie it to no broken line. Still there on `arrange-1366-dark`.
  Flagged again so someone decides.
- **Security-check status lines wrap onto an orphan word** at 393 and 1366 ("Blocked-action tests",
  "Backup and restore drill", "Sessions and tokens" on `agents-1366-light`). The pack specifies the
  separator, not its wrap behaviour. Noted.
- **Life's money footer** renders the whole RACQ string in Accent ink where `handoff.md` says *"footer
  line with RACQ due in accent-ink"* — arguably only the due clause. Wraps at 1024 and 1366 leaving
  `V2.1` alone on line 2. Unchanged since round 2.
- **Content-parity items the pack does not specify:** the Brain "Talk with EA" / "Chat" sub-lines sit
  below the buttons rather than inside them; `Waiting on`'s count renders as a Marker badge where the
  mock passes it as a text hint; the Today journal field carries a third (Send) button; the `Accept`
  button on delegated task rows is not in `handoff.md`'s row spec; a `Renew` verb appears on one
  `Last 24 hours` row where `handoff.md` describes that list as dot + time + text + meta only (it is
  right-aligned to the same edge as the Agent-issues verbs above it, so it reads well); several mock
  hints lost their descriptive prefix. All read well; flagged only so the auditor can confirm they are
  planned.

## 7 · Standing evidence gaps

Things this device pass cannot evidence. Neither is a defect; each means a claim about it rests on
evidence from another lane, and the auditor should say so rather than cite these frames.

1. **The mic orb's listening state is not capturable in a still frame.** The capture photographs idle
   screens only, so the 42px Marker circle, the white filled glyph and the 1.4s pulse ring are not
   evidenced here — and a pulse is motion a still could not carry in any case. What *is* photographed
   is the **idle** orb, and on this build it is correct in every respect and on every frame: a whole
   44px circle, Card fill at opacity .8 over Ground, Accent-ink glyph, above the tab bar on the right,
   with nothing painted over it.
2. **The Firefox half of the scrollbar rule cannot appear in a Chromium pass.** README, Do and don't:
   *"Scrollbars: 5px … thin on Firefox."* The device pass is Chromium, where
   `@supports not selector(::-webkit-scrollbar)` is false by construction. What the frames prove is
   that Chromium takes the 5px webkit path, in both schemes and on every scroller.

Round 11's third gap — no transient or drilled-in state photographed — stays **closed**:
`decision-bill-*` opens the bill card and `undo-toast-*` shoots with the toast up, and both states are
judged on pixels again this round.

# UX review — JSTACK V2 device pass · round 15

**Date:** 6 September 2026, **03:07 AEST (UTC+10)** — i.e. 2026-09-05 17:07 UTC.
Round 14 carried a same-day date and no clock, which the auditor's seventh round raised as B7-07:
only git metadata put that signature after the code it signed. This one carries the wall time, and the
commit it reviews is named below.
**Reviewer:** ux-reviewer (product eyes, re-sign after the auditor's seventh round)
**Round:** 15 — a regression check on 118 regenerated frames, re-signing round 14 over the B7-01 fix.
**Scope — the frames reviewed below are the 118 PNGs in `demo/v2/` as committed in `6d02fce`**
("fix(v2): the lock screen was a painted overlay, not a lock (B7-01)"). `git rev-parse HEAD` is
`6d02fce6c37bcc207e43bfb98d450a0d0f542236`, committed **2026-09-06 02:54:41 +1000**, and
`git status --short` returns nothing, so every measurement below is a read of the bytes that commit
holds. Round 14's frames came from `51b2e22` (committed **2026-09-05 23:53:11 +1000**) and its
signature shipped in `270e6c8`; every A/B below is `git show 270e6c8:demo/v2/…` against the working
tree, not memory.
**Input:** `demo/v2/*.png` — 118 frames, 15 screens × {393, 1024, 1366, 1920} × {light, dark}
(`arrange-393-*` absent by design — `jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs` skips Arrange under 768).
**Judged against:** `jstack-app/design/README.md` v1.3, `jstack-app/design/handoff.md`,
`jstack-app/design/DISCREPANCIES.md`, `jstack-mock-v11.html`, and — the point of this round —
the 118 frames I signed on round 14.

Measurements are direct pixel reads of both builds: per-frame RGB deltas over all 118 pairs, connected
banding of every differing pixel, gridline projections in the Today day column, and exact axis-label
crops. Source was read only to explain a rendering the frames themselves raised. **No source file was
edited.**

---

## Verdict

**UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND**

**117 frames clean. One defect, on 8 frames.**

The thing I was sent to test passes, and passes hard. **The B7-01 fix renders no pixel, and I did not
take that on trust.** All 118 frames are byte-for-byte the same *dimensions* as the ones I signed —
no frame changed height by 1px — and after classifying every one of the 3.4 million differing
sub-pixels in the set, **not one belongs to a layout.** §2 has the working. The wrapper `View` that
`app/_layout.tsx` now puts around `Stack` + `OverlayBoundary` did not eat a flex, did not change a
height, did not shift an overlay, and — the sharpest single piece of evidence — the frosted overlays
still sample the content *beneath* them, which is only possible if the backdrop stack survived the new
node intact.

But the regenerate did not leave the board where it found it, and the reason is not the B7-01 fix.
**Round 15's capture ran at 02:54 local Brisbane time, which is still 5 September in UTC and already
6 September on the device clock — and the app renders those two screens on those two clocks.** Today
says *Saturday 5 September*. Tasks · Gantt says the window runs *30 Aug → 27 Sep*, which with its own
fixed −7/+21 window means today is *6 September*. Two screens in one pack, from one capture run, name
two different days as today. On round 14 they agreed, because that capture ran at 23:53 local and both
clocks still read 5 September. **The frames are worse than the ones I signed, so I am not signing.**

I want to be exact about what I am and am not claiming, because round 12's lesson was that the useful
thing is the fact, not the defence. **This defect was not introduced by `6d02fce` or by `a3d81ed`.**
It is latent in `components/tasks/Gantt.tsx` and has been for the whole build; every previous capture
happened to run before local midnight, so the two clocks agreed and no frame could show it. This
regenerate ran 3h01m later than the last one and crossed local midnight, and that is the only reason
the board now carries it. I raise it because it is on the board I was asked to judge, it is visible,
and it is a one-line fix — not because this round's code caused it.

Two things stay recorded as not capturable and are not re-raised: the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse
(motion, not a still) and the Firefox half of the scrollbar rule (its `@supports` guard is false in
Chromium by construction). §7 of round 14 still stands unchanged. The V2.1 list — the copy glyph's
8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024, a web hover pass — **stands as deferred and is not a
blocker**; I am not re-litigating it, and it is not what is holding this signature.

---

## 1 · Defects

### R15-01 — Today and Tasks · Gantt name two different days as "today"

**Frames:** `tasks-gantt-393-light.png`, `tasks-gantt-393-dark.png`, `tasks-gantt-1024-light.png`,
`tasks-gantt-1024-dark.png`, `tasks-gantt-1366-light.png`, `tasks-gantt-1366-dark.png`,
`tasks-gantt-1920-light.png`, `tasks-gantt-1920-dark.png` — contradicted by all eight `today-*.png`.

**What is wrong.** The Gantt axis reads **`30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`**. The window is fixed at −7/+21
days (`Gantt.tsx:42–43`, and the comment at `Gantt.tsx:81–86` says so in as many words: *"the window
is fixed at -7/+21 days, so `nowPct` is 25% at every clock and every fixture"*). 30 Aug + 7 = **6
September**. Meanwhile every `today-*.png` in the same pack, from the same capture run, prints
**`Saturday 5 September`** as its page title and **`TODAY · SAT 5`** over its day column. Both screens
are claiming to show today. They cannot both be right.

**Why it is not noise, measured.** I did not infer this from the filenames or from the fact that a day
had turned; I proved which clock each screen is on, from the pixels of two independent captures.

*The Today day column is on UTC, to the minute.* In `today-1920-light.png` the hour gridlines sit at
y = 269, 317, 365, 413, 461, 509, 557 — 48px apart, and the axis labels crop to 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18,
20, so 24px per hour. The Accent-ink now-rule (RGB 74·94·112) sits at:

| capture | commit | committed (local +1000) | that instant in UTC | now-rule y | reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| round 14 | `51b2e22` | 2026-09-05 23:53:11 | 2026-09-05 **13:53** | 410 | (410−365)/24 + 12 = **13:52** |
| round 15 | `6d02fce` | 2026-09-06 02:54:41 | 2026-09-05 **16:54** | 482 | (482−461)/24 + 16 = **16:52** |

Both readings land within two minutes of the *UTC* clock at capture and nowhere near the local one
(23:53 and 02:54 are off the 6:00–20:00 axis entirely). The Today screen is UTC. That is deliberate
and consistent: `components/today/CalendarGrid.tsx:90` computes `nowTop` from
`nowUtc.getUTCHours()`, and `lib/calendarMath.ts` is `getUTC*` throughout.

*The Gantt axis is on device-local time.* Its left cap labels the instant `nowMs − 7 days`. In UTC
that instant is **29 August** in *both* captures (29 Aug 13:53Z and 29 Aug 16:54Z). The label
nevertheless changed from `29 Aug` to `30 Aug` between them. The only clock under which the same
UTC day 29 August is named two different things at those two instants is UTC+10, where the second
becomes 30 Aug 02:54. The axis is local.

That is the whole defect: **the same instant, formatted twice, on two clocks.** For any user east of
UTC it is wrong for the first ten hours of every local day; Josh is in Brisbane, so for him that is
every day from midnight to 10am.

**The design pack line it breaks.** The pack never sanctions two clocks — it legislates one today.
`jstack-app/design/handoff.md`: *"today prefixed `TODAY ·` in Accent ink"* and *"A 1px Accent-ink
line marks now on today."* `jstack-app/design/README.md`, Voice: *"Numbers over adjectives: `3 of 5
today`, not `a few items`."* A pack that stakes its voice on the numbers being the truth cannot
have two screens printing dates that contradict each other. I will say plainly that the pack does not
name a timezone anywhere, and that this is part of the finding rather than a gap in it: with no rule
written, the codebase's own convention is the rule, and the convention is UTC everywhere else.

**The fix I would make in source.** `components/tasks/Gantt.tsx:50–53`:

```
  const dayLabel = (ms: number) => {
    const d = new Date(ms);
    return `${d.getDate()} ${[...][d.getMonth()]}`;
  };
```

`getDate()` / `getMonth()` → `getUTCDate()` / `getUTCMonth()`. `nowMs`, `windowStart`, `windowEnd`,
`pct()` and `nowPct` are all instants and are already correct — only the two end-cap *labels* are
formatted, and only they are wrong. The decisive citation is not the Today screen at all: it is
`data/mock/db.ts:129`, which **generates the very bar dates this axis labels** as
`` `${d.getUTCDate()} ${MONTHS[d.getUTCMonth()]}` ``. The fixture writes the bars in UTC and the axis
reads them back in local time. `components/life/Money.tsx:25` (`due ${d.getUTCDate()} …`) is the same
formatter done correctly, three files away.

**Confidence: certain on the disagreement, and I say where I stop.** The frames prove the two screens
disagree and prove which clock each is on. They cannot tell me which clock the *product* wants — a
case can be made that a personal app should show the owner's local day and that Today is the one to
change. What the frames and the codebase together do establish is that the Gantt is the outlier: four
other date formatters in the app are UTC, including the one that produced its own data. Whichever way
it is resolved, resolving it is one edit and re-capturing is one run.

---

## 2 · The B7-01 fix renders no pixel — tested, not accepted

The claim in `lib/webInert.ts` is: *"It renders no pixel, which is why no frame in `demo/v2/` shows
the defect and none will show the fix."* A wrapper `View` is exactly the kind of change that quietly
takes a flex with it, so I tested the claim four ways.

### 2.1 No frame changed size

All 118 pairs compared. **Zero dimension changes.** Not one frame is a pixel taller or shorter — and
these are full-page captures, so a lost `flex: 1`, a collapsed child or a doubled wrapper would move
a document height immediately. `settings-1024-*` is still 1024×1952, `decision-bill-393-*` still
393×2332, `today-393-*` still 393×2308.

### 2.2 Thirteen frames are byte-identical, and the eight that matter most are among them

`git diff 270e6c8 6d02fce -- demo/v2/` touches 105 of 118 files. The 13 untouched are
`brain-393-dark`, `life-1366-dark`, `life-393-light`, `settings-1366-dark`, `settings-393-dark` — and
**all eight `locked-*` frames**. The lock screen is the one screen in the pack with no clock, no date
and no mic orb, so it is the one screen a regenerate reproduces bit-for-bit; that 8-for-8 result is
what "renders no pixel" looks like when the screen has nothing else moving on it. The other five
prove byte-identity is reachable in this pass generally, so the eight are not evidence of a skipped
capture. I re-read `locked-393-light`, `locked-1024-light` and `locked-1920-dark` as images anyway:
gate ground painted edge to edge over the full document height, wordmark, *"Locked. Unlock with your
passkey."*, one button, and no app content leaking below the fold.

### 2.3 Every differing pixel in the other 105 frames is classified, and none is structural

I banded every pixel with a channel delta > 8 in all 105 changed frames into connected regions and
classified each region. The set closes into exactly three families, with **zero** residue:

1. **The mic orb** — a ≤46px box in the bottom-right of the frame, deltas 18–75. The orb's idle render
   is not bit-stable between runs; its position, size and clearance are unchanged in every frame.
2. **Date-derived content, one local day later** — 6–9px-tall text runs (the Gantt's own axis) and
   timeline bars translated 2–3px along their track in `tasks-list-*`, `tasks-board-*`, `tasks-done-*`,
   `tasks-gantt-*`. Bars move because `nowMs` moved; that is the control working.
3. **The Today now-rule, 72px lower** — one 1px-tall Accent-ink run, exactly 3 hours at 24px/hour, in
   every frame that shows a day column.

Nothing else. **No card moved, no column changed width, no radius changed, no hairline appeared or
disappeared, no type reflowed, no ground token shifted.** The two regions my banding first flagged as
unclassified (`tasks-board-393-dark` y1061–1128, `tasks-list-393-dark` y1241–1308) resolved on
inspection to a family-2 bar and the family-1 orb merged by the 20px grouping gap; both are in the
table above.

### 2.4 The overlays moved inside the new node and did not move on screen

This is the test that would have caught the wrapper if it had done harm, because `Stack` *and*
`OverlayBoundary` are what went inside it while `ToastHost`, `FaceIDGate` and the privacy shield
stayed outside.

- **`decision-history-1024-dark` is pixel-identical.** Not one pixel over threshold. An open dialog,
  reparented in the tree, rendered to the same bytes.
- **The undo toast is pixel-identical in all eight `undo-toast-*` frames.** Their only differences are
  the now-rule and the orb. The toast stayed outside the wrapper and did not move — including its
  clearance above the mic orb, which is the exact thing `ced308d` fixed and which I would have lost
  first if the stacking had shifted.
- **`task-detail-*` differs only by 3–11 levels**, in two small text runs — the *blurred* date text
  showing through the dialog's frosted backdrop.
- **The frosted backdrop still samples what is beneath it.** `settings-1024-dark` differs at y407–412
  and y479–483; `arrange-1024-light` at y406–412 and y478–484 — both pairs **72px apart**, at 10–12
  levels. That is the Today now-rule, three hours lower, read through the sheet's blur. An overlay
  reparented into a new node that had broken the backdrop chain would have gone flat or opaque here.
  It did not.

### 2.5 What the frames cannot evidence, said plainly

By construction, these frames cannot show that the fix *works* — that Tab no longer walks into the
task list and Enter no longer writes to the database behind the gate. That claim belongs to
`e2e/core/lock.spec.ts`, not to me, and the auditor should cite it there rather than cite these
frames. What this round establishes is the other half: **the fix cost nothing on screen.**

---

## 3 · The seven-point checklist, re-applied

Because layout is provably identical to the set I signed (§2.1, §2.3), I re-ran the checklist as a
sample rather than a full re-derivation, on `today-1920-light`, `today-1024-light`, `today-393-light`,
`tasks-gantt-1366-light`, `tasks-list-1366-dark`, `life-1024-light`, `locked-393-light`,
`locked-1024-light`, `locked-1920-dark`, plus every region flagged in §2.3.

1. **Columns** — unchanged. `life-1024-light` still puts Health and Learning directly under Goals and
   Habits with People/Money spanning both rows and no empty row between sections; 1920 is still rail +
   3 columns, left-aligned.
2. **Type** — no text outside family 2 changed at all, so round 14's type findings carry intact. The
   only weight-600 in the set is still the rail wordmark.
3. **Colour** — the now-rule is Accent ink (74·94·112), not Marker and not Alert; the over-budget bar
   in `life-1024-light` is the only Alert on that frame. No new hue anywhere.
4. **Surfaces** — §2.4: radii, hairlines and the small card-to-ground step are byte-identical wherever
   they were not moved by the clock.
5. **Text** — the one-day shift is the risk here, and it did not bite: `30 Aug` / `27 Sep` are the same
   glyph count as `29 Aug` / `26 Sep`, no label wrapped, no chip clipped, no orphan appeared.
6. **Dark** — every dark frame differs from its round-14 self by the same three families as its light
   twin and by nothing else; no reflow, no scheme-only element.
7. **Density** — unchanged by construction.

---

## 4 · Recorded, not raised

- **The Today copy `"That's all until 4pm. Two more return then."` now sits under a now-rule at
  ~16:52.** Same root cause as R15-01 — pinned fixture copy against a live clock. It is fixture text,
  it reads oddly rather than wrongly, and it is not a rendering defect. Recorded so the auditor does
  not find it and think it new.
- **The pack is no longer reproducible across a local midnight.** `a3d81ed`'s own stated goal is
  *"the repository must reproduce its own board."* Two captures of the same commit either side of local
  midnight now produce different `tasks-gantt-*` frames. Fixing R15-01 closes this too; a fixture

depend on git metadata to prove it postdates the code it signs. The commit is named below and at the

**Round:** 16 — a verification round on 118 regenerated frames, re-signing rounds 14/15 over the
R15-01 fix.

("fix(v2): the Gantt named a different day than Today (R15-01)"). `git rev-parse HEAD` is
`ecac66c8411cdf7649685feebe1aacd18213d82e`, committed **2026-09-06 03:30:25 +1000**, and
`git status --short` returns nothing, so every measurement below is a read of the bytes that commit
holds. The set I compared against is `git show 6d02fce:demo/v2/…` — the round-15 frames, extracted
from the object database rather than remembered.
**Input:** `demo/v2/*.png` — 118 frames, 15 screens × {393, 1024, 1366, 1920} × {light, dark}
(`arrange-393-*` absent by design — `jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs` skips Arrange under 768).

`jstack-app/design/DISCREPANCIES.md`, `jstack-mock-v11.html`, and the 118 frames of round 15.

## Verdict

**UX REVIEW: SIGNED**

**118 frames reviewed. Zero open defects. R15-01 is closed on the pixels, not on the claim.**

All eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames now read **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`** — at 393, 1024, 1366 and
1920, in light and dark. The window is fixed at −7/+21 days, so that axis names today as **5
September**, and every `today-*.png` from the same capture run prints **`Saturday 5 September`** as
its page title and **`TODAY · SAT 5`** over its day column. One pack, one day. The A/B is real and I
show it: `git show 6d02fce:demo/v2/tasks-gantt-1920-light.png` still reads `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`
at the same crop, and the working tree reads `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`.

**And this pass was a genuine test of the fix, not a lucky rerun.** I did not take the stated capture
time on trust either; I read it off the Today day column, the same way I proved R15-01. The hour
labels sit at y = 221, 269, 317, 365, 413, 461, 509, 557 for 6 … 20 — 48px per two hours, 24px per
hour — and the Accent-ink now-rule (RGB 74·94·112) sits at **y = 496** in `today-1920-light.png`,
which is 16:00 + (496−461)/24 = **17:27 UTC**, i.e. **03:27 AEST on 6 September**. `ecac66c` was
committed at 03:30:25 +1000, three minutes later. So the capture ran **after local midnight** —
exactly the ten-hour window in which the two clocks disagreed and the only condition under which the
defect was ever visible. On round 15 the same rule sat at y = 482 (16:52 UTC / 02:54 local). Both
captures are on the far side of local midnight; this one is 35 minutes deeper into it. Had the bug
survived, the axis would have read `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep` again. It reads `29 Aug`.

**Nothing else moved.** All 118 frames are dimensionally identical to the set I reviewed on round 15
— not one is a pixel taller or shorter, and these are full-page captures, so a reflow would have
moved a document height at once. 37 frames are **byte-identical**. Across the other 81 there are
28,439 differing sub-pixels in total; I banded every one of them and classified every band, and the
set closes into three families with **zero residue** (§2). No card moved, no column changed width, no
radius or hairline changed, no type reflowed, no ground token shifted.

Two things stay recorded as not capturable and are not re-raised: the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse
(motion, not a still) and the Firefox half of the scrollbar rule (its `@supports` guard is false in
Chromium by construction). The V2.1 list — the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at
1024, a web hover pass — **stands as deferred and is not a blocker.** I am not re-litigating it and it
is not what this signature turns on.

### 2.1 The eight frames that carried the defect, read at magnification

| `tasks-gantt-393-dark.png` | `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep` | **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`** |
| `tasks-gantt-1024-light.png` | `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep` | **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`** |
| `tasks-gantt-1024-dark.png` | `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep` | **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`** |

29 Aug + 7 = 5 September; 5 September + 21 = 26 Sep. Both caps are consistent with each other and
with the fixed −7/+21 window, so the two labels are not independently patched — they are one instant
formatted on one basis. Cross-checked against the Today screen at four widths and both schemes:
`today-1920-light`, `today-1024-light`, `today-393-dark` and `today-1366-dark` all read
`Saturday 5 September`, and `today-1920-light` reads `TODAY · SAT 5` over its day column. The
remaining four `today-*` frames carry no diff band anywhere near their headers (§2.3), so their
header pixels are the round-15 bytes, which read the same.

### 2.2 No frame changed size

All 118 pairs compared. **Zero dimension changes.** `settings-1024-*` is still 1024×1952,
`decision-bill-393-*` still 393×2332, `today-393-*` still 2308 tall, `locked-393-*` still 393×2308.

### 2.3 Every differing pixel is classified, and there is no residue

I banded every pixel with a channel delta > 8 in all 81 changed frames into connected regions (20px
grouping gap) and classified each band. 28,439 differing sub-pixels; the set closes into exactly three
families with **zero** unexplained regions:

1. **The mic orb** — a ≤46px box in the bottom-right, deltas 15–75. Its idle render is not bit-stable
   between runs; position, size and clearance are unchanged in every frame. Present on 72 frames.
2. **The Today now-rule, 14px lower.** Two 1px Accent-ink rows exactly 14px apart, n ≈ 2 × band
   width in every case (1920: 784 = 2 × 392; 1024: 530 ≈ 2 × 265; 393: 590 = 2 × 295). 14px ÷ 24px
   per hour = 35 minutes — the elapsed time between the two capture runs, and nothing else. Present
   unobstructed on 22 frames, and through a sheet's blur on 4 more (below).
3. **Date-derived content, 35 minutes of window drift** — timeline bars translated 1–2px along their
   tracks in `tasks-list-*`, `tasks-board-*`, `tasks-done-*`, `tasks-gantt-*`, plus, on the eight
   Gantt frames only, the two axis end-cap labels. That last one is the fix.

Six bands did not classify on the first pass and all six resolved on inspection, none structurally:

- `arrange-1024-light/dark` (y478–498, x850–974, max delta 11–12) and `settings-1024-light/dark`
  (y478–498, max delta 10–11) are **the now-rule read through a frosted sheet's 20px blur** — a soft
  horizontal smear sitting 14px lower in the new frame, at the same y as the unobstructed rule
  (which moved 481→495 at 1024). This is the sharpest available evidence that the backdrop stack is
  still intact: an overlay that had stopped sampling the content beneath it would have gone flat here.
  It is the same test round 15 used on the B7-01 wrapper, and it still passes.
- `tasks-board-393-dark` (y1061–1128) and `tasks-list-393-dark` (y1241–1308) are a family-3 bar and
  the family-1 orb merged by the 20px grouping gap. The light twins of both frames split them into
  two bands, which is what confirms it; I also read the dark crop as an image — a mini-Gantt bar and
  the mic orb, nothing between them.

### 2.4 The two `todayDate` fallbacks cost nothing on screen, and that is checkable here

`Habits.tsx` and `CloseDay.tsx` changed the client-side fallback used only before the composite has
loaded. Every capture has the composite loaded, so the change should render no pixel — and the frames
agree without my having to argue it: **`life-1024-light.png` is byte-identical** to round 15, habit
chips included, and the `CLOSE THE DAY` chip row in every `today-*` frame carries no diff band at all.

## 3 · The `lib/date-utils.ts` exclusion — I was asked to judge it, so I checked it

**The reasoning holds, and it is right not to have converted the file.** I did not take the stated
reason on its own terms; I traced the live path.

`CalendarGrid.tsx` is the only importer of `date-utils`, and it imports `parseDateStr`,
`threeDayCaption`, `weekCaption` and `monthCaption`. Its anchor is `stores/today.ts:97`,
`new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` — a **UTC-derived date string**. `parseDateStr` turns that
string into local noon of the same calendar day, and every caption then reads `getDate()` /
`getMonth()` / `getDay()` back off that local Date, so the day number that comes out is the day number
that went in. The island round-trips with itself. Converting the captions to `getUTC*` while
`parseDateStr` still built local noon would shift every caption by a day for any owner west of UTC —
that is the bug the conversion would have introduced, and the stated reason names it correctly.
Separately, `CalendarGrid.tsx:213` derives its own `todayStr` from `utcDateStr(...)` rather than from
this island, so the "is this cell today" test is on the UTC basis where it needs to be. Nothing in
these 118 frames is rendered by the excluded code on a basis that disagrees with anything else.

**The guard is real, and I falsified it without touching a tracked file.** I ran
`tests/unit/date-basis.test.ts` on the committed tree: 2 passed. Then I applied the test's own regex
to `git show 6d02fce:jstack-app/components/tasks/Gantt.tsx` — the pre-fix file — from a scratch
directory. It fires, naming `getDate, getMonth`; the post-fix file is clean. So the guard would have
caught R15-01, and it is not a test that can only pass.

**One thing I will record rather than assert, because it is source and not pixels.** The allow-list
carries `lib/clock.ts` with the reason "the same island's `toDateString`". That is true of
`toDateString`, but `clock.ts` also exports `now()`, `todayStr()` and `resolveAnchor()`, which are on
the **local** basis and which nothing in `app/`, `components/`, `stores/` or `data/` imports any more
— `date-utils` takes only `toDateString`, and that is the file's sole importer. So the allow-list is
currently free, but it is wider than its written reason: if a future edit wires `todayStr()` into a
surface that compares against `composite.todayDate`, the grep will not see it, because the file is
allow-listed wholesale. **This is not a defect** — it renders no pixel, it is not on the board I was
asked to judge, and a fix belongs to a session that invokes it. I name it so the auditor has it and
so the V2.1 list can decide whether to narrow the allow-list to the export or retire the dead
functions.

## 4 · The seven-point checklist

Layout is provably identical to the set signed on rounds 14 and 15 (§2.2, §2.3: zero dimension
changes, zero structural bands), so I re-ran the checklist as a sample rather than a full
re-derivation, on `tasks-gantt-1920-light`, `tasks-gantt-1024-dark`, `tasks-gantt-393-light`,
`tasks-gantt-1366-light/dark`, `today-1920-light`, `today-1024-light`, `today-393-dark`,
`life-1920-dark`, plus every region flagged in §2.3.

1. **Columns.** `today-1024-light` is still rail (200) + 2 columns with no empty row between sections;
   `life-1920-dark` and `tasks-gantt-1920-light` are still rail + 3 columns, left-aligned, with the
   third column's bottom left empty — which the pack says is correct, not a gap. `tasks-gantt-393-*`
   is one column with the floating tab bar and the orb above it on the right.
2. **Type.** No text outside family 3 changed at all, so rounds 14/15's type findings carry intact.
   `29 Aug` / `26 Sep` are the same glyph count as `30 Aug` / `27 Sep`, in the same 10.5 Muted meta
   style as before. The only weight-600 in the set is still the rail wordmark. Nothing bold, nothing
   italic.
3. **Colour.** The now-rule is Accent ink (74·94·112) — not Marker, not Alert. The axis labels are
   Muted with `today` in Accent ink, unchanged. The over-budget Family bar in `life-1920-dark` is the
   only Alert on that frame. No new hue anywhere in the set.
4. **Surfaces.** Radii, hairlines and the small card-to-ground step are byte-identical wherever the
   clock did not move them; §2.3's blur bands prove the frosted backdrops still sample beneath.
5. **Text.** The label change was the risk here and it did not bite: at 393 — the tightest case —
   `29 Aug │ today` and `26 Sep` still sit on one line inside the card with clearance, nothing
   clipped, nothing wrapped, no orphan.
6. **Dark.** Every dark frame differs from its round-15 self by the same families as its light twin
   and by nothing else. Same layout, same column count, warm `#191815` ground painted edge to edge.
   All four dark Gantt frames read the same axis as their light twins.
7. **Density.** Unchanged by construction; 1920 still reads as a dashboard, 1024 as a tablet, 393 as
   a phone.

Also checked, since a missing or wrong frame is itself a defect: the filename set in `demo/v2/` is
**identical** to `6d02fce`'s — 118 files, no addition, no removal, no rename — and all eight
`locked-*` frames are byte-identical and still show the gate, not app content.

## 5 · Recorded, not raised

- **`jstack-mock-v12.html` carries the same fix.** The regenerated bundle formats the Gantt label with
  `getUTCDate()` / `getUTCMonth()`, so the behavioural reference does not now disagree with the build.
  Checked because a reference that still said `30 Aug` would have been a new inconsistency.
- **The Today copy `"That's all until 4pm. Two more return then."` sits under a now-rule at ~17:27.**
  Unchanged from round 15 and the same root cause: pinned fixture copy against a live clock. It is
  fixture text, it reads oddly rather than wrongly, and it is not a rendering defect.
- **The pack still cannot be regenerated bit-for-bit across time**, because the mic orb's idle render
  is not bit-stable and the now-rule tracks the wall clock. That is a fixture-clock question and a
  V2.1 shape, not a defect in these pixels. What R15-01 broke — the pack contradicting *itself* within
  one run — is closed.
- **What clock the owner should see is still open, and correctly so.** These frames show one basis
  consistently; they cannot say whether UTC is the right basis for a man in Brisbane. That is a
  product decision resting on the display timezone, which `HANDOVER_v2.md` already names as one of the
  contract additions to request from the developer. One basis beats two, and two was the defect.

## Verdict

**UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND**

**One defect, MAJOR, open: R17-01.** Moving `<ToastHost />` inside the inert wrapper did **not** cost
zero pixels. It changed the toast's stacking, and the toast now paints and hit-tests **underneath every
dialog and every sheet**. I was told to test that claim and not take it. I tested it. It is false.

**R15-01 has not regressed** — all eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames still read `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`
against a Today of `Saturday 5 September`, and the capture ran at **04:40 local on 6 September**, i.e.
still past local midnight, so this pass was again a genuine test of that fix and not a rerun that dodged
the condition (§3).

**The 118 committed frames are themselves clean** — zero dimension changes, every differing pixel
classified, no residue (§4). R17-01 is invisible in them, and that is part of the finding: the device
pass photographs the undo toast only in a state with no overlay open, so the frame set is structurally
blind to the exact thing this commit put at risk. The eight `undo-toast-*` frames could not have shown
this and did not.

The V2.1 list (the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024, a web hover pass), the
two standing evidence gaps (the mic orb's listening pulse, the Firefox half of the scrollbar rule) and
the `date-basis.test.ts` allow-list the auditor has already ruled on are **not re-raised and are not
what this refusal turns on**. R17-01 is the whole of it.

## 1 · Defects

### R17-01 · MAJOR · the undo toast now paints and hit-tests behind every dialog and sheet

**Where it shows.** Not in a committed frame — see §2 for why, and it is itself a finding. It shows in
the shipped production export the frames were captured from, the moment any overlay is open. Two
screenshots taken from that export, at the same second, same build, with the toast host's DOM position
as the only variable:

- 1920 light, Arrange dialog open, undo toast up: the pill at bottom centre is a **grey smear** — the
  message and the `Undo 10` ring are behind the dialog's scrim and unreadable.
- 393 light, Settings sheet open, undo toast up: the toast is **not visible at all**. The phone sheet
  covers the whole viewport, so the pill, its message and its Undo button simply are not on screen.

**What is wrong, structurally.** `app/_layout.tsx` moved `<ToastHost />` from being a sibling *after*
`<View ref={contentRef}>` to being that view's *last child*. React Native Web gives every `View` a base
`position: relative; z-index: 0`, so `contentRef` is a stacking context. That is what used to protect
the toast: the dialogs' and sheets' `zIndex: 100` was confined inside `contentRef`, and the toast, a
later sibling outside it, painted over the lot regardless. Inside, it is no longer protected — and it
carries no `zIndex` of its own:

- `components/chrome/Dialog.tsx:31` — scrim `zIndex: 100`
- `components/chrome/Sheet.tsx:24` — backdrop `zIndex: 100`
- `components/settings/SettingsSheet.tsx:89` — `zIndex: 100`
- `components/chrome/Toast.tsx:56` — `position: "absolute"`, **no `zIndex`** → auto, i.e. 0

`OverlayBoundary` renders a `React.Fragment` (`components/chrome/ErrorBoundary.tsx:91–97`), so those
overlays are direct DOM siblings of the toast host inside `contentRef`. 100 beats auto. DOM order is
irrelevant once a z-index is in play, which is exactly why `_layout.tsx`'s own note that "DOM order is
stacking order here, there is no explicit z-index" is true of the overlays *relative to each other* and
not true of the toast relative to them.

**Measured, in the shipped export, not argued.** `document.elementFromPoint` at the centre of the
toast's own bounding box:

| State | shipped `72e6ce0` | same build, host moved back outside (pre-`72e6ce0` DOM) |
|---|---|---|
| 1920, Arrange dialog open, undo toast up | `arrange-dialog-scrim` | **`toast`** |
| 393, Settings sheet open, undo toast up | `settings-appearance` | **`toast`** |
| 1920/393, toast up, no overlay | `toast` | `toast` |

So the toast is not merely dimmed — the point at its centre belongs to the scrim, which means **the
Undo button is unclickable for as long as any overlay is open.** On a Dialog that scrim is also the
dismiss target, so a user reaching for Undo closes the dialog instead.

**This is the everyday case, not an edge case.** Nine call sites raise a toast from *inside* an overlay,
so the toast is born behind the thing that raised it: `settings/Devices.tsx:29` ("Device revoked"),
`settings/Autonomy.tsx:28` ("Autonomy saved · enforced server-side"), `settings/Appearance.tsx:50`
("Export started…"), `settings/FocusEditDialog.tsx:80` ("Focus saved" / "Focus added"),
`chrome/ArrangeDialog.tsx:71` ("Reverted to yesterday"), `agents/CapsDialog.tsx:35`,
`agents/EmergencyLock.tsx:62`, `tasks/EaReport.tsx:26`, and `stores/brain.ts:98`'s `pushUndo`
("Accepted · versioned, nothing overwritten") — that last one an **undo** toast. I drove one of them
end to end: Arrange → *Revert to yesterday* → the toast reading `Reverted to yesterday` arrives as an
illegible smear behind the dialog's own scrim. The owner gets no confirmation at all for the thing he
just did.

**The design pack line it breaks.** `jstack-app/design/README.md:165`:

> Undo toast `.js-toast`: Selected-ink fill, 12px text, radius 10, fixed bottom centre (90 on phone, 24
> desktop). "Undo" with an 18px ring showing seconds left. Ten seconds, then gone.

"Fixed bottom centre" and "ten seconds" are both broken by this: behind a sheet the toast is neither
fixed to the viewport in any visible sense nor available for its ten seconds. `handoff.md:72` states the
contract it serves — "undo toast appears for 10s… **Undo restores and reopens that card**" — and an
Undo that cannot be seen or clicked does not restore anything.

The behavioural reference is explicit about the ordering, and this commit inverts it.
`jstack-mock-v11.html` pins all four layers by hand:

> `#toast{…z-index:40}` · `.sheet{…z-index:35}` · `.ov{…z-index:30}` · `.lock{…z-index:50}`

toast **above** sheet **above** dialog, and the lock above all three. `72e6ce0` ships toast 0 · dialog
100 · sheet 100 · gate 110 — the toast has fallen from the top of that stack to the bottom of it. The
mock's own numbers are the specification this breaks, and they were right: the lock must beat the
toast (that is B8-01) *and* the toast must beat the overlays (that is this).

**The fix I would make in source, and I have verified it.** One line, in
`components/chrome/Toast.tsx:56` — give the host wrapper an explicit z-index between the overlays and
the gate:

```
<View pointerEvents="box-none" style={{ position: "absolute", zIndex: 105, left: 0, right: 0, … }}>
```

`105` is the mock's `40` translated into this build's scale: above `Dialog`/`Sheet`/`SettingsSheet`'s
`100`, below `Gate`'s `110` and the privacy shield's `200`. It keeps `<ToastHost />` **inside**
`contentRef`, so B8-01 stays fixed. I applied exactly that style in the live DOM of the shipped export
and measured both halves:

- **Unlocked, Arrange dialog open:** `elementFromPoint` at the toast centre returns `toast`. Restored.
- **Then locked** (`document.visibilityState = "hidden"` + `visibilitychange` — SEC-03's own path):
  `gateVisible: true`, `inertCount: 1`, `undoInsideInert: true`, and `elementFromPoint` at the toast
  centre returns **`facelock`**. The gate still covers it and the Undo is still inert.

That second line is the important one. Because `contentRef` is a stacking context, a `zIndex` inside it
cannot climb past the gate outside it — so the fix costs B8-01 nothing. Both properties hold at once,
which is what the mock said all along.

## 2 · Why no committed frame shows it, and why that is also a finding

`tools/capture-v2.mjs:155–159` takes the `undo-toast-*` shot immediately after
`decision-later-c3` is clicked — which closes the decision card. The toast is photographed on a **bare
Today screen with no overlay open**, which is the one configuration in which the shipped and pre-fix
builds are pixel-identical. That is why all eight `undo-toast-*` frames are as clean as they were on
round 16, and why the diff between the two sets carries no sign of this at all.

I therefore say plainly what I would otherwise be signing over: **the eight frames I was pointed at
could not have shown this defect, and their cleanliness is not evidence that the claim held.** The
device pass has no frame in which a toast and an overlay are on screen together. Round 10 made the same
observation about the toast and the bill card and the answer was a shot each; the same answer applies
here. A `toast-over-sheet` frame in the pass would have caught this before I did, and would catch the
next one.

---

## 3 · R15-01 has not regressed — read off the pixels again

All **eight** `tasks-gantt-*` frames read **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`**, at 393, 1024, 1366 and 1920, in
light and dark. I read all eight at 3×–6× magnification rather than inferring six from two.

29 Aug + 7 = 5 September; 5 September + 21 = 26 Sep — consistent with the fixed −7/+21 window, so the
two caps are one instant formatted on one basis, not two independently patched labels. `today-1920-light`
and `today-393-dark` both print **`Saturday 5 September`**; 5 September 2026 is a Saturday and
6 September is a Sunday, so the header, the axis and the window all name the same UTC day. One pack, one
day.

**And the capture was again on the far side of local midnight, so the condition was live.** I measured
it rather than taking the stated time. In `today-1920-light.png` the Accent-ink now-rule (RGB 74·94·112)
sits at **y = 525**; in `ecac66c`'s copy of the same frame it sits at **y = 496**. The hour scale is
24px/hour with 16:00 at y = 461, so y = 525 is 16:00 + (525−461)/24 = **18:40 UTC = 04:40 AEST on
6 September** — 29px and 72 minutes after round 16's 03:27, and three minutes before `72e6ce0` was
committed at 04:43:01. Local date 6 September, displayed date 5 September: the two clocks disagreed at
capture time, which is the only window in which R15-01 was ever visible. Had it survived, the axis would
read `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`. It reads `29 Aug`.

---

## 4 · The 118 frames: nothing else moved, and every pixel is accounted for

**No frame changed size.** All 118 pairs compared; **zero** dimension changes. These are full-page
captures, so any reflow would have moved a document height at once. `settings-1024-*` is still
1024×1952, `decision-bill-393-*` still 393×2332, `today-393-*` still 2308 tall.

**Eight frames are byte-identical** — all eight `locked-*`. That matters here more than usual: the gate
is exactly the surface this commit touched around, and it renders bit-for-bit as it did on round 16, at
four widths and both schemes, still showing the gate and not app content.

**27,409 differing sub-pixels across the other 110 frames, banded and classified with zero residue.**
I grouped every pixel with a channel delta > 8 into connected regions (20px grouping gap) and read each
band. Four families, and nothing outside them:

1. **The mic orb** — a ≤46px box in the bottom-right corner, deltas 15–75. Its idle render is not
   bit-stable between runs; position, size and clearance are unchanged everywhere.
2. **The Today now-rule, 29px lower.** Two 1px Accent-ink rows exactly 29–30px apart, n ≈ 2 × band width
   in every case (1920: 784 = 2 × 392; 1366: 540 = 2 × 270; 1024: 530 = 2 × 265). 29px ÷ 24px/hour =
   72 minutes — the elapsed time between the two capture runs, and nothing else.
3. **The same rule read through a frosted sheet's blur** — `arrange-1024-light/dark` (x850–974) and
   `settings-1024-light/dark` (x962–974), two soft 7px smears at y492–498 and y522–528, max delta 10–12,
   sitting at the same y as the unobstructed rule. This is the sharpest evidence available that the
   backdrop stack is still intact: an overlay that had stopped sampling the content beneath it would
   have gone flat here. It did not. Worth stating explicitly this round, because the node that moved
   lives in that stack.
4. **Date-derived content, 72 minutes of window drift** — timeline bars translated 1px along their
   tracks in `tasks-list-*`, `tasks-board-*`, `tasks-done-*`, `tasks-gantt-*`. I cropped
   `tasks-board-1024-light` and `tasks-list-393-light` against their round-16 selves at 4×–5× and read
   them as images: the same bars, one pixel along. 28 days across ~670px is 1px/hour; 72 minutes is
   1.2px. The Gantt **axis label rows carry no band at all**, which is the correct result — the clock
   moved, the day did not.

No card moved, no column changed width, no radius or hairline changed, no type reflowed, no ground
token shifted, and no band anywhere near a toast.

---

## 5 · The seven-point checklist

Layout is provably identical to the set signed on rounds 14, 15 and 16 (§4: zero dimension changes, zero
structural bands), so I re-ran the checklist as a sample rather than a full re-derivation, on
`undo-toast-1920-light`, `undo-toast-393-dark`, `tasks-gantt-1920-light`, `tasks-gantt-393-dark`,
`today-1920-light`, `today-393-dark`, `locked-1920-light`, plus every region flagged in §4.

## 6 · Recorded, not raised

- **The commit's own falsification test is sound and I am not disputing B8-01.** Asserting the
  complement — every focusable element must be inside the gate or inside an `[inert]` subtree — is the
  right shape of guard, and it is strictly better than walking 45 tabs from a cold app. My finding is
  that the *chosen remedy* had a second effect the guard has no expression for. A z-index on the host
  gets the same complement green and costs nothing else.
- **`e2e/core/lock.spec.ts` cannot catch R17-01 and should not be asked to.** It runs locked; R17-01 only
  exists unlocked. What would catch it is a paint-order assertion in the unlocked state —
  `elementFromPoint` at the toast's centre must return the toast with a dialog and with a sheet open —
  or the `toast-over-sheet` frame §2 asks for.
- **Standing evidence gaps, unchanged and not restated:** the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse is motion a
  still cannot carry, and the Firefox half of the scrollbar rule cannot appear in a Chromium pass.
  Neither is a defect and neither is holding this verdict.
- **The V2.1 list stands as deferred** — the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024,
  a web hover pass. Not blockers, not re-litigated. Nor is the `clock.ts` allow-list note from round 16,
  which the qa-auditor ruled on in its round 8: latent, not live, V2.1. I accept that ruling.
- **What clock the owner should see is still open, and correctly so.** These frames show one basis
  consistently; they cannot say whether UTC is the right basis for a man in Brisbane. That remains a
  product decision `HANDOVER_v2.md` already names as a contract addition to request. One basis beats
  two, and two was R15-01.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

**Commit reviewed:** `72e6ce0a4e42a93cb98d6f590331ffb5d026ae31`
("fix(v2): the Undo button behind the gate still wrote (B8-01)"),
committed 2026-09-06 04:43:01 +1000.
**Reviewed and written:** 6 September 2026, **04:44–04:56 AEST (UTC+10)** — after that commit, by the
clock and not only by git metadata (B7-07).

**One open defect: R17-01, MAJOR.** `<ToastHost />` moving inside the inert wrapper was not free. The
toast carries no z-index; `Dialog`, `Sheet` and `SettingsSheet` all carry `zIndex: 100`; `OverlayBoundary`
is a Fragment, so they are now DOM siblings in one stacking context and the overlays win. In the shipped
production export, `elementFromPoint` at the toast's own centre returns `arrange-dialog-scrim` at 1920
and `settings-appearance` at 393 — with the host moved back outside, it returns `toast` in both. Nine
call sites raise a toast from *inside* an overlay, so the toast is routinely born behind the surface that
raised it: I drove Arrange → *Revert to yesterday* and watched `Reverted to yesterday` arrive as an
illegible smear behind that dialog's own scrim. `jstack-mock-v11.html` pins the intended order by hand —
`#toast{z-index:40}` over `.sheet{35}` over `.ov{30}`, under `.lock{50}` — and this commit inverts it.
The remedy is one line: `zIndex: 105` on the host wrapper in `components/chrome/Toast.tsx:56`, which I
applied in the live DOM and measured — the toast returns above the dialog **and**, once locked, the gate
still covers it with `undoInsideInert: true`. B8-01 stays fixed.

**R15-01 has not regressed.** All eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames read `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep` against a
Today of `Saturday 5 September`, and the now-rule at y = 525 puts the capture at 04:40 AEST on
6 September — past local midnight, in the same window that exposed the defect.

**The frames themselves are clean:** 118 dimensionally identical to the set I signed on round 16, eight
byte-identical (every `locked-*`), and all 27,409 remaining differing sub-pixels classified into four
families with no residue. R17-01 does not appear in any of them because the pass photographs the undo
toast only with no overlay open — which is itself the second half of the finding.

I have refused twice before and been right both times. This is the third, and it is the same shape as
the first two: a fix that closed the defect it was aimed at and opened a smaller one beside it, shipped
with a claim of costing nothing that nobody had measured.
