## Verdict

**UX REVIEW: SIGNED**

**Zero open defects across 126 frames.**

**R17-01 is fixed, and I verified it rather than took it.** In all eight new `toast-over-sheet-*` frames
the undo toast paints **fully above** the Settings sheet and its scrim: the pill's fill reads exactly
`43·42·38` (light) / `236·233·226` (dark) — the same values as in the `undo-toast-*` frames where no
overlay is open. A scrim painting over it could not leave those numbers untouched. Better than that: with
a 3px inset, the pill's **interior is byte-identical** between `undo-toast-<w>-<s>` and
`toast-over-sheet-<w>-<s>` at all four widths and both schemes — bbox `None`, max delta `0`. Only the
anti-aliased perimeter differs, which is the pill's own edge blending against a different background. The
message, the `Undo` label and the countdown ring are therefore exactly as legible over the frosted sheet
as they are over bare Today, which is the composition rounds 14–17 already signed (§1).

**And it cost nothing where nothing was wrong.** The toast plus an 8px shadow margin in
`undo-toast-1024/1366/1920-*` is **byte-identical to round 17** (max delta 0); at 393 that same box clips
the mic orb and reads max delta 7, below threshold. `zIndex: 105` changed no pixel in the state the pass
was already photographing (§1).

**The eight new frames are good work in their own right, not merely proof.** Judged against the pack as
new material: pack-correct offsets (24 desktop, 90 phone) and widths (280 / 248), centred on the same
axis as the 900-wide dialog, opaque over the frosted surface, one soft shadow, the mic orb and tab bar
correctly *under* the sheet exactly as `jstack-mock-v11.html` pins them (§2).

**R15-01 has not regressed**, and this pass was again a genuine test of it: all eight `tasks-gantt-*`
frames read `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep` against a Today of `Saturday 5 September`, and the capture ran at
**05:16–05:19 local on 6 September** — past local midnight, the only window in which that defect was ever
visible (§3).

**All eight `locked-*` frames are byte-identical to round 17** and still show the gate and nothing else
(§3).

**The 118 shared frames are clean** — zero dimension changes, 24,982 differing sub-pixels banded and
classified into four families with no residue, and no band anywhere near a toast (§4).

The V2.1 list (the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024, a web hover pass), the
two standing evidence gaps (the mic orb's listening pulse, the Firefox half of the scrollbar rule) and
the `date-basis.test.ts` allow-list the qa-auditor ruled on in its round 8 are **not re-raised**. I add
one narrow evidence gap of the same kind in §6 and it is not a blocker.

I have refused three times. This is not a fourth, and it is not agreement for its own sake: R17-01 was
the one thing I asked for, the remedy that shipped is the one I proposed, and it is now visible in the
frame set instead of only in a live DOM I had to drive myself.

---

## 1 · The fix, verified as SHIPPED on the pixels — not accepted

I was told what the fix does. I checked each claim against the committed bytes.

### 1.1 The toast owns its own pixels over the sheet

Pill geometry, located by fill colour in every one of the sixteen toast-bearing frames:

| Frame family | Pill x | Pill y | W × H | Bottom inset | Centre offset from viewport centre |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `*-1920-*` | 820–1099 | 1000–1055 | **280 × 56** | **24** | **0.0** |
| `*-1366-*` | 543–822 | 820–875 | **280 × 56** | **24** | **0.0** |
| `*-1024-*` | 372–651 | 688–743 | **280 × 56** | **24** | **0.0** |
| `*-393-*` | 73–320 | 706–761 | **248 × 56** | **90** | **0.5** (odd viewport width) |

Identical in `undo-toast-*` and `toast-over-sheet-*` — the same pill, to the pixel, in both states. That
satisfies `jstack-app/design/README.md:165` exactly:

> Undo toast `.js-toast`: Selected-ink fill, 12px text, radius 10, fixed bottom centre (90 on phone, 24
> desktop). "Undo" with an 18px ring showing seconds left. Ten seconds, then gone.

**Fill, over an overlay, is unchanged.** `43·42·38` light, `236·233·226` dark — the same values the
no-overlay frames carry. Round 17's defect showed as "a grey smear"; a scrim in front of the pill cannot
leave the fill numerically identical to a pill with nothing in front of it. It does. The toast is in
front.

**Interior byte-identity, the stronger test.** Cropping the pill inset 3px on every side and differencing
`undo-toast-<w>-<s>` against `toast-over-sheet-<w>-<s>`:

| | 393 | 1024 | 1366 | 1920 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| light | bbox `None`, max `0` | bbox `None`, max `0` | bbox `None`, max `0` | bbox `None`, max `0` |
| dark | bbox `None`, max `0` | bbox `None`, max `0` | bbox `None`, max `0` | bbox `None`, max `0` |

Eight pairs, zero differing pixels inside the pill. This is what answers the question I was asked to
answer — **contrast against the frosted surface behind it**: there is no contrast question, because the
surface behind it contributes nothing. The pill is opaque, the ring's hairline and its `10` sit on the
same Selected-ink they always sat on, and the `Undo` target reads at the same weight-500 12px it does on
bare Today. I read all eight rings at 6× to confirm rather than infer: full circle, `10` centred, no
clipping, no fringing beyond the LCD subpixel fringe round 14 already recorded for this build.

### 1.2 It cost nothing where no overlay is open

The whole risk of a z-index is that it moves something else. Cropping the pill plus an 8px shadow margin
in the `undo-toast-*` frames and differencing against round 17:

- `undo-toast-1024/1366/1920-{light,dark}` — bbox `None`, max delta **0**. Byte-identical.
- `undo-toast-393-{light,dark}` — max delta **7**, below the 8 threshold, and confined to x 300–329,
  which is the mic orb's box clipped by my crop, not the toast.

So the shipped z-index is invisible in the state the pass was already photographing, and visible only in
the state it was not. That is the correct signature for this fix.

### 1.3 It cannot climb over the gate — the one claim a still cannot carry

Verified structurally, because no frame can show it: `app/_layout.tsx:194` renders `<ToastHost />` as the
last child of `<View ref={contentRef}>` (opened at `:150`), and `<FaceIDGate />` sits at `:196`, **outside**
that view. `Gate.tsx:77` is `zIndex: 110` and the privacy shield `_layout.tsx:200` is `zIndex: 200`, both
outside. React Native Web gives `contentRef` its own stacking context, so `105` is bounded by the wrapper
and cannot reach past `110`. The eight byte-identical `locked-*` frames are the pixel half of the same
statement (§3).

**The stack now matches `jstack-mock-v11.html`'s own hand-pinned numbers, in order:**

| Mock v11 | Shipped `e296ea8` |
|---|---|
| `.tabbar` 20, `.mic` 21, `#deskbar` 22 | unset (auto) inside the content wrapper |
| `.ov` 30, `.sheet` 35 | `Dialog.tsx:31`, `Sheet.tsx:24`, `SettingsSheet.tsx:89` — all `zIndex: 100` |
| `#toast` **40** | `Toast.tsx:71` — **`zIndex: 105`** |
| `.lock` **50** | `Gate.tsx:77` — **`zIndex: 110`** (and the shield at 200) |

Round 17 said the mock's numbers were the specification the commit had inverted. They are now the
specification the commit satisfies, rank for rank.

### 1.4 The new test, and why I am not re-running its falsification

I read `e2e/core/decisions.spec.ts`'s added block. It asks the only question that matters —
`document.elementFromPoint` at the toast's own bounding-box centre — in **both** directions: with the
Settings sheet open it must return something matching `^toast`, and after the SEC-03 `visibilitychange`
path it must return `facelock`. That is the paint-order assertion round 17 §6 asked for, in the shape it
asked for. `evidence/e2e-summary.json` moves 410 → **412** total, 381 → **383** passed, **0 failed**.

I did not re-run the red half, and it does not need re-running by me: `Received string:
"settings-appearance"` is *my own round-17 measurement*, taken at 393 with the Settings sheet open, on
the same build. The falsification replays a number I produced. What I owed this round was the pixels, and
the pixels are in §1.1.

## 2 · The eight new frames, judged as new work against the pack

`toast-over-sheet-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}` — 393 × 852, 1024 × 768, 1366 × 900, 1920 × 1080,
viewport captures, one per width and scheme. No frame is blank, none is the wrong screen, none shows the
gate. I applied the seven-point checklist to each.

**Composition — deliberate, not merely on top.** The Settings dialog is **900 wide, centred on the
viewport** at all three desktop widths (x 510–1409 at 1920, 233–1132 at 1366, 62–961 at 1024). The toast
is 280 wide, centred on the viewport. Both therefore sit on the same vertical axis, and the pill lands
with ~310px of dialog either side of it. That is not an accident of layering; it is two centred things
agreeing.

**Position relative to the sheet's own edges — measured, then judged.** The dialog's bottom edge sits at
y 1036 (1920), 863 (1366), 736 (1024); the pill's bottom at 1055 / 875 / 743. So the pill **overhangs the
dialog's bottom edge by 19 / 12 / 7px** onto the scrim. I looked hard at this, because a 7px overhang at
1024 is exactly the near-miss shape Josh calls amateur when it is one. It is not one. The toast is
anchored to the viewport at the pack's 24; the dialog has its own margin; they are independent layers and
the pill is fully opaque with one soft shadow, so it reads as a floating layer above the dialog rather
than as a child of it that failed to align. Aligning the two would require the toast to know a dialog is
open, which is the coupling that produced R17-01 in the first place. Correct as shipped.

**The phone, and the tab bar.** At 393 the Settings sheet fills the viewport, so there is no tab bar
under the toast in this state — and the toast still sits at the pack's 90, not at 24. That is the right
call: the offset does not jump when the sheet closes and the tab bar comes back. The pill's 248 width
leaves 73px of margin on the left and 72 on the right; the ellipsis on `RACQ home insurance …` is message
body, unchanged from the set signed on rounds 14–17, and I am not re-raising it.

**The mic orb and the tab bar are correctly *under* the sheet.** This is the first frame set in which
that could be seen at all, so I checked it rather than assumed it. `jstack-mock-v11.html` pins `.mic`
at 21 and `.tabbar` at 20, both below `.ov` 30 and `.sheet` 35 — so the orb disappearing behind a
full-viewport phone sheet and dimming through the desktop scrim is the mock's own intent, not a casualty
of this commit. At 1920 dark the orb is visible through the scrim at 40% as the mock's
`rgba(25,24,21,.4)` predicts. Not a defect.

**Surfaces.** The sheet renders on exactly the same tokens as the already-signed `settings-*` frames —
frame corners `220·220·219` light and `38·36·33` dark in both, to the value. Frosted panel, hairline row
rules, radius 10 cards, one soft shadow on the pill. No 2px border anywhere, no float, no stretched card.

**Colour.** Nothing new. The pill is Selected-ink on the sheet's own surface (README:53's one sanctioned
use of Selected fill); the ring hairline is the toast-ring token, not Marker; no Alert anywhere in the
Settings sheet except `Hold to lock`, which is the emergency lock and is exactly where the pack puts
Alert. No per-category hue, no v1.2 green, no pure black or white surface.

**Type.** Every string in these frames is a string the `settings-*` frames already carry, in the same
scale: `Settings` 26/1 serif, section labels 11.5 uppercase tracked in Accent ink, row titles 12.5, row
subtitles 10.5 Muted, segment labels 12.5. Nothing bold, nothing italic, the only 600 in any frame is the
rail wordmark, and it is under the scrim.

**Text.** No word broken mid-word, no clipped or ellipsised label inside a button, chip or segment. The
toast covers row *labels* it happens to sit over (`Theme` at 1024, `Export everything` at 1366/1920), but
covers no control — the Auto/Light/Dark segment, the `Export` button and the `manage` link all stay
whole and visible — and it is a ten-second transient. The Settings sheet has no Save button to hide;
`One account · 3 devices · changes save as you make them` is its own contract.

**Dark.** Same layout as light at every width, same column count, nothing appearing or disappearing. The
pill inverts to `236·233·226` on `43·42·38` text, which is the same pair the signed `undo-toast-*` dark
frames carry.

**Density.** 1920 and 1366 read as a dashboard with the sheet as a two-column panel over it; 1024 as a
tablet with the sheet as one column; 393 as a phone with the sheet filling the screen. Each is the
`settings-*` composition at that width, already signed, plus one pill.

## 3 · R15-01 has not regressed, and the `locked-*` frames still show only the gate

**All eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames read `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`.** I cropped the axis band out of each
of the eight and read the label clusters at 3× rather than inferring six from two: 393 light and dark,
1024 light and dark, 1366 light and dark, 1920 light and dark — the same three strings in every one.
`today-1920-light` and `today-393-dark` both print **`Saturday 5 September`**. 29 Aug + 7 = 5 September;
5 September + 21 = 26 Sep — the fixed −7/+21 window around one instant, formatted on one basis.

**And the capture was again past local midnight, so the condition was live.** Two independent readings
agree:

- The Accent-ink now-rule in `today-1920-light` sits at **y = 540**; in `72e6ce0`'s copy it sat at
  **y = 525**. At round 17's measured 24px/hour that is **+37.5 minutes**.
- The frames' own mtimes put the run at **05:16:17 → 05:19:09 local on 6 September**, i.e. 19:16–19:19
  UTC on 5 September, and `e296ea8` was committed at 05:19:57. Round 17's run was at 04:40. Elapsed:
  **38 minutes** — which matches the 37.5 the pixels gave to within half a minute, and confirms round
  17's px/hour scale from the other end.

Local date **6 September**, displayed date **5 September**: the two clocks disagreed at capture time,
which is the only window in which R15-01 was ever visible. Had it survived, the axis would read
`30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`. It reads `29 Aug`.

**The `locked-*` frames.** All eight are **byte-identical** to `72e6ce0`'s — zero differing pixels, at
four widths and both schemes. I opened `locked-1920-light` and `locked-393-dark` and read them: warm
ground edge to edge, the `JSTACK` wordmark, `Locked. Unlock with your passkey.`, one `Unlock with
passkey` button. No app content, no card, no rail, no tab bar, no toast. Ground samples at all four
corners and the centre of `locked-393-dark` and `locked-1920-dark` are `25·24·21` — `#191815`, not black,
painted behind the safe area. The commit that touched the gate's neighbourhood rendered it bit-for-bit as
it did on rounds 16 and 17.

## 4 · The 118 shared frames: nothing else moved, and every pixel is accounted for

**No frame changed size.** All 118 pairs compared against `72e6ce0`; **zero** dimension changes. These
are full-page captures for 15 of the 16 screens, so any reflow would have moved a document height at
once. `settings-1024-*` is still 1024 × 1952, `today-393-*` still 2308 tall, `decision-bill-393-*` still
2332.

**Ten frames are pixel-identical** — all eight `locked-*`, plus `settings-1366-dark` and
`settings-1920-light`.

**24,982 differing pixels across the other 108, banded and classified with zero residue.** I grouped
every pixel with a channel delta > 8 into connected regions (20px grouping gap) and read every band.
Four families, and nothing outside them:

1. **The mic orb** — a ≤46px box in the bottom-right corner of every frame that has one (x from W−70 to
   W−24), deltas 15–65. Its idle render is not bit-stable between runs; position, size and clearance are
   unchanged everywhere. Standing evidence gap, not a defect.
2. **The Today now-rule, 15px lower.** Exactly two 1px Accent-ink rows 15px apart, and the pixel count is
   exactly **2 × the band width** in every case — 1920: 784 = 2 × 392 (x 880–1271); 1366: 540 = 2 × 270
   (x 720–989); 1024: 530 = 2 × 265 (x 713–977); 393: 590 = 2 × 295 (x 64–358). One line, moved, nothing
   else. Present in `today-*`, `decision-bill-*` and `undo-toast-*` — the three screens that show the day
   strip. 15px ÷ 24px/hour = 37.5 minutes, the elapsed time between the two capture runs (§3).
3. **The same rule read through a frosted overlay's blur** — `arrange-1024-{light,dark}` (y 522–543,
   x 850–974, n ≈ 1,700) and `settings-1024-{light,dark}` (y 522–543, x 962–974), max delta 10–12, at the
   same y as the unobstructed rule. This is the sharpest evidence available that the backdrop stack is
   still intact: an overlay that had stopped sampling the content beneath it would have gone flat here.
   Worth stating again this round, because the node that moved lives in that stack — and it is not flat.
4. **Date-derived content, 37.5 minutes of window drift** — timeline bars translated 1px along their
   tracks in `tasks-list-*`, `tasks-board-*`, `tasks-done-*` and `tasks-gantt-*`, in 7-row bands at the
   42px row pitch. 28 days across ~670px is ~1px/hour; 37.5 minutes rounds to 1px on some bars and 0 on
   others, which is what the counts show (15–184 per band).

**The Gantt axis label rows carry no band at all.** The `tasks-gantt-*` bands begin at y 201 — the first
bar row — and the axis text band at y 162–188 is empty in every one of the eight. The clock moved; the
day did not. That is R15-01's fix holding under the only condition that can break it.

**No band touches a toast.** In `undo-toast-1920-light` the two bands are the now-rule (y 526–541,
x 880–1271) and the orb (y 1025–1057, x 1851–1891). The pill occupies x 820–1099, y 1000–1055 — no band
inside it. Same at every width.

No card moved, no column changed width, no radius or hairline changed, no type reflowed, no ground token
shifted.

## 5 · The seven-point checklist

Layout across the 118 shared frames is provably identical to the set signed on rounds 14–17 (§4: zero
dimension changes, zero structural bands), so I re-derived the checklist in full on the **eight new
frames** (§2) and re-ran it as a sample on `undo-toast-1920-light`, `undo-toast-393-dark`,
`tasks-gantt-1920-light`, `tasks-gantt-393-light`, `today-1920-light`, `today-393-dark`,
`locked-1920-light`, `locked-393-dark`, plus every region flagged in §4.

1. **Columns.** `tasks-gantt-1920-light` and `undo-toast-1920-light` are still rail (200) + 3 columns,
   left-aligned, the third column's bottom left empty — which the pack calls correct, not a gap.
   `tasks-gantt-393-light` and `undo-toast-393-light` are one column with the floating tab bar and the
   orb above it on the right. The new frames put a 900-wide centred panel over that, at every desktop
   width, and a full-viewport sheet at 393.
2. **Type.** No text outside §4's family 4 changed at all, so rounds 14–17's type findings carry intact,
   and §2 re-derives the scale on the new frames. The only weight-600 in any frame is the rail wordmark.
   Nothing bold, nothing italic. The one sub-10.5 numeral in the set is the countdown ring's `10`, which
   the pack's own scale sanctions — *"Badge: 10 white on Marker"*, *"Tab label: 10 (phone)"* — the
   `body never below 10.5px` rule governs body, and a numeric badge inside an 18px ring is not body.
   Judged correct, recorded so it is not re-litigated.
3. **Colour.** The now-rule is still Accent ink (74·94·112) — not Marker, not Alert. The toast is
   Selected-ink fill, README:53's one sanctioned use. Alert appears only on `Hold to lock`. No new hue
   anywhere, in any frame.
4. **Surfaces.** Radii, hairlines and the deliberately small card-to-ground step are byte-identical
   wherever the clock did not move them; §4's family-3 blur bands prove the frosted backdrops still
   sample beneath, which is exactly the stack this commit reached into. One soft shadow on the pill.
5. **Text.** Nothing newly clipped or wrapped. The toast's `RACQ home insurance · …` ellipsis at all four
   widths is unchanged from the set signed on rounds 14–17 and is message body, not a button, chip or
   segment label; not re-raised.
6. **Dark.** Every dark frame differs from its round-17 self by the same families as its light twin and
   by nothing else. Same layout, same column count, warm `#191815` ground painted edge to edge, verified
   at four corners and centre on `locked-393-dark` and `locked-1920-dark`.
7. **Density.** Unchanged by construction; 1920 still reads as a dashboard, 1024 as a tablet, 393 as a
   phone. The new frames hold that: the sheet is two columns at 1366/1920, one at 1024, full-screen at
   393.

Also checked, since a missing or wrong frame is itself a defect: the filename set in `demo/v2/` is
`72e6ce0`'s **plus exactly eight** `toast-over-sheet-*` files — no removal, no rename, no other addition.
126 files for 16 screens × 8, less the two `arrange-393-*` the capture skips by design.

## 6 · Recorded, not raised

- **The evidence gap round 17 named is closed, and closed the right way.** `capture-v2.mjs` now takes the
  shot from inside the state the defect lived in, at every width and both schemes, rather than adding a
  single token frame. That is the difference between a regression photograph and a reviewable
  composition, and §2 could only be written because it is the latter.
- **One narrow new evidence gap, of the same kind as the mic pulse.** The countdown ring reads `10` in
  both the `undo-toast-*` and the `toast-over-sheet-*` frames, because `capture-v2.mjs` takes them inside
  the same first second (300ms + one click + a `waitFor` + 300ms), and `Toast.tsx`'s interval is 1000ms.
  So these stills confirm the ring's shape, its legibility and its start value, and they cannot confirm
  that it depletes. That is motion a still cannot carry — the same class as the mic orb's 1.4s listening
  pulse. Not a defect, not a blocker, and I am not asking for a frame: a second `toast-over-sheet` shot
  three seconds later would prove it, if the qa-auditor wants it cheap.
- **The pill's 7–19px overhang below the dialog's bottom edge is correct** (§2), and I record the measured
  numbers here so the auditor can see it was measured and decided rather than skated over: dialog bottom
  y 1036 / 863 / 736, pill bottom y 1055 / 875 / 743, at 1920 / 1366 / 1024.
- **Standing evidence gaps, unchanged and not restated:** the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse, and the
  Firefox half of the scrollbar rule which cannot appear in a Chromium pass. Neither is a defect.
- **The V2.1 list stands as deferred** — the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024,
  a web hover pass. Not blockers, not re-litigated. Nor is the `clock.ts` allow-list note from round 16,
  which the qa-auditor ruled on in its round 8: latent, not live, V2.1. I accept that ruling.
- **What clock the owner should see is still open, and correctly so.** These frames show one basis
  consistently; they cannot say whether UTC is the right basis for a man in Brisbane. That remains a
  product decision `HANDOVER_v2.md` already names as a contract addition to request. One basis beats two,
  and two was R15-01.

## Verdict

**UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND**

**One open frame defect (R19-01, MINOR) and one source-level finding I was asked for (R19-02).**

**B9-01's fix is real and I verified it rather than took it.** In all eight new frames "Lock everything
now" is transparent — the most common colour inside its box is the dialog surface itself, contrast
**1.00:1** against the panel beside it, so there is no fill — outlined 1px in Alert with Alert text at
12.5/500, radius 8, 140 × 36 at every width and both schemes. Measured off the pixels: light
`#B0553F` on `221·221·221` = **3.61:1**; dark `#D9785E` on `39·37·34` = **4.79:1**. The auditor's
2.88 / 2.55 are gone (§1).

**And it reads as the dangerous one without shouting.** It is the only coloured element in the dialog;
Cancel is the same 500 weight and the same 36px height in Hairline and Ink, 76px wide against the alert
button's 140. Colour, not size, not a fill, does the work — and it is the same treatment as the
`Hold to lock` button on the Emergency card that opens it, which is visible in the same frame at 1024
(§1.2).

**R19-01, and it is in the new frames, not the fix.** The four consequence lines lost mock v11's
full-width `card pad0 list` container and ship as bare text. Two things follow, both measured: the
destructive button row sits **9px** below the last consequence line — *less* than the **11px** between two
consecutive consequence lines, and against the **14px** the app's own decision cards put above their verb
rows; and at 1366 and 1920 this is **the only dialog in the set whose content does not reach its own
panel's right edge** (51% filled at 1920, 57% at 1366, against Arrange, Task detail and Decision history,
which all fill theirs). One fix cures both (§3).

**R19-02 — I was asked whether `saturated-fill.test.ts`'s allow-list is wrong, and it is, though not in its
judgement.** Both allow-listed files produce **zero** matches against the guard's own pattern: `Header.tsx`
writes `backgroundColor: summary.health === "degraded" ? c.alert : c.ok` and `Spend.tsx` writes `stroke=`,
neither of which `/backgroundColor:\s*c\.(alert|ok)/` can match. The exemptions exempt nothing. Worse, the
form `Header.tsx` uses — a ternary — is the most natural way this fill comes back, and the guard is blind
to it; and it never scans `theme/`, where `Btn`, `Card` and every surface primitive live (§3.2).

**R17-01 has not regressed, and the new frames are a second, independent witness.** The toast's message
region is **byte-identical** between `undo-toast-<w>-<s>` and `emergency-confirm-<w>-<s>` at all four widths
and both schemes (max delta `0`), with the same fills — so it is fully opaque and fully in front of the
dialog and its scrim. At 393, where the dialog fills the viewport, the pill sits directly on the panel (§4).

**And it closed round 18's own evidence gap by accident.** The ring reads `10` in `undo-toast-*` and **`7`**
in `emergency-confirm-*` — same run, same page context, three seconds apart. The countdown depletes. I
asked for nothing and got the proof (§4).

**R15-01 has not regressed**, and this pass was again a genuine test of it: all eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames
read `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep` against a Today of `Saturday 5 September`, and the capture ran
**06:35:49 → 06:39:22 local on 6 September** — past local midnight, the only window in which that defect was
ever visible (§4).

**All eight `locked-*` frames are byte-identical to round 18** and still show the gate and nothing else (§5).

**The 126 shared frames are clean** — zero dimension changes, ten pixel-identical, 18,717 differing
sub-pixels banded and classified into four families with no residue (§5).

This is my fourth refusal. It is not a refusal of the fix, which is correct and was executed against the
right three documents. It is a refusal of the dialog around it, which no pass had ever photographed, and
which the same commit put in front of me and told me to judge as new work.

## 1 · The B9-01 fix, verified as SHIPPED on the pixels — not accepted

I was told what the fix does. I checked each claim against the committed bytes.

### 1.1 There is no fill, and the outline is the pack's

The button's box is located by its Alert-coloured border in every one of the eight frames — two 126px
horizontal runs and two 22px vertical runs, which is a 140 × 36 rounded rectangle with radius 8 corners
(140 − 2 × 8 = 124, plus antialiasing = 126). Identical at every width and in both schemes:

| Frame family | Button box | W × H | Cancel box start |
|---|---|---|---|
| `*-1920-*` | (477, 614)–(616, 649) | **140 × 36** | 622 |
| `*-1366-*` | (249, 524)–(388, 559) | **140 × 36** | 394 |
| `*-1024-*` | (191, 458)–(330, 493) | **140 × 36** | 336 |
| `*-393-*` | (16, 272)–(155, 307) | **140 × 36** | 161 |

Inside the box, the most common colour is the dialog surface itself — `221·221·221` light, `39·37·34`
dark — and the surface sampled 40px to its right is the same value. **Contrast of the button's interior
against the panel beside it: 1.00:1.** There is nothing there. That is what an outlined button looks like
measured, and it is what `jstack-app/design/README.md:149` requires:

> Primary `.js-btn-primary`: Accent soft fill, Accent ink text, 12.5/500, padding 9, radius 8. **Never a
> saturated fill, never white text.**

and README:225's Don't list — *"saturated button fills"* — and `handoff.md:59`'s
*"'Hold to lock' outlined in alert"*, and mock v11's `.btn.alert{color:var(--alert);border-color:var(--alert)}`,
which sets colour and border only. Four documents, one rendering, and the rendering now matches.

**Contrast, measured rather than asserted.** Glyph core against the button's own interior:

| | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| Label `#B0553F` / `#D9785E` on the panel | **3.61:1** | **4.79:1** |
| 1px border on the panel | **3.66:1** | **4.95:1** |

The auditor's numbers for the fill it replaced were 2.88 and 2.55 — under even the 3:1 floor. Both halves
now clear 3:1, which is the bar for a non-text control boundary (the border) and for large text; the label
at 12.5/500 is not large text, so the light figure does not reach 4.5:1. **I am not raising that**, and the
reason is that the pixel matches the pack exactly: `README.md:52` fixes Alert at `#B0553F` and README:213's
contrast table names Ink, Muted and Accent-ink pairs and no Alert pair at all. The same token pair on the
already-signed `Hold to lock` measures **4.18:1** light on the lighter card surface, so the dialog's 3.61 is
the same token meeting a darker bar surface, not a regression this commit introduced. It is a pack-token
question for V2.1, recorded in §7 with the numbers so nobody has to re-measure it.

### 1.2 It reads as the dangerous one — the composition, not the rule

Judged as a pair, not as a checkbox:

- **It is the only coloured thing in the dialog.** Title, meta, four consequence lines, close glyph and
  Cancel are all Ink or Muted. One warm red object, and it is the irreversible one. That is README's
  Principle 3 working the way it is meant to — *"Colour means you can act"* — with Alert reserved to
  README:68's *"needs-eyes items, over-budget bars, the emergency lock"*.
- **It does not shout.** No fill, no white text, no size jump: same 36px height and same 12.5/500 weight as
  Cancel. The only differences are hue and a 140 vs 76 width the label itself earns.
- **Cancel is quiet without being weak.** Hairline border, Ink label, full 36px target. It is not a text
  link and it is not styled as an escape hatch — a person who wants out has an equal-height button.
- **It matches the control that opened it.** At 1024 the Emergency card is visible below the dialog in the
  same frame, its own `Hold to lock` outlined in the same Alert against the same 1px Alert card border. The
  card and the thing it opens finally agree — which is the half of B-50 that had been wrong for a stage.
- **Both schemes, all four widths.** The box geometry above is identical light and dark; only the token
  values swap. Dark reads slightly stronger (4.79 vs 3.61) and that is the correct direction for a warm red
  on a warm dark ground.

The destructive verb leads and Cancel follows, which is mock v11's own order in `lockc()`. Left-aligned,
hug-width, not stretched and not centred — the same button-row grammar as Arrange's `Revert to yesterday ·
Done`. Nothing here is centred on desktop.

## 2 · The eight new frames, judged as new work against the pack

`emergency-confirm-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}` — 393 × 852, 1024 × 768, 1366 × 900, 1920 × 1080,
viewport captures, one per width and scheme. No frame is blank, none is the wrong screen, none shows the
gate; the rail's active item is Agents in all six desktop frames and the Agents page is legible behind the
scrim. I applied the seven-point checklist to each.

**The chrome.** Desktop: `Dialog.tsx`'s 66vw capped at 1000 — 1000 wide at 1920 (x 460–1460), 901 at 1366
(x 233–1134), 676 at 1024 (x 174–850) — centred on the viewport, radius 10, one 1px Card-border hairline,
one soft shadow, frosted over a blurred scrim. Phone: the panel fills all 393 × 852; I sampled the ground
down the left margin, the centre and the right margin at 20px intervals and it holds `220·219·219` from
y 0 to y 851, so the page rows visible below the content are the Agents tab read *through* the translucent
bar surface, not the panel ending early. Header 68px with a hairline under it; the close glyph is Muted at
20px in a 36px target. No 2px border anywhere, no float, no stretched card.

**Title.** `Emergency lock`, Source Serif 4 upright at 20px, weight 400 — the same chrome as the Task
detail, Decision history and Arrange dialogs already signed, and gentler than mock v11's `.dlg h2{font:500
22px}`. Ink band 440–459 at 1920. Nothing bold, nothing italic. The only weight-600 in any of these eight
frames is the rail wordmark, and it is under the scrim.

**The meta line.** `For a stolen or unlocked phone, a compromised account or a suspected intrusion.` at
10.5 Muted on the bar surface — the pack's *"Keep meta text at 10.5 only in Muted on Card or Ground"*
(README:213), and this is the bar surface, which is the overlay recipe `Dialog.tsx` cites. It leads the
four lines and is visibly subordinate to them. Correct.

**The four consequence lines.** 12.5 Ink, weight 400, left-aligned, on an 11px rhythm. As copy they are
well ordered — two destructions, one reassurance, one recovery path — and they say what the lock does
without a single word of hedging. As a composition they are where R19-01 lives (§3).

**Vertical rhythm, measured at every width (light; dark is identical to the row).** Ink-band gaps:

| | meta → line 1 | line → line | line 4 → button box |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920 | 13 | 11 · 11 · 11 | **9** |
| 1366 | 13 | 11 · 11 · 11 | **9** |
| 1024 | 13 | 11 · 11 · 11 | **9** |
| 393 | 15 | 11 · 11 · 11 | **9** |

Even, deliberate, and wrong in exactly one place — the last column (§3.1).

**Colour.** Alert appears twice per frame: the button, and the Emergency card's 1px border behind the
scrim. Nowhere else. No Marker inside the dialog. No per-category hue, no v1.2 green, no pure black or
white surface, no gradient. The toast is Selected-ink, README:165's one sanctioned use.

**Text.** No word broken mid-word. No clipped or ellipsised label inside a button, chip or segment —
`Lock everything now` and `Cancel` are whole at all four widths, and the button hugs its label rather than
truncating it. No two-line button label. At 393 the fourth consequence wraps to `…secrets rotate / before
anything resumes`, three words on the second line, which is a clean wrap.

**Dark.** Same layout as light at every width, same column count, nothing appearing or disappearing, the
button box identical to the pixel. Warm `#191815`-family ground painted edge to edge behind the scrim; the
dialog surface reads `39·37·34`, not black.

**Density.** 1920 and 1366 read as a dashboard with a panel over it, 1024 as a tablet, 393 as a phone with
the panel filling the screen. The Agents page behind is the composition already signed on rounds 14–18,
dimmed and blurred, with the mic orb and the tab bar correctly *under* the overlay exactly as mock v11 pins
them (`.tabbar` 20, `.mic` 21, `.ov` 30).

**And how it sits over the Agents tab.** Well, and with one accidental grace: at 1024 the dialog clears the
Emergency card, so the owner can see the card they held and the dialog it opened in one frame, both
outlined in the same Alert. At 1920 and 1366 the dialog covers the middle of the page and the Security
checks column stays readable to its right. Nothing important is hidden that the dialog does not replace.

## 3 · Defects

### 3.1 R19-01 · MINOR · the consequence block lost its container, and the destructive button lost its gap

**Frames:** all eight `emergency-confirm-*`. The button-gap half is visible in every one; the
panel-emptiness half in `emergency-confirm-1366-{light,dark}` and `emergency-confirm-1920-{light,dark}`.

**What is wrong.** `jstack-mock-v11.html:630` — the behavioural reference this build is judged against —
renders the four consequences inside a full-width bordered card with hairline row rules:

> `openDlg('Emergency lock','<p class="meta">…</p><div class="card pad0 list"><div class="li"><span class="x">Every session and token revoked</span></div>…</div><div class="verbs" style="margin-top:10px">…`

`EmergencyLock.tsx:72` ships them as bare `Text` in a `View` with `gap: 8` and no container, and the button
row follows on `marginBottom: space[4]` = 9. Two measured consequences:

1. **The destructive button is separated from the prose above it by less than the prose is separated from
   itself.** 9px from the last consequence's ink to the button's border, against 11px between two
   consecutive consequence lines — and against the **14px** the app's own decision cards put above their
   verb rows (`decision-bill-1920-light`: meta ink ends y 354, the `Open NAB · Revise · Later` row's box
   starts y 368; the *From your EA* card: `because:` ink ends y 751, the `Block it · Leave it` box starts
   y 765). So the single most irreversible control in the app has the tightest body-to-verb gap in the
   build, at every width and in both schemes. In the mock the same junction carries `margin-top:10px`
   *plus* the card's bottom border and its own padding — a break you can see.
2. **At 1366 and 1920 it is the only dialog in the set whose content does not reach its own panel.** The
   longest line runs to x 972 inside a panel that ends at x 1460: **495 of 968 usable px, 51% filled**, with
   488px of empty surface beside it. At 1366: 495 of 869, **57%**. Every sibling in the same chrome fills
   its width — `arrange-1920-light`'s rows run edge to edge with their toggles pinned right,
   `task-detail-1920-light`'s subtask rows and Activity card span the panel, `decision-history-1920-light`'s
   search field and its two rows span it. The mock's container is what fills it; it was dropped, so this one
   dialog reads like a letterbox with the content pushed into its top-left corner. At 1024 (77% filled) and
   393 (wraps) the composition is fine, which is why this half is width-specific.

`Dialog.tsx`'s own header comment is the standard the build set for itself, from ux-review R2-10:

> the old 60vh floor left the decision history standing 640px tall with two rows in its top 220px and 66%
> empty frosted panel below … README, Principles 2 defends blank space at the END of a list, **not a slab
> sized past it**.

That was ruled on height and fixed by making the dialog hug. The dialog does not hug horizontally, and this
is the first content short enough to expose it. `jstack-app/design/DISCREPANCIES.md` records no entry for
the emergency dialog, so the decision to drop the mock's container was never taken; it was never noticed,
for the same reason the fill was not — nobody had photographed this screen.

**I am confident about the measurements and about the button gap. I am less certain the panel emptiness
must block on its own** — no pack line fixes a dialog's content width, and Principles 2 does defend blank
space. I am naming it because my brief says a defect I am unsure about is still a defect, and because one
fix closes both halves.

**The fix I would make in source.** In `EmergencyLock.tsx`, wrap the four consequence lines in the mock's
container — a `Card` with `padding: 0` and four hairline-separated rows, the `card pad0 list` grammar the
Decision history dialog already uses — and give the button row the mock's own break above it. The container
spans the panel, so half 2 disappears; its bottom border plus the row's margin gives half 1 a visible gap.
If the container is judged wrong for a warning (a defensible view — a confirm dialog is not a list), then
the minimum fix is `marginBottom: space[7]` (16) or `space[9]` (24) on the consequence block, which brings
the destructive verb into line with the app's own 14px and above.

### 3.2 R19-02 · source-level · the saturated-fill guard's allow-list exempts nothing, and its pattern misses the form already in the tree

I was asked to say whether `jstack-app/tests/unit/saturated-fill.test.ts`'s allow-list is wrong. It is —
not in its judgement, which is right, but in fact.

The pattern is `/backgroundColor:\s*c\.(alert|ok)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])/g`. Run against the two allow-listed
files as they stand in `fb886e3`:

| File | The line the reason describes | Matches |
|---|---|---|
| `components/chrome/Header.tsx:96` | `backgroundColor: summary.health === "degraded" ? c.alert : c.ok` | **0** |
| `components/agents/Spend.tsx:38` | `stroke={clamped >= 1 ? c.alert : c.accent}` | **0** |

Neither file can ever hit the pattern, so both exemptions are inert: the suite passes identically with the
allow-list emptied. The second test only asserts that each entry names a real file and carries a reason
longer than 20 characters — it never asserts that the entry is *needed*, which is the one assertion that
would have caught this.

Two consequences that matter more than the dead entries:

- **The guard is blind to the ternary**, which is exactly how `Header.tsx` writes a conditional Alert fill
  today. `backgroundColor: bad ? c.alert : c.card` matches 0 times. That is the most natural way this
  defect comes back, and it is the form already modelled in the tree for somebody to copy.
- **It never scans `theme/`.** `sources()` walks `app` and `components` only, so `theme/ui.tsx` — where
  `Btn`, `BtnPrimary`, `BtnSm`, `Card` and every surface primitive are defined — is outside the rule. A
  saturated fill added to the base button would be invisible to the guard that exists to prevent exactly
  that.

I verified the guard does catch the defect it was written for: the removed line
`style={{ backgroundColor: c.alert, borderColor: c.alert }}` matches once. So the falsification the commit
describes is honest; the rule is just narrower than the sentence it claims to enforce
(*"no component may set `backgroundColor` to `c.alert` or `c.ok`"*).

**The fix I would make:** widen the pattern to `c.(alert|ok)` anywhere inside a `backgroundColor` value
(or lint the property's whole expression), add `theme` and `lib` to the scanned directories, and assert in
the second test that every allow-list entry actually produces at least one match — an entry that exempts
nothing should fail, not pass quietly.

This is a source finding, not a frame defect, and it is here because I was asked. It does not change what
the pixels say.

## 4 · R17-01 and R15-01 have not regressed — and one of them gained a witness

### 4.1 R17-01, confirmed twice over

The `emergency-confirm-*` frames were captured in the same page context as `toast-over-sheet-*`, three
seconds later, so the undo toast is still live in all eight. That makes them a **second, independent
witness** for R17-01 — an overlay of a different kind (a Dialog, not the Settings sheet) with the same
toast over it.

I located the pill by the geometry round 18 established (280 × 56 desktop at bottom inset 24; 248 × 56 at
90 on the phone; centred) and differenced its interior against the `undo-toast-*` frame at the same width
and scheme:

| | 393 | 1024 | 1366 | 1920 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| light — message region | max delta `0` | `0` | `0` | `0` |
| dark — message region | max delta `0` | `0` | `0` | `0` |
| pill fill | `43·42·38` / `236·233·226` — identical to `undo-toast-*` in all eight |

Eight pairs, **zero differing pixels** across the message and the `Undo` label. A scrim or a panel painting
over the pill could not leave the fill numerically identical to a pill with nothing in front of it. It
does. The toast is in front, and at 393 — where the dialog fills the whole viewport — the pill sits
directly on the dialog's own panel, which is the strongest form this witness can take.

The only difference inside the pill is the countdown region, and that is the point below.

### 4.2 Round 18's own evidence gap, closed by accident

Round 18 §6 recorded that the stills could confirm the ring's shape, legibility and start value but not
that it **depletes**, because every toast frame was taken inside the same first second. `emergency-confirm-*`
is taken three seconds later in the same run, so:

- `undo-toast-1920-light` ring reads **`10`**
- `emergency-confirm-1920-light` ring reads **`7`**

I read both at 6×. Same pill, same position, same fill, same `Undo` label at the same weight; the numeral
has counted down. The ring itself is a full hairline circle in both — the pack says *"'Undo' with an 18px
ring showing seconds left"*, and the seconds are shown by the numeral, not by an arc, so a full circle in
both is correct, not a stalled animation. **That gap is closed.** I asked for nothing and the capture
order gave it.

### 4.3 R15-01

All eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames read **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`**. I cropped the axis band out of each of
the eight and read the label clusters at up to 3×, rather than inferring six from two: 393 light and dark,
1024 light and dark, 1366 light and dark, 1920 light and dark — the same three strings in every one.
`today-1920-light` and `today-393-dark` both print **`Saturday 5 September`**. 29 Aug + 7 = 5 September;
5 September + 21 = 26 Sep — the fixed −7/+21 window around one instant, formatted on one basis.

**And the capture was again past local midnight, so the condition was live.** The frames' own mtimes put
the run at **06:35:49 → 06:39:22 local on 6 September**, i.e. 20:35–20:39 UTC on 5 September; `fb886e3` was
committed at 06:39:42. Local date **6 September**, displayed date **5 September** — the two clocks
disagreed at capture time, which is the only window in which R15-01 was ever visible. Had it survived, the
axis would read `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`. It reads `29 Aug`.

**And the diff proves it from the other side.** The `tasks-gantt-*` difference bands against round 18 all
begin at y 201 — the first bar row — and the axis label band at y 162–188 is **empty in every one of the
eight**. Between the two runs the clock moved 79 minutes; the day did not move at all.

---

## 5 · The 126 shared frames: nothing else moved, and every pixel is accounted for

**No frame changed size.** All 126 pairs compared against `e296ea8`; **zero** dimension changes. These are
full-page captures for 14 of the 17 screens, so any reflow would have moved a document height at once.
`settings-1024-*` is still 1024 × 1952, `today-393-*` still 2308 tall, `decision-bill-393-*` still 2332.

**Ten frames are pixel-identical** — all eight `locked-*`, plus `settings-1366-dark` and
`settings-1920-dark`.

**The filename set is `e296ea8`'s plus exactly eight** `emergency-confirm-*` files — no removal, no rename,
no other addition. 134 files for 17 screens × 8, less the two `arrange-393-*` the capture skips by design.

**18,717 differing pixels across the other 116, banded and classified with zero residue.** I grouped every
pixel with a channel delta > 8 into connected regions (21px grouping gap) and read every band. Four
families, and **nothing outside them** — a strict classifier left 0 unclassified bands:

1. **The mic orb** — 81 bands, 6,119px. A ≤70 × 60 box in the bottom-right corner of every frame that has
   one. Its idle render is not bit-stable between runs; position, size and clearance unchanged everywhere.
   Standing evidence gap, not a defect.
2. **The Today now-rule leaving the grid** — 22 bands, 6,734px, and this one deserves its own paragraph
   below. Each band is a single 1px row, 262–392px wide, at exactly the y where round 18 carried the
   Accent-ink rule; in round 19 that row is bare card surface. Present in `today-*`, `decision-bill-*` and
   `undo-toast-1024/1366/1920-*` — the screens that show the day strip, less `undo-toast-393-*`, whose
   viewport capture does not reach y 1312 where the strip sits. Exactly the right 22 frames.
3. **The same rule read through a frosted overlay's blur** — 2 bands, 1,694px, in
   `arrange-1024-{light,dark}` at y 537–543, x 850–974, max delta 11–12, at the same y as the unobstructed
   rule. Still the sharpest evidence available that the backdrop stack samples what is beneath it: an
   overlay that had stopped sampling would have gone flat here, and it did not.
4. **Date-derived content, 79 minutes of window drift** — 114 bands, 4,170px: timeline bars and the dashed
   EA bar translated 1px along their tracks in `tasks-list-*`, `tasks-board-*`, `tasks-done-*` and
   `tasks-gantt-*`, in bands at the 42px row pitch. 28 days across ~670px is ~1px/hour; 79 minutes rounds
   to 1px on some bars and 0 on others, which is what the counts show.

**On family 2 — the now-line is gone, and that is the app behaving correctly.** Round 18's frames carried
an Accent-ink `#4A5E70` rule at y 540 in the Today calendar; round 19's carry card surface there and no
rule anywhere in the track. `CalendarGrid.tsx:121` renders it only when `nowTop >= 0 && nowTop <=
TRACK_HEIGHT`, and the grid runs 06:00–20:00 on the app's UTC basis. Round 18's run was 19:16 UTC — inside
the window, y 540. Round 19's was 20:35 UTC — past 20:00, so the line correctly does not render. The
project's own e2e comment says as much: *"outside it the line correctly doesn't render"*. **Not a defect**,
and I record it rather than raise it because it is the previously-recorded clock-basis question becoming
visible instead of latent (§7).

**No card moved, no column changed width, no radius or hairline changed, no type reflowed, no ground token
shifted, and no band touches a toast.**

**The `locked-*` frames.** All eight are byte-identical to `e296ea8`'s — zero differing pixels, at four
widths and both schemes. I opened `locked-393-dark` and read it: warm ground edge to edge, the `JSTACK`
wordmark, `Locked. Unlock with your passkey.`, one `Unlock with passkey` button. No app content, no card,
no rail, no tab bar, no toast. The commit that touched the emergency lock's own neighbourhood rendered the
gate bit-for-bit as it did on rounds 16, 17 and 18.

## 6 · The seven-point checklist

Layout across the 126 shared frames is provably identical to the set signed on rounds 14–18 (§5: zero
dimension changes, zero structural bands), so I re-derived the checklist in full on the **eight new frames**
(§2) and re-ran it as a sample on `emergency-confirm-1920-light`, `emergency-confirm-393-light`,
`decision-bill-1920-light`, `task-detail-1920-light`, `decision-history-1920-light`, `arrange-1920-light`,
`tasks-gantt-1920-light`, `tasks-gantt-393-light`, `today-1920-light`, `locked-393-dark`, plus every region
flagged in §5.

1. **Columns.** `decision-bill-1920-light` is still rail (200) + 3 columns, left-aligned, the third
   column's bottom left empty — which the pack calls correct, not a gap. `tasks-gantt-393-light` is one
   column with the floating tab bar and the orb above it on the right. The new frames put a centred panel
   over that at every desktop width, and a full-viewport panel at 393. No section laid across columns.
2. **Type.** No text outside §5's family 4 changed at all, so rounds 14–18's type findings carry intact,
   and §2 re-derives the scale on the new frames: 20px serif dialog title at 400, 10.5 Muted meta, 12.5 Ink
   body, 12.5/500 button labels. Nothing bold, nothing italic, the only 600 in any frame is the rail
   wordmark. The one sub-10.5 numeral in the set remains the countdown ring's digit, which rounds 14–18
   judged sanctioned; it now reads `7` as well as `10` and is legible at both (§4.2).
3. **Colour.** Alert appears on the Emergency card border, its `Hold to lock`, the new dialog's `Lock
   everything now`, the Agent-issues dots and the over-budget row — README:68's list exactly, and nowhere
   near an expiry. The now-rule was Accent ink while it was on screen. The toast is Selected-ink. No
   Marker outside count badges and the mic. No per-category hue, no v1.2 green, no pure black or white
   surface, no gradient.
4. **Surfaces.** Radii, hairlines and the deliberately small card-to-ground step are byte-identical
   wherever the clock did not move them; §5's family-3 blur band proves the frosted backdrops still sample
   beneath. The new dialog is radius 10 with a 1px border and one soft shadow; its buttons are radius 8
   with 1px borders. No 2px border anywhere. Empty column bottoms left empty.
5. **Text.** Nothing newly clipped or wrapped inside a button, chip or segment. The toast's
   `RACQ home insurance · …` ellipsis is unchanged message body, not re-raised. The new dialog's one
   phone-width orphan is recorded in §7, not raised — my own checklist scopes the orphan rule to titles.
6. **Dark.** Every dark frame differs from its round-18 self by the same families as its light twin and by
   nothing else. Same layout, same column count, warm ground painted edge to edge, verified on
   `locked-393-dark` and inside the new dialog at `39·37·34`.
7. **Density.** Unchanged by construction; 1920 still reads as a dashboard, 1024 as a tablet, 393 as a
   phone. The new frames hold that at 1024 and 393; at 1366 and 1920 the dialog itself is the half of
   R19-01 I am least certain about (§3.1).

Also checked, since a missing or wrong frame is itself a defect: 134 files, no blanks, no wrong screens, no
frame showing the gate that should not, and the rail's active tab is correct in every new frame.

## 7 · Recorded, not raised

- **Alert's own contrast is a V2.1 token question, not this commit's.** The outlined label measures
  **3.61:1** light and **4.79:1** dark; the already-signed `Hold to lock` on the lighter card surface
  measures **4.18:1** light and **4.35:1** dark. Both clear the 3:1 floor for a control boundary and for
  large text; neither reaches 4.5:1 at 12.5/500 in light. The pixel matches `README.md:52`'s `#B0553F`
  exactly and README:213's contrast table names no Alert pair, so nothing in the pack is broken — the pack
  simply never set a bar for Alert. Darkening the light-mode Alert token would touch the card border, the
  issue dots and the over-budget bar too, which is a pack change, not a dialog change. Numbers recorded so
  it is measured and decided rather than skated over.
- **The phone meta line leaves `intrusion.` alone on its second line.** `emergency-confirm-393-{light,dark}`
  wraps `…or a suspected / intrusion.` — a single-word orphan. My checklist scopes that rule to titles and
  this is a 10.5 Muted meta line, so I am not raising it; but if R19-01 is fixed, shortening that sentence
  by one word would close it in the same edit.
- **The now-line's disappearance makes the clock-basis question visible for the first time.** At 06:35
  Brisbane the Today calendar shows **no now-line at all**, because on the app's UTC basis it is 20:35 and
  the grid ends at 20:00. The render is correct and guarded (§5). What is still open is whether UTC is the
  right basis for a man in Brisbane — round 18 recorded it, `HANDOVER_v2.md` names it as a contract
  addition to request, and this is the first frame set where the consequence is a missing element rather
  than a differently-placed one. One basis still beats two, and two was R15-01.
- **`jstack-app/evidence/contrast-report.json` is stale.** Its pairs are v1.2's green palette
  (`rgb(37,43,31)` grounds, `rgb(159,205,172)` fills), retired by ADR-05/ADR-06. It cannot speak to any V2
  colour, including the one this commit changed. Not a frame defect and the auditor owns the evidence
  files; noted because I opened it looking for a contrast bar and found a different app.
- **The pill's overhang below a dialog's bottom edge** — round 18 measured and decided this for the
  Settings sheet. It does not arise here: at 1024/1366/1920 the dialog clears the toast entirely, and at
  393 the dialog fills the viewport so there is no edge to overhang.
- **Standing evidence gaps, unchanged and not restated:** the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse, and the
  Firefox half of the scrollbar rule which cannot appear in a Chromium pass. Neither is a defect. Round
  18's third gap — the undo ring's depletion — is **closed** (§4.2).
- **The V2.1 list stands as deferred** — the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024, a
  web hover pass. Not blockers, not re-litigated. Nor is the `date-basis.test.ts` allow-list, which the
  qa-auditor ruled on: not required. I accept that ruling.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

**Commit reviewed:** `fb886e35e1ebcb7af3f2773a60b2e851a46cda62`
("fix(v2): a saturated alert fill in the one dialog no pass had photographed (B9-01)"),
committed 2026-09-06 06:39:42 +1000.
**Reviewed and written:** 6 September 2026, **06:41–07:04 AEST (UTC+10)** — after that commit, by the clock
and not only by git metadata (B7-07).

**One open frame defect across 134 frames — R19-01, MINOR — and one source-level finding I was asked for,
R19-02.**

**B9-01 is fixed and I verified it on the pixels, not accepted.** "Lock everything now" has no fill: the
most common colour inside its box is the dialog surface itself, 1.00:1 against the panel beside it. It is
outlined 1px in Alert with Alert text at 12.5/500, radius 8, 140 × 36 at every width and both schemes,
measuring 3.61:1 light and 4.79:1 dark against the auditor's 2.88 / 2.55 for the fill it replaced. As a
composition it reads as the dangerous one without shouting: the only coloured object in the dialog, the
same weight and height as Cancel, colour rather than a fill doing the work, and the same treatment as the
`Hold to lock` button on the card that opens it — visible together in `emergency-confirm-1024-light`.

**R19-01 is in the dialog around the fix, not in the fix.** The four consequence lines lost mock v11's
full-width `card pad0 list` container. The destructive button row now sits 9px below the last consequence
— less than the 11px between two consecutive consequence lines, and against the 14px the app's own decision
cards put above their verb rows — at every width and in both schemes. And at 1366 and 1920 this is the only
dialog in the set whose content does not reach its own panel's right edge: 51% filled at 1920, 57% at 1366,
where Arrange, Task detail and Decision history all fill theirs. One fix — restoring the mock's container
and its break — closes both halves; the minimum fix is a larger margin above the button row. I am confident
about the gap and less certain the emptiness must block on its own, and I have said so.

**R19-02, because I was asked.** `saturated-fill.test.ts`'s two allow-list entries are inert: `Header.tsx`
writes the fill as a ternary and `Spend.tsx` writes a `stroke`, and the guard's pattern matches neither,
so the suite passes identically with the allow-list emptied. The judgement in those entries is right; the
facts are not. Worse, the ternary form is the one already modelled in the tree, and the walk never enters
`theme/`, where every button and surface primitive is defined.

**R17-01 has not regressed, and the new frames are a second, independent witness** — the toast's message
region is byte-identical between `undo-toast-<w>-<s>` and `emergency-confirm-<w>-<s>` in all eight pairs
(max delta `0`), over a Dialog rather than the Settings sheet, and at 393 directly on the dialog's own
panel. **The same frames close round 18's evidence gap:** the ring reads `10` in one shot and `7` three
seconds later in the same run, so the countdown demonstrably depletes.

**R15-01 has not regressed.** All eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames read `29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep` against a
Today of `Saturday 5 September`, and the capture ran 06:35:49–06:39:22 local on 6 September — past local
midnight, the only window in which that defect was ever visible. The gantt difference bands begin at the
first bar row; the axis label band is empty in all eight.

**The 126 shared frames are clean:** zero dimension changes, ten pixel-identical (all eight `locked-*` plus
two Settings frames), and all 18,717 remaining differing pixels banded into four families with zero
unclassified residue — orb noise, the now-line correctly leaving the 06:00–20:00 grid, that same line read
through the Arrange blur, and 1px timeline drift over 79 minutes.

I have refused three times before and been right each time. This is the fourth, and it is not a refusal of
the fix: the fix is correct, was executed against the right three documents, and is better than what I was
asked to check. It is a refusal of the dialog the same commit put in front of me and told me to judge as
new work. A screen nobody had photographed for eighteen rounds was always going to have more than one thing
wrong with it, and the second thing does not stop being real because the first one is now fixed.

## Verdict

**`UX REVIEW: SIGNED`** — commit `1518176`, 6 September 2026, 07:55 AEST.

134 frames, **134 CLEAN, zero open frame defects.**

Both round-19 findings are closed, and I closed them by measuring, not by looking:

- **R19-01 — CLOSED, both halves.** The four consequences now render inside a `ListCard` of four `Row`s.
  The container spans **100.0% of the dialog's content width at every one of the four widths** — it was 51%

## 1 · R19-01, verified as SHIPPED on the pixels — not accepted

I was told the container is back and asked to verify both halves **by measuring again, not by looking**. I
did, on all eight frames.

### 1.1 The structure, read off every frame

Probing a column through the card at each width, the four consequences now sit in a bordered container with
three hairline row rules. The numbers are identical in light and dark at every width — which is checklist
point 6 discharged arithmetically rather than by eye:

| width | card top border | row rules | card bottom border | button top | **clear gap** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 393 | y 164 | 200 · 234 · 268 | y 319 | y 330 | **10px** |
| 1024 | y 336 | 372 · 406 · 440 | y 476 | y 487 | **10px** |
| 1366 | y 402 | 438 · 472 · 506 | y 542 | y 553 | **10px** |
| 1920 | y 492 | 528 · 562 · 596 | y 632 | y 643 | **10px** |

10px is `space[5]` in `theme/tokens.ts:212`, and it is the mock's own number:
`jstack-mock-v11.html:630` writes `<div class="verbs" style="margin-top:10px">` immediately after the
`card pad0 list`. The build now matches the reference at the exact junction R19-01 was about.

Row pitch inside the card is **34px** at every width (e.g. 1920: 528 → 562 → 596), against ~21px for the
old bare-`Text` stack. The first and last rows are 36px, which is `Row`'s `paddingVertical: 9` plus
`ListCard`'s `paddingVertical: 2` — the app's own list rhythm, not a special case.

### 1.2 Half 1 — the destructive button is no longer the most crowded control in the build

Round 19 measured 9px from the last consequence's ink to the button's border, against 11px between two
consecutive consequence lines and 14px above the decision cards' verb rows. Re-measured on `1518176`, at
1920 light:

- Consequence ink bands: **y 507–516 · 541–552 · 575–585 · 609–620**.
- Between two consecutive lines: **24px** of clear ground (516 → 541).
- Last line's ink to the button's box: **23px** (620 → 643), or **26px** to the body of the type (617 →
  643) — and a **hairline card border at y 632 sits inside that gap**, which the old version had nothing of.
- The decision-card comparator, re-read this round on `decision-bill-1920-light`: meta ink ends **y 352**,
  the verb row's box begins **y 366–368** → **14–16px**.

So the junction went from **9px, the tightest body-to-verb gap in the build**, to **23px plus a container
edge plus a surface change** — above the app's own 14px, and level with the 24px between two consequence
lines rather than below it. **Half 1 is closed.**

### 1.3 Half 2 — the dialog's content now reaches its own panel, at every width

I read the panel and container edges off a row inside the card in each frame:

| width | panel border L/R | card border L/R | padding L/R | content width | **card fills** | round 19 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 393 | (full viewport) | x 16 / 376 | 16 / 16 | 361 | **361 → 100.0%** | — |
| 1024 | x 174 / 848 | x 190 / 832 | 16 / 16 | 643 | **643 → 100.0%** | 77% |
| 1366 | x 232 / 1132 | x 248 / 1116 | 16 / 16 | 869 | **869 → 100.0%** | **57%** |
| 1920 | x 460 / 1459 | x 477 / 1442 | 16 / 16 | 966 | **966 → 100.0%** | **51%** |

The 488px of empty frosted surface beside the text at 1920 is gone. The padding is symmetric to the pixel
at all four widths. **Half 2 is closed**, and it is closed by the container filling the panel rather than by
the panel being made to hug — which is the fix I described and the one the mock implies.

### 1.4 The question I was asked: is a `ListCard` the wrong container here?

**No, and I can settle it without judgement.** I measured the Subtasks `ListCard` inside
`task-detail-1920-light` — a different dialog, in the same `Dialog` chrome, signed on rounds 14, 16, 18 and
19 — and compared it to the Emergency dialog's new card in the same frame set:

| | panel border | card border | card fill | card right border | panel right |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `task-detail-1920-light` (Subtasks) | x 460 | x 477 | `251·251·251` | x 1442 | x 1459 |
| `emergency-confirm-1920-light` | x 460 | x 477 | `251·251·251` | x 1442 | x 1459 |

**The same coordinates, the same surface value, the same border value.** This is not a new nested layer; it
is the container the app already puts inside this exact dialog chrome, at the exact same inset. Because it
spans the content width edge to edge it reads as the dialog's own content region, not as a card floating
inside a card — which is the failure mode I was asked to watch for and which would have shown up as a card
narrower than the panel. It does not.

Two more surface checks on the new card, since it is new geometry:

- **Radius.** The card's top-left arc runs from x 486 at y 492 to x 477 by y 501 — a **10px** corner,

- **Borders.** The card border is **one pixel** (x 477 = `254`, x 478 = `251`), the row rules are one pixel

## 2 · R19-02, verified by running the guard — not by reading it

Last round I checked the allow-list instead of taking it and found that neither entry matched. I applied the
same test to the new one: I re-implemented the walk in a standalone script and ran the widened pattern over
`app/`, `components/` and `theme/` myself.

**Every match in the tree, and there are exactly four:**

| file:line | what it paints | dot / bar / surface? | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `components/chrome/Header.tsx:96` | `width: 6, height: 6, borderRadius: 3, backgroundColor: summary.health === "degraded" ? c.alert : c.ok` | a 6px round dot, no children | **correct exemption** |
| `components/chrome/Rail.tsx:77` | byte-identical line on the desktop rail | the same dot | **correct exemption** |
| `components/life/Money.tsx:45` | `width: …%, height: "100%", backgroundColor: m.over ? c.alert : c.accent, opacity: m.over ? 0.8 : 1` | a fill inside a 6px track; the amount is printed *beside* it, never on it | **correct exemption** |
| `theme/ui.tsx:704` | the `Track` primitive's fill, same over/accent logic, `opacity: 0.8` | `Track` renders **no children at all** (`ui.tsx:693–706`) — nothing can be written on it | **correct exemption** |

Four entries, four matches, four cases where a saturated signal colour is genuinely not a surface with text
on it. **The list is honest and the second test now bites** — `expect({ rel, matches: hits.length > 0 })`
fails an entry that exempts nothing, which is the assertion that was missing.

**The pattern, falsified rather than read.** I ran `/backgroundColor:.*?c\.(alert|ok)(?![A-Za-z0-9_])/g`
against eight hand-written forms:

| form | matches | |
|---|---|---|
| `backgroundColor: c.alert, borderColor: c.alert` (the original B9-01 defect) | 1 | still caught |
| `? c.alert : c.ok` (Header's ternary) | 1 | **newly caught** |
| `backgroundColor: bad ? c.alert : c.card` | 1 | **newly caught** |
| `style={[base, { backgroundColor: c.ok }]}` | 1 | **newly caught** |
| `backgroundColor: c.okDim` | 0 | correctly declined |
| `backgroundColor: c.alertSoft` | 0 | correctly declined |
| `backgroundColor: color` (variable indirection) | 0 | not caught — §7 |
| value on the following line | 0 | not caught — §7 |

The negative lookahead survived the widening, which was the risk in going from `\s*c\.` to `.*?c\.`. It
guards no token that exists today (`theme/tokens.ts` defines only `ok` and `alert`), but it is correct and
cheap.

**The walk.** `theme/` is now entered, so `theme/ThemeProvider.tsx`, `theme/tokens.ts`, `theme/useLayout.ts`
and `theme/useReducedMotion.ts` are covered where none of them was before. I also ran the pattern over
`lib/` and `stores/`, which the walk still does not enter: **zero matches**, so nothing is hidden there
today.

**The suite passes and I watched it pass:** `npx jest tests/unit/saturated-fill.test.ts` → 2 passed,
including "every allow-list entry names a real file, carries a reason, and actually matches".

**R19-02 closed** as I raised it. The residual is in §7, where it belongs.

## 3 · R17-01 has not regressed — and this round's witness is stricter than round 19's

The eight `emergency-confirm-*` frames were captured in the same page context as `toast-over-sheet-*`, so
the undo toast is live in all eight, over a `Dialog` rather than the Settings sheet. I located the pill by
the geometry round 18 established (280 × 56 at bottom inset 24 on desktop; 248 × 56 at 90 on the phone;
centred) and differenced its interior against `undo-toast-*` at the same width and scheme.

Round 19 differenced the raw box and reported max delta 0 in a message region. That was slightly generous:
the box's **rounded corners** sample whatever is behind the pill, and that legitimately differs between the
two frames. Insetting 6px on all sides to exclude them gives a much sharper result:

| pair | interior max delta | differing x-range | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| 393 light / dark | 188 / 180 | x 284–294 | the countdown numeral |
| 1024 light / dark | 201 / 209 | x 615–625 | the countdown numeral |
| 1366 light / dark | 201 / 209 | x 786–796 | the countdown numeral |
| 1920 light / dark | 201 / 209 | x 1063–1073 | the countdown numeral |

**An 11px column, in the same place, in all eight.** Everything else inside the pill — the two-line
`Later · returns Mon 8am · / RACQ home insurance · …` message and the `Undo` label at its 500 weight — is
**byte-identical** to the same pill with no dialog in front of it. The fill reads `43·42·38` light and
`236·233·226` dark in both frames of every pair. A scrim or a panel painting over the pill could not leave
its interior numerically identical to an unobstructed one. It does. **The toast is in front.**

At 393 this is the strongest form the witness takes: the dialog fills the entire viewport, so the pill is
sitting directly on the dialog's own bar surface, and it is still bit-identical.

**And the ring depletes again.** `undo-toast-*` reads **`10`**, `emergency-confirm-*` reads **`7`**, from
one capture run three seconds apart — which is round 18's closed evidence gap holding for a second run
rather than being a one-off of round 19's.

## 4 · R15-01 has not regressed — read off the pixels at all eight widths

I cropped the axis band out of each of the eight `tasks-gantt-*` frames and read the label clusters at
3–4×, rather than inferring six from two.

**All eight read `29 Aug | today | 26 Sep`.** `today-1920-light` and `today-393-dark` both print
**`Saturday 5 September`**. 29 Aug + 7 = 5 September; 5 September + 21 = 26 Sep — the fixed −7/+21 window
around one instant, formatted on one basis.

**The condition was live.** The frames' own mtimes put the run at **07:22:11 → 07:24:53 local on 6
September**, i.e. 21:22–21:24 UTC on 5 September; `1518176` was committed at 07:25:43. Local date **6
September**, displayed date **5 September** — the two clocks disagreed at capture time, which is the only
window in which R15-01 was ever visible. Had it survived, the axis would read `30 Aug | today | 27 Sep`.

**And the diff proves it from the other side.** Between round 19's run and this one the clock moved 46
minutes. The `tasks-gantt-*` difference bands are all 8px-tall bar segments at the 42px row pitch, none of
them touching the axis label band. The window did not move by a day; it moved by the width of forty-six
minutes on a 28-day track.

Layout across the 126 unchanged frames is provably identical to the set signed on rounds 14–19 (§5: zero

`decision-history-1920-light`, `tasks-gantt-1920-light`, `tasks-gantt-393-dark`, `decision-bill-1920-light`,
`undo-toast-1024-dark`, `locked-393-dark`, plus every region flagged in §5.

1. **Columns.** `today-1920-light` is still rail (200) + 3 columns at `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`, left-aligned, the
   third column's bottom left empty — which the pack calls correct, not a gap. `emergency-confirm-393-*` is
   a full-viewport panel; at 1024/1366/1920 it is a centred dialog over an unchanged rail-plus-columns page,
   with the rail's active tab correctly on **Agents** in all six desktop frames. No section laid across
   columns.
2. **Type.** The consequence lines are still `typeScale.size.body` (12.5) in Ink; the meta is 10.5 Muted;
   the dialog title is the 20px serif at 400; the button labels are 12.5/500. Moving them into `Row`s
   changed the rhythm, not the scale. Nothing bold, nothing italic, nothing below 10.5 except the countdown
   ring's numeral, which rounds 14–19 judged sanctioned and which reads legibly at both `10` and `7`.
3. **Colour.** Alert appears on the Emergency card border, its `Hold to lock`, the dialog's outlined `Lock

   near an expiry. The new container introduces **no new colour**: `c.card`, `c.cardBorder`, `c.hairline`,

   dialog panel at the same inset as `task-detail`'s. Radii and hairlines elsewhere are byte-identical
   wherever the clock did not move them. No 2px border. Empty column bottoms left empty. Cards not

5. **Text.** Nothing clipped or ellipsised inside a button, chip or segment. The one wrap in the new card is
