## 7 · Recorded, not raised

- **The Decision history dialog is now the one dialog left without the mock's list container.**
  `jstack-mock-v11.html:625` writes the same `<div class="card pad0 list">` for `openDlg('Decision
  history', …)` that line 630 writes for the Emergency lock. `HistoryDialog.tsx:36–55` renders its rows as
  bare `Row`s inside a plain `View`; I measured `decision-history-1920-light` and its rows sit directly on
  the panel (`220·220·221`) with `205` hairlines and **no card border at all**, while its own search
  `Field` above them *is* bordered — so a bordered field sits over unbordered rows. `DISCREPANCIES.md`
  records no entry for it, so the divergence was never a decision, exactly as R19-01's was not.
  **I am not raising it, and I want to be explicit about why.** Neither measured consequence of R19-01
  exists here: the rows already span the panel (there is no fill problem), and there is no destructive verb
  crowded beneath them (there is no gap problem). All that is left is markup that differs from the mock,
  which is not on my seven-point checklist — and I have signed these frames CLEAN in rounds 14, 16 and 18
  and left them CLEAN in 17 and 19. Raising it now, in a round convened to verify a fix I demanded, would be
  moving a goalpost rather than reading a pixel. If anyone wants consistency-to-mock enforced across all
  dialogs, `HistoryDialog.tsx` is the one file left and it belongs in V2.1 or a DISCREPANCIES entry, not in
  this commit.
- **The new allow-list exempts `theme/ui.tsx` whole-file, and that file is 995 lines and 25 exported
  primitives.** The walk skips an allow-listed file entirely (`saturated-fill.test.ts:79`,
  `if (ALLOWED.has(rel)) continue;`), so the exemption granted is per-file, not per-line. I falsified it: I
  injected `backgroundColor: c.alert` next to `export function Btn(` in a copy of `theme/ui.tsx` and re-ran
  the walk — **offenders `[]`, the guard passes**. The file exempted for one 6px `Track` fill is the file
  that defines `Card`, `ListCard`, `Row`, `Btn`, `BtnPrimary`, `BtnSm`, `IconBtn`, `Chip`, `Seg`, `Tag`,
  `Field`, `Switch` and thirteen more.
  **This is not a regression** — before `1518176` the walk did not enter `theme/` at all, so that file was
  already outside the rule, and the commit strictly *increased* coverage by bringing the other four
  `theme/` files in. But the commit message says the walk now includes `theme/` "where Btn, Card and every
  surface primitive live", and the same commit then exempts precisely that file. The fix is a per-line or
  per-symbol exemption (allow-list `theme/ui.tsx:704`, not `theme/ui.tsx`), which is a small change to a
  guard nobody is currently violating. Named in full because I was asked to judge the list; not a frame
  defect, not blocking.
- **The pattern's two remaining blind spots, measured (§2).** One-hop variable indirection
  (`backgroundColor: color`) and a value on the following line both match zero times. The first form is
  already in the tree: `theme/ui.tsx:711`'s `Dot` computes `const color = kind === "alert" ? c.alert : …`
  and then writes `backgroundColor: color`. `Dot` is a dot and would be exempt anyway, so nothing is
  currently hidden — but it is the next shape of the same defect, and it is modelled in the tree for
  somebody to copy. Recorded for whoever next widens the rule.
- **Alert's own light-mode contrast is still a V2.1 token question, not this commit's.** Round 19 measured
  the outlined label at 3.61:1 light / 4.79:1 dark. Nothing in this commit touched the token or the button
  — its box is still 140 × 36 at all four widths and both schemes — so the numbers stand and so does the
  conclusion: README:213's contrast table names no Alert pair, and darkening the light-mode token would
  touch the card border, the issue dots and the over-budget bar too. A pack change, not a dialog change.
- **`intrusion.` is still a meta-line orphan at 393.** `emergency-confirm-393-{light,dark}` still wrap
  `…or a suspected / intrusion.`. The fix restored the container without shortening that sentence, which is
  what I asked for and no more. My checklist scopes the orphan rule to titles and this is a 10.5 Muted meta
  line, so it remains recorded rather than raised — one word out of that sentence would still close it.
- **`jstack-app/evidence/contrast-report.json` is still stale.** Its pairs are v1.2's green palette
  (`rgb(37,43,31)` grounds, `rgb(159,205,172)` fills), retired by ADR-05/ADR-06. It cannot speak to any V2
  colour. Not a frame defect and the auditor owns the evidence files.
- **The now-line's absence and the UTC clock basis.** At 07:22 Brisbane the Today calendar shows no
  now-line, because on the app's UTC basis it is 21:22 and the grid ends at 20:00. The render is correct and
  guarded. What is still open is whether UTC is the right basis for a man in Brisbane — `HANDOVER_v2.md`
  names it as a contract addition to request. One basis still beats two, and two was R15-01. Second run in a
  row where the consequence is a missing element rather than a misplaced one; recorded, unchanged.
- **Standing evidence gaps, unchanged and not restated:** the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse, and the
  Firefox half of the scrollbar rule which cannot appear in a Chromium pass. Neither is a defect. Round
  18's third gap — the undo ring's depletion — stays closed, and §3 shows it holding across a second run.
- **The V2.1 list stands as deferred** — the copy glyph's 8–9px inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024, a
  web hover pass. Not blockers, not re-litigated. Nor is the `date-basis.test.ts` allow-list, which the
  qa-auditor ruled on: not required. I accept that ruling.

# UX review — JSTACK V2 device pass · round 21

**Date:** 6 September 2026, **08:08–08:22 AEST (UTC+10)** — i.e. 2026-09-05 22:08–22:22 UTC.
The wall time is here for the reason B7-07 gave and rounds 15–20 kept: a signature must not depend on git
metadata to prove it postdates the code it signs. `0bb2948` was committed **2026-09-06 08:07:02 +1000**;
this round opened about a minute later and is written on the same clock.
**Reviewer:** ux-reviewer (product eyes)
**Round:** 21 — a **short** round by design, convened because QA-04 requires a signature dated after the last
code commit and `jstack-app/tests/unit/saturated-fill.test.ts` is a code commit. It is not convened because
anything is in doubt. That is a reason to keep it proportionate, not a reason to wave it through, so the one
claim the commit actually makes about the pixels is the one I tested hardest.
**Scope — the frames reviewed below are the 134 PNGs in `demo/v2/` as committed in `0bb2948`**
("fix(v2): an exemption now names the line, not the file (R20-01)"). `git rev-parse HEAD` is
`0bb2948e58168773867fbaf8fe5192eddc602d5e` and `git status --short` was empty when this round opened, so
every measurement below is a read of the bytes that commit holds.
The set I compared all 134 frames against is `git show 1518176:demo/v2/…` — the round-20 frames, extracted
from the object database rather than remembered, into a scratch directory outside the repository.
**Input:** `demo/v2/*.png` — **134** frames, 17 screens × {393, 1024, 1366, 1920} × {light, dark}
(`arrange-393-*` absent by design — `jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs:105` skips Arrange under 768).
**Judged against:** `jstack-app/design/README.md` v1.3, `jstack-app/design/handoff.md`,
`jstack-app/design/DISCREPANCIES.md`, `jstack-mock-v11.html`, and the 134 frames of round 20.

**No tracked file was edited** except this one. The guard was falsified against an **in-memory** mutation of
`theme/ui.tsx`, never a written one; the working tree was clean before this round and is clean apart from
this file now.

## Verdict

**`UX REVIEW: SIGNED`** — commit `0bb2948`, 6 September 2026, 08:22 AEST.

134 frames, **134 CLEAN, zero open frame defects.**

- **The commit message's claim — "touches no app source" — is true, and the frames prove it independently.**
  `git diff --name-only 1518176 0bb2948` over `app/`, `components/`, `theme/`, `lib/`, `stores/` and
  `tools/` returns **nothing**. The regenerated frames agree: **zero dimension changes**, the filename set
  identical, **12 frames byte-identical**, and every one of the **9,760** pixels that differ by more than 8
  levels falls into **three capture-time families with zero unclassified residue**. Nothing moved that a
  source change would have moved.
- **R20-01 is closed, and closed the way I would have fixed it.** I ran the falsification the commit message
  cites, on an in-memory copy: a fill planted beside `export function Btn` now fails, naming
  **`theme/ui.tsx:240`** — the exact line the message claims. Three further mutations I invented also go red.
- **The `lib/` + `stores/` extension is real coverage, not decoration.** 28 source files that were outside
  the rule are inside it now, and a planted fill in either directory fails with a `file:line`. I verified
  that by planting one in each.
- **R15-01 has not regressed.** All eight `tasks-gantt-*` read `29 Aug | today | 26 Sep`; `today-*` reads
  `Saturday 5 September`. The run was again past local midnight, so the condition was live.
- **R17-01 has not regressed, and this round's witness is the strictest yet.** `toast-over-sheet-*` is now
  **bit-identical** to its unobstructed `undo-toast-*` twin inside the pill in **seven of eight** pairs.

One thing is recorded, not raised, in §4: the two mutations that abuse an *exemption fragment* fail through
the arity assertion rather than the offender list, so the suite goes red with a message that names the
allow-list rather than the offence. The defect cannot ship either way.

## 1 · The honest test: 134 frames against the round-20 set

If no app source changed, the frames must come back the same. I compared all 134 pairs pixel by pixel.

| | |
|---|---|
| filename set vs `1518176` | **identical** — 134 files, no addition, removal or rename |
| dimension changes | **0 of 134** |
| frames byte-identical | **12** |
| frames differing only below a delta of 8 | **40** (max channel delta **7** of 255) |
| frames with any pixel over delta 8 | 82 |
| pixels over delta 8, whole set | **9,760** of ~253M |
| **unclassified after banding** | **0** |

Fourteen of the seventeen screens are full-page captures, so a reflow of any kind would have changed a
document height. None did. `settings-1024-*` is still 1024 × 1952, `today-393-*` still 2308 tall,
`decision-bill-393-*` still 2332, `emergency-confirm-393-*` still 852.

**The 12 byte-identical frames** are all eight `locked-*` — a fourth consecutive commit rendering the gate
bit-for-bit unchanged — plus `arrange-1024-light`, `arrange-1366-{light,dark}` and `settings-393-light`.

**The 40 sub-threshold frames** differ by at most **7 levels out of 255**, concentrated in `arrange-*` and
`decision-history-*` — the frosted/blurred surfaces. That is blur re-rasterisation between runs, below any
visible threshold, and it moves no edge.

### The three families, grouped and read

I grouped every pixel with a channel delta > 8 into connected regions at a 21px grouping gap — 145 bands —
and classified each. **Zero fell outside the three families**, and I re-ran the classifier with the family
order reversed to make sure the ordering was not doing the work (my first pass had `tasks-*` bands landing
in the wrong bucket; corrected, then re-derived).

1. **The mic orb — 76 bands, 7,288px.** Every frame's union bbox is at most **47 × 47** and sits within
   **46px of the right edge**. Position, size and clearance unchanged everywhere. The orb's idle render is
   not bit-stable between runs; this is the standing evidence gap, not a defect.
2. **Date-derived timeline drift — 66 bands, 2,307px.** **Every single band is exactly 8px tall**, and
   within each frame every band's `y0` is congruent mod 42 — the row pitch. Widest band 120px, on a ~1,250px
   28-day track at 1920. The capture ran **08:02:54 → 08:06:36 local**, 41 minutes after round 20's
   07:22–07:25 run; 28 days across ~670–1,250px is roughly 1px per hour, so 41 minutes rounds to 1px on some
   bars and 0 on others. That is what the counts show.
3. **The undo ring's countdown numeral — 3 bands, 165px.** Narrow high-delta glyph columns inside the toast
   pill (§3).

**No card moved, no column changed width, no radius or hairline changed, no type reflowed, no ground token
shifted.** The `emergency-confirm-*` frames, which carried 75k–340k differing pixels last round because
R19-01 rebuilt their container, are down to **45–46px each** this round — the numeral and nothing else. The
R19-01 fix is stable across a second capture.

## 2 · The guard, judged — I am the reason it exists, so I ran it rather than read it

Four entries, each quoting one line, each required to match exactly one line. **The granularity is right,**
and I will say why rather than assert it.

**The four entries correspond exactly to the four matches in the tree.** I enumerated every line in the
walked directories matching the pattern:

| file:line | what it paints |
|---|---|
| `components/chrome/Header.tsx:96` | the 6px health dot, phone header |
| `components/chrome/Rail.tsx:77` | the same dot, desktop rail |
| `components/life/Money.tsx:45` | a budget bar's fill past its cap |
| `theme/ui.tsx:704` | the shared `Track` primitive's fill |

Four matches, four entries, no entry excusing nothing and no match unexcused. `npx jest
tests/unit/saturated-fill.test.ts` → **2 passed**, and I watched it pass.

**The falsification, run on an in-memory mutation.** I re-implemented the walk exactly — same pattern, same
five directories, same `includes`-on-a-quoted-fragment exemption, same arity assertion — and first validated
the re-implementation against the unmodified tree (offenders `[]`, all four entries `hits=1`, matching the
real suite). Then, four mutations:

| mutation | test 1 (offender list) | test 2 (arity) | suite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backgroundColor: c.alert` planted beside `export function Btn` | **FAILS → `theme/ui.tsx:240`** | passes | **RED** |
| a near-miss sharing the ternary *shape* but not the fragment (`over ? c.ok : c.accent`) | **FAILS → `theme/ui.tsx:240`** | passes | **RED** |
| a fill planted in `lib/authTokens.ts` | **FAILS → `lib/authTokens.ts:56`** | passes | **RED** |
| a fill planted in `stores/agents.ts` | **FAILS → `stores/agents.ts:113`** | passes | **RED** |

**`theme/ui.tsx:240` is exactly what the commit message claims.** Under the old whole-file exemption the
first of these left the offender list empty; it does not now. R20-01 is closed as I recorded it.

**Is the granularity right?** Yes, and the interesting case is the one that tests the *fragment* rather than
the file. Two of the four entries quote `width: 6, height: 6`, which is not distinctive prose — so I asked
what happens if somebody reuses it. Two more mutations:

| mutation | test 1 | test 2 | suite |
|---|---|---|---|
| the exempted `over ? c.alert : c.accent` **copied verbatim** onto a padded surface in `theme/ui.tsx` | passes (both lines excused) | **FAILS → `hits: [240, 705]`** | **RED** |
| `width: 6, height: 6` reused on a padded surface in `Header.tsx` | passes (both excused) | **FAILS → `hits: [21, 97]`** | **RED** |

Both go red. **The "matches exactly one line" assertion is what makes a non-distinctive fragment safe**, and
it is the load-bearing half of the design: it is why the fragment does not have to be clever, and it is what
turns "every other matching line in the same file is still a defect" from a sentence into a rule. That is
the shape R19-02 and R20-01 were both about — a claim wider than its enforcement — and here the enforcement
is the wider of the two.

**`lib/` and `stores/` are real coverage.** 21 and 7 source files respectively, 28 files that were outside
the rule and are inside it now, and the walk goes from 95 to **123** files. They hold zero matches today,
which is the stated point rather than a hole — the mutations above show a fill planted in either fails by
`file:line`. A rule scoped to where the defect was already found finds it once; this one is scoped ahead of
the defect. I judge the extension real, not decorative.

## 3 · R15-01 and R17-01 have not regressed

**R15-01 — the Gantt axis against Today's date.** I cropped the axis band out of each of the eight
`tasks-gantt-*` frames and read the labels at 2–3×, rather than inferring six from two. **All eight read
`29 Aug | today | 26 Sep`.** `today-1920-light`, `today-1024-light`, `today-1366-dark` and `today-393-dark`
all print **`Saturday 5 September`**. 29 Aug + 7 = 5 September; 5 September + 21 = 26 Sep — the fixed −7/+21
window around one instant, formatted on one basis.

**The condition was live**, which matters more than the reading. The frames' mtimes put the run at
**08:02:54 → 08:06:36 local on 6 September**, i.e. 22:02–22:06 UTC on 5 September. Local date **6
September**, displayed date **5 September** — the two clocks disagreed at capture time, which is the only
window in which R15-01 was ever visible. Had it regressed the axis would read `30 Aug | today | 27 Sep`. It
does not. Third consecutive run captured inside the live window.

**R17-01 — the toast above overlays.** I located the pill by the geometry round 18 established (280 × 56 at
bottom inset 24 desktop; 248 × 56 at 90 on the phone; centred), inset 6px on all sides to exclude the
rounded corners, and differenced the interior against the unobstructed `undo-toast-*` at the same width and
scheme:

| overlay | interior max delta | differing region |
|---|---|---|
| `emergency-confirm-*`, all 8 | 188–209 | an **11px column** — the countdown numeral — in all eight |
| `toast-over-sheet-*`, 7 of 8 | **0** | **nothing at all** |
| `toast-over-sheet-1920-light` | 201 | the same 11px countdown column |

**Seven of the eight `toast-over-sheet` pairs are bit-identical inside the pill** — max delta 0, not merely
small. That is stricter than round 20's witness, which had the emergency dialog in front and always carried
the numeral. A scrim or a panel painting over the pill cannot leave its interior numerically identical to an
unobstructed one. The pill fill reads `43·42·38` light and `236·233·226` dark, the same value in both frames
of every pair. **The toast is in front**, over the Settings sheet and over a `Dialog`, at four widths and
both schemes.

**And the ring depletes again — three distinct values from one run.** `undo-toast` reads **`10`**,
`toast-over-sheet` **`9`**, `emergency-confirm` **`6`**. Round 18's closed evidence gap now holds across a
third run, and this is the first run to catch three points on the same countdown.

## 4 · The seven-point checklist

§1 establishes that layout across all 134 frames is provably identical to the set signed on rounds 14–20 —
zero dimension changes, zero structural bands, zero unclassified pixels. So the checklist carries over on
evidence rather than on memory. I still re-derived it by eye on `today-1920-light`, `today-1024-dark`,
`tasks-gantt-393-light`, `life-1920-dark`, `settings-1366-dark` and `emergency-confirm-1920-light`, plus
every region flagged in §1.

1. **Columns.** `today-1920-light`: rail (200) + 3 columns at `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`, left-aligned, third
   column's bottom left empty — which the pack calls correct, not a gap. `today-1024-dark`: rail + 2
   columns, with Your tasks / At a glance / Close the day stacked **directly under column 1** and the
   calendar column spanning both rows — **no empty row**. `tasks-gantt-393-light`: 1 column, floating tab
   bar, mic orb above it on the right. No section laid across columns.
2. **Type.** Serif card titles upright at 500; `Saturday` at 32/1 desktop and 26/1 phone at 400; section
   labels 11.5 uppercase tracked in Accent ink (`NEEDS YOU`, `AT A GLANCE`, `WAITING ON`). Nothing bold,
   nothing italic, nothing below 10.5 except the countdown numeral, which rounds 14–20 judged sanctioned and
   which reads legibly at `10`, `9` and `6`.
3. **Colour.** Accent only where a tap does something. Marker on the `NEEDS YOU 5` and `WAITING ON 2` count
   badges and the mic — nowhere else. Alert on the Agent-issue dots, the Money `Family` over-budget bar, the
   Emergency card's `Hold to lock` and the dialog's outlined `Lock everything now` — README:68's list
   exactly, and nowhere near an expiry (`expires Wed 5pm`, `expires 17 Sep`, `expires in 2 days` are all
   Accent ink). Habits, calendars and budgets all Accent; calendar categories tonal, not hued. No v1.2
   green, no pure black or white surface, no gradient.
4. **Surfaces.** Frosted cards on the stone ground with the deliberately small card-to-ground step. Radius
   10 cards/bars, 8 buttons/chips, hairlines only — byte-identical wherever the clock did not move them. The
   Emergency dialog's `ListCard` still spans the panel edge to edge with its four rows and three hairline
   rules, and the destructive button still sits clear beneath it. Empty column bottoms left empty
   (`life-1920-dark`'s three columns end where their content does). Cards not stretched to equal heights.
5. **Text.** No word broken mid-word. Nothing clipped or ellipsised inside a button, chip or segment — the
   `RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 · due 19 Sep` truncations at 1024 are card body, not control labels, and
   are unchanged. No two-line button label anywhere.
6. **Dark.** Every dark frame differs from its round-20 self by the same families as its light twin and by
   nothing else — same layout, no reflow, nothing appearing or disappearing. Warm `#191815`-family ground
   painted edge to edge, including under the tab bar, verified on `today-1024-dark`, `life-1920-dark` and
   `settings-1366-dark`.
7. **Density.** 1920 reads as a dashboard, 1024 as a tablet, 393 as a phone.

Also checked, since a missing or wrong frame is itself a defect: **134 files, 17 screens**, `arrange-393-*`
absent by design and nothing else missing; no blanks (the four lowest-variance frames are all `locked-*`,
which is a near-empty gate by design and byte-identical to round 20's); no wrong screens; no frame showing
the gate that should not.

## 5 · Recorded, not raised

- **The two fragment-abuse mutations fail through the wrong assertion.** In §2's last table, copying an
  exempted fragment onto a real surface leaves **test 1's offender list empty** — both lines are excused by
  `text.includes(a.line)` — and the suite is saved by **test 2's arity check**, which reports
  `hits: [240, 705]`. The defect cannot ship; the guard is sound. But the failure message names the
  allow-list entry rather than "a saturated fill on a padded surface", so whoever hits it reads a complaint
  about the exemption and not about what they wrote. That is diagnostic quality, not a hole, and I am not
  raising it: the rule I asked for is enforced, and the shape of this log is that a rule and a claim about a
  rule are different things. This is the rule being *wider* than the claim for once.
- **The pattern's two blind spots are unchanged and unmeasured this round** — one-hop variable indirection
  (`backgroundColor: color`, modelled in the tree at `theme/ui.tsx:711`'s `Dot`) and a value on the
  following line. §2 of round 20 measured both at zero matches; nothing in this commit widened or narrowed
  them. Recorded for whoever next widens the rule.
- **`HistoryDialog.tsx` is still the one dialog without the mock's `card pad0 list`.** I named this in round
  20 and chose not to raise it, for reasons I set out in full there: neither measured consequence of R19-01
  exists in it, and I had signed those frames CLEAN across five rounds. **That reasoning stands and this
  session has not overruled it** — the commit message says so explicitly and it is right to. V2.1, or a
  `DISCREPANCIES.md` entry. Not this commit, and not this round, which touched no component at all.
- **Standing, and deliberately not re-litigated:** the mic orb's 1.4s listening pulse and the Firefox half
  of the scrollbar rule (neither can appear in a Chromium pass); the V2.1 list — the copy glyph's 8–9px
  inset, the `— Now` legend orphan at 1024, a web hover pass; Alert's own light-mode contrast (3.61:1 light
  / 4.79:1 dark) as a **pack-token** question, since README:213's contrast table names no Alert pair and
  darkening the token would touch the card border, the issue dots and the over-budget bar too; `intrusion.`
  as a meta-line orphan at 393, which my checklist scopes to titles; and
  `jstack-app/evidence/contrast-report.json` still holding v1.2's retired green palette, which is the
  auditor's file and not a frame defect.
- **The now-line's absence, third run running.** At 08:02 Brisbane the Today calendar shows no now-line,
  because on the app's UTC basis it is 22:02 and the grid ends at 20:00. `CalendarGrid.tsx:121` renders the
  line only when it is inside the grid, so the render is correct and guarded, and the `— Now` legend entry
  is still present. Whether UTC is the right basis for a man in Brisbane remains a contract question
  `HANDOVER_v2.md` already names. One basis still beats two, and two was R15-01. Unchanged.

## Verdict

**`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`** — commit `f3aaa07`, 6 September 2026, **10:02 AEST (UTC+10)**.

The two halves of this round come apart, so I will state both:

- **134 frames, 134 CLEAN, zero open frame defects.** Nothing in any picture is wrong.
- **One open finding, R22-01, source-level, raised because I was asked to judge it** — the new
  completeness check in `capture-v2.mjs` does not catch the failure its own comment says it catches, for
  **16 of the 17 frame families**, and the guard paired with it closes only 4 of those 16. Twelve
  families, `today` among them, can stop being captured with both guards green. This is the machinery
  that guarantees the input set I sign is complete, so it is not somebody else's row.

I was told the frames "should come back unchanged" and that the honest test of that claim is the frames.
**The claim is false as stated and true as meant, and the difference is worth the paragraph:** 124 of the
134 PNGs differ from `0bb2948` byte-for-byte. I have accounted for **every differing pixel** in §1. All of
it is the live mic orb, a live countdown numeral, and a live timeline redrawn against a clock ninety
minutes further on. No layout, type, colour, surface or wrapping value moved anywhere in the pass.

## 1 · What changed in the frames, accounted for pixel by pixel

I differenced each of the 134 frames against its round-21 twin at full resolution, then grouped the
differing pixels into spatial clusters (60px buckets, union-found over 8-neighbours) so that a frame with
two unrelated changes reports two, not one bounding box spanning both.

**Ten frames are bit-identical** — not one channel of one pixel moved. **Forty-five carry no cluster above
a channel delta of 3**, i.e. the thirty-five beyond the ten differ only by amounts no eye resolves, at the
edges of the same three elements below. Every remaining differing pixel in the pass belongs to one of
these, and to nothing else:

| what | frames carrying it | max channel delta | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| mic-orb listening pulse | 84 | 5–77 | the orb, bottom-right, at every width |
| timeline bars redrawn ±1px | 36 | 129–151 | the Tasks timeline card, and the Gantt track |
| countdown numeral | 2 | 201, 211 | an ≤11px column inside the undo pill |

(51 orb only, 33 orb + timeline, 3 timeline only, 2 countdown, 45 clean = 134.) Concretely: all six
`arrange-*`, all eight `locked-*`, all eight `settings-*`, seven of eight `decision-history-*` and seven of
eight `toast-over-sheet-*` carry no cluster above delta 3 at all.

**The orb is the standing item and I am not re-raising it.** It is the listening pulse, sampled at a
different phase.

**The ±1px timeline is a clock, not a layout change, and I proved it rather than assumed it.** The
cluster is the same 53×133 (desktop) / 62×133 (phone) box in every `tasks-list`, `tasks-board`,
`tasks-done` and `task-detail` frame, and the Gantt track in every `tasks-gantt` frame. Cropped at 2× it
is four capsule bars on four rails, each sitting **one pixel to the left** of where it sat in round 21,
with the rails, the labels, the dashed in-progress bar's stroke and the card's every other pixel
unmoved. The window is fixed at −7/+21 days = 28 days across a 670px track at 1920, so one pixel is
**60 minutes**. Round 21's frames were written 08:02–08:06 local; these were written **09:35–09:38
local**, ninety minutes later. One pixel is exactly what ninety minutes buys. In `task-detail-1366/1920`
the same shift appears at max delta **5–6** instead of 140 — because there the timeline is behind the
dialog scrim. That attenuation is itself the confirmation: it is the same element, seen through glass.

**The two countdown numerals.** `toast-over-sheet-1920-light` reads **`10`** where it read `9`, and
`emergency-confirm-393-dark` reads **`7`** where it read `6`. I checked the fit rather than only the
value: at 8× the two-digit `10` sits inside the ring with clear padding on both sides and no clipping —
checklist item 5 holds at the widest glyph the ring will ever carry.

## 2 · The three things I was told to confirm

### R15-01 — the Gantt axis against Today's date. **Not regressed.**

I cropped the axis band out of **all eight** `tasks-gantt-*` frames into one montage and read them at 2×,
rather than inferring six from two. All eight read **`29 Aug │ today │ 26 Sep`**. I did the same with the
page title of **all eight** `today-*` frames: all eight read **`Saturday 5 September`**. 29 Aug + 7 = 5
September; 5 September + 21 = 26 September — the fixed −7/+21 window around one instant, formatted on one
basis.

**The condition was live again, which matters more than the reading.** The frames' mtimes put the run at
**09:35:24 → 09:38:53 local on 6 September**, i.e. 23:35–23:38 UTC on **5** September. Local date 6
September, displayed date 5 September — the two clocks disagreed at capture time, which is the only
window in which R15-01 was ever visible. Had it regressed the axis would read `30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`.
It does not. **Fourth consecutive run captured inside the live window.**

### R17-01 — the toast above overlays. **Not regressed, and this round witnesses it more strictly than round 21 did.**

I located the pill by the geometry round 18 established (280 × 56 at bottom inset 24 on desktop; 248 × 56
at inset 90 on the phone; centred), inset 6px on all sides to exclude the rounded corners, and differenced
the interior against the unobstructed `undo-toast-*` at the same width and scheme:

| overlay | pairs | interior max delta | differing region |
|---|---|---|---|
| `toast-over-sheet-*` | **8 of 8** | **0** | **nothing at all** |
| `emergency-confirm-*` | 8 of 8 | 180–209 | an **11px column** — the countdown numeral — in all eight |

**All eight `toast-over-sheet` pill interiors are now bit-identical to their unobstructed twin** — max
delta 0, not merely small. Round 21 had seven of eight; the eighth is the frame whose numeral has since
ticked into agreement. A scrim or a panel painting over the pill cannot leave its interior numerically
identical to an unobstructed one. The pill fill reads `43·42·38` light and `236·233·226` dark, the same
value in both frames of every pair, at all four widths. **The toast is in front**, over the Settings sheet
and over a `Dialog`.

The ring still depletes — `undo-toast` and `toast-over-sheet` at `10`, `emergency-confirm` at `6` or `7`
depending on the frame — so the countdown is live and not a painted still. Two distinct values this run
where round 21 caught three; that is the timing of one capture pass, not a change in behaviour.

### B9-01 — the outlined button in `emergency-confirm-*`. **Unchanged, measured not looked at.**

I scanned a horizontal line through the middle of "Lock everything now" in six of the eight frames and
read the actual values on both sides of the border, in both the round-21 and round-22 bytes:

## 3 · R22-01 · the new completeness check counts a number that is right about itself

**Severity:** MEDIUM. Source-level, not visible in any frame. Raised, not merely recorded, for the reason
in §3.4.

**I was asked directly:** *"Is counting the right check, or is it another number that can be right while
the thing it stands for is wrong?"* It is the second one, and I can show it rather than argue it.

### 3.1 What the code claims

`jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs:246–259`, added by this commit, carries its own claim in a comment:

> *"this asserts the completeness of the RUN, which is what catches a family that silently stops being
> captured, on the day it stops."*

The check under that sentence is:

```js
const written = readdirSync(outDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".png"));
const screens = [...new Set(written.map((f) => f.replace(/-(393|1024|1366|1920)-(light|dark)[.]png$/, "")))];
const expected = screens.length * WIDTHS.length * 2 - 2; // less Arrange on the phone (RL-05)
if (written.length !== expected) { … process.exit(1); }
```

`screens` is derived **from `written`**. So `expected` is derived from `written` too, and the comparison
is `written.length === written-derived-length`. When a whole family disappears, the numerator and the
denominator fall together and the equation stays true. `outDir` is wiped at line 219 before the run, so
there are no stale frames to make up the difference either — the shortfall is simply never visible.

### 3.2 Falsified, not reasoned about

I ran the expression verbatim against the real 134 filenames, removing one family at a time:

| what I removed | wrote | screens | expected | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing (as shipped) | 134 | 17 | 134 | **passes**, exit 0 |
| the whole `emergency-confirm` family | 126 | 16 | 126 | **passes, exit 0** |
| the whole `today` family | 126 | 16 | 126 | **passes, exit 0** |
| the whole `tasks-gantt` family | 126 | 16 | 126 | **passes, exit 0** |
| …and 13 of the other 14 families, each alone | 126 | 16 | 126 | **passes, exit 0** |
| the whole `arrange` family | 128 | 16 | 126 | fails, exit 1 |
| one frame, `emergency-confirm-1920-dark` | 133 | 17 | 134 | fails, exit 1 |

**Sixteen of seventeen whole families vanish silently.** The check catches a *partial* family — losing one
width or one scheme — and nothing else. The one family it does catch, `arrange`, it catches **by
accident**: the hard-coded `- 2` stops being right when the only phone-exempt screen is the one that left,
and the message the operator would see is `wrote 128, expected 126`, which points at a surplus of two
frames rather than at the six that are missing.

`emergency-confirm` is on that list. That is the sharp edge of this: **the same commit** removed
`if (holdBox != null)` from line 197 precisely so the emergency dialog could not go missing in silence —
"a screen nobody photographs is a screen nobody reviews", and it is right — and then, fifty lines later,
added a check that would let that exact family go missing in silence by any other route: the block deleted
in a refactor, the `data-testid` renamed, an `await` that throws inside a per-scheme catch. The throw
guards one cause. The count was supposed to guard the outcome. It does not.

### 3.3 What the paired guard does and does not cover

`handover.test.ts`'s new QA-07 block is the other half of the pair, and it is stronger, because one of its
three tests pins families **by literal name** instead of deriving them. I ran the same falsification
against its logic:

- Test 1, the cross-product, has the identical self-derivation flaw — `screens` comes from `frames` — so a
  vanished family leaves a complete cross-product over the survivors. `expect(screens.length)
  .toBeGreaterThan(10)` is the only floor, and 16 clears it.
- Test 2 pins `decision-bill`, `undo-toast`, `toast-over-sheet`, `emergency-confirm` by name. Those four
  **do** go red. That is real coverage and I want it on the record as such.
- Test 3 is correct and complete: `QA_REPORT_v2.md` no longer writes a frame count anywhere, not only in
  the QA-07 row — I grepped the whole document for `\d+ frames` and for the literals 118/126/134 and it is
  clean. The sentence "a document should not be the place it is remembered" is, unusually, exactly as wide
  as its enforcement.

Union the two guards and the residual is precise:

| family | capture-v2 count | handover QA-07 | covered? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decision-bill`, `undo-toast`, `toast-over-sheet`, `emergency-confirm` | no | **yes, by name** | yes (4) |
| `arrange` | yes, by accident | no | yes (1) |
| `today`, `tasks-list`, `tasks-board`, `tasks-gantt`, `tasks-done`, `brain`, `life`, `agents`, `settings`, `task-detail`, `decision-history`, `locked` | no | no | **no (12)** |

**Twelve of seventeen families can stop being captured with both guards green** — including `today`, the
app's home screen, and all four Tasks views. The four that are covered are covered because a reviewer once
forced them into existence one at a time; the thirteen ordinary screens have never had to be argued for,
and so nothing names them.

### 3.4 Why I am raising this rather than recording it in §7

Round 20 recorded two source-level things without raising them, on the test that neither was a regression
and neither made a claim. This one fails that test twice. It is **new in the commit under review**, and it
**asserts in its own comment a property it does not have** — the same shape as R19-02 ("a claim wider than
its enforcement") and R20-01 ("an exemption now names the line, not the file"), both of which I raised and
both of which were fixed. And its subject is the completeness of **my own input set**. B9-01 existed for
eighteen rounds, and R19-01 with it, because a screen was never photographed. This is the guard that is
meant to stop that happening again. I will not sign over a guarantee I have just watched fail sixteen
times out of seventeen.

### 3.5 The design pack line it breaks

The pack does not legislate build tooling, so I will not stretch a line to cover it — but the pack's own
standard of evidence is the point at issue. `jstack-app/design/README.md`, Voice: *"Numbers over
adjectives: `3 of 5 today`, not `a few items`."* The pack's case for numbers is that a number is checkable
where an adjective is not. A number computed from the thing it is checking is an adjective wearing a
number's clothes. `134 === 134` here carries exactly as much information as "looks complete."

### 3.6 The fix I would make in source

`capture-v2.mjs` already knows its seventeen screens — every one is a string literal passed to `shot()`.
Stop rediscovering them from the output:

```js
const SCREENS = ["locked", "today", "arrange", "settings", "tasks-list", "tasks-board", "tasks-gantt",
  "tasks-done", "brain", "life", "agents", "task-detail", "decision-history", "decision-bill",
  "undo-toast", "toast-over-sheet", "emergency-confirm"];
const PHONE_EXEMPT = new Set(["arrange"]);          // RL-05
…
const want = SCREENS.flatMap((s) => WIDTHS.flatMap(([w]) =>
  PHONE_EXEMPT.has(s) && w === 393 ? [] : ["light", "dark"].map((sc) => `${s}-${w}-${sc}.png`)));
const missing = want.filter((f) => !written.includes(f));
const extra = written.filter((f) => !want.includes(f));
if (missing.length || extra.length) {
  console.error(`device pass incomplete — missing ${missing.join(", ")}; unexpected ${extra.join(", ")}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
```

Two properties the count does not have: a vanished family fails **by name**, so the operator is told which
screen is gone rather than handed a delta; and adding an eighteenth screen has to be a deliberate edit to
`SCREENS`, so the list cannot drift away from the capture silently in either direction. The `- 2` constant
disappears, and with it the accident that made `arrange` the one covered family.

The same one-line change closes it in `handover.test.ts`: assert `screens` **equals** that sorted array of
seventeen, rather than `toBeGreaterThan(10)`. Then test 2's four literal names become belt to test 1's
braces instead of the only thing holding the trousers up. It also lets the block that follows keep its
comment honestly — *"A frame family that quietly stops being captured is how the pass goes back to
certifying only the arrangements that look fine"* — which is true, well put, and currently enforced for
four families out of seventeen.

---

## 4 · What this commit got right, which is most of it

I would not want the finding above to stand in for the whole commit.

- **The `if (holdBox != null)` removal is correct and is the right instinct.** A null box now throws with a
  message naming the width and scheme. That is the `if (await bill.count())` pattern of B-98 recognised in
  a new place and closed, and it is closed properly: loudly, at the point of failure.
- **Test 3 of QA-07 is complete**, as measured in §3.3 — the report writes no frame count anywhere now, and
  neither do QA-04 and QA-05. The count is a fact about a directory; taking it out of a document that had
  it wrong twice is the right move, and the removal was done thoroughly rather than only where the test
  looks.
- **Test 2's four literal names are real coverage**, and they are the four families that history says are
  most likely to be dropped. My objection is that they are the *only* names, not that naming is wrong —
  naming is exactly right, and §3.6 is a proposal to do more of it.
- **The four 0x08 bytes are gone from the delivery documents.** I checked: `grep -c $'\x08'` returns zero
  across every tracked `.md` at the repository root.

## Verdict

**134 frames, 134 CLEAN.** The pictures are right, and they are the same pictures I signed in round 21
apart from a pulsing orb, a ticking ring and a timeline ninety minutes older. R15-01, R17-01 and B9-01 are
all confirmed intact by measurement, and R17-01 is confirmed more strictly this round than last.

**One finding is open: R22-01**, which I was asked to judge and which I judge unfavourably. The check that
was added to stop a frame family disappearing in silence lets sixteen of seventeen families disappear in
silence, and the guard paired with it recovers four of those sixteen. It is a number that is right about
itself. Twelve families, `today` among them, are covered by neither. §3.6 is the fix, and it is smaller
than the check it replaces.

I will not sign a round whose only open item is the integrity of the set I am signing.

## Verdict

**`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`** — commit `8b1c976`, 6 September 2026, **10:41 AEST (UTC+10)**.

Two things, and they point opposite ways:

- **R22-01 is fixed, and fixed properly.** I falsified it three ways rather than reading it. The failure
  it was written for — a frame family silently stops being captured — is now caught **17 times out of 17,
  by name**, where the version I reviewed last round caught **one**, by accident. Both halves of the pair
  go red, and set equality catches the mirror case too. §4 has the working, including an answer to each
  of the two questions I was asked.
- **One frame defect is open: R23-01.** The Life Money footer and the bill decision card now print
  **different due dates for the same bill** — `due 20 Sep` on Life, `due 19 Sep` on Today and on the
  expanded bill card. This is the first pass ever captured after UTC midnight on 5 September, and it is
  the coincidence that had been hiding it: one of the two is computed as `{{TODAY+14}}` and the other is
  the literal string `due 19 Sep`, and 5 + 14 = 19. It carries on all eight `life-*` frames.

I was told this commit "changes no component and no theme token" and that `demo/v2` had been regenerated.
**Both are true, and neither means the frames are the same.** 126 of 134 differ byte for byte, and the
eight that do not are the eight `locked-*` gate frames, which carry no clock-dependent glyph at all. The
day turned between the two capture runs: round 22's pass ended at **23:38:53 UTC on 5 September** and this
one began at **00:02:07 UTC on 6 September**. Every date on every screen moved by one day. §1 accounts for
every differing pixel; §2 is the one place where they did not all move together.

---

## 1 · What changed in the frames, accounted for pixel by pixel

I differenced each of the 134 frames against its round-22 twin at full resolution, then grouped the
differing pixels into spatial clusters (60px buckets, union-found over 8-neighbours) so that a frame with
two unrelated changes reports two, not one bounding box spanning both.

**Eight frames are bit-identical** — all eight `locked-*`. **Five more carry no cluster above a channel
delta of 3.** Every remaining differing pixel in the pass belongs to one of six things, and to nothing
else:

| what | frames carrying it | what it reads now (round 22 →) | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| page-title date | 44 | `Saturday 5 September` → **`Sunday 6 September`** | 2× crop, all 8 `today-*` montaged |
| day column / Gantt axis caps | 32 | `TODAY · SAT 5` → **`TODAY · SUN 6`**; `29 Aug`/`26 Sep` → **`30 Aug`/`27 Sep`** | 2× montage of all 8 `tasks-gantt-*` |
| timeline / Gantt bars, shifted ≈+24px | 41 | bars anchored to a day boundary, window anchored to the instant | 1× crop, both frames stacked |
| relative-date meta lines | 33 | `passed 29 August` → `30 August`; `clean · 3 September` → `4 September`; `restored … 31 August` → `1 September`; `EA · 4 September` → `5 September`; `due 19 Sep` → `20 Sep` | 2× crops of each |
| toast countdown numeral | 5 | `6` → `7`, `9` → `10` | 8× crop of the ring |
| mic-orb listening pulse | 91 | the standing item | — |

**The ≈24px bar shift is arithmetic, not a layout change, and I checked it rather than assumed it.** The
Gantt track is 670px wide at 1920 over a fixed −7/+21 = 28-day window, so a day is 23.9px and an hour is
60 minutes per pixel. Between the two runs the *instant* advanced 23 minutes but the *day boundary* the
bars are anchored to advanced a full day, so the bars move **right** by (24h − 23min) ≈ 23.3px relative to
the window. Measured: 23–25px right in every affected frame, with the rails, labels, the dashed
in-progress bar's stroke and the `today` tick at 25% all unmoved. Round 22 saw the same mechanism at
1px because that pair straddled no midnight; this pair straddles one.

**The `- 2` frames.** `arrange-1024-light` and `decision-history-393-light` carry one cluster each whose
maximum channel delta is 4 — an antialiasing edge on a glyph that moved behind glass. I looked at both at
8×; there is nothing there but a softer edge.

## 2 · R23-01 · one bill, two due dates

**Severity:** MEDIUM. Visible in the frames. **Open.**

**Frames:** all eight `life-*.png` — `life-393-light`, `life-393-dark`, `life-1024-light`,
`life-1024-dark`, `life-1366-light`, `life-1366-dark`, `life-1920-light`, `life-1920-dark`.
Contradicted by all eight `today-*.png` and all eight `decision-bill-*.png`.

**What is wrong.** The Life Money card's footer reads

> `RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 due 20 Sep · feed: Redbark, V2.1`

while the same bill on the Today screen's Needs-you list, and again in the expanded bill decision card,
reads

> `RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 · due 19 Sep`

Same payee, same cents, two due dates, in one app, in one capture run. The bill card also says
`expires 17 Sep · then reminds you` and `silence reminds you 17 Sep`, which is coherent with 19 Sep and
one day short of coherent with 20 Sep.

**Why it is not noise, measured.** I cropped the two lines from the round-22 and round-23 bytes of the
same six frames and read them at 2×:

| screen | round 22 (`f3aaa07`) | round 23 (`8b1c976`) | moved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Today · Needs you · BILL row | `due 19 Sep` | `due 19 Sep` | no |
| Decision · bill card title | `due 19 Sep` | `due 19 Sep` | no |
| Life · Money footer | `due 19 Sep` | **`due 20 Sep`** | **yes, +1 day** |

The full-resolution diff agrees: the Today BILL row's pixels are byte-identical between the two commits,
and the Life footer's cluster is the second-largest non-orb cluster in every `life-*` frame
(max channel delta 158–173). The two lines agreed in every previous round because every previous round
was captured while the clock still read **5 September**, and 5 + 14 = 19.

**Where it comes from**, since the fix is not otherwise findable: `jstack-app/data/mock/fixtures/life.json:41`
gives the Money footer `"date": "{{TODAY+14}}"`, and `jstack-app/data/mock/fixtures/actions.json:53`
gives the bill card the literal `"title": "RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 · due 19 Sep"`. One is a clock,
one is a string, and they described one fact.

**The design pack line it breaks.** `jstack-app/design/README.md`, Voice: *"Numbers over adjectives:
`3 of 5 today`, not `a few items`."* This is the line R15-01 was decided on and for the same reason — a
pack that stakes its voice on the numbers being the truth cannot have two screens print contradicting
numbers for one object. `jstack-app/design/handoff.md:52` names both renderings as one thing:
*"footer line with RACQ due in accent-ink"* on Life, and the bill card on Today. And the behavioural
reference settles which value the pack intends: `jstack-mock-v11.html:317` has
`'RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 · due 19 Sep'` and `jstack-mock-v11.html:518` has
`'RACQ $1,184.20 due 19 Sep'` — **the mock pins both to the same literal date.** The build made one of
them live, and on the first day the two bases disagreed, they disagreed in front of the owner.
`DISCREPANCIES.md` resolves one row about this card (row 12, the `copy` links) and says nothing about
its date, so this is not a frame matching a resolved discrepancy's winner.

**Why I am raising it rather than filing it under round 15's "pinned fixture copy against a live clock".**
That entry covers copy that *reads oddly* — "That's all until 4pm" under a now-rule at 16:52. This does
not read oddly; it reads **wrongly**. A bill has one due date, the app shows two, and the owner has no way
to know which to pay against. It is the same shape as R15-01, which I raised and which was fixed, and
R15-01 was a component bug while this one is a fixture bug — but a reviewer judging pixels cannot see the
difference and neither can Josh.

**The fix I would make in source.** One line, and the mock says which way: give the Life footer the same
value the card carries rather than a second basis. Either

```json
// jstack-app/data/mock/fixtures/life.json:41 — was "date": "{{TODAY+14}}"
{ "text": "RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20", "date": "19 Sep", "feed": "Redbark, V2.1" }
```

which matches `jstack-mock-v11.html:518` exactly, or — better, if the demo is to keep breathing with the
clock — put the token on **both** and let one `{{TODAY+n}}` feed the card title too, so the two can never
be formatted on two bases again. What must not stay is one of each.

**One related thing I checked and am not raising.** `life.json:3` carries the same shape internally —
`"status": "on track · due 12 Sep"` beside `"due": "{{TODAY+8}}"` — and those two have disagreed since
before this pass. The `due` field is not rendered on the Goals card in any of the 134 frames (only the
status string is), so nothing contradicts anything on screen. I record it because it is the same trap one
row up in the same file, and whoever fixes R23-01 will be looking straight at it.

## 3 · The three things I was told to confirm

### R15-01 — the Gantt axis against Today's date. **Not regressed, and this round proves it harder than any round since 15.**

I cropped the axis band out of **all eight** `tasks-gantt-*` frames into one montage and read them at 2×.
All eight read **`30 Aug │ today │ 27 Sep`**. I did the same with the page title of **all eight**
`today-*` frames: all eight read **`Sunday 6 September`**, and the day column in each reads
**`TODAY · SUN 6`**. 30 Aug + 7 = 6 September; 6 September + 21 = 27 September. One window, one basis.

**The pair of runs is a sharper witness than either run alone, and I want to be exact about why.**

*Taken alone, these frames cannot distinguish a fixed Gantt from a broken one.* The capture ran
**10:02:07 → 10:05:39 local**, i.e. **00:02:07 → 00:05:39 UTC on 6 September**. Local date and UTC date
agree there, because UTC midnight in Brisbane is 10:00 and the run began two minutes after it. The live
window R15-01 was only ever visible in — local 00:00 to 10:00 — had closed. Rounds 19–22 each caught it
open; **this is the first run outside it**, and I will not claim a confirmation the frames do not carry.

*Taken as a pair, they discriminate exactly.* Round 22's pass finished at **09:38:53 local** (`f3aaa07`
was committed 09:39:30) showing `29 Aug` and `Saturday 5 September`. This pass began at
**10:02:07 local** showing `30 Aug` and `Sunday 6 September`. **Both labels flipped inside a 23-minute
window that contains 00:00 UTC and does not contain 00:00 local.** Under the pre-fix rendering the Gantt
cap turned over at local midnight — ten hours earlier — and round 22's 09:36-local frames would already
have read `30 Aug`. They read `29 Aug`. The Gantt is on UTC, the Today title is on UTC, and they turned
over on the same tick. That is the whole content of R15-01 and it holds.

### R17-01 — the toast above overlays. **Not regressed; measured at the same strictness as round 22.**

I located the pill by the geometry round 18 established (280 × 56 at bottom inset 24 on desktop; 248 × 56
at inset 90 on the phone; centred), inset 6px on all sides to exclude the rounded corners, and differenced
the interior against the unobstructed `undo-toast-*` at the same width and scheme:

| overlay | pairs | interior max delta | differing region |
|---|---|---|---|
| `toast-over-sheet-*` | **8 of 8** | **0** | **nothing at all** |
| `emergency-confirm-*` | 8 of 8 | 193–209 | an **11px column** — the countdown numeral — in all eight |

**All eight `toast-over-sheet` pill interiors are bit-identical to their unobstructed twin.** A scrim or a
panel painting over the pill cannot leave its interior numerically identical to an unobstructed one. The
pill fill reads `43·42·38` light and `236·233·226` dark, the same value in both frames of every pair, at
all four widths. The toast is in front, over the Settings sheet and over a `Dialog`. I also looked at
`toast-over-sheet-1024-light` and `emergency-confirm-1920-light` whole, and the pill is plainly in front
of the sheet and in front of the dialog.

The ring still depletes — `undo-toast` and `toast-over-sheet` at `10`, `emergency-confirm` at `7` — so the
countdown is live and not a painted still.

### B9-01 — the outlined button in `emergency-confirm-*`. **Unchanged, and this round measures all eight.**

I scanned a horizontal line through the middle of "Lock everything now" in **all eight** frames (round 22
measured six) and read the values on both sides of the border, in both the round-22 and round-23 bytes:

| frame | border-to-border span | border ink | interior 4px inside | ground 6px outside | r22 → r23 |

## 4 · R22-01 judged · the guard now catches what it claims to catch

**Closed.** This is my finding and the third attempt at this check, so I ran it rather than read it.

I lifted the shipped code **as text** and executed it: `capture-v2.mjs`'s `SCREENS`/`wanted`/`missing`/
`extra` block, and `handover.test.ts`'s QA-07 `declared` extraction and set-equality body, both pulled out
of the real files by string slice and evaluated with the inputs varied. Nothing in the repository was
written. I also ran the real suite unmodified: `npx jest tests/unit/handover.test.ts` → **10 passed**,
QA-07's four tests among them.

### 4.1 The failure the guard exists for: 17 of 17, by name

A family stops being captured; `SCREENS` untouched. This is the case that the previous version passed 16
times out of 17.

| | round 22's check | round 23's check |
|---|---|---|
| whole families caught by `capture-v2.mjs` | **1 of 17** (`arrange`, by accident of the `- 2`) | **17 of 17** |
| whole families caught by QA-07 | 4 of 17 (the four pinned by literal name) | **17 of 17** |
| what the operator is told | `wrote 128, expected 126` — a surplus of two | `device pass is MISSING 8 frame(s): agents-1024-dark.png, …` |
| one frame missing | caught | caught |

The hard-coded `- 2` is gone and the RL-05 exemption is a named condition. The residual I flagged last
round — twelve families, `today` among them, covered by neither guard — is **zero**.

### 4.2 First question: can a family still be dropped silently, by removing it from `SCREENS` too?

**Yes for thirteen of seventeen, no for four — and the two cases are not the same kind of risk.** I ran all
three shapes, seventeen removals each:

| scenario | families that stay green | caught by |
|---|---|---|
| A · dropped from the capture, `SCREENS` intact | **0 of 17** | both guards, by name |
| B · dropped from `SCREENS`, frames still on disk | **0 of 17** | both guards, as `extra` |
| C · dropped from **both** | 13 of 17 | QA-07 test 3's four pinned names catch `decision-bill`, `undo-toast`, `toast-over-sheet`, `emergency-confirm` |

A and B are the drift cases, and set equality closes them in both directions: the declaration and the
output cannot get out of step without something going red and naming the file. C is not drift. It is a
person deleting a line from a named list in one commit, which is a reviewable diff line rather than a
silent regression, and it is the irreducible residual of *any* declared list: no guard inside this
repository can say whether the declaration is the right declaration, because there is no second,
independent enumeration of the app's screens to check it against — I looked; `e2e/matrix/theme.spec.ts`
walks screens but does not list them, and no route table names these seventeen. This is the shape I
proposed in round 22 §3.6 and I am not going to raise the property I asked for. It is worth one sentence
in the tool's comment that the four pinned names are the belt for exactly this, which the comment already
almost says.

### 4.3 Second question: does reading the declaration out of the tool prevent drift, or just move the single point of failure?

**It prevents drift, and the point of failure it concentrates fails safe.** I mutated the tool text ten
ways a future edit plausibly would and asked what QA-07 does. **Not one mutation produced a false green:**

| mutation to `capture-v2.mjs` | `declared` | QA-07 |
|---|---|---|
| as shipped | 17 | green |
| `SCREENS` renamed to `ALL_SCREENS` | 0 | **RED** (test 1, then test 2 as 134 `extra`) |
| a formatter switches the array to single quotes | 0 | **RED** |
| the array built by spread from two lists | 0 | **RED** |
| an inline comment inside the array containing `];` | 1 | **RED** |
| an unrelated `const SCREENS = [` declared *above* the real one | 2 | **RED** |
| a new screen named in camelCase (`taskDetailV2`) | 17 | green — the name is silently skipped, then caught as `extra` the moment it is captured |
| an inline comment inside the array with a quoted word (`// the "home" screen`) | 18 | **RED**, naming a phantom `home-1024-dark.png` |
| the array collapsed onto one line | 17 | green, correct |
| `SCREENS` moved below the check | 17 | green, correct |

The parse is brittle — a rename or a quote-style change zeroes it — but it is brittle in the safe
direction, and `expect(declared.length).toBeGreaterThan(10)` exists precisely to catch the zero. The one
mildly unpleasant case is the phantom screen from a quoted word in a comment: it goes red, correctly, but
with a message about a file nobody was expecting. That is a footnote, not a finding.

**The genuine second copies are elsewhere, and I checked them too.** The widths list and the RL-05
exemption are each written twice — once in the tool, once in the test — which the commit message's
"stated once" claims only of the tool, fairly. I tested whether they can disagree silently: adding a
fifth width to the tool's `WIDTHS` and capturing it makes QA-07 red with `extra 34`. So the duplication
is real but self-announcing. Recorded, not raised.

### 4.4 What I would still say about it

The check is now what its comment says it is, which is the whole of what I asked for. Two smaller notes
for whoever touches it next, neither of them a defect:

- The tool's message truncates at eight names (`missing.slice(0, 8)`) and then prints a count, which is
  right for a console. QA-07's `expect({ missing, extra })` prints the full arrays, which is right for a
  test. Between them the operator always gets the names. Good split.
- `SCREENS` is declared but nothing asserts that every name in it is ever passed to `shot()`; a name
  declared and never shot fails as `missing` at the end of a full run, which is the right outcome but
  arrives three minutes late. Not worth changing.

**134 frames · 126 CLEAN · 8 carrying R23-01.** All from commit `8b1c976`.

The eight are all `life-*`. The contradiction is only visible by holding a `life-*` frame beside a
`today-*` or `decision-bill-*` frame of the same width and scheme, which is why the other sixteen frames
are marked CLEAN: nothing inside them is wrong, and the wrong number is the one that moved.

**What I checked in the frames beyond the delta, since the day turned and text lengths changed.** The
seven checklist items, applied at every width:

1. **Columns** — 393 one column with the floating tab bar and the orb above it on the right; 1024 rail +
   2 columns with column 3 stacked under column 1 and column 2 spanning, no empty row; 1366 and 1920 rail
   + 3 columns at `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`, content left-aligned and ending at x≈1730 at 1920 (≈1498 of a 1500
   max). No section laid across columns.
2. **Type** — page title 32/1 desktop and 26/1 phone; card titles Source Serif 4 upright; section labels
   11.5 uppercase tracked in accent ink. `Sunday` is one glyph shorter than `Saturday` and nothing
   reflowed around it.
3. **Colour** — alert appears on the over-budget Family track and amount in Life, on the Agents issue
   dots, and on the emergency lock. Nowhere else. Expiry is accent ink. Marker is on count badges and the
   orb only.
4. **Surfaces** — frosted cards, small card-to-ground step, hairlines, empty column bottoms left empty
   (Brain's column 3, Tasks' column 3 below the mini-Gantt).
5. **Text** — the one-day shift was the risk and it did not bite. `30 Aug`/`27 Sep` are the same glyph
   count as `29 Aug`/`26 Sep`. `1 September` is two glyphs longer than `31 August`; I cropped that row in
   `agents-393-light` before and after and it wraps identically, `August` and `September` each alone on
   the second line of a right-aligned meta value — the same shape round 22 signed, and not a title. The
   two-digit `10` in the countdown ring sits inside it with clear padding at 8×.
6. **Dark** — same layout as light, no reflow, no scheme-only element. The ground samples `25·24·21`
   (`#191815`) at the corner, mid-right and bottom edge of every dark frame I measured, including under
   the phone tab bar; light samples `237·235·229`. No pure black, no pure white.
7. **Density** — 1920 reads as a dashboard, 1024 as a tablet, 393 as a phone.

| R22-01 · scenarios A/B/C | the shipped `capture-v2.mjs` block and QA-07 body lifted as text and executed, 17 removals per scenario, 51 runs |
| R22-01 · drift | 10 textual mutations of `capture-v2.mjs`, QA-07's three tests evaluated against each |
| R22-01 · as shipped | `npx jest tests/unit/handover.test.ts` → 10 passed, 1 suite |
| dark ground is `#191815` | RGB sampled at the top-left corner, mid-right edge and bottom edge of 5 dark frames |

---

## Verdict

**134 frames, 126 CLEAN, 8 carrying one defect.** The pictures are the same pictures I signed in round 22
with one day added to every clock in them, and I have accounted for every pixel of that.

**R22-01 is closed, and closed well.** The check I objected to caught one family in seventeen; the check
that replaced it catches seventeen in seventeen, by name, in both halves of the pair, and every mutation I
could think of makes it red rather than green. Reading the declaration out of the tool does prevent drift
— it is the two-sided set equality that does the work, not the sharing — and the single point it
concentrates on fails safe. What it cannot do is vouch for the declaration itself, and nothing in this
repository can; that residual is a reviewable diff line, not a silent one, and four of the seventeen names
are pinned against even that.

**One finding is open: R23-01.** The Life Money footer says the RACQ bill is due 20 September and the
bill card says 19 September. It is one line of fixture, the mock pins both to the same literal date, and
it has been latent since the pack was first captured — invisible for nine rounds because every one of
them was photographed on 5 September, where the computed value and the written one happened to agree.
This pass is the first taken after that midnight, which is the only reason anyone can see it. That is
worth saying plainly: the defect is not new, the evidence is.

I will not sign a pass in which the app tells its owner two different days to pay a bill.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

**Reviewed:** 6 September 2026, **10:41 AEST (UTC+10)** — 2026-09-06 00:41 UTC.
**Commit:** `8b1c976` (`8b1c9765e1530d6fca43e48c9d158b944d52b9db`).

## 2 · Defects, most severe first

### D1 · A multiline `Field` renders twelve rows tall at rest on desktop — MAJOR

**Frames (12):** `today-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}`, `decision-bill-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}`
(the "How was today?" journal), `brain-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}` (the mind-dump box).

**What is wrong.** Measured heights of the same two controls:

| control | 393 | 1024 | 1366 | 1920 | mock v11 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Today journal "How was today?" | ~48px | ~50px | **~193px** | **~193px** | `rows="2"` |
| Brain mind-dump box | ~85px | ~84px | **~195px** | **~195px** | `rows="2"`, `min-height:64px` |

At 1366 and 1920 the journal is a ~193px rectangle holding one line of placeholder and three
30px icon buttons — roughly 150px of dead space — and it is the last thing in column 3, so
"Close the day" ends in a large empty box. The mind-dump box does the same in Brain's column 1,
overriding its call site's own `minHeight: 64` by a factor of three.

**Pack lines broken.**
- `handoff.md` Today Column 3: *"Close the day: nine habit chips … then a journal field (hairline border, radius 8, "How was today?" with mic and keyboard icons)."* — no tall writing area is specified.
- `handoff.md` Brain: *"Mind dump box (card, min-height 64, placeholder 12.5 muted, mic (accent-soft) and arrow_upward (outlined) 30px buttons)."*
- `README.md` Layout: *"Leave the bottom of a column empty when the content ends. Do not stretch cards to match heights."* — the field stretches its card by ~150px of nothing.
- Reference build `jstack-mock-v11.html:469` (journal) and `:504` (mind dump) both use `<textarea rows="2">` at every width.

**Root cause.** `theme/ui/fields.tsx:162`:

```
numberOfLines={expanded ? undefined : expands ? (hasDraft ? PREVIEW_LINES : 1) : multiline ? DESKTOP_MAX_LINES : undefined}
```

with `DESKTOP_MAX_LINES = 12` (line 195). On react-native-web `numberOfLines` compiles to the
`<textarea rows>` attribute, which is a **fixed resting height, not a ceiling**. The constant's
own comment (line 194) reads *"UX-03: how far a desktop field grows in place before it scrolls"*
— i.e. it was written as a maximum, and `rows` cannot express a maximum.

**Fix in source.** Leave `rows` at the reference's 2 (or let the caller's `minHeight` stand) and
express the ceiling on the box instead — `maxHeight: DESKTOP_MAX_LINES * lineHeight` in the
`style` array at `fields.tsx:133`, with `scrollEnabled` once the content passes it. That gives
UX-03 the behaviour its comment describes without changing the resting size.

**Why this one matters most.** The stage claims S-2b's `Field` change altered focus behaviour on
touch widths only, and that *"resting state should be unchanged"*. At ≥1180 the resting state is
changed, in the opposite direction from where the change was scoped, and it is the most visible
thing in the set.

---

### D2 · Today's delta line is painted Accent ink where the pack says Muted — MODERATE

**Frames (16):** all eight `today-*` and all eight `decision-bill-*`.

**What is wrong.** The whole sentence *"Since 9pm: 2 things landed while you slept, 4 memory
proposals waiting. Review the week"* renders in the steel accent ink, not the warm Muted grey.
Median stroke-core samples from `today-1920-light.png`, measured as blue-minus-red (warm greys
are negative, the steel accent positive):

| element | rgb | b−r |
|---|---|---|
| header subtitle "6 September" (Muted) | (132,126,122) | **−10** |
| why-line "both calendars · Alex…" (Muted) | (150,147,141) | **−9** |
| glance label "Habits" (Muted) | (148,146,139) | **−9** |
| "history" link (Accent ink) | (109,111,131) | **+22** |
| "NEEDS YOU" section label (Accent ink) | (89,107,122) | **+33** |
| **delta line body** | (104,116,144) | **+40** |

The delta body is cooler than both accent-ink references — it is unambiguously not Muted.

**Pack lines broken.**
- `handoff.md` Shell: *"Today adds a delta line beneath (11.5 muted) ending in a "review the week" link."*
- Reference build `jstack-mock-v11.html:55`: `.delta{font-size:11.5px;color:var(--muted);margin-top:6px;max-width:70ch}`
- `README.md` Principles 3: *"Colour means you can act. The steel accent marks verbs, labels, the recommended option and the current tab. Nothing decorative gets colour."*
- `README.md` Colour, *Where colour goes*: *"Accent ink: section labels, primary-verb text, links, expiry text, recommended option number, active tab, provenance links."* A delta sentence is none of the seven.

**Consequence.** The one genuinely tappable phrase in the line — "Review the week" — is now the
same hue as the twelve non-tappable words in front of it, and is separated only by weight 500.
A link is not on the pack's weight-500 allow-list (*"Weight 500 for a card title, a primary verb,
a selected chip, a person's name in People, the answered verb in history"*), so the accent is
carrying no information and the weight is doing a job the colour was supposed to do.

**Root cause.** `components/chrome/Header.tsx:61`:

```
<Txt testID="header-delta" kind="meta" style={{ color: c.textExpiry }}>
```

Two deviations on one line: `c.textExpiry` (the accent-ink expiry token) where the pack wants
`c.muted`, and `kind="meta"` (10.5px) where the pack says 11.5px.

**Fix in source.** Drop the `style` override so the `meta` kind's own Muted default applies, and
give the delta its own 11.5px kind in `theme/ui/textKinds.ts` (the pack's `label` step is 11.5
but is uppercase and tracked, so it cannot be reused). Keep the trailing "Review the week" in
`accentInk` — as a link it is the one part that has earned the colour — and drop its weight 500.

**Honest limit.** The colour is measurable and plainly visible. The 1px size difference is **not**
something I can see in these frames; I am reporting it from the source line, not from the pixels.

---

### D3 · The Settings sheet title renders at ~20px where the pack says 26 — LOW

**Frames (8):** all `settings-*`.

**What is wrong.** Cap-height measurement of the "S" of "Settings" against known scale steps in
the same pass:

| element | pack size | measured cap height |
|---|---|---|
| Today page title "Sunday" (desktop) | 32 | 22px |
| Today page title "Sunday" (phone) | 26 | 18px |
| Card title "RACQ home insurance…" | 15 | 10px |
| **Settings sheet title** | **26 (pack)** | **14px → ~20px rendered** |

The dialog's title reads a step smaller than the page titles it is covering.

**Pack lines broken.**
- `README.md` Type, Scale: *"Section heading in a sheet (Settings): 26 / 1, Source Serif 4 400."*
- `handoff.md` Settings: *"Header: "Settings" in Source Serif 4 400 at 26, sub-line "One account · 3 devices · changes save as you make them", 32px close button."*

**Root cause.** `components/settings/SettingsSheet.tsx:102` renders `<Txt kind="heading">Settings</Txt>`,
and `theme/ui/textKinds.ts:64` defines `heading: { fontFamily: fonts.heading, fontSize: 20 }`.

**Fix in source.** Either give `SettingsSheet` the pack's 26 through a `sheetHeading` kind, or add
a DISCREPANCIES row ruling 20 the winner. Right now it is neither: `textKinds.ts` lines 57-63 say
*"design/DISCREPANCIES.md records the scale gap"*, but DISCREPANCIES row 13 catalogues the eleven
**S-2b** roles and has no row for `heading` at 20 against the Settings 26.

**Honest note.** `textKinds.ts` states this literal predates the migration (*"both overlays have
always used this literal"*), so **this is not a stage regression** — S-2b only gave it a home. It
is reported because it is visible and because the deviation is currently undocumented.

---

### D4 · "Read the brief at 06:30" is zero-padded; every other time on the sheet is not — LOW

**Frames (8):** all `settings-*`.

**What is wrong.** The same Settings sheet shows the same 6:30am brief in two formats. The
Schedules card reads `6:30 daily`, `2:00 nightly`, `6:00 daily`, `Mon 8:00`, `Sun 18:00` — no
leading zeros anywhere — while the Voice card two cards away reads **"Read the brief at 06:30"**.

**Pack lines broken.**
- `handoff.md` Settings: *"Voice (Style and Speed as bordered value buttons with `expand_more`, "Read the brief at 6:30" switch)."*
- Reference build `jstack-mock-v11.html:693` renders the literal `Read the brief at 6:30`.
- `README.md` Content: *"Times: 24-hour in lists (`15:00`), spoken form in prose (`2:00pm`)."* — the sheet's own convention drops the pad, and this row breaks it.

**Root cause.** `components/settings/Voice.tsx:46` interpolates the stored canonical value straight
into display copy:

```
<Txt>Read the brief{voice.readBriefAt != null ? ` at ${voice.readBriefAt}` : ""}</Txt>
```

`readBriefAt` is seeded `"06:30"` (line 53) — correct as data, wrong as copy. This sits in S-5's
blast radius: the stage unified the time library, and this is the one display site that does not
pass through it.

**Fix in source.** Format `readBriefAt` through the shared time-display helper (the one the
Schedules cadences already use) rather than interpolating the raw `HH:mm` string.

---

### D5 · Brain's Find placeholder is clipped mid-glyph at 393 — LOW

**Frames (2):** `brain-393-light`, `brain-393-dark`.

**What is wrong.** The placeholder *"Find · what did Andy say about the memory layer?"* is sliced
through the "r" of "layer" at the input's right edge and butts against the send button. No
ellipsis, no fade — a raw pixel cut through a letterform. At 1024 and above the same string fits
with room to spare.

**Pack line broken.** Reviewer checklist item 5 / `README.md` Do-and-don't: *"No word broken
mid-word. No clipped or ellipsised label."*

**Root cause.** The string is longer than the 393 field; a single-line `TextInput` clips its
placeholder at the box boundary with no ellipsis.

**Fix in source.** Shorten the placeholder at phone widths (`"Find · ask anything"` or similar),
or set `ellipsizeMode` so the cut lands on a word boundary with an ellipsis.

**Honest note.** The string is the mock's own (`jstack-mock-v11.html:506`), so the reference build
clips identically at 393. **This is inherited, not introduced by this stage** — the fix is a
design call, not a regression to back out.
