## 3 · What was checked and is correct

Named explicitly, because a clean report is only useful if it says what it actually looked at.

**S-4 · Fonts — clean, and verified against the shipped binaries, not by eye.** I rendered
specimens from `jstack-app/public/fonts/InstrumentSans_400Regular.ttf` and
`SourceSerif4_400Regular.ttf` and compared them with Segoe UI (the system UI font this build would
fall back to on Windows). Every frame's body text, chip label, button label, meta line and
placeholder matches Instrument Sans; every page title, card title and wordmark matches Source
Serif 4. **No frame in the set renders in a system UI font**, including the Settings dialog, which
renders through a different portal path. The 140-line runtime shim's deletion is clean.

**S-7 / CD-15 · The bill card — correct at all four widths, both schemes.** All three rows carry
an equal 36px height, so the payee row (which has no link) lines up with the two that do — the
round-10 finding is fixed and holds. The label column measures 44px with a 10px gutter, matching
the mock's `.bill{grid-template-columns:44px 1fr auto;gap:6px 10px}` exactly. Both `copy` links
are right-aligned flush at the same x; labels, values and links sit within 1px of a common
baseline in every row. `copy` appears on BSB and ref and not on payee, per DISCREPANCIES row 12.
Nothing clips or wraps badly even at 393, where the title still fits on one line.

**S-5 · Dates — consistent.** "Sunday" / "6 September" / "TODAY · SUN 6" agree with each other and
with the calendar; 6 September 2026 is genuinely a Sunday. The grid and the list agree on every
event (Andy · V2 kickoff 9:00, Lunch · Joce 12:30, School pickup 15:00), and the bill's
`expires 18 Sep · then reminds you` against `due 20 Sep` is coherent. The only time defect found
is D4.

**S-3 · The Settings dialog — renders correctly through DialogHost.** Nine notification groups,
four device columns, seven schedule rows, six autonomy rows, four focus filters plus "Add a
focus". Switches move their knob in both schemes (on = accent-soft track, accent-ink knob at the
right; off = hairline track, bar-colour knob at the left) — the states differ by position *and*
colour, not colour alone. The device columns stay visually separate at 393, so the R2-01 fix in
DISCREPANCIES row 8 holds. The scrim samples (173,172,167) over the light ground, which is exactly
`rgba(28,26,22,.3)` over `#EDEBE5`. Two columns at 1366/1920 and one at 1024/393, correct against
the 1180 rule; reading down column 1 then column 2 gives Appearance → Schedules → Autonomy →
Voice → Focus filters, exactly the order `handoff.md` lists.

**Locked screen — clean at every width.** Content is centred in its viewport at all four widths
(measured centre offset 5-6px from page mid, which is the button's own optical padding), and the
ground is painted edge to edge including all four corners at exactly `#EDEBE5` light and
`#191815` dark.

**Light/dark parity — no reflow anywhere.** Row-occupancy structure compared for all 20 pairs:
0.0%-3.6% of rows differ, which is threshold noise on hairlines and shadows. A reflow would shift
everything below its origin and show 30-60%. Nothing appears, disappears or moves between schemes.

**Columns and density.** At 1920 and 1366: rail + three columns, content spanning x=232..1732 —
**exactly 1500 wide, left-aligned**, with 188px of bare ground to its right (a centred layout
would have split that 94/94). At 1024: rail + two columns with column 3 stacked directly under
column 1 and column 2 spanning both rows — no dead row — verified on Today, Brain and
decision-bill. At 393: one column, floating tab bar inset from the edges, mic orb above it on the
right, header trimmed to Settings + Theme with the health line on its own line beneath. 1920 reads
as a dashboard; 393 reads as a phone.

**S-2b · Type migration — no mis-sizing found beyond D2 and D3.** Measured cap heights are
consistent with the pack at every step I could isolate: page title 32 (cap 22) desktop and 26
(cap 18) phone, card title 15 (cap 10) on both the clash and bill cards, meta 10.5 (band 10px) on
why-lines, glance labels and option why-lines. No text is mis-sized relative to its neighbours,
and nothing renders bold or italic. The claim that S-2b was a refactor holds everywhere except the
delta line, whose 10.5 is one step under the pack's 11.5 (folded into D2).

**Colour.** The health dot samples (176,85,63) = `#B0553F`, the pack's Alert exactly, and Alert
appears nowhere else in the set — expiry text is accent ink throughout, never red. Marker appears
only on the count badges ("Needs you 5", "Memory 4", "Rules for my EA 4") and nowhere else; the
idle mic orb is correctly Card surface with an accent-ink glyph, not Marker. No per-category hue
on habits or calendar categories. No v1.2 green. No pure black or white surface in either scheme.

**Resting states (S-2b hover work).** Hover is not observable in a static frame, but a wrong
resting state would be, and none is: chips are radius 8 (not pills), primary buttons are
accent-soft fills with accent-ink text and never saturated, outlined buttons sit on hairlines,
there are no 2px borders, and the card-to-ground step stays small in both schemes.

On `offline-d{1,2}-393-{light,dark}-test` the chip is inside the Rules card and covers "or ask Joce first." completely, punching a ground-coloured hole through a frosted card. Round 2's defect was the mark being covered; round 3's is the mark covering · pack: row A-1 brief, the watermark "must be legible and **must not sit over a control or another line** (it printed over the rail's health line for eight rows before anyone looked: B-32)" · fix: the raise must go to a position that is empty, not merely above `TOAST_BOTTOM.phone` — while a toast is up on the phone, put the mark in the toast's own band (the pill is centred and about 250px wide at 393, so the left inset is free) or suppress it for the ten seconds the toast lives, instead of translating it by a fixed constant into whatever content happens to be there. `e2e/core/identity.spec.ts` ID-02 asserts the mark is disjoint from the toast; it needs to assert the mark is disjoint from the page content too.

R3-02 · MAJOR · `task-detail-d2-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-test` (8) · the Activity card prints a raw machine timestamp: "Bundaberg memo drafted / EA · **2026-09-07T03:00:00.000Z**", directly above its correctly formatted sibling "2 of 3 subtasks done / EA · 6 September". Measured on `task-detail-d2-393-light-test`, `task-detail-d2-1366-light-test` and `task-detail-d2-1920-dark-test`; the day-1 frames carry only the one activity row and so do not show it. It is not only unformatted — it is UTC, so the one thing the EA did today is stamped 03:00 · pack: README Content "Times: 24-hour in lists (`15:00`), spoken form in prose (`2:00pm`). Dates: `4 September`, `19 Sep` in tight spaces" — an ISO-8601 instant is none of those; README Principles 6, "plain words" · fix: the day-2 activity's timestamp reaches the row unformatted while its sibling goes through the formatter — send every Activity row's time through `lib/time.ts`, the same call the "6 September" row already makes, and guard it: no rendered meta line may match `/\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T/`.

R3-03 · LOW · every frame carrying the Needs-you waiting list — measured on `today-d1-1366-light-prod`, `today-d2-1920-dark-test`, `decision-bill-d2-1366-light-test`, `decision-section-d1-393-light-test` · one card stack spells expiry four ways in five consecutive lines: "expires Thu 5pm", "expires Fri 5pm", "expires Sat 7am", "expires 19 Sep", "expires **in 2 days**", "expires **in 5 days**". The pack sanctions the first shape and the fourth; the relative "in N days" is a duration, not a time or a date, and it is the only one that does not tell the owner when · pack: README Content "Expiry is stated as a time and a consequence: `expires Wed 5pm · then proposes 1`" and "Dates: `4 September`, `19 Sep` in tight spaces" · fix: one formatter for row expiry — weekday plus time inside seven days, `19 Sep` beyond it — so "in 2 days" becomes "expires Wed 9am" and "in 5 days" "expires Sat 5pm". R-29 fixed the long/short weekday split and left this; it is the same inconsistency one level up.

R3-04 · LOW · `brain-*` (24) and the Brain-backed `offline-*` frames at 1024/1366/1920 (12) · two of the four memory proposals break badly at every width and in both schemes: "File "Moz discovery call" under Work / **· jstack**" starts its second line with a middle dot, which reads as a bullet rather than a separator, and "Label 3 captures from Saturday as / **Personal**" leaves a single word alone on the second line. Both breaks fall between the sentence and the weight-500 value it is about, so the emphasised phrase is the part that gets orphaned (`brain-d1-1366-light-prod` at 4×, `offline-d2-1366-dark-test`) · pack: reviewer checklist 5 "No single-word orphan line in a title"; README Content "Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`" — the dot belongs between two things on one line · fix: in `lib/richText.tsx` bind the separator to the token that follows it with a non-breaking space so the dot can never lead a line, and keep the emphasised value with at least one preceding word.

R3-05 · LOW (unsure) · `settings-*` and `toast-over-sheet-*` at 1024/1366/1920 (36) · in the Settings sheet, "Push to this device / blocked in your browser settings — JSTACK cannot ask again" renders as a bare title-plus-meta row on the sheet ground, between the Notifications card's quiet-hours footer and the APPEARANCE AND ACCOUNT label. It is the only content in the sheet that is neither on a card nor a section label, so it reads as a row that fell out of the card above it — on `settings-d1-1366-light-prod` the surface behind it samples the sheet ground `221,221,221`, not the card's `251,251,251` · pack: README Components, Settings sheet "scrim + one frosted sheet, **section label above each card**, rows 8px tall with hairlines"; handoff Settings specifies the Notifications card as "Nine groups … Footer line about quiet hours" and no loose row · fix: put the permission notice inside the Notifications card as a tenth row with its own hairline, or give it the Muted footer treatment the quiet-hours line beside it already has. Unsure: it may be a deliberate inline notice, but at 12.5 Ink over 10.5 Muted it is dressed as a row, not as a notice.

R3-06 · LOW (unsure) · `talk-d{1,2}-{1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-test` (12) · Talk's Reply is the only primary in the app stretched to the content width: on `talk-d1-1920-light-test` it is a 1395px button with a five-letter label centred in it, beside Mute and End which hug their labels at about 44px, under a left-aligned transcript and a centred orb — four alignments in one screen, which is the read Josh called "amateur" on the v1.1 frames. Every other primary in the pass (Approve, Go with 1, Block it, Open NAB, Done, Save, Lock everything now) sizes to its label · pack: README Components, Buttons "Primary `.js-btn-primary`: Accent soft fill, Accent ink text, 12.5/500, **padding 9**, radius 8" — the primary is specified by its padding, not by a stretch; README Do-and-don't, "centred layouts on desktop" · fix: give `TalkScreen`'s verb row the decision card's proportions (primary at `flex 1.3` against the two outlined buttons) rather than `flex: 1` against fixed-width siblings, so Reply is wide without being a banner. Unsure: a full-width send control under a composer is a common convention and the pack does not draw this surface.

Coverage: 508 of 508 frames read. Programmatic: inventory against the 23-screen matrix regenerated from the file-name grammar (17 screens × 24, Arrange and Arrange · Life × 18 with no phone frame, the four rig-only states × 16 — no frame missing, none extra, no name that fails to parse, every frame's pixel width equal to the width in its name); corner samples on all four corners of all 508 (exact `#EDEBE5` / `#191815` on every non-overlay frame; the 173 that differ are the scrimmed overlay frames plus the `undo-toast` top-right, which is the 5px scrollbar thumb at `202,200,194` — the pack's own thumb colour over ground — and is not a defect); an edge-energy floor that found no blank frame and none stuck on the gate (the twelve lowest are the twelve desktop `locked-*`, correctly, and every `locked-*` including the four phone ones carries the watermark); 254 light↔dark pairs matched on document height (**0 mismatches**) with row-profile correlation ≥0.80 on every pair, so no reflow and nothing appears or disappears between schemes; 254 prod↔test pixel diffs at day 1 (largest 0.11%, 862px; every diff bbox resolves to the calendar's 1px "now" rule shifting between capture runs or to the toast countdown ring — verified by crop on `today-d1-1920-light-{prod,test}` — so R1-06 stays clear); and 118 day-1↔day-2 test pairs, of which 78 are within 0.02% — `locked`, `sync`, `arrange-life`, `emergency-confirm` and `life-config` are pixel-identical across the fixture days and `tasks-*`, `brain` and `life` differ only by capture noise, so the second day exercises the Today family and `task-detail` and little else. By eye: 34 frames read full-size and 27 more as 2–5× crops, covering all 23 screens at 1366 plus at least two other widths each, both schemes and both fixture days; the Section card in Needs you reads as a picture of a section, its preview inset sampling `227,229,229`, the same Accent-soft inset as Today's recommended option row, rather than a section escaped into a card; Talk carries the 96px orb, the words-only state line and no digit anywhere; the queued row and the offline health line both read as reassurance.

**Reviewed:** 7 September 2026.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

## V2.2 F-1 (Tasks)

**Date:** 8 September 2026
**Reviewer:** ux-reviewer (product eyes)
**Row:** F-1 - ADR-44 (slicer row on all four views, range chip, Clear, filter + edit buttons), with
T-4 (per-row usage/cost) and T-5 (agent working marker) visible in the same frames.
**Scope:** the 40 PNGs in `demo/v22/` named in the brief - `tasks-{list,board,gantt,done}` and
`task-detail`, day 1, production build, {393, 1024, 1366, 1920} x {light, dark}. All 40 present, none
blank, none the wrong screen, none showing the gate.
**Comparison:** `demo/v21/` at the same file names, used only to separate what F-1 introduced from
what it inherited. **No source file was read for a verdict and no source file was edited.**

Measurements below are pixel reads of the PNGs: contiguous-run scans against each frame's own ground
token, vertical and horizontal extent probes on named coordinates, and exact RGB samples. Where I give
a size or a colour, I measured it.

### Verdict

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

**8 defects introduced by F-1** (F1-01 .. F1-08) and **4 carried** (C-1 .. C-4) that F-1 did not cause
but that are in front of Josh on these frames. The eight `task-detail` frames are **clean** - F-1 does
not touch the detail dialog and it shows no sign of the row.

The short answer to the question behind the row: **the slicer row does not yet read as one row of
controls.** Not because of any one thing, but because of three independent misfits stacked on one
line - a chip guillotined at the scroll edge, a 6px height mismatch between the chips and the two
buttons, and a right-hand pair anchored to the column edge instead of to the chips, so at 393 it
collides with them and at 1920 it sits 443px away from them. Each is small. Together they are the
"pile".

### Defects, ranked

**F1-01 - MAJOR - the chip scroller is guillotined, not faded** - `tasks-list-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod`,
`tasks-board-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod`, `tasks-gantt-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod`,
`tasks-done-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod` (8 frames).

On List, Board and Gantt the third chip is cut at x=289 through the "g" of "Waiting", and the cut is a
flat vertical edge: the chip's radius-8 right corner and its border are amputated with it, so what is on
screen is not a chip continuing off-stage but a chip with its end sliced off. On Done, where the range
chip is the shorter "All time - edit", the cut lands 4px into "Delegated" and leaves a 4px vertical stub
of chip fill floating in the gap, which reads as a rendering artefact rather than a control. There is no
fade and no mask - measured, the chip fill runs at full opacity to x=288 and the ground resumes at
x=289. The gap from that edge to the filter button is **6px**, so the amputated chip and the button
touch at conversational distance.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 5 - "No word broken mid-word. **No clipped or ellipsised label inside a
button, chip or segment.**" The pack sanctions the ellipsis only where it names it (the waiting-row
title), never at a scroll edge.

*Root cause, not the pixel:* the row is a `space-between` flex with a horizontal scroller on the left
and the two buttons on the right. The scroller is handed whatever width is left and clips on its own
bounds - it has no reserved right-hand gutter, no mask, no scroll-indicator inset. Nothing in the
component knows that its right edge is a *visible* edge rather than a viewport edge.

*Fix in source:* on the scroller's container only - `paddingRight: 20` inside the clip box,
`maskImage: linear-gradient(to right, #000 calc(100% - 20px), transparent)` (and the `-webkit-` twin),
and raise the scroller-to-button gap from 6 to 12. Three properties on one element; it fixes all eight
phone frames and touches nothing else. **That is the smallest correct fix** - do not solve it by
shortening the chip labels or dropping a chip, both of which cost information.

**F1-02 - MAJOR - the chips and the two buttons are different heights and share a top edge, so the row
has a ragged bottom** - all 32 view frames (List, Board, Gantt, Done x 393/1024/1366/1920 x
light/dark).

Measured on every one of the 32: the chips occupy a **30px** band and the two icon buttons a **36px**
box, and the two share a top edge, so the buttons hang **6px** below the chips. At 393, chips y180-210
against buttons y180-216. At 1024/1366/1920, chips y154-184 against buttons y154-190. Identical in both
schemes, on all four views. At 1024, where the chips wrap, the buttons' overhang lands exactly in the
6px gutter between chip row 1 and chip row 2, so the pair looks like it is sinking into the second row.

This is the single largest contributor to the "pile" read. The eye takes the bottom edge of a control
row as the row's edge, and this row has two.

Secondary, and I am **unsure** about this half: 30px is under the pack's phone tap target. The enclosing
band is 36px, so the real target may be 36 if the row passes the press through - the frame cannot prove
which. The alignment half is certain.

*Pack:* README Components, Focus chip - "6 x 12, radius 8, 12px" (which computes to the 30px the slicer
chips render) beside README Components, Buttons - "Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: **32 or 36 square**"; and
README Accessibility - "**Tap targets 36px minimum on phone**". The pack pairs a 30px chip with a 36px
icon button and never says how they align; the frame shows what happens when nobody decides.

*Root cause:* the slicer row sets no cross-axis alignment, so its children start at the top. Note also
that the focus chip row 58px above renders its chips at **36px** (measured y86-122 at 393) - two chip
rows on one screen, 8px apart, at two different heights. ADR-44 unified the *editor* ("the
`FocusEditDialog` generalised to `ChipSetEditDialog`, one component serving focuses and slicers") but
not the chip.

*Fix in source:* `alignItems: "center"` on the slicer row's container - that alone removes the ragged
bottom at every width without changing a single height. Then, separately, settle the chip metric once:
give the slicer chip the focus chip's 36px min-height under 768, so the two rows agree and the tap
target question closes with it.

**F1-03 - MAJOR - on the Gantt the range chip claims a window the axis does not draw** -
`tasks-gantt-d1-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-prod` (8 frames).

The chip reads **"Next 90 days - edit"**. The axis directly beneath it reads **"1 Sep | today |
29 Sep"** - 29 days. Day 1 is 8 September, so the chip promises 8 Sep to 6 Dec and the chart draws
1 Sep to 29 Sep, a window that does not even begin where the chip says it begins. The card then closes
with "Bar dates come from Twenty. Open in Twenty for the full timeline." - so above the chart a control
says it governs the range, and below it a line says the real range is somewhere else.

This one is F-1's, not the Gantt's. `demo/v21/tasks-gantt-d1-393-light-prod.png` shows the same
four-week axis ("31 Aug | today | 28 Sep") with **no range chip above it and no claim attached**. F-1
added the claim without adding the behaviour.

*Pack:* ADR-46 - "**The axis is built from the active range (ADR-44)**"; TF-01 - "The range chip is the
first item of the slicer row and always visible ... a task outside the range is absent from the open
views"; README Principles 7 - "**Show the work.**"

*Root cause:* the Gantt still derives its axis from its own fixed four-week window rather than from
`filters.range`. F-1 mounted the shared slicer row on the Gantt ahead of the ADR-46 axis work, so the
row renders a value the view does not consume.

*Fix in source:* either make the axis read `filters.range` (the ADR-46 change), or - if that work
belongs to a later row - do not render the range chip on the Gantt until the axis honours it. A chip
that lies is worse than a chip that is absent.

**F1-04 - MODERATE - the two icon buttons do not read as two controls, and one is the second `tune` on
the screen** - all 32 view frames.

The pair is: 36px square, radius 10, 1px hairline border, **no fill** (the ground reads straight through
both - sampled `#EDEBE5` light and `#191815` dark inside each box), 6px apart, both glyphs Muted, both
outline (verified at 6x: neither is a filled glyph and neither is visibly heavier than the other), and
neither labelled. Nothing groups them, nothing separates them, and they are the only unfilled surfaces
in a row of Card-filled chips. They read as one two-part control.

The compounding problem is above them: the focus chip row 58px up carries a **third identical 36px
`tune` button**, which edits the focus set. So a phone frame now shows the same glyph twice, in two
adjacent rows, meaning two different things - filter-the-tasks and edit-the-focuses.

*Pack:* README Icons, fixed set - "**Filter `tune`**" (one meaning per glyph is the point of a fixed
set); README Components, Buttons - "Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: 32 or 36 square, radius 8 or 10,
**Card fill with Card border** (header) or Hairline border (in cards)" - these sit on the ground, are
neither case, and carry no fill at all.

*Root cause:* both are the generic `IconButton` with a different glyph name and no grouping, labelling
or variant. Nothing in the component expresses that one opens a panel that will come back wearing a
count badge and the other opens an editor.

*Fix in source:* make them different kinds of control rather than two of the same. Keep `tune` as the
icon button - it is the one that has to carry the count badge - and render the slicer editor as the
pack's text link ("edit", Accent ink, 11px Small, `.js-btn-sm` metrics) at the row's end. That removes
the duplicate glyph, removes the twin, and echoes the range chip's own "- edit" affordance. If both must
stay icons, then at minimum 10px apart with a hairline divider between them, and change the focus row's
trailing glyph so only one `tune` exists on any screen.

**F1-05 - MODERATE - the range chip is dressed as an off toggle** - all 32 view frames.

"Next 90 days - edit" (and "All time - edit" on Done) renders in the **unselected** chip style: Card
fill, hairline border, Muted text. Sampled: the darkest ink in "Next 90 days" is `(126,123,116)` and the
darkest in "edit" is `(126,123,116)` - the same value, and `#7A776F` Muted within antialiasing. Same
size, same weight, same colour, in the same chip, as its neighbours "This week" and "Waiting", which are
toggles that are currently **off**.

So the one chip in the row that is always in force wears the styling that, everywhere else in that row,
means "not applied"; and the one chip that opens a dialog is typographically identical to the ones that
toggle. Josh asked whether the "- edit" distinction lands. It does not. It reads as a chip whose label
happens to end in the word "edit".

*Pack:* README Components, Focus chip - "Unselected: Card fill, Card border, Muted text. **Selected:
Accent soft fill, Accent ink text, 500**"; README Type, Rules - "Weight 500 for a card title, a primary
verb, **a selected chip**"; README Colour, Where colour goes - "Accent ink: ... **links**".

*Root cause:* one `Chip` component with a boolean `selected` and no third variant for "always in force,
and opens something". A range is neither on nor off; it is a value.

*Fix in source:* give the range chip the selected treatment (Accent soft fill, Accent ink text, weight
500 - all three sanctioned above) and set "edit" in Accent ink with a 14px `expand_more` in place of the
middle dot, so the chip that opens a picker is the only chip in the row carrying a disclosure. The row
then reads as one value chip, N toggles, then the controls.

**F1-06 - MODERATE - the buttons are anchored to the column edge rather than to the chips, so the row
either collides or divorces** - all 32 view frames, most visibly at 1920 and 1024.

Measured on the List frame at each width, from the last chip's right edge to the filter button's left
edge: **393 = 6px** (and the chip is cut to make even that, F1-01); **1024 = the buttons sit on wrapped
row 1 while row 2 runs alone under ~300px of empty ground**; **1366 = 161px**; **1920 = 443px**. At 1920
the six chips end at x=761 and the pair sits at x=1204-1280, alone against the column's right edge with
443px of empty stone between them and anything they relate to. They stop looking like the end of the row
and start looking like two orphaned header buttons.

At 1024 the failure is different and reads worse: the chips wrap to two rows, the buttons stay anchored
to row 1's right, and the second chip row's right half is empty - a staircase silhouette. A control the
brief places "at the right end of the slicer row" is at the right end of the *first* row.

*Pack:* README Layout - "Content max-width 1500; **left-aligned after that**" (the principle being that
things sit where their content puts them, not stretched to their container); README Do-and-don't, don't
- "**stretch cards to equal heights**", the same instinct applied to a container; reviewer checklist 7 -
"1024 reads as a tablet, not a stretched phone".

*Root cause:* `justifyContent: "space-between"` on the row. It is correct only when the chips exactly
fill the space. Above that width the slack goes into the middle; below it there is no slack left.

*Fix in source:* drop `space-between`. Let the scroller size to its content up to `flex: 1` with the
button group as a fixed sibling immediately after it (`marginLeft: 12`, no auto margin), so the pair
follows the last chip on desktop and is separated from it by a real gutter on the phone. When the chips
wrap, move the button group to the end of the wrap flow rather than anchoring it to row 1 - or set it
below the chips at 1024, right-aligned to the column, which keeps "at the right end" true.

**F1-07 - LOW (unsure) - the working marker is a second meta line, at meta size, in Accent ink** -
`tasks-list-d1-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-prod`, `tasks-gantt-d1-*` and the Board's NEXT lane
(the "Redact the 200 sample emails" row; 20 frames in all).

Answering the question directly first: **at 393 the marker holds.** The dot is 8px and samples
`(74,94,112)` = `#4A5E70` Accent ink in light, `(183,200,216)` = `#B7C8D8` in dark - the correct token
in both. The line's cap height is 8px, the same as the meta above it, and the two baselines are 14px
apart (y326 and y340), which is 10.5 x 1.33, the pack's own meta leading. Nothing wraps, nothing
collides with the chevron, nothing crowds.

What I would still raise: the row now carries **two** lines of identical typographic rank under its
title - "EA - in progress - 41% - $0.40" and "EA working - since 2:14am" - separated only by colour and
a dot. The coloured one wins the eye, so the line that gets read is the state and the line that gets
lost is the **cost**, which is what T-4 was added to show. And a 10.5px line in Accent ink is the one
combination the pack pins shut.

*Pack:* README Accessibility - "**Keep meta text at 10.5 only in Muted on Card or Ground**"; README Type
- "Meta: 10.5 / 1.4, **Muted** (sources, times, why-lines)".

*Unsure because:* README Components, Waiting row sanctions "Expiry short form in **Accent ink**" at row
scale, so there is precedent for accent ink at small size inside a row, and the Accessibility line may
be about contrast rather than about the token. The rank collision is the part I would fix regardless.

*Root cause:* the marker was added as a sibling line at the meta style rather than as a member of the
meta line the row already has. *Fix in source:* fold it in - "EA - working since 2:14am - 41% - $0.40",
with the dot ahead of it - which is the shape ADR-51 chose for Latest-in rows ("to keep the row short
... the routing and the source sit on **one meta line**") and restores one meta line per row across the
list.

**F1-08 - LOW - four control strata now stand above the first pixel of content on the phone** - all 8
phone view frames, worst on `tasks-gantt-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod`.

Measured at 393: title block y20-70, focus chips y86-122 (36px), segmented control y130-172 (42px),
slicer row y180-216 (30/36px). Content begins at **y218 of an 852px viewport - 26%** of the phone given
to chrome before a task. The three control rows have three heights (36 / 42 / 30), three fills
(Accent-soft selected chip / Hairline segment track / Card chip) and, in the third row, two radii side
by side. On the Gantt this is at its worst, because the axis it sits over is a 26px strip carrying three
labels - the controls are taller than the chart's own header, and the chart reads as an afterthought.

This is F-1's cost, honestly counted: the row is 36px plus an 8px gap, and V2.1's Board, Gantt and Done
did not carry it (`demo/v21/tasks-gantt-d1-393-light-prod.png` starts its content at y172). I am **not**
calling the row's presence on all four views a defect - ADR-44 is right that a filter you cannot see is
a filter you forget is on. The defect is that three control rows were allowed to accumulate without
anyone deciding what they look like together.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 7 - "**393 reads as a phone, not a squeezed desktop**"; README Principles 1 -
"One thing at a time"; README Spacing - "Between header blocks: 12" (three blocks at 8 read as one
undifferentiated stack).

*Fix in source:* settle the three rows as one header group - one height (36) for the chips and the
segment cells, `alignItems: "center"` throughout, and 12px between blocks rather than 8, so the reader
sees three deliberate strata instead of a stack. If that is not enough at 393, the segmented control is
the row to reconsider: four view names on a phone is the only one of the three with an alternative
shape.

### Carried - visible in these frames, not caused by F-1

Recorded because they are in front of Josh on the F-1 pass, and because two of them make F-1's own
findings read worse than they are. Each verified against `demo/v21/` at the same file name.

**C-1 - two columns where the pack says three, at 1366 and 1920** - 16 frames. The content region is
correctly capped and left-aligned (measured x=232..1735 at 1920, exactly 1500), but inside it the page
renders rail + List + one stacked column (Waiting on over Gantt). There is no third column, so column 1
runs 1050px wide at 1920 and its list rows carry a ~700px void between title and chevron. Present
identically in `demo/v21/tasks-list-d1-1920-light-prod.png`. *Pack:* README Layout - "1180 and up: rail
+ three columns `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`"; reviewer checklist 7 - "1920 reads as a dashboard".

**C-2 - the segmented control is stretched to the column width** - 16 frames at 1366 and 1920. Four view
names spread across 1050px at 1920 (262px per cell). Correct at 1024 (419px). *Pack:* README Components,
Segmented control specifies it by padding and radius, never by a stretch; README Do-and-don't -
"stretch cards to equal heights" is the same instinct.

**C-3 - the Board's lanes are stretched to equal height and clipped at the strip edge** - `tasks-board-*`
at 393 (both schemes: NEXT's cards cut mid-word - "Redact the 200 sample", "Book the Term 4 holida",
"Passport renewal form", "EA working - since 2:14a" - and NOW's single card above ~500px of empty
stretched lane), at 1366 (DONE cut to "Notion export reconcil" / "report attac") and at 1024 (only NOW
and NEXT are on screen at all; WAITING and DONE are entirely behind the scroller). Correct at 1920,
where four lanes fit. Already on the ledger in this file as **R2-03 / UX-I**, and unchanged. *Pack:*
reviewer checklist 4 - "**Cards are never stretched to equal heights**"; checklist 5 - "No word broken
mid-word".

**C-4 - list rows run the full 1050px column at 1920** - 4 frames. Title at the far left, chevron at the
far right, nothing between. Noted because F-1's 443px button void (F1-06) sits directly above it, and
the two together are what makes the 1920 List read as one stretched phone column.

### The five questions, answered plainly

1. **The 393 clip - acceptable?** No. A partly visible chip is a legitimate scroll affordance; a chip
   with its corner, border and final letter guillotined against a hard edge is not - it reads as a bug,
   and on Done it degrades to a 4px stub. The smallest correct fix is F1-01's three properties on the
   scroller: 20px inner right padding, a right-edge fade mask, a 12px gutter to the buttons.
2. **Does the pair read?** No. Two 36px unfilled hairline squares 6px apart, unlabelled outline glyphs,
   in a row of filled chips - and a third identical `tune` square 58px above them meaning something
   else. Make them different kinds of control (F1-04), not two of the same.
3. **Does "- edit" land?** No - measured identical Muted ink at identical size and weight to its own
   label and to the toggles beside it. Worse, the always-in-force range chip wears the styling that
   means "off" everywhere else in that row. It needs a variant, not a suffix (F1-05).
4. **Density on Board, Gantt and Done with the new row?** Survivable, but only just, and the Gantt at
   393 is the weak one: 26% of the viewport is chrome before content, in three strata of three different
   heights and fills. The row's presence is right; its accumulation with the two rows above it was never
   designed (F1-08). And the Gantt's real problem is not density - it is F1-03, a chip asserting a
   90-day window over a 29-day axis.
5. **Does the working marker hold at 393?** Yes, metrically - 8px dot at the correct Accent-ink token in
   both schemes, meta cap height, 14px baseline separation, no wrap, no crowding. My reservation is
   rank, not space: it is a second meta line of equal size to the first, the coloured one wins, and the
   cost line T-4 added is the one that loses (F1-07).

### Frames that are fine, said plainly

- All eight `task-detail-d1-*` frames are clean at every width and in both schemes. The dialog is
  centred and complete, the priority segment, the date pair, the tag row, the three subtask rows with
  their EA marks and dashed checkbox, the composer, the two verbs and the Activity card all render
  without clipping, wrapping or orphaning; the demo watermark sits clear of the dialog and is legible
  over the scrim. F-1 does not reach this surface and it shows.
- Ground is exact and edge to edge on all 40 frames - `#EDEBE5` light, `#191815` dark, including behind
  the phone safe area and under the tab bar. No black, no white, no v1.2 green anywhere in the pass.
- Light and dark are the same layout on all 20 pairs: identical document heights, no reflow, no column
  count change, nothing appearing or disappearing.
- The slicer row is genuinely present on **all four views at all four widths in both schemes**, with the
  same six items and the correct default range label - "Next 90 days" on List, Board and Gantt, "All
  time" on Done. TF-01 and TF-05 hold on the pixels. No `Clear` and no count badge appear, which is
  correct for a state with no slicer, no filter and a default range (TF-07).
- The working marker's tokens are right in both schemes, and the per-row usage line ("EA - in progress -
  41% - $0.40") renders at Muted meta without clipping at any width.

### Coverage

40 of 40 frames read. Programmatic: all 40 present against the brief's matrix (5 screens x 4 widths x 2
schemes), every frame's pixel width equal to the width in its name; an edge-energy floor found no blank
frame and none stuck on the gate (the lowest is `task-detail-d1-1920-light-prod` at 0.436, correctly - a
dimmed-scrim overlay); **20 light/dark pairs matched exactly on document height, 0 mismatches**, so no
reflow; corner and mid-field ground samples on all 40; chip-versus-button vertical extent probed on all
32 view frames (30px / 36px, top-aligned, without exception); horizontal run scans for the chip and
button edges at every width; the range chip's ink sampled against its own label and its neighbours; the
working marker's dot and line sampled in both schemes. By eye: 16 frames read full-size, 10 more as
2-6x crops and 12 through contact sheets, covering all five screens at every width in both schemes,
plus three `demo/v21/` frames read only to separate introduced from carried.

**Reviewed:** 8 September 2026.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

#### The five points, judged

##### F1-01 - the chip scroller - **STILL WRONG**

The row moved; the cut did not. On all eight phone frames the scroller's right edge is at **x=328/329**
(round 1: x=288/289) and the cut has the same three properties it had then:

- **Full opacity to the edge, no fade, no mask.** Sampled along y=197 on `tasks-list-d1-393-light-prod`,
  the last chip's fill holds `247,247,244` unbroken from x=314 to x=328 and the ground `237,235,229`
  resumes at x=329. The delta from ground is a flat 37-40 across those fifteen pixels, then 0. The same
  constant-then-cliff profile on all eight frames (dark delta 54-60).
- **No radius, no border on the cut side.** At y=186 and y=208 - the rows where a radius-8 corner would
  be curving in - the fill still runs the full width to x=328. The chip is a rectangle with three
  rounded corners and one amputation.
- **A glyph cut mid-stroke.** On List, Board and Gantt what survives is a 15px stub of chip fill holding
  a single 1px vertical stroke at x=327 (`148,145,138`) - the left stem of the "D" of "Delegated" and
  nothing else. On Done the range chip is shorter, so the cut lands further into the word and the chip
  reads **"Deleg"** against a flat vertical edge, 8px from the filter button's hairline.

The two-line move gave the scroller 40 more pixels and raised the scroller-to-button gap from 6px to
8px. Both are improvements to the row's shape. Neither is the defect. The gutter that was added sits
**outside** the clip box, between the scroller and the button; the clip is still taken on the scroller's
own bounds, so nothing about a chip's relationship to its own right edge has changed. Six chips do not
fit on 393 at any width the scroller has been given - which is exactly what the brief concluded - but
the conclusion drawn was "give the row a second line", and the second line was spent on the link rather
than on the chips.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 5 - "No word broken mid-word. **No clipped or ellipsised label inside a
button, chip or segment.**"

*Fix in source:* unchanged from round 1, and it is three properties on the scroller's own container, not
on the row - `paddingRight: 20` **inside** the clip box, `maskImage: linear-gradient(to right, #000
calc(100% - 20px), transparent)` with its `-webkit-` twin, and leave the 8px gutter as it is. The
two-line row does not remove the need for these; it moved where they have to go.

##### F1-02 - the 6px hang - **RIGHT**

Measured on all 32 view frames, without exception:

| Width | Chips | Icon button | Shared centre |
|---|---|---|---|
| 393 | y183-212 (30px) | y180-215 (36px) | **197.5 / 197.5** |
| 1366, 1920 | y157-186 (30px) | y154-189 (36px) | **171.5 / 171.5** |
| 1024 | block y154-219 (two rows) | y169-204 (36px) | **186.5 / 186.5** |

The ragged bottom edge is gone at every width and in both schemes. The "Slicers" link's ink sits at
y167-174 at 1366/1920 (optical centre 170.5, within 1px of the row's 171.5) and at y235-243 on the
phone's second line. The 30-vs-36 height difference is still there in the tokens, but it is now
symmetric about a shared centre line and the eye no longer reads it as a misfit. This was the largest
single contributor to round 1's "pile" read and it is fixed. **No caveat at 393, 1366 or 1920.** The
1024 caveat is F2-02 and it is a consequence of the wrap, not of the centring rule.

##### F1-03 - the Gantt window - **RIGHT in substance**

The axis now draws what the chip claims, at all four widths and in both schemes: the caption pair reads
**"8 Sep"** left and **"7 Dec"** right. Day 1 is 8 September; 8 Sep to 7 Dec is 90 days from the start.
The chip says "Next 90 days · edit" and the chart draws the next 90 days. Round 1's F1-03 - a control
asserting a window the view did not consume - is closed.

The "today" caption is correctly absent from all eight frames. The 6% drop rule works.

What it brought with it is F2-01, below.

##### Q2 - the slicer editor as a text link - **RIGHT in kind, wrong in three details**

Right: there is now exactly one icon button in the slicer row, it is the `tune` that will carry the
count badge, and the second control is a different kind of thing. The two no longer read as one two-part
control. That was the substance of F1-04's first half and it is fixed.

The three details that are not right are F2-03 (the phone pays 45px for it), F1-04's remainder (the
button is still unfilled and there is still a second `tune` on the same screen), and F2-04 (the link is
a noun). Each is written up below.

##### Q3 - the range chip always `selected` - **RIGHT**

Measured, light, `tasks-list-d1-393-light-prod` and `tasks-list-d1-1366-light-prod`:

- Range chip fill `217,218,215`. Accent soft `rgba(102,121,138,.14)` composited over ground `#EDEBE5`
  computes to `218,219,216`. Within one unit on every channel.
- Range chip label and its "edit" suffix both peak at exactly `74,94,112` = **`#4A5E70` Accent ink**.
- Its neighbours: fill `247,247,244` (Card), label peaks `132,130,121` (Muted `#7A776F`,
  under-saturated at 12px).

Dark, same frames: range chip fill `45,48,48` against a computed `46,48,48` for
`rgba(154,174,192,.16)` over `#191815`; label peaks exactly `183,200,216` = **`#B7C8D8` Accent ink**.

Both tokens are the pack's "Selected: Accent soft fill, Accent ink text" verbatim, in both schemes, on
all 32 view frames. The chip that is always in force no longer wears the styling that means "off", and
it is now the only chip in the row wearing it, so the row reads as one value chip followed by toggles.
I could not verify the 500 weight from the pixels - an ink-density comparison is confounded by the
colour difference - and I am not calling that either way; the fill and the ink are what carried the
"dressed as an off toggle" read and both are correct now.

#### Defects, ranked

**F2-01 - MAJOR - NEW - the now-rule is drawn through the "8" of the start caption** -
`tasks-gantt-d1-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-prod` (8 frames). **This answers Josh's question 2:
no, it is not acceptable, and it is not only a 393 problem.**

The now-rule is a 16px vertical tick living entirely inside the caption strip - measured at
x=201 / y279-294 (393), x=447 / y241-256 (1024), x=505 / y211-226 (1366), x=602 / y211-226 (1920). It
does not descend into the chart at all. The bar track begins at x approximately 500 at 1366, so the rule
sits at roughly 1% of the window: correct arithmetic, and exactly the collision the brief predicted.

What it does to the caption is worse than "passes through it":

- At **393** the rule removes the left half of the numeral. Read at 8x, the caption is not "8 Sep" with
  a line over it - it is a vertical bar followed by the right bowl of an 8, which reads as "3 Sep" or a
  Greek beta. The one date the chart states at its origin is misread.
- At **1366 and 1920** the rule runs vertically through the middle of the 8 and extends above its cap
  height and below its baseline, so the numeral reads as struck out - the typographic gesture for
  "cancelled", on the date the window starts.
- Identical in dark at every width; the rule is Accent ink in both schemes, which is the correct token
  and is precisely why it is opaque enough to destroy the glyph.

The caption got the 6% clamp. The rule did not, and the rule is the element that is drawn *over* text.
The clamp was applied to the wrong half of the collision.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 5 - "**No word broken mid-word.** No clipped or ellipsised label inside a
button, chip or segment." Also README Principles 7 - "**Show the work.** Every card states the source,
the expiry and what happens on silence" - a chart whose start date cannot be read does not state it. And
README Surfaces - "Blur is for frosted surfaces only. **Never blur text or images**" is the neighbouring
instinct: nothing is painted over type.

*Fix in source, in order of preference:*

1. **Drop the rule inside the same 6% band the caption is dropped in.** At the `next` preset the rule
   marks the window origin, and the origin already has a caption naming that exact date; the rule
   carries no information there and destroys the caption that does. One condition, symmetric with the
   one already written for the caption, and it is the smallest change.
2. If the rule must always be drawn, give the **caption** the offset instead: when `|now% - 0| < 6`,
   start the start-caption at `ruleX + 6` rather than at the track origin. The rule then sits clear to
   the left of the "8" and both are legible.
3. Do **not** solve it by making the rule translucent or thinner. At 393 a 1px Accent-ink stroke through
   an 8 is already the minimum weight and it still ruins the glyph.

**F1-01 - MAJOR - STILL OPEN - the chip scroller is guillotined, not faded** - 8 phone frames.
Full write-up above. Unchanged in kind from round 1; ranked first among the carried-forward items
because it is the one Josh named and the one a person meets on the phone before anything else.

**F2-03 - MODERATE - NEW - the phone's second line costs 45px of viewport to deliver one 33px word** -
all 8 phone view frames. **This answers Josh's question 1: no, a whole line of chrome for one link is
not worth it.**

Measured down `tasks-list-d1-393-light-prod`:

```
y180-215   slicer row 1 (scroller + tune button)
y216-234   19px of ground, nothing
y235-243   "Slicers" - 9px of ink, right-aligned to the page edge, 33px wide
y244-260   17px of ground, nothing
y261       the first pixel of the first card
```

Forty-five vertical pixels, of which nine carry ink, for one word that is the **least** frequently
needed control in the row - it edits the chip set, which is a setup action, not a daily one. The line
has no left-hand anchor, no label, and no visual relationship to the scroller it belongs to; it is a
single word floating at the right margin under a row it is not touching. Round 1's checklist-5 concern
about single-word orphan lines was written about titles, but this is the same shape and the same read.

And it lands on the screen that was already the round's density complaint. Content top has moved from
**y218 to y261** - see F1-08r.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 7 - "**393 reads as a phone, not a squeezed desktop**"; README Principles 1 -
"**One thing at a time.** The first decision is open; the rest wait as single rows"; README Layout -
"Leave the bottom of a column empty when the content ends" (the converse of which is that a line is
earned by its content, and 9px of ink does not earn 45px).

*Fix in source - where the link should live instead, in order of preference:*

1. **Inside the filter panel the `tune` button already opens.** Editing the slicer set and applying
   slicers are the same subject; the panel is the natural home for "Slicers" as its footer action. The
   phone then keeps a one-line slicer row, the second line disappears entirely, and 45px comes back.
2. **On the range chip's own pattern.** If the chip set is to be editable from the row, it belongs at
   the row's *start*, beside the value chip that already says "· edit", not alone at the far right of a
   line of its own.
3. If the second line survives at all, it must not be spent on one word - give the **chips** the second
   line (three chips per line, no scroller, no clip) and put the link back inline with the button. That
   single reallocation closes F1-01 and F2-03 together and costs the same 45px the current line already
   spends.

**F1-06 - MODERATE - UNCHANGED - the right-hand controls are anchored to the column edge rather than to
the chips** - all 16 frames at 1366 and 1920, and in a different form at 1024 (F2-02).

Measured from the last chip's right edge to the "Slicers" link's left edge on the List frame:

| Width | Last chip ends | "Slicers" | `tune` button | Void |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1366 | x=759 | x=923-954 | x=963-998 | **164px** |
| 1920 | x=759 | x=1205-1236 | x=1245-1280 | **446px** |

Round 1 measured 161px and 443px. The text link is three pixels narrower than the icon button it
replaced; that is the entire difference. At 1920 the six chips end at x=759 and the two controls sit
against the column's right edge at x=1205, alone, with 446px of empty stone between them and anything
they relate to. They still read as two orphaned header buttons rather than as the end of the slicer row -
and the "Slicers" link, being lighter than the icon button it replaced, floats more, not less.

*Pack:* README Layout - "Content max-width 1500; **left-aligned after that**"; README Do-and-don't,
don't - "**stretch cards to equal heights**"; reviewer checklist 7 - "1920 reads as a dashboard, not
three phone columns".

*Fix in source:* unchanged from round 1 - drop `justifyContent: "space-between"` on the row; let the
scroller size to its content and place the control group as a fixed sibling immediately after it with
`marginLeft: 12` and no auto margin, so the pair follows the last chip.

**F2-02 - MODERATE - NEW - at 1024 the control pair is centred on a two-row chip block and therefore
aligned to nothing** - all 8 frames at 1024.

The centring fix from F1-02 is applied to the whole row, so at 1024, where six chips wrap to two rows,
the button and the link are centred on the **block**: chip row 1 y154-183, chip row 2 y190-219, control
group y169-204, block centre and control centre both 186.5. The result is a `tune` button and a
"Slicers" link hanging in the gutter *between* the two chip rows, sharing a baseline with neither.
Row 2's last chip ends at x=466 and the column's right edge is x=650, so 184px of row 2 is empty
underneath them.

This is a lateral move, not a regression I can prove - round 1's version was top-aligned to row 1, which
at least read as "the end of row 1"; this version reads as a pair floating in the middle of a block. I
am recording it as **traded, not fixed**: round 1's complaint at 1024 ("a staircase silhouette";
"a control the brief places at the right end of the slicer row is at the right end of the *first* row")
is unresolved and has changed shape.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 7 - "**1024 reads as a tablet, not a stretched phone**"; README Spacing -
"Between chips or verbs: 6" (the row's internal rhythm is 6px; a control sitting 6px below one row and
6px above another belongs to neither).

*Fix in source:* when the chips wrap, move the control group to the **end of the wrap flow** so it
follows the last chip on row 2, or drop it to its own right-aligned line below the chips. Either keeps
"at the right end of the slicer row" true. What it must not do is centre on the block.

**F1-08r - MODERATE - REGRESSED - the phone now gives 31% of the viewport to chrome before a task** -
all 8 phone view frames.

Content top, measured at the first card's top edge: **y261** on List and Gantt, **y264** on Board and
Done, against round 1's y218 and V2.1's y172. On an 852px viewport that is **31%** of the phone spent on
control strata before the first task, up from 26% last round. The strata are now: title block, focus
chips (36px), segmented control (42px), slicer row 1 (36px), slicer row 2 (45px including its
whitespace). Five bands, four heights, three fills.

This is the direct cost of F2-03 and it closes with it. I record it separately because it is the number
Josh will feel rather than the reason for it.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 7 - "393 reads as a phone, not a squeezed desktop"; README Spacing -
"Between header blocks: 12".

**F1-04 - LOW/MODERATE - PARTLY FIXED - the icon button carries no fill, and there are still two `tune`
glyphs on one screen** - all 32 view frames.

Fixed: the pair is gone, the two controls are different kinds, and only one of them is an icon.

Not fixed, and both were named in round 1:

- **No fill.** Sampled inside the `tune` button at every width and in both schemes, the interior is
  *exactly* the ground - `237,235,229` light, `25,24,21` dark - at 393, 1024, 1366 and 1920. It is a
  hairline outline with the ground showing through, sitting in a row of Card-filled chips.
  *Pack:* README Components, Buttons - "Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: 32 or 36 square, radius 8 or 10,
  **Card fill with Card border** (header) or Hairline border (in cards)". This one is on the ground, so
  it is the header case, and it has no fill.
- **The duplicate glyph.** The focus chip row 58px above still ends in an identical 36px `tune` button
  (measured x=536-566, y=66-101 at 1024/1366/1920; the same on the phone). So every Tasks frame still
  shows the same icon twice, in two adjacent rows, meaning filter-the-tasks and edit-the-focuses. Round
  1's fix note said "change the focus row's trailing glyph so only one `tune` exists on any screen";
  that half was not done.

*Pack, second half:* README Icons, fixed set - "Filter `tune`" (one meaning per glyph is the point of a
fixed set).

*Fix in source:* give the slicer `tune` the Card fill its own component spec calls for, and give the
focus row's editor a different glyph from the fixed set (`more_horiz` is the pack's "More" and is
already sanctioned) so one `tune` means one thing.

**F2-04 - LOW - NEW - "Slicers" is a noun, and the row now carries three different edit affordances** -
all 32 view frames. **Unsure about the severity, certain about the observation.**

The link reads **"Slicers"**. It is a noun with no verb, so it does not say what tapping it does - show
them? edit them? clear them? - and it sits in a row where the range chip's own affordance is the word
"edit" and the icon beside it is the filter. Three edit-ish mechanisms in one row, expressed three ways:
a suffix inside a chip, a bare noun as a link, and a glyph.

The token is right: the link peaks at `96,113,128` light and `171,187,202` dark. Both are Accent ink
(`#4A5E70` / `#B7C8D8`) under-saturated by the same ~13% at 11px - it cannot be plain Accent, which is
*lighter* than the measured value in light and *darker* than it in dark. So the colour is correct; the
word is the question.

*Pack:* README Content - "**Voice: a capable assistant speaking to one person.** Short sentences. Plain
words. Present tense. **Say what happened and what happens next**"; README Components - "Text link:
Accent ink, no underline, cursor pointer".

*Unsure because:* "Slicers" is the row's own name in ADR-44, and a person who has met the row once may
read the noun as a destination, the way "Settings" does. But "Settings" is a place and a slicer set is a
thing you edit, and the chip 300px to its left already teaches the word "edit" for exactly this gesture.

*Fix in source:* make it the verb the chip already uses - "Edit slicers", or simply "edit" if it moves
beside the range chip per F2-03's fix - so one word means one gesture across the row.

**F1-07 - LOW - CARRIED BY DECISION - the working marker is a second meta line of equal rank** -
20 frames. Josh has explicitly not changed this and it is recorded as carried, not fixed. Re-verified on
these pixels: the row still shows "EA · in progress · 41% · $0.40" over "● EA working · since 2:14am",
two lines of identical typographic rank under one title, the Accent-ink one winning the eye and the cost
line T-4 exists to show losing it. Metrics and tokens remain correct. No change to round 1's finding or
its proposed fix.

#### Carried - unchanged, verified again on these pixels

- **C-1 - two columns where the pack says three, at 1366 and 1920** - 16 frames. Rail + one content
  column + one stacked column (Waiting on over Gantt). *Pack:* README Layout - "1180 and up: rail +
  three columns `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`".
- **C-1b - at 1024 the third section stacks under column 2, not column 1** - 8 frames. The pack is
  explicit: "At two columns, **column 3 sits directly under column 1** and column 2 spans both rows".
  Here Gantt sits under Waiting on. There is no empty row, so the stricter half of the rule is honoured.
  New to this round's notes only because I probed 1024's stacking this time; it is present in
  `demo/v21/` at the same file names and is not F-1's. **Unsure** whether it is worth changing while
  C-1 is open - with only two columns rendered, stacking the third under the very tall column 1 would
  read worse.
- **C-2 - the segmented control stretched to the column width** - 16 frames at 1366/1920. Four view
  names across roughly 768px at 1366 and 1050px at 1920.
- **C-3 - the Board's lanes stretched to equal height and clipped at the strip edge** - `tasks-board-*`
  at 393 (NEXT's cards cut mid-word: "Redact the 200 sample", "Book the Term 4 holida", "Passport
  renewal form", "Recruitment risk memo,", "Task from Joce: swim c"; NOW's single card above roughly
  500px of stretched empty lane), at 1024, and at 1366 (DONE cut to "Notion export reconcil" / "report
  attac"). Correct at 1920. On the ledger as R2-03 / UX-I.
- **C-4 - list and done rows run the full ~1050px column at 1920** - title far left, chevron far right,
  nothing between.

#### What is right, said plainly

- The Gantt window is real. "Next 90 days" draws 8 Sep to 7 Dec at all four widths, in both schemes, and
  the "today" caption is correctly dropped at the edge. The chip no longer lies.
- The slicer row has one bottom edge at every width. Chips and the icon button share a centre line to
  the pixel on all 32 view frames.
- The range chip is the pack's `selected` chip exactly - Accent soft fill and Accent ink label, measured
  to within one RGB unit of the composited token in both schemes - and it is the only chip in the row
  wearing it.
- One `tune` in the slicer row, and the editor is a different kind of control. The "two halves of one
  widget" read is gone.
- All eight `task-detail-d1-*` frames are clean at every width and in both schemes - dialog centred and
  complete; priority segment, date pair, tag row, three subtask rows with their EA marks and dashed
  checkbox, composer, two verbs and the Activity card all render without clipping, wrapping or
  orphaning; the watermark is legible over the scrim and clear of the dialog.
- Ground exact and edge to edge on all 40 - `#EDEBE5` light, `#191815` dark, including behind the phone
  safe area and under the tab bar. No black, no white, no v1.2 green.
- **20 light/dark pairs, 0 document-height mismatches.** No reflow, no column-count change, nothing
  appearing or disappearing between schemes.
- The watermark sits clear of the rail health line on every desktop frame and clear of the tab bar and
  the mic orb on every phone frame.
- No `Clear` and no count badge, correct for a state with no slicer and a default range (TF-07).

#### Coverage

40 of 40 read. Programmatic: presence and pixel-width check on all 40; an edge-energy floor found no
blank frame and none on the gate; 20 light/dark pairs matched on document height, 0 mismatches; chip and
icon-button vertical extents probed on all 32 view frames in both schemes; horizontal run scans of the
slicer row at every width; the scroller clip-edge profile sampled pixel by pixel on all 8 phone frames
in both schemes; the range chip's fill and label sampled against computed token composites in both
schemes; the `tune` button interior sampled against ground at all four widths in both schemes; the
"Slicers" link's ink peak sampled in both schemes; the Gantt now-rule located by column scan and its
extent measured on all 8 Gantt frames; the Gantt bar track measured at all four widths; phone content
top measured on all 8 phone view frames. By eye: 8 frames read full-size, 9 more as 4-8x crops,
covering all five screens at every width in both schemes.

**Reviewed:** 8 September 2026.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

## V2.2 B-1 (Board)

**Date:** 8 September 2026
**Reviewer:** ux-reviewer (product eyes)
**Row:** B-1 ★ — the board is Twenty's board (BD-01..BD-06). Five `col-*` lanes from
`GET /tasks/columns`, horizontal strip, agent/person card markers, `more_horiz` per card,
Done dimmed, two text links under the strip.
**Scope:** the 40 PNGs in `demo/v22/` — `tasks-{list,board,gantt,done}` and `task-detail`,
day 1, production build, {393, 1024, 1366, 1920} × {light, dark}. All 40 present, every frame's
pixel width equal to the width in its name, none blank, none the wrong screen, none on the gate.
**Comparison:** `demo/v21/tasks-board-d1-*-prod` at the same widths, read **only** to separate
what B-1 introduced from what it inherited. **No source file was read for a verdict and no source
file was edited.**
**Method:** contiguous-run scans against each frame's own ground token, vertical and horizontal
extent probes on named coordinates, exact RGB samples, WCAG contrast computed from the sampled
pairs, and full-size / 4–12× reads by eye. Every number below is a pixel read of these frames.

### Verdict

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

**8 defects introduced by B-1** (B1-01 .. B1-08), **1 open defect that B-1 did not introduce but
that no round has yet raised** (B1-09), and **8 carried** (C-1 .. C-8). The eight `task-detail`
frames are clean; B-1 does not reach the dialog.

**R3-04 has not regressed.** The lane headings are the section-label style exactly: measured
`(78,98,115)` on all five lanes at 1920 light — identical to the `GANTT` label on the same frame
and to Accent ink `#4A5E70` within antialiasing — 9px cap height (the same as `WAITING ON`,
measured y123–131 against the lanes' y204–212), uppercase, tracked, weight 400. Dark reads
`(180,196,212)` against `#B7C8D8`. This is right at every width and in both schemes.

**The short answer to the row.** Twenty's five lanes are the correct data and the strip mechanics
are correct — 200px flat minimum below 1180, `(strip − gaps) / 5` at 1920, a 5px scrollbar in the
pack's own thumb token, five lanes and five counts that agree with the page header. What went
wrong is arithmetic nobody did: a fifth lane took the lane from **256px (V2.1) to 203px**, and B-1
then spent **18–23px on an owner marker and 36px on an overflow button** inside it. The card title
is left **106px at 1920** — narrower than it was on a V2.1 phone. Six of the thirteen card titles
now break onto a single-word orphan line and one breaks onto two. The board did not get denser; it
got narrower, and the titles paid.
