### Defects, ranked by what they cost a person using the board

**B1-01 — MAJOR — the card title column is 106px at every width, and six of thirteen titles now
break onto a single-word orphan line** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames.

Measured on `tasks-board-d1-1920-light-prod`, NEXT lane, card 1: card 444–644 (200px), content box
454–634 (180px), initial circle x459–476 (18px), title x484–590, `more_horiz` button x595–630
(36px square). The title gets **106px of 180 — 59%** — and it gets the same 106px at 1366, 1024 and
393, because the lane is a flat 200px below 1180 and 203px at 1920.

The wraps that follow, read on the 1920 frame, where a desktop has 1920 pixels available:

- "Waiting-on / **digest**"
- "Passport renewal / **forms**"
- "Recruitment risk / **memo,** / **Bundaberg**" — two orphan lines on one title
- "Bali deposit to / **Steve**"
- "Task from Joce: / swim carnival / **forms**"
- "Notion export / **reconciled**"

This is B-1's, and `demo/v21/tasks-board-d1-1920-light-prod.png` proves it: there the lanes measure
**256px** (232–487, 500–747, 762–1015, 1025–1280), there is no marker and no overflow button, and
every one of those six titles renders on **one line** — "Recruitment risk memo, Bundaberg",
"Task from Joce: swim carnival forms", "Book the Term 4 holiday flights". B-1 added a fifth lane
(256 → 203) and then spent 60 of the remaining 203 on two ornaments.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 5 — "No word broken mid-word. No clipped or ellipsised label inside a
button, chip or segment. **No single-word orphan line in a title.**" Also README Principles 4 —
"Small type, clear hierarchy" — a title taking three lines to say five words is not a hierarchy.

*Fix in source:* the lane width is right; the budget inside it is not. Take the 36px overflow out
of the title's flow — anchor it to the card's top-right corner as an overlay (the card already has
9 × 10 padding to sit in), which returns 42px to the title — and drop the initial when the card's
owner is the viewer, which returns another 26px on ten of the thirteen cards (see B1-03). That
takes the title from 106px to ~174px and every one of the six wraps above resolves. Do **not**
solve it by truncating titles: a board where you cannot read the task is not a board.

**B1-02 — MAJOR — the `more_horiz` control is invisible at rest: three 2px dots at 2.05:1** —
all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames, on every card.

Read at 12×, the glyph inside each 36px hairline box is three separate **2px × 2px** squares. Peak
ink sampled `(172,170,165)` light on card fill `(241,240,238)` — **contrast 2.05:1**. Dark:
`(109,107,102)` on `(59,58,55)`. The button interior is the card fill exactly, so what is on screen
is an empty rounded rectangle with a faint smudge in the middle.

This is not a token question — it is a rendering-scale one, and the same frame proves it: the
header's `grid_view` glyph reaches `(122,119,111)`, which is Muted `#7A776F` **exactly**; the
slicer and focus `tune` glyphs reach `(145,142,134)`; the card `more_horiz` reaches 172. A weight-300
`more_horiz` at 18px puts three round dots on a 2px grid and antialiasing eats them.

It matters more here than anywhere else in the app: per B-1's own note, "a card moves by drag or by
menu", and this is the menu. The one non-drag path to moving a task — the path a keyboard, a screen
reader or a shaky hand needs — is the least visible mark on the card.

*Pack:* README Accessibility — "Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, **Muted on Card 4.6:1**";
README Components, Buttons — "Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: 32 or 36 square, radius 8 or 10, Card fill
with Card border (header) or Hairline border (in cards), **Muted glyph 17 or 18**"; README Icons —
"Material Symbols Rounded, **weight 300**".

*Fix in source:* the pack's 18px is a size, not a contrast budget. Render `more_horiz` in-card at
weight 400 (or 20px), or set it in Ink rather than Muted, until a sample of a dot reaches 4.5:1
against Card in both schemes. Verify by sampling, not by looking at a 4K monitor.

**B1-03 — MODERATE — the person marker says "J" on all ten person cards, and the two markers share
neither a width nor a vertical alignment** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames.

Two separate faults in one 26px slot.

*It distinguishes nothing.* Every non-agent card on this board carries an identical faint "J" —
"Send Moz the sample pack" (JSTACK), "Book the Term 4 holiday flights" (**from Joce**), "Book
dentist" (**you**), "Villa contract from Steve", and six more. Ten cards, one letter. Whatever the
initial is keyed to, on this fixture it resolves to the same glyph every time, so the only
information the marker carries is the one bit the EA tag already carries: agent or not. It costs
26px of every card's title width (B1-01) to say nothing. It is also barely there: the "J" peaks at
`(139,136,129)` on card `(241,240,238)` — **3.11:1** light, 3.07:1 dark — beside an EA tag that is a
filled Accent-soft pill with legible ink.

*The two markers do not line up.* Measured at 1920, NEXT lane, adjacent cards:

| | marker x | marker y | marker centre | title y | title centre | title starts at x |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| card 1 (person) | 459–476 (18px) | 241–258 | 249.5 | 237–264 | 250.5 | 484 |
| card 2 (agent) | 459–481 (23px) | 309–323 | 316.0 | 315–341 | **328.0** | **488** |

The circle is centred on its title block; the tag sits **12px high**. And because the tag is 5px
wider, the two titles start at two different x positions in the same lane. Scrolling a lane, the
titles walk left and right and the markers bob up and down. This is precisely the "some centred,
some left-aligned" read that started this whole review.

*Pack:* README Components, Waiting row — "Type label at **48px fixed width so titles align**" (the
pack's own rule for exactly this: a leading marker in a column of rows gets one fixed width);
README Do and don't, Do — "**fixed 48px label column in rows**"; README Accessibility — "Muted on
Card 4.6:1".

*Fix in source:* one marker slot, one fixed width, one alignment — centre both variants on the
title block, and give the slot a single width so titles align down the lane. Then decide what the
initial is for: if it is the assignee and the assignee is nearly always the owner, show it only
when it is **not** the owner, which frees the slot on ten of thirteen cards and makes the three that
carry it mean something.

**B1-04 — MODERATE — the card meta wraps with the middle dot stranded at the end of a line and the
money alone on the next** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames, at every width.

On the agent card: "EA · recurring · every Mon 8am **·**" / "**$0.05**". On the Done card:
"EA · 1,387 rows · report attached **·**" / "**$0.03**". The separator ends line 1 with nothing
after it and the value it was separating sits alone on line 2.

Also B-1's, and `demo/v21` proves it the same way: in a 256px lane those metas render on one line.
The 203px lane made them wrap, and nothing binds the runs.

The repo already solved this exact shape. `BUGLOG_v21.md` R-34 (V2.1 round 3, defect R3-04):
"the run computation is a pure `richRuns` that binds ' · ' to both neighbours and the word before an
emphasised run to it with non-breaking spaces". That binding is not reaching the board card's meta.

*Pack:* README Content — "Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`" (the dot
sits **between** two things on one line); reviewer checklist 5 — "No single-word orphan line".

*Fix in source:* run the board card's meta through the same `richRuns` binding the list rows use,
so a separator can never end a line and the trailing value keeps at least one word with it.

**B1-05 — MODERATE — at 1024 the board is two lanes of five and nothing bleeds past the strip edge
to say there are three more** — `tasks-board-d1-1024-{light,dark}-prod`, and in a milder form at 393.

Measured at 1024: NOW 232–431 and NEXT 440–639, both **complete**; the strip clips at 640; **In
progress, Waiting and Done are entirely off-stage.** Because the second lane ends exactly at the
clip, there is no partial card, no half-lane, no bleed — nothing on screen except a 5px scrollbar
thumb (232–401 of a 232–640 track, 42%) says the board has more than two columns. A person on an
iPad sees a board with a Now and a Next and no way to know that the task the EA is running right
now, the two things blocked on other people, and everything finished are all one horizontal swipe
away.

At 393 the same arithmetic gives 1.8 lanes of 5 (NOW 20–219 complete, NEXT 228–393, 83% of it
visible), and there at least the second lane bleeds off the edge, which reads as "more this way".
At 1366, 3.7 of 5 (WAITING cut at x=998, 143px of 200 showing, its cards' overflow buttons off
screen with it, DONE hidden). At 1920 all five fit (203px each, no scrollbar — correct).

Honest attribution: `demo/v21` at 1024 showed **2 of 4** lanes with a 209px thumb, so the shape is
carried. What B-1 changed is the ratio (2 of 5) and, more to the point, **which** lane went dark:
V2.1's hidden pair was Waiting and Done; V2.2's hidden trio is led by **In progress**, the lane the
row was built to create and the only one carrying T-5's working marker.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 7 — "**1024 reads as a tablet, not a stretched phone**"; README
Principles 7 — "**Show the work**"; README Principles 2 — "Say when the list ends" (the converse:
say when it has not).

*Fix in source:* at 1024 the board is the wrong shape for a 419px content column. Either let the
board view use the full content width under 1180 (it is a view, not a section — checklist 1's "no
single section laid across columns" is not in the way), or drop the lane minimum under 1180 so
three lanes fit, or stack the lanes as collapsible sections on the phone. Whichever, put a
persistent affordance on the strip — a right-edge fade and a "2 more" marker on the last visible
lane heading — because a 5px scrollbar is not a statement.

**B1-06 — LOW — the two links under the strip read as one line of text** — all 8 `tasks-board-*`
frames.

Measured at 1920: "Columns · edit in Twenty" x232–347, "Refresh" x360–396 — a **13px** gap. Same
ink (both Accent ink), same size (11px ink height), same baseline, no separator, no rule, no
change of weight. The line reads "Columns · edit in Twenty Refresh". The internal middle dot in the
first label is consistent with the range chip's "Next 90 days · edit" and I am **not** calling that
wrong; the fault is that the *second* control sits closer to the first than the first's own two
halves read apart, so a person parses one label, not two controls.

I cannot verify the stated 36px minimum height from a still — the visible ink is 11px tall and
nothing draws the box. If the hit boxes are 36px, that is its own problem: two 36px targets 13px
apart with no visible boundary. A mis-tap on "Refresh" costs nothing; a mis-tap on "edit in Twenty"
leaves the app.

*Pack:* README Components — "Text link: Accent ink, no underline, cursor pointer"; README Spacing —
"Between chips or verbs: 6. **Between header blocks: 12**" (13px is a within-a-block value, and
these are two blocks); README Content — "Voice: a capable assistant speaking to one person.
Short sentences."

*Fix in source:* raise the gap to at least 24, or separate the two with the pack's own middle dot
used the way the pack uses it. "Refresh" is also a bare verb sitting beside a label that already
ends in "in Twenty"; if the two must share a line, make the second read "Refresh from Twenty" so
the line says what each half touches.

**B1-07 — LOW — at 393 the strip clips the second lane mid-word with a flat, unmasked edge** —
`tasks-board-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod`.

The NEXT lane is cut at x=393. Read at 5×, what survives is "from Joce · Fri 11 Sep · **Famil**"
and "EA · recurring · every Mon **8**", and on the agent card the **dashed Accent-ink border is
amputated** on its right side, so the card reads as an open-ended dashed box rather than an
outlined one. There is no fade and no mask: the card fill runs at full value to the last column and
the frame ends.

I am ranking this **low deliberately**, and saying why: unlike F1-01's chip, a partly visible card
in a horizontal scroller is a legitimate affordance, and the scrollbar here is present and correct
(5px, thumb `(202,200,194)` = `rgba(122,119,111,.3)` over ground exactly, 121px of a 353px track).
The complaint is only that the cut is a hard edge. The remedy round 2 prescribed for the slicer
scroller — a right-edge fade mask inside the clip box — would fix this for free and is already
written down.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 5 — "**No word broken mid-word.**"

*Fix in source:* `maskImage: linear-gradient(to right, #000 calc(100% − 24px), transparent)` with
its `-webkit-` twin on the strip's clip box, under 1180 only.

**B1-08 — LOW, and I am unsure — the lane counts do not match the counts this row was briefed to
produce** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames.

The row's brief states day-1 counts of Now·1, Next·**6**, In progress·1, Waiting·2, Done·2. The
frames read Now·1, Next·**7**, In progress·1, Waiting·2, Done·2, and the NEXT lane genuinely holds
seven cards (Book the Term 4 holiday flights · Waiting-on digest · Passport renewal forms ·
Recruitment risk memo, Bundaberg · Bali deposit to Steve · Three workouts · Task from Joce: swim
carnival forms).

Nothing on the frame contradicts itself: the header reads "11 open · 2 waiting", and 1 + 7 + 1 + 2
open with 2 of those waiting, plus 2 done excluded, is exactly 11 and 2. So the pixels are
internally consistent and it is the *expectation* that is out by one.

*Unsure because:* a frame cannot tell me whether a task is sitting in the wrong Twenty column or
whether the brief's number is stale. I am naming it because I was asked to judge the counts hardest
and because the seventh card — "Waiting-on digest", an EA recurring task — is exactly the kind of
row that lands in Next by default when nobody decided where it goes.

*Fix in source:* none derivable from a frame. Reconcile the fixture's `column` values against the
row's stated counts before the auditor runs.

**B1-09 — MODERATE — the Done lane's meta is unreadable at 1.9:1, and the same two tasks render
legibly one segment away** — `tasks-board-d1-1920-{light,dark}-prod` (the only two frames where
the Done lane is on screen at all; see B1-05 for why). **Not introduced by B-1** — verified
identical in `demo/v21` — but never raised in any prior round, and open. I am ranking it here
rather than under Carried because the row's brief asked me to judge the 0.55 dim, and because a
reviewer must not sign over it.

| | ink | ground | contrast |
|---|---|---|---|
| Done meta, light | `(171,169,162)` | `(232,230,227)` | **1.89 : 1** |
| Done meta, dark | `(97,95,90)` | `(52,51,48)` | **1.98 : 1** |
| Done title, light | `(125,125,119)` | `(232,230,227)` | 3.27 : 1 |
| Done title, dark | `(148,146,140)` | `(52,51,48)` | 4.06 : 1 |

A 10.5px Muted meta line at 1.89:1 is not dim, it is gone — "EA · 1,387 rows · report attached ·
$0.03" cannot be read on either frame. And because the dim is applied to the whole card,
the live `more_horiz` on a Done card is dimmed with it while remaining a control (compounding
B1-02: 0.55 of 2.05:1).

What makes it a defect rather than a taste is that the app already has a better answer for the same
two records. `tasks-done-d1-1366-light-prod` shows "Notion export reconciled" and "Book dentist"
with a **filled Accent-ink checkbox, a strikethrough title and a full-opacity Muted meta** —
legible, unambiguous, and one segment click away. Two treatments of the same two tasks on the same
screen.

*Pack:* README Accessibility — "Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, **Muted on Card 4.6:1** …
**Keep meta text at 10.5 only in Muted on Card or Ground**"; README States — "**Disabled: opacity
.45, no pointer**" (a Done card is not disabled — it is tappable and carries a live overflow menu,
so it must not wear the disabled treatment).

*Fix in source:* drop the blanket card opacity and use the Done view's own treatment in the lane —
checked box, strikethrough title, Muted meta at full opacity. One task then looks like itself
wherever it appears.

### Carried — verified again on these pixels, not B-1's

The four the row named, plus four more that are in front of Josh on this pass.

- **C-1 — F1-06 — the slicer row's right-hand controls anchor to the column edge.** Re-measured on
  `tasks-board-d1-1366-light-prod`: last chip ends x=759, "Slicers" x=922–954, `tune` x=963–998 —
  **164px** of void. At 1920: last chip x=759, controls at x=1204–1280 — **446px**. Unchanged from
  round 2. *Pack:* README Layout — "Content max-width 1500; **left-aligned after that**".
- **C-2 — F2-02 — at 1024 the centring rule centres the trailing pair on the two-row chip block**,
  so the `tune` button and the "Slicers" link hang in the gutter between chip row 1 and chip row 2
  and share a baseline with neither. All 8 frames at 1024. Unchanged.
- **C-3 — F1-04 — the filter `IconBtn` renders unfilled against its own spec**, its interior
  sampling as the ground exactly, and an identical `tune` glyph 58px above it means
  edit-the-focuses. Unchanged. *Pack:* README Components, Buttons — "**Card fill with Card border**
  (header)"; README Icons — "Filter `tune`".
- **C-4 — F2-04 — "Slicers" is a noun where the chip beside it teaches "edit".** All 32 view
  frames. Unchanged.
- **C-5 — the lanes are stretched to the tallest lane and the stretch is painted.** Measured at
  1920: lanes span y198–804 (607px); bare Hairline fill down each column — NOW 536, IN PROGRESS 515,
  WAITING 470, DONE 452, NEXT 79 — **2,052 of 3,035 lane pixels (68%) are empty painted surface**.
  At 393 the NOW lane is 603px tall holding one 71px card: **86% empty**, and it is the largest
  single shape on the phone. Carried: `demo/v21` at 1920 measures **67%** by the same probe, so B-1
  did not worsen the ratio — it added a fifth column of it. On the ledger as **R2-03 / UX-I**.
  *Pack:* reviewer checklist 4 — "Empty column bottoms are left empty — that is correct, not a gap.
  **Cards are never stretched to equal heights**"; README Layout — "Leave the bottom of a column
  empty when the content ends. **Do not stretch cards to match heights.**" I record the
  counter-argument honestly: `jstack-mock-v11.html` line 207 sets
  `.board{display:grid;grid-auto-flow:column}` with `.bcol{background:var(--hairline)}`, so a grid
  stretch is what the reference build does, and README says the build wins where they disagree.
  What the pack forbids is *painting* the empty space; `align-items:start` on the strip, with the
  drop target kept full height and unpainted, satisfies both.
- **C-6 — the lane count is plain text where the same screen's section label uses the Marker
  badge.** The five lane headings render "NOW · 1", "NEXT · 7" … with the count as another tracked
  cap in Accent ink; 330px to the right, "WAITING ON" carries the pack's badge, sampled as
  `(79,127,168)` = Marker `#4F7FA8` light and `(127,169,207)` = `#7FA9CF` dark, both **exact**.
  Present identically in `demo/v21`, so carried. *Pack:* README Components, Section label —
  "`.js-label` — 11.5px tracked caps in Accent ink, padding 0 2. **Count badge: 16px tall pill,
  Marker fill, white 10px.**" The Marker rule ("count badge next to a section label … Nowhere
  else") sanctions the badge here; a lane heading **is** a section label.
- **C-7 — "WAITING · 2" and "WAITING ON ②" are the same two tasks, twice, on one screen.** At 1366
  and 1920 both are visible at once, ~330px apart: the lane shows them as cards ("Villa contract

- **C-8 — two columns where the pack says three, at 1366 and 1920** — 16 frames across all four

### The five questions, answered plainly

1. **Do the lane headings now match the section-label style — is R3-04 fixed?** **Yes, completely.**
   All five headings sample `(78,98,115)` light and `(180,196,212)` dark, which is Accent ink in
   both schemes; 9px cap height, identical to the `WAITING ON` and `GANTT` labels on the same frame;
   uppercase, tracked, weight 400, not 500, not sentence case. The style that sat 300px away in
   round 3 of V2 now sits in the lane heading too. Nothing to raise.
2. **Where does the strip scroll, is the scrollbar visible, and is a lane guillotined with nothing
   to signal a sixth?** It scrolls at **393, 1024 and 1366** and does not need to at **1920**, and
   the arithmetic is exactly the stated rule: flat 200px lanes below 1180 (measured 200, 200, 200)
   and `(1049 − 4×8) / 5 = 203` at 1920 (measured 203–204). The scrollbar is **visible at all three
   scrolling widths** and is the pack's own thumb — 5px tall, `(202,200,194)` = `rgba(122,119,111,.3)`
   over ground exactly — 121px of 353 at 393, 170px of 419 at 1024, 570px of 766 at 1366. A lane
   **is** guillotined at 393 and 1366; at 393 it cuts mid-word ("Famil", "8") and amputates a dashed
   border — that is B1-07, and it is low because the bleed itself is honest. The worse case is the
   one that does **not** guillotine: at **1024 the second lane ends exactly at the clip**, so there
   is no bleed at all and only a 5px thumb says three lanes exist (B1-05).
3. **Does the `⋮` crowd the title at 393?** **Yes — and not only at 393.** It takes 36px plus a 6px
   gap out of a 180px content box at every width, and because the lane is a flat 200px the crowding
   is identical on a 1920 monitor. Together with the 26px marker slot it leaves the title 106px, and
   six of thirteen titles break onto an orphan line as a result (B1-01). The control itself is also
   the least visible thing on the card — 2px dots at 2.05:1 (B1-02) — so the board pays 42px of
   every title for a button a person cannot see.
4. **Do the card ornaments read?** Half of them. The **EA tag and the dashed Accent-ink border read
   very well** — the tag is a filled Accent-soft pill with legible ink, the dash is unmistakable,
   and an agent's card is identifiable at a glance in both schemes; that part of BD-06 landed. The
   **work marker** is correct in token and metric (Accent-ink dot at `(74,94,112)` light /
   `(183,200,216)` dark, meta cap height) and is carried as F1-07 for its rank, not its pixels. The
   **person marker fails**: the same "J" on all ten person cards at 3.1:1, in a slot that shares
   neither a width nor a vertical alignment with the tag it alternates with (B1-03). The **Done
   dim** is applied as specified and the specification is the problem — 1.9:1 meta in both schemes,
   against a legible treatment of the same two tasks one segment away (B1-09).
5. **Do the "Board columns" chips or the column chips leak onto List, Gantt or Done?** **No leak.**
   Read at every width and in both schemes, all 24 non-board view frames carry the same six slicer
   chips and nothing else — "Next 90 days · edit" (or "All time · edit" on Done), This week,
   Waiting, Delegated, Agent, Recurring — plus the "Slicers" link and the `tune` button. No column
   chip and no "Board columns" group on any of them, and the two under-strip links appear on the
   board only. **Coverage caveat, stated plainly:** no frame in this pass has a column filter
   applied and none has the filter panel open, so I have verified the *negative* (they do not
   appear where they must not) and **cannot** verify the positive (that they appear on the board
   when a column filter is on). That state needs a driven capture.

### Frames that are fine, said plainly

- **All eight `task-detail-d1-*` frames are clean** at every width and in both schemes. The dialog is
  centred and complete: rename link, the three-cell priority segment with High selected, the date
  pair, the tag row, "SUBTASKS 2 of 3 done" with three rows carrying their EA tags and the dashed
  checkbox on the undone one, the "+ subtask" composer, "Complete all subtasks" outlined beside
  "Delegate to EA" primary, and the Activity card. Nothing clips, wraps or orphans; the watermark is
  legible over the scrim and clear of the dialog. B-1 does not reach this surface and it shows.
- **The strip mechanics are right.** Five lanes, five `col-*` counts that agree with each other and
  with the page header ("11 open · 2 waiting" = 1 + 7 + 1 + 2 open, 2 of them waiting, 2 done
  excluded). Lane width follows the stated rule to the pixel at all four widths. Gaps measured 8–9px
  against the mock's `gap:8px`. Scrollbar in the pack's exact thumb token, 5px, never a visible
  track.
- **Every surface token on the board is exact.** Lane fill `(221,219,214)` light / `(43,42,39)` dark
  — Hairline over ground, which is `jstack-mock-v11.html` line 208 (`.bcol{background:var(--hairline)}`)
  composited correctly. Card on lane `(241,240,238)` / `(59,58,55)` — `rgba(255,255,255,.58)` and
  `.08` over that lane. Ground `#EDEBE5` / `#191815`, edge to edge, including behind the phone safe
  area and under the tab bar. No pure black, no pure white, no v1.2 green, no gradient, and **no
  per-category hue** anywhere in the pass — Now, Next, In progress, Waiting and Done are five
  identical Hairline surfaces, which is right.
- **Light and dark are the same layout on all 20 pairs.** Identical document heights (1450/1450 at
  the 393 board, 993/993 at 1024, 963/963 at 1366, 1080/1080 at 1920, and the same across List,
  Gantt, Done and detail). No reflow, no column-count change, nothing appearing or disappearing.
- **The in-card icon button is per spec.** 36px square, radius 10, hairline border, no fill — which
  is the pack's "Hairline border (in cards)" case, correctly distinct from the header case. Its
  glyph is the problem (B1-02), not its box.
- **The overflow button is vertically centred on the title block** on every card measured — 249.5 vs
  250.5 on card 1, 326.5 vs 328.0 on card 2. It is the EA tag that is out of alignment, not the
  button.
- **The watermark** — "Demo · fixture data · nothing sends" — is legible and clear of every control
  on all 40 frames: bottom-left above the rail's "needs attention · $0.40" health line on desktop,
  and clear of the tab bar and the mic orb on the phone.
- **No `Clear` and no count badge on the slicer row**, correct for a state with no slicer and a
  default range (TF-07).

### Coverage

40 of 40 frames read. **Programmatic:** presence and pixel-width check on all 40 against the row's
matrix (5 screens × 4 widths × 2 schemes); an edge-energy floor (0.507 – 3.909, none near zero)
found no blank frame and none on the gate; ground-token coverage measured per frame in its own
scheme; 20 light/dark pairs matched on document height, **0 mismatches**; lane-fill runs scanned
row-wise and column-wise on all 8 board frames at every width to fix lane edges, widths, gaps and
bare-fill extents; scrollbar thumbs located and measured on all 8 board frames in both schemes;
card, marker, title and icon-button extents probed at named coordinates at 1920 and cross-checked at
1366 and 393; RGB samples with WCAG contrast computed for the Done lane's title and meta, the
person initial, the `more_horiz` dots, the lane headings, the section label, the Marker badge, the
EA tag, the dashed border and the work-marker dot, in **both** schemes; the same probes run on

#### The geometry, first, because everything else follows from it

The title's row is now its own. The marker (20px), the meta and the 36px `⋮` share the row below.
So the title gained 64px and the meta lost 77. The card is 8px narrower than round 1 measured, and

**Titles: 13 total, 4 break, and all 4 break onto a single-word orphan.**
"Book the Term 4 holiday / **flights**" · "Recruitment risk memo, / **Bundaberg**" ·

#### Defects, ranked by what they cost a person using the board

**B2-01 — MAJOR — the 106px column did not go away, it moved to the meta: 8 of 13 metas now break,
6 of them with a middle dot stranded at the end of a line or leading the next** — all 8
`tasks-board-*` frames, every width, both schemes.

Read off `tasks-board-d1-1920-light-prod` unless noted. Card by card:

| Card | Meta as rendered | Fault |
|---|---|---|
| Send Moz the sample pack | `JSTACK · Tue 8 Sep ·` / `high` | stranded dot **+** orphan |
| Book the Term 4 holiday flights | `from Joce · Fri 11 Sep ·` / `Family` | stranded dot **+** orphan |
| Waiting-on digest | `EA · recurring · every` / `Mon 8am · $0.05` | clean |
| Passport renewal forms | `Home · Mon 14 Sep ·` / `EA added from the` / `RACQ email` | stranded dot, 3 lines |
| Recruitment risk memo, Bundaberg | `Practice · Fri 11 Sep ·` / `high` | stranded dot **+** orphan |
| Bali deposit to Steve | `Bali trip · Fri 11 Sep` | clean |
| Three workouts | `Health · recurring` | clean (but see B2-07) |
| Task from Joce: swim carnival forms | `from Joce · Family` | clean |
| Redact the 200 sample emails | `EA · in progress · 41% ·` / `$0.40` — at **1366, both schemes**: `EA · in progress · 41%` / `· $0.40` | stranded dot at 1920, **leading dot** at 1366, money alone at both |
| Villa contract from Steve | `waiting on Steve · 9` / `days` | orphan, **and the number is split from its unit** |
| Dev allocation from Andy | `waiting on Andy · 4` / `days` | orphan, number split from unit |
| Notion export reconciled | `EA · 1,387 rows ·` / `report attached ·` / `$0.03` | **two** stranded dots, money alone, 3 lines |
| Book dentist | `you` | clean |

Round 1 found this on two cards. It is now on eight. Round 1's Done card was two lines with one
stranded dot; it is three lines with two. And `· $0.40` at 1366 is a new shape nobody has had to
look at before: a line of body text that **begins** with a separator.

`waiting on Steve · 9` / `days` is the one I would put in front of Josh first. The board's only
statement of how long something has been blocked is broken across a line at the space between the
number and its unit. In the Waiting-on rail 330px to the right, the same fact reads "9 days" on one
line, in a card the same screen is already drawing.

That this is the trade and not bad luck is arithmetic, not opinion. `JSTACK · Tue 8 Sep · high` and
`waiting on Steve · 9 days` are 24–25 characters at 10.5px — about 125px. They fit round 1's 180px
meta column and they do not fit round 2's 103px one. Six metas that were one clean line are now
two or three. `demo/v21/tasks-board-d1-1920-light-prod.png` is the control: in a 256px lane with no
marker and no button, **every** meta on that board renders on one line.

*Pack:* README Content — "Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`" (the dot
sits **between** two things, on one line; it is not a line ending and it is not a line beginning);
reviewer checklist 5 — "**No single-word orphan line in a title.** No two-line button label where
wrapping the row would have avoided it"; README Principles 4 — "Small type, clear hierarchy. Body
12.5px. **Three levels: title, body, meta**" — a meta that takes three lines to say four facts is
not the third level of anything.

*Fix in source:* two changes, and the first is the one that matters.

1. **Take the 36px `⋮` out of the meta's flow.** It is the only element on the card that does not
   need to be in a row with text: anchor it to the card's top-right corner as an overlay (the card
   has 10px padding to sit in, and the title's first line is 15px tall against the button's 36px
   box, so it clears). That returns 42px to the meta and takes it to ~145px — every two-line meta
   in the table above except `Passport renewal forms` collapses to one line. This is the same fix I
   proposed in round 1 for the title; it was not applied then, and moving the title instead is what
   pushed the problem down a row.
2. **Bind the runs.** Run the board card's meta through the same `richRuns` binding the list rows
   use — `BUGLOG_v21.md` R-34 already ties " · " to both neighbours with non-breaking spaces, and
   the same binding must hold "9" to "days" and "$0.03" to the word before it. A separator can then
   never end or begin a line, and a value can never sit alone.

**B2-02 — MODERATE — the two markers share a row but not a baseline: the person circle is centred
on the whole meta block, the EA tag hangs 11–12.5px above it** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames.

Your note says the two markers "share a row and a baseline". They share the row. Measured at 1920:

| Card | Marker box | Marker centre | Meta block | Block centre | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NEXT card 1, person | y272–291 (**20px**) | 281.5 | y271–294 | 282.5 | **1.0** |
| NEXT card 2, agent | y343–357 (**15px**) | 350.0 | y350–372 | 361.0 | **11.0** |
| WAITING card 1, person | y257–276 | 266.5 | y256–279 | 267.5 | **1.0** |
| DONE card 1, agent | y249–263 | 256.0 | y251–286 | 268.5 | **12.5** |

The circle is block-centred to within a pixel everywhere. The tag is not: it sits level with the top
of the first meta line and stays there however many lines follow, so on a three-line meta it is
12.5px high. Scroll the NEXT lane and the marker bobs up and down as agent and person cards
alternate — which is the same complaint B1-03 named, relocated from the title row to the meta row
rather than removed.

The horizontal half **is** fixed, and I want that on the record: all 13 titles start at x=459/460,
one edge, no walk. The residue is that the slot is still not a fixed width — person 20px, tag 25px —
so the meta text starts at x=485/486 after a circle and x=488 after a tag. 2–3px is inside
glyph-bearing noise and I am not calling it a defect; the vertical 11–12.5px is not.

*Pack:* README Components, Waiting row — "Type label at **48px fixed width so titles align**";
README Do and don't, Do — "**fixed 48px label column in rows**"; README Layout — "Header: title and
date **on one baseline**" (the pack's habit everywhere: things in a row share a line).

*Fix in source:* give the marker slot one fixed width and one alignment. `alignSelf: "center"` on
both variants, or `alignItems: "center"` on the marker column, and a single `width` so the two
variants occupy the same box. If the tag must stay 15px tall and the circle 20px, centre both inside
a 20 × 25px slot.

**B2-03 — MODERATE — the strip's guillotine now amputates card titles mid-word, where in round 1 it
amputated metas** — `tasks-board-d1-393-{light,dark}` and `tasks-board-d1-1366-{light,dark}`.

At **393** the clip box ends at **x=372** — not at the frame edge, but 20px inside it, against the
page's own right padding, with ground visible beyond. The NEXT lane shows 146 of its 200px and each
card shows 138 of 192. What survives, read at 5×:

- "Book the Term 4 **holida**" — the `y` cut through its bowl
- "Passport renewal **form**" — the `s` gone
- "Recruitment risk **mem**" / "Bundaberg"
- "Task from Joce: swim **c**" / "forms"

At **1366** the WAITING lane is cut at x=998 and does the same to "Villa contract from **Ste**" and
"Dev allocation from **A**", in both schemes.

Round 1 measured the same cut falling on meta text ("from Joce · Fri 11 Sep · **Famil**",
"EA · recurring · every Mon **8**"). It now falls on the title, because the title is the element
that runs to the card's full content width. I ranked B1-07 low on the honest ground that a partly
visible card in a horizontal scroller is a legitimate affordance. That ranking assumed the thing
being clipped was a supporting line. A card whose *name* is cut mid-glyph is not bleeding, it is
broken — and at 393 it is broken 20px inside the page, so it does not even read as "more this way".
The agent card's dashed Accent-ink border is still amputated on its right side at 393, so the one
card that is outlined reads as an open-ended box.

*Pack:* reviewer checklist 5 — "**No word broken mid-word.**"

*Fix in source:* the fade mask that round 2 of F-1 prescribed for the slicer scroller, applied to
the board strip's clip box — `maskImage: linear-gradient(to right, #000 calc(100% − 24px),
transparent)` with its `-webkit-` twin, under 1180 only — plus `paddingRight` inside the clip box so
the last visible card's own right edge is never the cut. A fade over a cut title still hides a word,
so pair it with B1-05's "2 more" marker: a person who can see that lanes continue does not need to
read the amputated one.

**B2-04 — LOW — the person marker is now high-contrast and still says nothing, and the same build's
List view proves it knows better** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames.

The contrast half of B1-03 is properly fixed: the letter is now Ink, sampled `(70,69,65)` on card
`(241,240,238)` = **8.43:1** light and `(227,224,216)` on `(59,58,55)` = **8.62:1** dark, on a 20px
`cardBorder` ring. It was 3.11:1. Good.

The other half is untouched, and the fix made it louder. All ten non-agent cards on this board carry
the same "J" — "Send Moz the sample pack" (JSTACK), "Book the Term 4 holiday flights" (**from
Joce**), "Book dentist" (**you**), "Villa contract from Steve", "Dev allocation from Andy" and five
more. Ten cards, one letter, now at 8.4:1 instead of 3.1:1, still costing 27px of every meta line.

`tasks-list-d1-1920-light-prod.png` shows the same eleven tasks one segment away and puts a person
marker on **two** rows — "Book the Term 4 holiday flights" and "Task from Joce: swim carnival
forms", the two that came from someone else and carry the "Accept" verb. "Send Moz", "Passport
renewal forms", "Villa contract from Steve" and the rest carry no marker at all. So the build
already contains the rule I proposed in round 1 — show it only when the owner is not the viewer —
and the board does not use it. Two treatments of the same eleven records, one segment apart.

*Pack:* README Principles 3 — "**Colour means you can act** … Nothing decorative gets colour";
README Do and don't, Do — "accent only where a tap does something" (the same discipline: a mark that
carries no information does not earn 27px of a 103px line); README Type, Rules — weight 500 is for
"a person's **name** in People", which is the pack's only sanctioned person-identity mark, and it is
a name, not a repeated initial.

*Fix in source:* use the List's own predicate. Render the circle only when the task's owner is not
the viewer; on this fixture that is two cards, and those two then mean something. That also returns
27px to ten of thirteen metas, which is most of B2-01 solved for free.

**B2-05 — LOW, and I am unsure — the board card title is set in Instrument Sans, where the pack says
card titles are Source Serif 4** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames (and, for the same reason, the 32
list/gantt/done frames).

Read at 8×, "Book the Term 4 holiday" has no serifs, a straight-tailed `y` and a flat-topped `4`.
The serif is loaded and rendering on the same frame — "Tasks" at 32px is unmistakably Source Serif
4, and `task-detail`'s sheet title is too — so this is a family assignment, not a missing font.

*Unsure because:* `jstack-mock-v11.html` line 484 renders a board card's title as a bare `<div>`
inside `.card`, with no heading class, so it inherits the body sans in the reference too; the list
rows behave the same way; and README's own preamble says "When this guide and the build disagree,
**the build wins**". By that rule the app is right and the pack's Type section is out of date for
this component. I am naming it because I was told to name what I am unsure about, and because the
round-1 change moved the title onto its own row and made it the most prominent thing on the card — a
family that was arguable at 106px on a shared row is conspicuous at 170px on its own. **I would not
hold B-1 for it.** It is a pack question and belongs in `DISCREPANCIES.md` beside row 21, not in a
build row's defect list.

*Pack:* README Type, Scale — "**Card title: 15 / 1.3, Source Serif 4 500.**"

*Fix in source:* none derivable from a frame. Rule the discrepancy — either the pack drops the serif
for board and list card titles, or `BoardCard` and the list row take the heading family.

**B2-06 — LOW — the in-progress card's state line ends 2px past the overflow button's left edge and
3px below its bottom** — `tasks-board-d1-1366-{light,dark}`, and 1px at 1920.

Measured at 1366: the `⋮` box is x796–831, y264–299 (36 × 36). The work-marker line "● EA working ·
since 2:14am" occupies y302–312 and its last glyph ends at **x=798**. Nothing overlaps and nothing
is clipped, so every automated sweep passes it. To the eye the card's live state line runs under the
button with a 3px shelf and no gutter, and it is two pixels into the button's column. At 1920 the
same pair is 1px apart horizontally (line ends 805, button starts 806). Three more characters of
timestamp — "since 11:14am" — and it collides.

*Pack:* README Spacing — "4px base. Used values: 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 32" (1px
and 2px are not spacing values in this app); README Surfaces — "Rows inside separated by 1px
Hairline, **9px vertical padding**".

*Fix in source:* the same fix as B2-01 — lift the `⋮` out of the flow to the card's top-right — puts
the whole width back under the state line and removes the near-miss with it.

**B2-07 — LOW, and I am unsure — "Three workouts" says one less thing on the board than in the
List** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames.

Board: `Health · recurring`. `tasks-list-d1-1920-light-prod`, the same task: `Health · recurring ·
weekly`. The board's line ends at x=566 against a limit of ~589, so it is not clipped and there is
no ellipsis — it is a shorter string. Every other meta I could compare across the two views is
identical, including the long one (`Home · Mon 14 Sep · EA added from the RACQ email`), so this is
not a length cap.

*Unsure because:* a frame cannot tell me whether the board composes a different meta or the fixture
carries two values. I am naming it because the same task telling a person two different things one
segment apart is exactly the class of thing this review exists to catch.

*Pack:* README Content — "Numbers over adjectives: '3 of 5 today', not 'a few items'" (a recurrence
the List states and the board withholds is the app being *less* specific in the denser view, which
is backwards).

*Fix in source:* none derivable from a frame. Reconcile the board card's meta composition against
the list row's.

**B1-01r — MAJOR residue — four card titles still break onto a single-word orphan line, at every
width** — all 8 `tasks-board-*` frames. Enumerated above. The pack line is unqualified: reviewer
checklist 5, "**No single-word orphan line in a title.**" Four is better than seven and it is not
zero. The fix is B2-01's first change: the 42px the `⋮` returns to the row goes to whichever element
is on it, and if the `⋮` leaves the card's flow entirely then both the title and the meta get the
full 170px, and only "Task from Joce: swim carnival forms" still needs two lines — with "carnival
forms" on the second, which is not an orphan.

**B1-09r — MODERATE residue — the Done lane's meta is still roughly half the contrast the pack asks
for** — `tasks-board-d1-1920-{light,dark}` (the only two frames where the Done lane is on screen at
all; see B1-05).

| | round 1 | round 2 | pack |
|---|---|---|---|
| Done meta, light | 1.89:1 | **2.31:1** | 4.6:1 |
| Done meta, dark | 1.98:1 | **2.37:1** | 4.6:1 |
| Done title, light | 3.27:1 | **4.98:1** | — |
| Done title, dark | 4.06:1 | **5.50:1** | — |

Measured against each card's own fill — Done `(235,234,231)` light, `(53,53,50)` dark; the un-dimmed
NEXT card is `(241,240,238)` / `(59,58,55)`. The title is now comfortable and that is a real
improvement. The meta is not. My peak-ink probe reads antialiased 10.5px text about 1.3× low — the
un-dimmed meta on the same frame measures 3.47:1 against a pack target of 4.6:1 — so scaling the
Done reading by the same factor gives roughly **3.1:1**. Under either the raw or the calibrated
reading it is short of 4.5:1, and "EA · 1,387 rows · report attached · $0.03" is still the hardest
line on the board to read.

The comparison that decides it is on the same 40 frames: `tasks-done-d1-393-dark-prod.png` renders
that identical string on **one full-opacity line** beside a filled checkbox and a struck-through
title. One task, two treatments, one segment apart, and the board's is the one you cannot read.

*Pack:* README Accessibility — "Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, **Muted on Card 4.6:1** … Keep
meta text at 10.5 only in Muted on Card or Ground"; README States — "**Disabled: opacity .45, no
pointer**" (a Done card is not disabled: it is tappable and carries a live overflow menu, so it must
not wear a disabled treatment at all).

*Fix in source:* stop dimming the meta. Dim the title and the marker if the lane needs to read as
finished, or better, use the Done view's own treatment — checked box, struck title, meta at full
opacity — so one task looks like itself wherever it appears. `0.7` on a card whose 10.5px Muted meta
is already at the bottom of its contrast budget is a token applied to the wrong element.

#### The two carries, judged

**B1-05 — your reasoning is right about the lane minimum and wrong about the finding.**

I accept the narrow point without reservation. `jstack-mock-v11.html` line 207 is
`.board{grid-auto-columns:minmax(200px,1fr)}`; V2.1's 256px lanes came from the `1fr` branch with
four columns, not from a 256px floor; and raising the floor to contradict the reference's own grid
is a pack decision, not a build row's. `DISCREPANCIES.md` row 21 already settled a neighbouring
question the same way and settled it against the pack. You were right not to do it, and right to
write the reasoning down rather than quietly widen the lane.

But B1-05 never asked for that. Round 1's fix reads: "**Whichever**, put a persistent affordance on
the strip — a right-edge fade and a '2 more' marker on the last visible lane heading — because a 5px
scrollbar is not a statement." That sentence costs nothing in the grid, contradicts no line of the
pack or the mock, and is the half of the finding a person actually pays for. It is unaddressed, and
the carry note answers the structural options instead.

These frames make the case stronger than round 1 could:

- **The one signal is below the fold.** At 1024 the strip's scrollbar thumb is 170px of a 419px
  track, at **y855–859**. `tasks-done-d1-1024-*` and `tasks-gantt-d1-1024-*` are 768px tall, so 768
  is the viewport; `tasks-board-d1-1024-*` is 1011. The scrollbar is **87px below the fold.** On the
  iPad this row is named for, there is nothing on the first screen that says the board has more than
  two lanes. (At 393 the thumb is at y887–891 against an 852 viewport — also below the fold — but
  there at least the lane visibly bleeds.)
- **The bleed is three pixels.** I said in round 1 that nothing bleeds; that was very slightly wrong
  and I correct it. The IN PROGRESS lane shows x648–650 — three columns of flat hairline-coloured
  rectangle with no heading, no card and no letter. It reads as a border on the strip, not as a lane.
- **The lane that is hidden is the row's own.** IN PROGRESS is off-stage at 1024 and 393, and it
  holds the only card carrying the live work marker — "● EA working · since 2:14am", the one thing
  on this screen that says an agent is doing something right now. On a phone and on an iPad the
  board never shows it.

*Pack:* README Principles 2 — "**Say when the list ends.** 'That's all until 4pm.' Blank space after
it is correct, not a gap to fill" (the converse duty: say when it has *not* ended); README Principles
7 — "**Show the work**"; reviewer checklist 7 — "**1024 reads as a tablet, not a stretched phone**".

**So: your call is right, and B1-05 stays open.** What I would do is the cheap half — a right-edge
fade on the clip box and a count on the last visible lane heading, or on the "Columns · edit in
Twenty" line, saying how many lanes are off-stage. If you would rather not do even that in this row,
then it belongs in `CARRIED_DEFECTS_v21.md` beside UX-A with Josh's name on it, not only in a source
comment — the ledger is where this repo puts decisions a reviewer disagreed with, and it is the only
place the auditor will look.

**B1-02 — your reasoning holds as scope and does not hold as a resolution.**

The factual claim checks out on these pixels. The dot peaks at `(172,170,165)` on button interior
`(241,240,238)` = **2.04:1** light and `(109,107,102)` on `(59,58,55)` = **2.14:1** dark, unchanged
from round 1 to within antialiasing. `task-detail-d1-393-light-prod.png` shows the identical faint
glyph on all three Subtasks rows, so it is genuinely the same glyph at the same size rendering the
same way, and it is not B-1's to restyle. I would not want a board row quietly changing how a shared
control draws across three components either.

Two things stop that from closing it.

1. **The role is not the same.** On a decision card and in Subtasks, `more_horiz` sits beside
   labelled controls — Approve, Revise, Later, a checkbox, a "+ subtask" field. It is a *second* way
   to do things. On a board card it is the **only** control besides the card itself, and per B-1's
   own brief "a card moves by drag or by menu". This is the menu. It is the entire non-drag path —
   the keyboard path, the screen-reader path, the shaky-hand path — and on this surface it is the
   least visible mark on the card. A hairline border, a 36px target and an `accessibilityLabel` are
   all real, and none of them makes the affordance *visible*; a person has to already know it is
   there.
2. **The frame shows the pack does not require it.** On the same 1920 frame the header's `grid_view`
   glyph reaches Muted `#7A776F` exactly and the two `tune` glyphs reach `(145,142,134)`. It is this
   glyph's three 2px dots at 18px that antialiasing eats, not a token. Rendering *this instance* at
   20px, or in Ink, is a local change that touches no shared value and no other component.

*Pack:* README Accessibility — "Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, **Muted on Card 4.6:1**"; README
Components, Buttons — "Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: 32 or 36 square … **Muted glyph 17 or 18**" (18 is
a size, not a contrast budget, and the contrast line is not optional).

**So: I do not think the reasoning holds as a reason to close it, and I do think it holds as a reason
not to fix it *pack-wide* here.** Fix the board's instance — it is the only place the glyph is a sole
path — and raise the pack-wide question as an A-2 row. Whichever you choose, B1-02 is an open defect
on these frames and I will not sign over it.

#### What the restructure broke, and what it did not

You asked me to look for the F-1 shape. It is there, and it is B2-01: things fixed, one introduced,
and the introduced one is larger than two of the ones it fixed.

**Broken by the change:** the meta column (B2-01), the marker's vertical alignment (B2-02 — moved
rather than removed), and what the 393/1366 guillotine amputates (B2-03).

**Not broken, checked because you named them:**

- **Card height.** The lane grew 14px overall (round 1 y198–804, now y200–820) and cards did not
  become uniform: NEXT measures 82, 68, 70, 82, 67, 67, 82px down the lane. Checklist 4 — "Cards are
  never stretched to equal heights" — holds. Nothing is pushed off any viewport that was not already
  off it.
- **The work marker's position.** "● EA working · since 2:14am" now has its own third row below the
  meta, at the card's left content edge, in Accent ink, unbroken and unclipped at 1366 and 1920. It
  is the right place for it. Its only fault is the 2px near-miss with the button (B2-06).
- **The dashed agent border.** Intact and unmistakable at 1024, 1366 and 1920, both schemes, on all
  three agent cards. Still amputated on its right side at 393, which is B1-07 and unchanged.
- **Density at 393.** The phone frame is not worse: the same 13 cards, the same 200px lanes, chips
  that now wrap to two rows without clipping, a floating tab bar and the mic orb above it on the
  right. It reads as a desktop board on a phone for the same reason it did in round 1 — the lane
  minimum — not for anything this change did.
- **Dark.** Lane runs are identical light and dark to the pixel at 1024 (232–431), 1366 (232–431,
  648–847, 856–998) and 1920 (232–434, 655–857, 866–1069, 1078–1280). Same wraps, same cuts, same
  card count, nothing appearing or disappearing. Grounds are `#EDEBE5` and `#191815` exactly, edge
  to edge, on all 40 frames.
- **B1-06.** "Columns · edit in Twenty" ends at x=347 and "Refresh" begins at x=372 — **24px**,
  against 2–3px between the words inside the first label. They read as two controls now. Fixed.
- **The watermark.** "Demo · fixture data · nothing sends" sits at the foot of the rail on desktop
  with the health line "● needs attention · $0.40" on its own line below it, and above the tab bar on
  the phone, clear of the mic orb. Legible, over nothing, in both schemes, on all 40 frames.
- **The lane headings.** R3-04 still holds: Accent ink, 9px caps, tracked, weight 400, on all five
  lanes at every width in both schemes.
- **The chip scroller at 393.** Not my row, but worth recording since it was F-1's open MAJOR: on
  these frames the six slicer chips **wrap to two rows and none is clipped**. "Delegated" is whole.
  F1-01 is clean on this capture.
- **The Gantt caption.** Also not my row: "8 Sep" carries no strike-through on any of the 8 Gantt
  frames, and the axis runs 8 Sep → 7 Dec. F2-01 is clean on this capture.
- **`task-detail`.** All 8 frames clean, as in round 1. This change does not reach the dialog.

#### Carried — verified again on these pixels, not this round's

- **C-1** — the slicer row's right-hand controls anchor to the column edge. Re-measured at 1920:
  last chip ends x=759, "Slicers" and `tune` at x1204–1272 — **446px** of void. Unchanged.
  *Pack:* README Layout — "Content max-width 1500; **left-aligned after that**."
- **C-2** — at 1024 the trailing pair is centred on the two-row chip block and shares a baseline with
  neither row (chips y169 and y205, controls y186). All 8 frames at 1024. Unchanged.
- **C-3** — the filter `IconBtn` renders unfilled. Sampled at 1920: both `tune` buttons' interiors
  are `(237,235,229)` — the ground exactly — while the header's `grid_view` button is `(247,247,244)`
  = Card. *Pack:* README Components, Buttons — "**Card fill with Card border** (header)." Unchanged.
- **C-4** — "Slicers" is a noun where the chip beside it teaches "edit". All 40 view frames.
  Unchanged. (Its colour is right: Accent ink in both schemes, sampled at 393 — `(99,102,122)` light
  and `(168,194,203)` dark.)
- **C-6** — the lane count is plain text where the same screen's section label uses the Marker badge.
  Unchanged.
- **C-7** — "WAITING · 2" and "WAITING ON ②" are the same two tasks, twice, on one screen, at 1366
  and 1920. Unchanged.
- **C-8** — two columns where the pack says three, at 1366 and 1920, across all four views. The

**C-5 is withdrawn**, per `DISCREPANCIES.md` row 21. The stretch is the reference's and the reference
wins.

#### Coverage

**By measurement:** all 40 frames opened, pixel dimensions and both ground tokens verified against
the light and dark values; lane runs probed at a named y at all four widths in both schemes; card
boxes, marker boxes, title lines, meta lines and the `⋮` box extent-probed on 13 cards at 1920 and
cross-checked at 1366 and 393; WCAG contrast computed from sampled pairs for the person initial, the
`⋮` dots, the Done title and meta, the un-dimmed title and meta, and the four text links, in both
schemes; scrollbar thumb and track measured at 393, 1024 and 1366 and compared against each width's
viewport height; the same probes run on `demo/v21/tasks-board-d1-1920-light-prod.png` to hold the
three builds side by side. **By eye:** 8 frames read full size, 9 more as 4–8× crops, the remainder
at full size in sequence, covering all five screens at every width in both schemes.

**Reviewed:** 8 September 2026.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

## V2.2 G-1 ★ round 1

**Reviewed:** 8 September 2026. Scope: the eight `tasks-gantt-d1-*-prod` frames in `demo/v22/`,
day 1, production flavour, only. No other screen and no `-test` frame was judged at this round.

### 1 · Every frame reviewed

| File | Screen | Width | Scheme | Verdict |

No frame is missing, blank, gated, or the wrong screen. All eight show Tasks with the Gantt segment
selected, the range chip, the axis, four lanes, the Unscheduled lane, "Fit" and the new footer.

Measured geometry, common to all eight: label column **160px** (label ink starts x=33 at 393, x=245
on desktop; chart origin x=193 at 393, x=405 on desktop). Day width **28px exactly** — ticks at
193/221/249/277/305/333 and 405/433/461/489/573/601/…. Range starts **Tue 8 Sep**; weekend blocks
sit at day indices 4–5, 11–12, 18–19, 25–26 = 12/13, 19/20, 26/27 Sep and 3/4 Oct, all Sat+Sun.
Plot viewport: 166px / **5.9 days** at 393 · 232px / 8.3 days at 1024 · 580px / 20.7 days at 1366 ·

### 2 · Defects, most severe first

**G1R1-01 · HIGH · Accent soft now carries three meanings on one card.**
All 8 frames. Sampled: weekend shading `(227,229,229)` light / `(60,62,63)` dark; Unscheduled row
fill `(227,229,229)` / `(60,62,63)`; EA bar fill `(227,229,229)`. All three are the identical token.
`rgba(102,121,138,.14)` composited on card `#F7F7F4` computes to `(226.7, 229.4, 229.2)`;
`rgba(154,174,192,.16)` on dark card `(43,42,39)` computes to `(61,63,64)`. That is Accent soft, to
the pixel, three times over.

*Pack:* README Colour, Where colour goes — "**Accent soft: primary-verb fill, selected focus chip,
recommended option row, owner tags (EA, J)**". README Principle 3 — "**Colour means you can act.**
… **Nothing decorative gets colour.**" `handoff.md` Tasks — "**EA bars are accent-soft with a dashed
accent border**". The pack has already spent this token on the Gantt, on EA ownership. G-1 spends it
twice more: on a calendar fact (weekend) and on a state (no dates).

*Your Q3, answered:* it reads as a **selection artefact**, not as "these are weekends" — because it
is literally painted in the selected-state fill. At 393 and 1024 only one shaded pair is in view, so
there is no rhythm to read as weekly; at 1366 and 1920 the rhythm arrives but the slabs then become
the loudest thing in the chart, louder than any bar.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttAxis.tsx` — the weekend overlay uses
`backgroundColor: c.surfaceInset`; `components/tasks/GanttUnscheduled.tsx` — the row uses
`backgroundColor: dragging ? c.selected : c.surfaceInset`. Both reach for the inset token because it
is the only "one step off the card" fill in the set.

*Fix in source:* give weekends a neutral, chroma-free tint derived from Hairline (a Hairline-alpha
overlay, not `surfaceInset`), and give the Unscheduled rows Card fill with a 1px Hairline border.
Accent soft then means EA / selected / recommended on this card and nowhere else.

---

**G1R1-02 · HIGH · one text kind for the whole label column, so a lane, a task and a heading are
typographically identical.**
All 8 frames. Sampled darkest ink, light: "JSTACK" `(134,131,123)` · "Bali" `(131,129,121)` ·
"Send Moz the sample pack" `(130,128,120)` · "Passport renewal forms" `(134,131,123)` ·
"Unscheduled" `(137,133,126)` · an Unscheduled row label `(133,130,122)`. Dark, same six:
`(140,137,131)`, `(137,134,129)`, `(138,135,130)`, `(136,133,127)`, `(138,136,131)`. Every one is
Muted (`#7A776F` light, `#93908A` dark) at an 8px cap height (≈11px). No difference in weight, size,
case, colour, indent or rule separates any of them.

*Pack:* README Principle 4 — "**Small type, clear hierarchy.** … **Three levels: title, body,
meta.**" README Type — "**Meta: 10.5 / 1.4, Muted (sources, times, why-lines).**" README
Accessibility — "**Keep meta text at 10.5 only in Muted on Card or Ground.**" A task title is not a
source, a time or a why-line; a lane heading is a structural label, which the pack scales at 11.5
uppercase tracked .08em in Accent ink.

*Your Q5, answered:* **no.** You cannot tell a lane from a task. "Home" and "Bundaberg" read as
tasks that happen to have no bar. The only cue is absence — a row with no bar — which is also what an
undated task would look like if one ever reached the chart.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttChart.tsx` renders the lane heading as `<Txt kind="meta">` and
the task title as `<Txt kind="meta">` — the same call, six lines apart.

*Fix in source:* lane heading → the section-label kind (11.5 / caps / .08em / Accent ink) the pack
already defines; task title → body (12.5, Ink); indent task rows under their lane by `space[2]`.
That restores all three levels in one edit.

---

**G1R1-03 · HIGH · the row title is cut mid-word at every width, including 1920 where 640px of the
card is empty.**
All 8 frames. "Recruitment risk memo, Bundaberg" prints as **"Recruitment risk memo, Bund…"** at
393, 1024, 1366 and 1920, light and dark — because the label column is a constant 160px regardless
of how much room the card has. At 1920 the card is 1046px wide and the plot area right of x=601 is
empty; the title is still amputated.
Additionally at **1366 only**: the week label at the plot's right clip prints **"28 S"**, cut inside
the token.

*Pack / hard rules:* hard rule 23 — "**1024 reads as a tablet: nothing clipped mid-word**"; hard
rule 24 — "**nothing is cut mid-word; a lane or column scrolls or wraps, never clips**"; checklist 5
— "**No word broken mid-word.**"

*Relationship to B2-03:* **same defect class** — a title amputated mid-word by a container that will
not grow. Different component and different root cause: B2-03 is the board strip's clip; this is a
fixed `LABEL_W` with a one-line ellipsis. I have given it its own id because fixing B2-03 will not
touch this code path; if you would rather carry it as a B2-03 sub-row, it belongs there.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttChart.tsx` — `const LABEL_W = 160` is a module constant with no
breakpoint, and both label `<Txt>`s carry `numberOfLines={1}` with no two-line fallback. This is the
opposite of the C-5 fix, which took the phone waiting row to **two lines** rather than ellipsising it.

*Fix in source:* measure the column to the widest title present, floored at 120 and capped at
`min(240, 0.4 × chart box width)`; at <768 fall to two lines as C-5 does and grow that row's height.
Clip the axis a whole day early so a week label is never half-drawn.

**G1R1-04 · HIGH · at 393 a fixed 160px label column leaves a 166px porthole onto a 90-day range.**
393 light and dark. Measured: card inner edge 21→371, content 33→359 = **326px**. Label column
33→193 = **160px = 49% of the content width**. Plot 193→359 = **166px = 5.9 days of 90 (6.6%)**.
What is on screen is two solid bars, one dashed bar, one weekend pair and one week label. Nothing
in the frame lets you place a bar against anything except "today", and "today" is 21px from the
left edge.

*Pack:* checklist 7 — "**393 reads as a phone, not a squeezed desktop.**" README Layout — "Under
768: one column." README Principle 4 — the phone is the constrained surface, and half of it here is
spent on labels that are already truncating (G1R1-03).

*Your Q1, answered:* **the split is not usable.** The label column eats the timeline. A phone user
gets a scrolling porthole, and the only cue that it scrolls is the 5px thumb at the foot of the chart.

*Root cause:* `LABEL_W = 160` and `DAY_WIDTH = 28` are both constants that never consult the
container (`components/tasks/GanttChart.tsx`, `lib/ganttAxis.ts`). "Fit" exists and would help, but
it is not the state you land on.

*Fix in source:* under 768, take `LABEL_W` to ~104–120 **and** make the phone's first paint the
fitted window (`fitWindow` over the bars actually present) rather than the 90-day range — the phone
should open on the work, and "Next 90 days · edit" is one tap away.

**G1R1-05 · MEDIUM · the three axis bands are two identical grey lines and one invisible one.**
All 8 frames. Month "Sep" sampled `(139,136,129)`; week "14 Sep" sampled `(132,130,121)` — both
Muted, both ~9px glyph extent, differing only by 16px of vertical position. The day band is a
**4px × 1px Hairline** tick: light `(231,230,228)` on card `(247,247,244)` = **1.13:1**; dark
`(59,58,55)` on `(43,42,39)` = **1.27:1**.

*Pack:* README Accessibility — "**Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, Muted on Card 4.6:1**". The
ticks are not text, but they are the band that carries the 28px unit, and at 1.1:1 they carry
nothing at arm's length. README Principle 4 — "**clear hierarchy**": a band structure with no
hierarchy between its bands is not a structure.

*Your Q2, answered:* the week band's date **is** readable at 28px/day — labels fall every 196px and
never collide, and "7 Sep", "14 Sep", "21 Sep", "28 Sep", "5 Oct" are all legible. Month and week
are **not** distinguishable from each other: same family, same size, same colour, only y separates
them, so "Sep" over "7 Sep" reads as a two-line caption rather than as two scales. The day band is
not visible at all. Net: two bands read as one caption and the third is missing — grey mush is fair.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttAxis.tsx` renders `axis.months` and `axis.weeks` through the
same `<Txt kind="meta">`, and the day band is a bare `backgroundColor: c.hairline` stub specified
against no particular surface.

*Fix in source:* month → the section-label kind (caps, tracked, Accent ink) as the band that names
the epoch; week stays Muted meta; replace the 4px tick stub with a full-height day gridline at
Hairline **or** a Muted tick at ~30% alpha — something with a measurable contrast against the card
it is drawn on.

**G1R1-06 · MEDIUM · the Unscheduled rows read as disabled, or as loading skeletons.**
All 8 frames. Full-bleed rows — 326px wide at 393, **1023px at 1920** — flat Accent-soft fill, no
border, Muted ~11px label, **radius 6**, 38px tall, seven of them at identical height with 4px gaps.

*Pack:* README States — "**Disabled: opacity .45**"; "**Loading: skeleton rows in Hairline, same
heights as content.**" A stack of seven equal-height flat-filled bars with grey text is the
skeleton the pack describes, near enough that a person will wait for it to finish loading. README
Surfaces — "**Radii: 10 cards, bars, icon buttons · 8 buttons, chips, rows-as-buttons, insets · 5
tags and checkboxes**": **6 is not on the scale**, and a row-as-button is 8. README Components,
Habit chip — "**Chips wrap in a 6px-gap row**": these do not wrap, they stretch.

*Your Q6, answered:* they read as **disabled/loading**, not as "waiting to be placed". At 1920 a
1023px block holding "Book dentist" is checklist 7's density failure in a single object.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttUnscheduled.tsx` — the row is a full-width `View` with
`backgroundColor: c.surfaceInset`, `borderRadius: 6`, and `<Txt kind="meta">`, inside a plain
vertical `View` with no wrap.

*Fix in source:* make them chips as the brief intended — `alignSelf: "flex-start"` inside a
`flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 6` container, radius 8, Card fill with a 1px Hairline
border, label at body weight in Ink. A chip that hugs its words and sits beside its neighbours reads
as a movable object; a full-bleed grey bar reads as a dead row.

---

**G1R1-07 · MEDIUM · the footer instructs a drag that nothing on screen affords.**
All 8 frames. The footer reads "**Drag a bar to change its dates.**" The bars are flat 8px blocks
(solid `(102,121,138)` Accent; EA `(227,229,229)` with a dashed `#4A5E70` border). Probing the bar
row pixel by pixel at 393 finds one uniform fill from end to end — the 12px grab zones paint
nothing.

*Pack:* README Principle 7 — "**Show the work.**" The component's own header records why this
matters: V2 printed this sentence "with no drag behind it", A-45 removed it "as an instruction with
no affordance", and G-1 restores it. The affordance G-1 built is a **hit region**, not a visible
one, so a still frame is in exactly the state A-45 objected to.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttBar.tsx` — both handles are `pointerEvents="none"` Views with
geometry and no paint.

*Fix in source:* give the ends a resting cue — a 1px Card-border cap at each end, or darken the
first and last 3px of the fill one step. Anything a screenshot can carry.

*Flagged as a product call:* if the intent is that only pointer hover reveals a handle, then the
sentence should not appear on the 393 frames at all, where there is no hover to reveal it.

---

**G1R1-08 · LOW · the work marker floats inside the plot area, at a date position it does not mean.**
1024, 1366 and 1920, both schemes; at 393 it is additionally cut mid-token — the frame ends inside
"**EA working · since 2**". Measured at 1366: the line runs x481–601, which on this axis is **11 Sep
to 14 Sep**, and it crosses the 12–13 Sep weekend shading. The bar it belongs to ends at x=461. A
person scanning the chart for "what is happening on the 12th" reads a sentence.

*Pack:* README Layout and Components put no free prose inside a plotted coordinate space; a chart's
x-axis is a promise about what x means, and this text breaks it for three days' worth of pixels.

*Not re-reported:* the marker's **colour**. `F1-07` in this file already covers it as "a second meta
line, at meta size, in Accent ink" and already names `tasks-gantt-d1-*` among its frames. This
finding is the **position** only, which is new at G-1.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttBar.tsx` positions `WorkMark` absolutely at
`left: box.x + box.width + 6` **inside the horizontally scrolled chart**.

*Fix in source:* move the marker into the frozen label column, on or under the title, where it is a
fact about the task rather than about a date. That fixes the 393 cut for free.

---

**G1R1-09 · LOW (partly unsure) · the week band's hairline reads as a leading pipe, and the first
band's sits on the wrong day.**
All 8 frames. Measured at 393: a 1px Hairline `(231,230,228)` runs y326–337 (12px) at x=193, then
"7 Sep" begins at x≈196. At that size the mark reads as a "|" glyph in front of the date:
"**| 7 Sep**".

Separately, and measurably: the range starts **8 Sep** (tick 0 at x=193/405; the weekend at day
indices 4–5 = 12/13 Sep Sat+Sun; the "14 Sep" divider at x=573 = index 6). So the first week band is
a truncated week-of-7-Sep band clamped to the chart's left edge — its label **and** its divider both
land on 8 Sep's boundary, with nothing saying the band is cut. Every later band is correct.

*Pack / carried rule:* the V2.1 R-34 rule carried into this review's checklist — "**a separator never
leads a line**".

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttAxis.tsx` places the hairline as the first child of the week
row (`flexDirection: "row"` → hairline, then the label at `marginLeft: 4`), and `lib/ganttAxis.ts`
clamps a partial first band's `x` to 0 without marking it partial.

*Fix in source:* draw the week divider as a positioned element on the band's true boundary at full
band height rather than inline before the label, and suppress it (or say "week of") for a first band
that is clamped.

*Unsure:* how much the off-by-one costs in practice. The labels after the first are all correct, the
weekend geometry is correct and the today line is exact, so a reader who counts from any later
hairline is right. Ranked last for that reason — but it is still a hairline that asserts a boundary
one day away from where the boundary is.

---

**G1R1-10 · LOW · two links to Twenty, one line apart, in different case.**
1024, 1366, 1920, both schemes. The new Gantt footer ends "**Open in Twenty for the full timeline.**"
in Accent ink; 42px below it, outside the card, the pre-existing line reads "Tasks live in Twenty ·
**open in Twenty**", also Accent ink. Same destination, twice, capitalised two ways.

*Pack:* README Content — "Voice: **a capable assistant speaking to one person. Short sentences.**"
README Principle 3 — accent marks the thing you can act on; two accent phrases for one action is
noise, not emphasis.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/Gantt.tsx` appends its own footer with an `external-link` press
handler, under a `TaskViews` footer that already carries one. G-1 added the second without removing
the first.

*Fix in source:* drop "Open in Twenty for the full timeline." from the Gantt footer and leave the
instruction as "Drag a bar to change its dates." — the tab-level line already says where Twenty is.

### 3 · Checked because you asked, or because it looks like a defect, and is correct

- **The today line (your Q4).** Sampled `(74,94,112)` = `#4A5E70` Accent ink exactly in light and
  `(183,200,216)` = `#B7C8D8` exactly in dark, **1px**, at x=214 (393) and x=426 (desktop) — 0.75 of
  a day past the range start, its true fractional position. *Pack:* README Components, Calendar grid
  — "**Now is a 1px Accent-ink line.**" It **is** findable at 393 and 1024, where it is the only
  chromatic mark in the chart. At 1366 and 1920 it is much harder to find, but not because of the
  line — because of G1R1-01: four and five Accent-soft slabs carry far more visual mass than a 1px
  stroke, so the eye lands on a weekend first. Fix G1R1-01 and this resolves itself. No change to
  the line.
- **Weekend geometry.** 56px blocks at day indices 4–5, 11–12, 18–19, 25–26 from a Tue-8-Sep origin
  = 12/13, 19/20, 26/27 Sep and 3/4 Oct. Every one a Saturday and a Sunday. The maths is right; only
  the token is wrong.
- **Bar tokens.** Solid bars `(102,121,138)` = `#66798A` Accent; EA bars Accent-soft fill inside a
  dashed `#4A5E70` border. That is `handoff.md` Tasks, verbatim: "EA bars are accent-soft with a
  dashed accent border." Correct — and it is why G1R1-01 matters, since the pack has already
  assigned this fill on this surface.
- **The card spanning two of three columns at 1366 and 1920.** Measured 1050px at 1920 = col1 586 +
  gap 18 + col2 450 at `1.3fr 1fr .95fr`. That is `handoff.md`'s own rule for Tasks and
  `layout/registry.tsx`'s `span: 2`, not "a single section laid across columns" in checklist 1's
  sense. Correct.
- **Hard rule 23's lane half.** Four lanes are visible at 1024 — JSTACK, Bali, Home, Bundaberg —
  against a floor of two. That half passes; it is the mid-word half that fails (G1R1-03).
- **Dark parity.** Identical to the pixel at all four widths: same label x-starts (33 / 245), same
  chart origin (193 / 405), same row baselines, same clip points, same lane and chip counts, nothing
  appearing or disappearing. Ground `(25,24,21)` = `#191815`; card `(43,42,39)` = the .08 white over
  it. Painted edge to edge behind the safe area and under the tab bar at 393.
- **The 1500 cap.** At 1920 content runs x231→1733 = 1502px, left-aligned against the rail, not
  centred. Correct.
- **Empty column bottoms.** The 322px right column at 1024 holds a 100px card and then stops; the
  page's right two-thirds at 1920 is empty. *Pack:* "**Leave the bottom of a column empty when the
  content ends.**" Correct, not a gap.
- **The horizontal scroll thumb.** 5px, Muted at ~30%, transparent track — the pack's scrollbar, and
  currently the only thing in the frame telling you the chart scrolls. Correct. Do not remove it
  while fixing G1R1-04.
- **Bar end radius** is `BAR_H / 2` — a 4px cap on an 8px bar. The pack's "don't" on pills is scoped
  to chips; the progress bar has no stated radius. **Cosmetic and tolerated** — saying so plainly
  rather than listing it.
- **The demo watermark.** (14,1023) on desktop, clear of the rail health line at y1061; (14,1216) at
  393, clear of the tab bar at y1233+ and of the mic orb at x330+. No B-32 recurrence.

### 4 · Your Q7, answered directly

At 1920 the plot is 862px = **30.8 of 90 days**, and every bar sits in the first 112px of it. From
x=601 to x=1267 — **77% of the chart** — there is nothing but four Accent-soft slabs. It does not
look padded wrongly; it looks like a **striped empty field with the data shoved into a corner**. The
cause is three defaults meeting: a 90-day range, a fixed 28px day, and fixture data that spans nine.
The fix is not padding — it is that "Fit" should be where you land (G1R1-04's fix), or that the
default range should be the data's span. I have not raised it as a separate finding because it is
G1R1-01 and G1R1-04 seen at the widest viewport.

- **Not re-reported, per the brief:** B2-02 (owner-tag height), B2-03 (board strip clip — class

All eight frames opened at full size; twelve crops read at 2–5× (axis header, lane block, Unscheduled

width from six consecutive tick positions at each width; weekend block extents; label-column and
plot-viewport widths at all four breakpoints; today-line x and colour in both schemes; glyph cap
heights and darkest ink for six text elements per scheme; card box extents; light-vs-dark row

### 3 · New defects, most severe first

**G1R2-01 · HIGH · the label column takes its share of the window, so at 1024 it eats 61% of a card
that is 417px wide, and the timeline is now shorter than it was in round 1.**
`tasks-gantt-d1-1024-light-prod.png`, `-dark-prod.png`. Measured: card 233–649; content 245–637
= 393px; label column 245–484 = **240px**; plot 485–637 = **153px = 5.46 days of 90**. Round 1's
1024 plot was 232px / 8.3 days. The visible axis is one week label ("| 7 Sep") and one month; the
14 Sep weekend slab is sliced in half by the clip edge; two of the five bars run off the right edge.
At 1920 the same constant is 240px against a longest title measuring **170px** — 70px of unused air
taken from the plot, which fell 862→783px.

*Pack:* hard rule 20 — "**a fixed column is sized to the widest word it must hold, measured
(R-18)**". A quarter of the browser window is not a measurement of the words. Checklist 7 —
"**1024 reads as a tablet, not a stretched phone**"; a 153px timeline beside a 240px list of titles
is a list with a sliver of chart attached. Hard rule 23 — "**the board, the Gantt, Talk and Find are
judged at 393, 1024, 1366 and 1920**": 393 was fixed and 1024 was not measured after.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttChart.tsx:52`
`const labelWidth = (width: number) => Math.max(LABEL_MIN, Math.min(LABEL_MAX, Math.round(width * 0.25)))`
fed at line 108 by `useLayout().width` — the viewport, not the card. At 1024 the Gantt sits in
column 1 of two, so the card is 40% of the window and the column is sized as if it were the page.

*Fix in source:* measure, don't guess. Take the share from the chart's own `onLayout` width (the
same box `chartTarget()` already measures), or better, from the widest rendered title: clamp to
`[104, min(240, 0.34 × chartBoxWidth)]`. At 1024 that gives ~133px and a 260px / 9.3-day plot; at
1920 it gives ~180px, restoring 60px to the timeline with the longest title still intact.
