**G1R2-02 · MEDIUM · the month label is bisected by the today line, in all eight frames.**
Zoomed at 10× on `tasks-gantt-d1-1920-light-prod.png`: "SEP" occupies x486–505 and the today line
is a 1px Accent-ink stroke at x=506, landing on the right stem of the **P**, whose bowl is cut. The
same collision at 393 (label from x137, line at x158), 1024 and 1366. Because the month is now
Accent ink and the today line is Accent ink, the two are the same value and merge into one mark:
the band reads "SEF|" or "SEP|" rather than as a month name and a now-line.

Round 1 sampled this label as Muted mixed-case "Sep"; the caps change made it wider, so I read this
as introduced by the G1R1-05 fix rather than pre-existing — but I did not have a round-1 frame to
diff against, so treat the "new" as inferred and the collision as measured.

*Pack:* README Components, Calendar grid — "**Now is a 1px Accent-ink line.**" A line that means
*now* cannot also be a letterform. Hard rule 18 — "**Floating chrome never covers content or
controls** … every floating box is disjoint from every control box and from text". The today line
is the Gantt's own overlay and it is sitting on text.

*Fix in source:* the month band's label belongs at the month boundary, not at the range origin, and
it should be pushed clear of the today line — offset the first month's label by the today line's
width plus `space[1]` when they overlap, or drop the band's label to the right of the line and keep
the band's own divider at the boundary.

than beside either of them. The marker's text is also indented 14px past the task title it belongs
to, which is what makes it wrap in a 104px column at all: the title above it fits two lines in the
same space.

*Pack:* hard rule 24 — "**a separator never leads a line and an emphasised value never sits alone
(`lib/richText.tsx` `richRuns`, R-34; applied to card footers too, C-4)**". The rule as written
names the leading case; this is the mirror of it and the same orphaned separator. README Content —
"**Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces**", i.e. the dot joins two things on one line.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttBar.tsx`'s `WorkMark`, moved into the label column at G1R1-08
with its dot-plus-indent intact and no `richRuns` treatment.

*Fix in source:* run the marker through `richRuns` so the dot can never end a line; drop the 14px
indent so the marker starts on the title's own left edge (which alone is enough to fit "EA working ·
since 2:14am" — 135px of text at 1920 — inside 104px over two lines with the dot mid-line); and
align the dot to the first line's baseline rather than to the block.

---

**G1R2-05 · LOW · the Unscheduled lane is the only lane still typeset as meta.**
All 8 frames. "Unscheduled" sampled `(137,133,126)` — Muted, sentence case, untracked — sitting
directly under four lane headings that are now Accent-ink tracked caps. It is a lane: the element
carries `testID="gantt-lane-unscheduled"`. From the frame it reads as a caption on the list below
it, not as the fifth group in the chart.

*Pack:* README Type — "**Section label: 11.5 / 1, uppercase, letter-spacing .08em, Accent ink.**"
README Principle 4 — "**Small type, clear hierarchy.**" Two objects of the same rank get the same
treatment or the hierarchy is not one.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttUnscheduled.tsx:52` renders `<Txt kind="meta"
testID="gantt-lane-unscheduled">Unscheduled</Txt>` while `GanttChart.tsx:124` renders every other
lane as `<Txt kind="label">`. The G1R1-02 fix landed in one file of two.

*Fix in source:* `kind="label"` on the Unscheduled heading, with the same `marginTop` the other
lanes get. One word.

---

**G1R2-06 · LOW · the month band now wears the lane heading's token, so "SEP" and "JSTACK" are the
same kind of object.**
All 8 frames. Both are Accent-ink uppercase at ~11.5px with `.08em` tracking; at 1920 "SEP" (x486,
y249–258) sits 55px right of and 55px above "JSTACK" (x245, y302–318) and the eye groups them as one
list of headings — a time scale and a project name at the same rank. Neither is tappable.

*Pack:* README Principle 3 — "**Colour means you can act.** … **Nothing decorative gets colour.**"
The pack spends Accent ink on section labels by name; a lane heading qualifies, a month tick on a
scale does not obviously. Hard rule 20 — "**a heading is a step of the scale (R-24)**": the month
band is not the same step as a lane.

*Unsure, and saying so:* this is the least certain finding in the round. The month band genuinely
needed to separate from the week band, promoting it did that, and an argument that the month *is*
the axis's section label is respectable. What I am confident about is the pair: G1R1-01's fix moved
one token off three meanings, and G1R1-05's fix put a second token onto two. If you take only one
action here, make it G1R2-02 (the collision), which is the part that actually hurts to read.

*Fix in source:* keep the month distinct from the week without borrowing the lane's token — Muted
at 500 in caps with the same tracking, or Ink at meta size. `components/tasks/GanttAxis.tsx`.

---

**G1R2-07 · LOW · the Unscheduled rows still stretch the full card width for two words.**
All 8 frames. Rows measured 33–359 (327px) at 393 and 245–1267 (1023px) at 1920, seven of them, all
36px, 3px apart, each holding one short left-aligned Muted phrase. "Book dentist" is 1023px wide at
1920. Now that they are transparent with a dashed edge, the shape they most resemble is an empty
text field awaiting input.

*Pack:* checklist 7 — "**1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns**"; README Layout —
"**Do not stretch cards to match heights.**" README Components, Habit chip — "**Chips wrap in a
6px-gap row**", which is the pack's own shape for a set of short movable labels.

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttUnscheduled.tsx` — the rows are children of a plain vertical
`View` with `gap: space[1]`, so each takes the container's full width.

*Fix in source:* `flexDirection: "row", flexWrap: "wrap", gap: 6` on the container and
`alignSelf: "flex-start"` on the row, so each hugs its words. Seven ghost chips in two wrapped rows
read as seven things waiting for a date; seven full-bleed bars read as a table with one empty column.

---

**G1R2-08 · LOW · the weekend is the page's ground painted inside the card, so it reads as a recess
through the card rather than a tint on it — clearest in dark.**
All 8 frames; strongest at `tasks-gantt-d1-1920-dark-prod.png` (four full-height `(25,24,21)`
columns against a `(43,42,39)` card, in a plot that is otherwise empty) and at
`tasks-gantt-d1-1024-dark-prod.png`, where a slab clipped in half at the plot edge reads as a dark
panel welded to the card's right side rather than as a Saturday and a Sunday.

*Pack:* README Principle 5 — "**Calm surfaces. Frosted cards on a warm stone ground.**" README
Surfaces — "**The card-to-ground step is deliberately small: one visible layer, no float.**" The
one step the pack defines is card-above-ground; using exactly that pair *inside* a card reproduces
the app's only depth cue as a chart fill, so the mark says "the card is not here" rather than
"this is a weekend". Contrast is also very low for a *fill*: **1.111:1** light — lower than the
1.13:1 day tick I called invisible in round 1, carried only by its area.

*Unsure, and saying so:* this is a judgement, not a measurement failure, and it is strictly better
than round 1's Accent soft. If you leave it, leave it — it is tolerable. If you touch it, the
cheapest change that keeps the neutral and loses the recess is a Hairline-alpha overlay
(`rgba(43,42,38,.05)` light / `rgba(255,255,255,.04)` dark) on the card rather than the ground
colour: same chroma-free warmth, no borrowed depth cue. `components/tasks/GanttAxis.tsx`.

All 8 frames. Measured corner run ≈5px. The comment in source is right that 6 was unchosen; 5 is on

row-as-button drawn in the ghost idiom.

*Pack:* README Surfaces — "**Ghost (a section without a feed): 1px dashed Hairline, radius 10,
Muted text**"; "**Radii: 10 cards, bars, icon buttons · 8 buttons, chips, rows-as-buttons, insets ·
5 tags and checkboxes**".

*Root cause:* `components/tasks/GanttUnscheduled.tsx:111` `borderRadius: radius.tag`.

*Fix in source:* `radius.card` (10) to match the ghost the row is imitating, or `radius.control` (8)
if G1R2-07 turns them into chips — a chip is 8.

## V2.2 K-1 delta

Reviewed 9 September 2026. Scope: the eight `demo/v22/find-d1-*-prod.png` frames only. The
global Find surface — `components/chrome/FindDialog.tsx` behind the `find` (modal, ≥768) and
`find-phone` (screen, <768) registry entries, searched for "steve". Nothing else on any frame
was judged; the page behind the scrim is another screen's review.

Already fixed before this pass and deliberately not re-reported: the title was not highlighted
because the index only ranged over the snippet. It is highlighted in all eight frames now.

| file | screen | width | scheme | verdict |

| find-d1-393-light-prod.png | Find (phone screen) | 393 | light | defects — K1-01, K1-02, K1-05, K1-06, K1-07, K1-09, K1-10, K1-11, K1-12 |
| find-d1-393-dark-prod.png | Find (phone screen) | 393 | dark | defects — as light, plus K1-08 |
| find-d1-1024-light-prod.png | Find (modal) | 1024 | light | defects — K1-03, K1-04, K1-05, K1-06, K1-07, K1-10, K1-11, K1-12 |

No frame is clean. **1366 light is the closest to fine** — nothing is clipped, nothing collides,

### Measurements taken

Panel boxes at all four widths in both schemes; content-band maps down each frame at 1px
resolution; side and top padding at 393 against three other 393 phone frames from the same

---

### K1-01 · The 393 frames are 2545px tall and cannot be used to judge the phone — rig, not layout · `find-d1-393-light-prod.png`, `find-d1-393-dark-prod.png`

**Your first question, answered: it is the capture rig, and here is the proof.** Find's own
content on the phone ends at **y=708**. Between y=709 and y=2523 there is not one pixel that
differs from the ground in either scheme — I scanned every row. The demo watermark, which is
positioned against the viewport, is pinned at y=2524–2534, i.e. to the *bottom of a 2545px
viewport*. Nothing in Find can produce 2545px from 708px of content.

The mechanism is in `tools/capture-v2.mjs`. `shot()` decides not to grow the viewport when it
finds `[data-testid$="-backdrop"]`. `find` is a `modal` and has one — which is why the 1024,
1366 and 1920 frames are honest 768/900/1080 viewports. `find-phone` is a `screen`, and a
screen has no backdrop, so the rig fell through to `needed = max(scrollHeight of every inner
scroller)` and picked up the Today scroller still mounted behind the opaque screen surface.
Today at 393 measures 2325px tall in `demo/v21/today-d1-393-light-prod.png`; Find's frame is
2545. Same order, different screen. This is the exact second cost the rig's own comment already
documents for overlays — the detector just does not cover the `screen` kind.

**What it costs.** At a real 393×852 the content (708px) fits with 144px to spare and never
scrolls, so nothing is *broken*. But the frame cannot answer the questions a 393 frame exists to
answer: where the watermark sits relative to the content, whether the ground reaches under the
safe area, whether the list scrolls, or what the density feels like in a phone-shaped window. It
is one of two widths in the pass and it is currently unjudgeable. The same hole will silently
mis-capture Talk, the other `screen`-kind entry.

**Smallest fix.** Widen the overlay test in `shot()` from the backdrop testid to "a registry
overlay of any kind is open" — e.g. also treat a visible `ScreenSurface` root as an overlay, or
have `ScreenSurface` render a `-backdrop`-suffixed testid node the way `Dialog` does, so one rule
covers both kinds. Then re-shoot 393.

*(Everything below that is attributed to a 393 frame was measured on the top 708px, which is laid
out at true 393 metrics and is unaffected by the grown height.)*

---

### K1-02 · Find's phone screen is on a different grid from every other phone screen · `find-d1-393-light-prod.png`, `find-d1-393-dark-prod.png`

Measured, first ink from the left and top edges on the same capture pass:

| screen | first content x | first content y |
|---|---|---|
| tasks-list-d1-393-light-prod.png | 20 | 22 |
| tasks-done-d1-393-light-prod.png | 20 | 22 |
| **find-d1-393-light-prod.png** | **9** | **44** |

Every element in Find's phone screen — title, field, chips, segment, group labels, cards, close
button — runs 9 → 383. Everything on every other phone screen runs 20 → 373. And Find starts its
title 44px down where the rest of the app starts 22px down.

Breaks: *"Page padding: 24 top, 32 sides, 80 bottom (desktop); `calc(env(safe-area-inset-top,0px)
+ 22px)` top, 20 sides, 120 bottom (phone, clears the bar)."*

**What it costs.** This is precisely the "some things centred, some left-aligned" read. Open Find
from Tasks and every card on the screen jumps 11px left while the header drops 22px — the app
stops feeling like one app for as long as Find is up. Half the pack's phone side margin also puts
row text and the chevron nearer the physical edge than anywhere else in the product.

**Smallest fix.** `FindDialog.tsx`, the phone branch: `paddingHorizontal: space[4]` is 9
(`theme/tokens.ts`, `space["4"] = 9`) and `paddingTop: 44` is a literal. Use the app's phone page
padding helper — the one the tab screens already use — for both the sides and the top, rather than
a raw space token and a magic number.

---

### K1-03 · At 1024 the demo watermark sits on top of the modal and beside a result title · `find-d1-1024-light-prod.png`, `find-d1-1024-dark-prod.png`

The watermark chip runs x 8–192, y ≈700–720. The modal's left edge is x=174 and its bottom edge
is y=709. The chip therefore covers the modal's bottom-left corner (roughly 174–192 × 700–709)
and its right end lands immediately left of the PEOPLE row's "Steve" title at x=204. At 10× the
chip visibly overlaps the panel's rounded corner. This is a genuine 1024×768 render — the modal
carries a backdrop, so the rig did not grow this viewport and the collision is what a person sees.
Clear at 1366 (panel bottom 795, watermark ~843) and at 1920 (885 vs ~1023); 1024 is the only
width where the panel reaches far enough down to meet it.

Breaks the A-1 watermark rule — *"bottom-left, on every screen … It must be legible and must not
sit over a control or another line"* — the same class as B-32.

**What it costs.** A demo mark printed across a live surface reads as a rendering fault, and at
1024 it lands on the one row that is already half cut off, so the bottom-left corner of the modal
is three overlapping things at once.

**Smallest fix.** Give the watermark a z-order below the modal layer, or offset it while a modal is
open. Fixing K1-04 (the panel's height at 1024) also separates them.

---

### K1-04 · At 1024 the panel ends mid-row and the list never says it has ended · `find-d1-1024-light-prod.png`, `find-d1-1024-dark-prod.png`

Panel 58–709 (652 tall) against 691 at both 1366 and 1920 — the shortest panel of the three, at
the width where the chrome above the results costs most. The PEOPLE·1 row's "Steve" is sliced
through the middle of its glyphs by the panel's bottom edge; 6½ of 7 result rows are visible.
There is a 5px scrollbar thumb, so the rest is reachable — but nothing tells you the list is
finished. The end-of-list sentence in `FindDialog.tsx` only renders when `response.truncated ===
true`, and this search is not truncated, so at 1024 the surface ends on a bisected word with no
statement either way.

Breaks: *"2. Say when the list ends. 'That's all until 4pm.' Blank space after it is correct, not
a gap to fill."* At 393 the blank space after the last card *is* the statement, correctly. At 1024
there is no blank space and no statement.

**What it costs.** A person at 1024 cannot tell whether PEOPLE·1 is the last group or the first of
five more, which is the one thing a search result list has to be honest about.

**Smallest fix.** Two parts: raise the panel's height allowance at short viewports (58px of dead
margin above and below a panel that is clipping content is the wrong trade at 768), and render a
calm end line whenever the groups are complete — not only when the cap bit.

---

### K1-05 · The REPLIES row's title is an unclamped 139-character paragraph and outranks the real titles · all eight frames

The reply's title — *"Steve is back from leave on Saturday. Last time you two spoke about Bali he
asked for the dates in writing first — they are in the trip note."* — is 139 characters and is
rendered in the title slot with no clamp. Measured:

| width | lines | title run |
|---|---|---|
| 1920 | **1** | 760px (~122 characters on one line) |
| 1366 | **1** | 769px |
| 1024 | 2 | 630px + 268px |
| 393 | 3 | ~3 × 350px |

At 1366 and 1920 it reads, in the sense that you can decode it — but it does not read as a *title*.
It is a 120-character measure at 12.5px, roughly twice the comfortable maximum, and because it is
the widest and longest thing in the list it is the first thing the eye lands on, above "Bali
deposit to Steve", which is the row that actually matters. At 393 it makes the reply row three
times the height of its neighbours and breaks the list's rhythm.

Breaks the waiting-row contract: *"Title truncates with ellipsis."* And principle 4: *"Small type,
clear hierarchy. … Three levels: title, body, meta."* A paragraph in the title level collapses the
three levels into one.

**What it costs.** The list stops being scannable at exactly the row that carries the most words,
and a person reads a whole paragraph to learn something a first clause would have told them.

**Smallest fix.** Two lines, both in `FindRow.tsx`: `numberOfLines={2}` on the title `Body` (nested
`<Text>` runs clamp correctly on RNW, so the highlight survives), and a `maxWidth` of about 720 on
the inner text `View` so that at 1366 and 1920 the reply wraps at a readable measure instead of
running the full panel. The 720 cap costs the short titles nothing — "Bali deposit to Steve"
measures 115px.

---

### K1-06 · The group labels float between the cards instead of belonging to the card below · all eight frames

Ink-to-ink, measured at 1366 (BRAIN·1, and the same at every group and every width):

- card above, bottom **452** → label top **460** = **8px**
- label bottom **468** → its card top **478** = **10px**

The label is 8px from the card it does *not* describe and 10px from the card it does. An eye
cannot resolve a 2px difference, so every label reads as sitting in an undifferentiated 8/10
rhythm and the five groups run together as one list.

Breaks: *"Between a section label and its card: 8. Between sections: 8 + margin-top 8 on the next
label (16 visual)."* The pack asks for 16 above and 8 below — a 2:1 ratio. The frames have roughly
0.8:1.

On the rest of your question 3 — weight, size and colour are correct. `TASKS · 2` measures a 9px
cap (≈11.5–12px uppercase), tracked, and samples `#4B5E70` light / `#AFBFCF` dark, which are
Accent ink in both schemes. Only the spacing is wrong, and it is the spacing that is doing the
grouping work.

**Smallest fix.** `FindDialog.tsx`: the group `View`s sit in a `gap: space[3]` (8) stack with the
`ListCard` at `marginTop: 6`. Take the label's own top margin to 16 (or set the outer gap to 16
and the card's `marginTop` to 8, which is the pack's own arithmetic).

---

### K1-07 · The match highlight is the same ink as links and section labels, and one row is now entirely accent · all eight frames

The highlight samples `(81,100,118)` light and `(179,196,211)` dark — the same `accentInk` token
as `TASKS · 2` three lines above it and as every link in the app. Contrast is fine (5.91:1 light,
6.66:1 dark on card), so this is not a legibility finding.

It is a meaning finding, and the PEOPLE row shows it plainly: that result's title is the single
word "Steve", the query matched all of it, so the entire title renders in accent ink. That row is
now the only row in the list with no Ink anywhere in it, and its title is indistinguishable from a
link. In the REPLIES row the paragraph opens on an accent "Steve", which reads as a link at the
head of a sentence.

Breaks: *"3. Colour means you can act. The steel accent marks verbs, labels, the recommended option
and the current tab. Nothing decorative gets colour."* and the enumeration *"Accent ink: section
labels, primary-verb text, links, expiry text, recommended option number, active tab, provenance
links."* A match highlight is none of those, and the whole row is the tap target — the highlighted
word is not separately actionable.

I am confident the highlight is right and the *tone* is wrong; I am less sure which replacement you
want, so treat the fix as a proposal. **Smallest fix:** highlight with an Accent-soft background
wash on the matched run and leave the glyphs in Ink. That keeps title colour meaning "title",
keeps accent ink meaning "you can tap this", and shows the match more clearly than a hue shift
does — particularly in dark, where the highlight and plain title ink are only ~1.4:1 apart in
luminance and the distinction is carried almost entirely by hue.

---

### K1-08 · The `sensitive` tag is the smallest and least legible text on the surface · all four dark frames primarily; the size applies to all eight

Measured at 1920: the tag box is 51 × 17px (x1297–1347, y453–469), with a corner radius of ~5px —
**that part is correct** against *"Radii: … 5 tags and checkboxes"*, which I checked because it
looks like a capsule at a glance and is not. The problem is inside it.

- **Size.** The label's tallest glyph runs y458→464 = 7px of ascender, against 8px of cap height
  for the 10.5px meta line and 9px for the 12.5px title in the same row. That puts the tag at
  **≈9.5px**. Breaks: *"Rules: body never below 10.5px."* (The pack's one 10px allowance is
  *"Badge: 10 white on Marker"* — a count badge on a saturated fill, not a word on a card.)
- **Contrast, dark.** Tag text `(213,118,92)` on card `(56,55,52)` = **3.73:1**. The pack's own
  floor for its smallest text is *"Muted on Card 4.6:1"*. Light measures 4.63:1 and just clears.

**What it costs.** The one word that tells a person a result is private is the hardest word on the
screen to read, and in dark it is below the pack's floor. On the rest of your question 5:
placement and competition with the chevron are **fine** — the tag sits right-aligned with 6px to
the chevron, the chevron is Muted at 16px, and at no width do they collide or read as one control.

**Smallest fix.** Take the tag label to 10.5 and darken the dark-scheme Alert tone used for tag
text (or give the tag an Alert-soft fill so the text can sit at full Alert weight against it).
Check whether `Tag tone="alert"` is used elsewhere before changing the token — this may be an
app-wide tag defect that Find is merely the first frame to show at this size.

### K1-09 · The only way out of the full-screen phone Find is a 33px target · `find-d1-393-light-prod.png`, `find-d1-393-dark-prod.png`

The close button's fill measures x351–383, y43–75 — **33 × 33px**.

Breaks: *"Tap targets 36px minimum on phone."*

**What it costs.** On the desktop modal there are three ways out (the ✕, the backdrop, Escape). On
the phone screen the tab bar is hidden and there is no backdrop, so this button is the only exit,
and it is under the minimum and — after K1-02's 9px padding — closer to the physical screen edge
than any other control in the app. A missed tap on a full-screen surface with no other way out is
a person stuck.

**Smallest fix.** `IconBtn` at 36 in the phone branch of `FindDialog.tsx`, and let K1-02's padding
fix pull it in from the edge.

### K1-10 · The three filter rows are unevenly spaced · all eight frames

Ink-to-ink, 1366: field bottom 227 → chips top 235 = **8px**; chips bottom 270 → segment top 287 =
**17px**. Same at 393 (7px, then 17px) and at 1920. All three are children of one `gap: space[3]`
(8) stack, so the 17 is something the chips row is carrying underneath itself.

Breaks: *"4px base. Used values: 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 32."* — 17 is not one of
them — and the general rhythm the Spacing section sets.

**What it costs.** Small, but it is the "amateur" tell: two identical-looking gaps that are not
identical. It also makes the segment read as belonging to the results rather than to the filters.

**Smallest fix.** Find the stray margin or padding under `FocusChips` and remove it, or set the
three gaps explicitly.

---

### K1-11 · The group counts are inline text where every other section label in the app uses a Marker badge · all eight frames

`TASKS · 2`, `BRAIN · 1` and the rest render the count as a middot and a numeral inside the label.
The pack specifies the count as a component of the section label: *"Section label `.js-label` —
11.5px tracked caps in Accent ink, padding 0 2. Count badge: 16px tall pill, Marker fill, white
10px."* and *"Marker: count badge next to a section label; mic orb while listening. Nowhere else."*
The Needs-you label on the Today frames behind the scrim in these same captures carries the badge;
Find does not.

**I am not certain this is a defect and I am naming it as one anyway.** The pack does not say every
label must carry a badge, and a count of 1 or 2 in a search result is arguably not the same object
as a count of open decisions. But a person moving between Today and Find sees the same
tracked-caps label render its number two different ways, and consistency of a named component is
what the pack exists to hold.

**Smallest fix.** If it should match: use the `Label` badge slot with the count. If it should not:
add a row to `DISCREPANCIES.md` saying search-group counts are text and why, so the next reviewer
does not raise it again.

---

### K1-12 · Meta separators mix a comma and a middot in the same line · all eight frames

The DECISIONS row's meta reads `Steve's email, 2 Sep · your voice · 34 words` — a comma where the
first separator should be a middot.

Breaks: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`."*

**What it costs.** Very little on its own; it is on the list because it is the one content-voice
slip in the surface and it is one character.

**Smallest fix.** It is snippet text from the search index, not layout — fix it where the decision
snippet is composed rather than in `FindRow.tsx`.

### Answers to the questions that did not become defects

**Q2, density and hierarchy — three filter rows above the first result.** Measured as chrome above
the first result card, as a share of the surface:

| width | surface | chrome above first row | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 393 | 852 (true viewport) | 248px | 29% |
| 1024 | 652 panel | 246px | **38%** |
| 1366 | 691 panel | 246px | 36% |
| 1920 | 691 panel | 246px | 36% |

The chrome is a *fixed* 246px at every desktop width, so it costs most where the panel is
shortest — 1024, which is also the only width that clips (K1-04). At 1366 and 1920 the ratio is
fine and I would not change it. At 393 the 29% includes 44px of doubled top padding that K1-02
gives back for free. So: **not too much chrome in principle, but wrong at 1024**, and the cheapest
route there is the panel height rather than removing a filter. If you do want a row back, the
chips row uses 332px of an 857px line at 1920 — the sensitivity segment could share it above 1180.

**Q6, dark mode.** Layout parity is exact. I compared band positions down all four dark frames
against their light twins: every element top matches to the pixel (1024: 85/144/188/240/286/304/
431/511/606/686; 1366: 132/191/235/287/333/351/478/540/558/638/718; 1920 likewise). No reflow, no
column change, nothing appears or disappears. Tokens are right: the dark ground samples exactly
`(25,24,21)` = `#191815` warm, not black; card `(43,42,39)`; the light ground `(237,235,229)` =
`#EDEBE5` and card `(247,247,244)`, which is `rgba(255,255,255,.58)` over that ground to the
integer. The accent highlight is legible in dark (6.66:1). The only dark-specific failure is the
`sensitive` tag at 3.73:1 (K1-08).

**Q5, the sensitive tag's placement.** Fine, as noted in K1-08 — right-aligned, 6px clear of the
chevron, never colliding at any width, and it does not read as one control with the chevron.

**Q7, wrapping and clipping.** Nothing is hyphenated mid-word at any width. No button, chip or
segment label is clipped or ellipsised — I measured the segment at 393, the tightest case: the
track runs 9–383 in thirds of 125px, the "All" pill sits at 12–134 with a 3px inset, and the two
unselected labels run 161–231 and 282–356, centred in their thirds to within 2.5px with 27px of
clearance at the right. No orphan lines: the reply's last line at 393 is "they are in the trip
note." and at 1024 "writing first — they are in the trip note.". Everything in the phone screen
aligns to a single 9–383 grid — the grid is the wrong one (K1-02), but it is internally consistent.

**Deliberately not raised.** The modal is centred at every desktop width (1920: x510–1409, dead
centre; 1366: 233 left / 234 right). The pack's *"Don't: … centred layouts on desktop"* is about
page layout, and the brief specifies a centred modal at 768 and up. Correct, not a defect. The
tag's 5px radius, checked and correct. The `Everything` chip's selected state, the segment's
selected-pill treatment, and the scrollbar (5px thumb) all match the pack.

**Could not be judged from these frames.** The blur budget under 768 — the phone `screen` paints an
opaque ground, so any backdrop blur behind it leaves no trace in a capture; it needs a devtools or
profiler check, not a pixel one. And the desktop placeholder (*"Find anything — a task, a capture,
a file, a person"*) never appears, because every frame has "steve" already typed.

`UX REVIEW: DEFECTS FOUND`

### 2 · Defects, ranked

#### X1-01 · At 1024 the new Files section pushes the task card's only two verbs off the bottom of the dialog — IN SCOPE, fix now

**Frames.** `task-detail-d1-1024-light-prod.png`, `task-detail-d1-1024-dark-prod.png`.

**Measured.** The dialog occupies y 58–710 (luminance probe down x = 500; below 710 is the dimmed
Tasks page). Inside it the FILES label ink is y 589–597 and the Files card starts at y 618. That
card is 99 px tall — measured on the 1920 frame where the whole dialog fits without a scrollbar,
card y 698–797, two single-line rows — so at 1024 it ends at ≈717, **7 px past the dialog's visible
edge**: the second file row's bottom padding and the card's bottom corner are cut. The verb row is
36 px tall and sits 9 px under the Files card (1920: card bottom 797, "Delegate to EA" fill
806–841), so at 1024 it occupies y ≈726–762 — **its top is 16 px below the visible edge and its
bottom 52 px below. None of it is on screen when the card opens.**

Without the Files block the arithmetic is comfortable: at 1920 the run from the "+ subtask" card's
bottom (646) to the verb row's top (806) is 160 px, of which the Files block is 128 px
(label ink 669 → card bottom 797) plus 32 px of gaps. Take it out and the 1024 verb row opens at
y ≈578–614, fully visible with 96 px to spare. X-1 added ~148 px above the verbs.

**Pack line it breaks.** `17_CC_V22_EXEC_PROMPT.md` hard rule 23: *"The width you did not run is
the width that fails … the board, the Gantt, Talk and Find are judged at 393, 1024, 1366 and 1920
at their ★ row, and 1024 reads as a tablet."* And README Principles 1: *"One thing at a time. The
first decision is open."* — a card whose verbs are below the fold is not open.

**Root cause.** X-1 inserted Files between "+ subtask" and the verb row, inside the scrolling body,
on the one width where `Dialog`'s maxHeight leaves only ~652 px of body (K1-03's constraint). The
verb row was already mid-scroll (ACTIVITY follows it) — this row pushed it past the edge.

**Smallest honest fix.** Move the Files section **below** the verb row in the task-detail
composition (between the verbs and ACTIVITY, or after ACTIVITY). One reorder; nothing else moves,
no other width changes. Pinning the verb row as a dialog footer outside the scroll area is the
better structural answer but it is a `Dialog` change and belongs with K1-03, not here.

**Does it make K1-03 worse?** The watermark collision itself is unchanged — at 1024 the chip
measures x 8–192, y 691–719 and the Files card's left edge is x 193, so the chip still clears the
dialog's content by ~1 px in both schemes, exactly as before. What changed is *what the 709 px edge
cuts*: it used to cut ACTIVITY, which is a log; it now cuts a file row and the two verbs, which are
the point of the card. So: no worse geometrically, materially worse in consequence.

---

#### X1-02 · Brain's Files section leaves column 2 running ~1,100 px past every other column — IN SCOPE, fix now

**Frames.** `brain-d1-1024`, `brain-d1-1366`, `brain-d1-1920`, both schemes (dark is identical to
the pixel — see §4).

**Measured** (light; ground `#EDEBE5` = (237,235,229), mic orb excluded from the column probes):

| width | col 1 ends | col 3 ends | col 2 ends | page height | col 2 running alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 571 (col 3 stacked under col 1) | — | 1603 | 1671 | **1,032 px · 62 % of the page** |
| 1366 | 329 | 370 | 1588 | 1656 | **1,218 px · 74 %** |
| 1920 | 329 | 342 | 1458 | 1526 | **1,116 px · 73 %** |

The Files block alone is 538 px at 1366 (label ink 1050 → card bottom 1588) and the same to within
8 px at 1024 and 1920. Remove it and the solo run roughly halves — 1366: 653 px; 1024: 484 px;
1920: 563 px. **X-1 doubled it.** At 1024 the consequence is a 423 px × 1,032 px blank slab
occupying the left half of a tablet while the right half scrolls a mile.

The second half of the cause is the row count. Files prints **ten** rows. Every other section on
the tab is capped and hands the remainder to a link: Latest in 3, Memory 4 + the hit-rate row,
Replies 2, Rules for my EA 4. Files carries the same `all` link and still prints its whole list, so
the link means nothing there.

At 393 the same block is 517 px (label ink ≈1344 → card bottom 1861) of a 2,270 px page — **23 % of
the phone page, 61 % of a phone screen**, for a reference list.

**Pack line it breaks.** README Layout: *"Columns flow top to bottom … Leave the bottom of a column
empty when the content ends."* The empty bottom is correct; a thousand pixels of it beside one
scrolling ribbon is not the layout that line describes. And the density rule for this review —
*"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns"* — fails: at 1920, 73 % of the page is one
phone column with 1,000 px of dead width beside it.

**Smallest honest fix.** Cap the Brain Files section at 4 rows, like Memory, and let `all` do the
job it does in every other section. That removes ~300 px from column 2 at every width and costs
nothing — the link is already there. If the full list is wanted on the tab, move Files to column 3
under Rules for my EA (which ends at 342–370 and has the whole page free beneath it) instead of
under Replies; that is a one-line change in `layout/sourcesBrain.ts` and it balances the page
without touching the data.

#### X1-03 · The attach control is a bare 10 × 15 px glyph in both places X-1 put it — IN SCOPE, fix now

**Frames.** All 16.

**Measured.** Task card, `task-detail-d1-1920-light-prod.png`: the attach ink is x 1370–1379,
y 667–681 — **10 × 15 px of glyph and nothing else.** No box, no radius, no border, no fill. Its
neighbour on the same card, the subtask `···`, is a proper icon button: a chromed box at
x ≈1352–1378 with a visible border and card fill. Brain capture field,
`brain-d1-393-light-prod.png`: the paperclip ink is x 269–278, y 186–200, sitting beside a
**30 × 30** accent-soft mic (x 296–325, y 175–204) and a **30 × 30** outlined send (x 330–359,
y 175–204). The gaps say the same thing: 18 px from the paperclip to the mic, 5 px from the mic to
the send — the paperclip is not read as part of the group, and it does not have the group's chrome.

**Pack lines it breaks.** README Components: *"Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: 32 or 36 square, radius 8
or 10, Card fill with Card border (header) or Hairline border (in cards), Muted glyph 17 or 18."*
And README Accessibility: *"Tap targets 36px minimum on phone."*

**Unsure about.** I cannot see a pressable's padding in a capture, so I cannot say the *touch*
target is 10 × 15. I can say the *visible* control is, and that it is the only one of three in the
Brain group without a box. Treat the tap-target half as unconfirmed and the reads-as-a-button half

#### X1-04 · The same file's meta reads in two different orders on the two surfaces X-1 touched — IN SCOPE, fix now

**Frames.** `task-detail-d1-393-light-prod.png` (Files rows, meta ink y 713–723 and 759–770) vs
`brain-d1-1366-light-prod.png` (Files rows 5 and 6).

**Measured.** Same file, same day, same pass:

- task card — `PDF · 217 KB · EA · Yesterday 11:40am` (kind · size · who · when)
- Brain — `EA · PDF · Yesterday 11:40am` (who · kind · when)

Inside Brain the kind vocabulary is mixed as well: `Document` (.docx), `Image` (.jpg), `Text`
(.md), `Spreadsheet` (.csv) are categories; `PDF` (.pdf) is a file format. A PDF is a document.

**Pack line it breaks.** Hard rule 21: *"No wire enum on screen, no copy in three places … Every
enum that reaches a row has one label map with a Jest test that every member has a label."* This is
also a second instance of carried **B2-07** ("Three workouts" meta differs between board and list) —
the row created a new one rather than making the old one worse.

**Smallest honest fix.** One `fileMeta` composer used by both rows and one kind label map. If size
only fits on the task card, drop it there rather than reordering the other three parts.

**Measured** (light, label ink bottom → card top):

|---|---|---|---|
| 393 | 404 → 415 = 11 px | 663 → 684 = **21 px** | 10 |

#### X1-06 · The chip row FL-06 emptied does not balance: a 15 px tag top-aligned against a 30 px button — IN SCOPE (you asked), low

**Measured.** `task-detail-d1-1920-light-prod.png`: the "Work" tag runs y 369–383 (15 px tall), the
"Twenty" button runs y 369–398 (30 px). **Both start at 369** — the row is top-aligned, so the tag

**Honest scope note.** This predates X-1 — removing the "Dropbox folder" button does not change a
row's cross-axis alignment — but you asked whether the row still balances without it, and the
answer is no: it is now two items of very different heights with nothing between them to disguise
the ragged bottom.

**Smallest honest fix.** `alignItems: "center"` on that row. One line.

### 4 · The four things you asked me to judge

**Q1 · Two links in one section-heading slot — right, do not touch.**
At 1366 the `all` ink runs x 919–929 and `configure` x 958–1004: a **29 px** gap against a ~3 px
word space at 11 px, so they read as two controls, not one phrase. `configure` is flush at the
column edge (1004) — exactly where REPLIES' lone `configure` sits (958–1004) — and both are Accent
ink, which is what DISCREPANCIES row 10 requires of the `right` slot (*"`right` is Accent ink flush
at the column edge, for anything with an `onPress`"*). At 393 the pair measures the same:
`all` 287–299, `configure` 327–373, gap 28, flush to the 373 content edge. Vertical alignment is
right too (label ink 1050–1058, both links on that line). Against the badge: there **is** no badge
here — see the note below — so nothing collides.

Two things worth knowing without changing anything: `all` now sits **75 px left** of where `all`
sits on MEMORY (994–1003) in the same column, so the same word doing the same job has two positions
on one screen; and **FILES is the only section on Brain with neither a count badge nor a
descriptive hint**, while carrying by far the longest list (10 rows against Memory's 4, Latest in's
3, Replies' 2, Rules' 4). If X1-02's cap lands, a Marker badge showing the real count would make
that section read like its neighbours. I am unsure enough not to call it a defect.

**Q2 · Three icon buttons in the capture field at 393 — not crowded, but not a group either.**
Nothing collides: the placeholder's first line ends at x ≈235 and the paperclip ink starts at 269,
**34 px clear**, which satisfies hard rule 24's *"a placeholder is measured against its field"*.
The paperclip does read as a paperclip at that size (10 × 15 px of ink, unambiguous in the zoom).
What it does not read as is a *button* — X1-03.

On "does the group still make the send arrow the obvious primary": **no, and it never did.**
Measured glyph-against-local-background contrast at 393 — paperclip **2.95 : 1**, mic **2.27 : 1**,
send **1.34 : 1** (light); 2.74 / 2.62 / 1.37 (dark). The send arrow is almost certainly rendered
disabled on an empty field (README States: *"Disabled: opacity .45"*), so its faintness is correct
behaviour, and the pack never made it primary anyway — handoff, Brain: *"mic (accent-soft) and
arrow_upward (outlined) 30px buttons"*. What X-1 changed is that **at rest the brightest glyph in
the group is now the paperclip**. Fix the chrome (X1-03) and the hierarchy is fine; do not restyle
the arrow.

**Q3 · The task card's Files meta at 393 — right, do not touch, but the case you asked about is not
in the pass.**
Widest meta rendered is `PDF · 1.8 MB · Josh · Mon 7 Sep, 9:05am` at **181 px** inside a **331 px**
content box (card x 16–371, 12 px padding each side) — 55 % of the line, 150 px of headroom. No
wrap, no ellipsis, nothing cut mid-word, at either scheme.

**But no frame in this pass carries the fifth `[subtask]` part, and no frame carries a long file
name.** At 10.5 px a subtask title like "Draft the covering note" adds ≈130–150 px, which puts the
line at ≈320 px against 331 — right on the edge, and over it for anything longer. Nor does any
frame show the "Nothing here yet" empty state. Under hard rule 22 (*"Captures are a proof only when
the rig is clean … the V2.2 pass … includes the driven states"*) that is a coverage gap, not a
clean result: drive a fixture with a subtask-linked file, a 40-character name, and an empty Files
section before this row closes.

**Q4 · Density.**
- **393 task card — fine.** The verbs land at y 792–819, 33 px clear of the viewport bottom and 7 px
  clear of the watermark chip (826–843), disjoint in both schemes. Only ACTIVITY falls below the
  fold, which is a log.
- **1024 task card — not fine.** X1-01.
- **393 Brain — the page grew to 2,270 px**, of which the new Files block is 517 px (23 %). See

complete content is: title · meta · rename · priority segment · Start/End · tags · SUBTASKS ·

#### New — what the reorder and the cap introduced

**X1-10 · The ACTIVITY label now sits 3 px under the Files card and 12 px above its own — HIGH,
caused by the reorder.**
**Frames.** `task-detail-d1-1366-{light,dark}`, `task-detail-d1-1920-{light,dark}` (at 393 and
1024 ACTIVITY is below the fold, so the fault is invisible there — it is not absent).

**Measured.** 1920: FILES card bottom border **849**, ACTIVITY label ink **852–860**, ACTIVITY card
top **872**. Gap above the label **3 px**; gap below it **12 px**. 1366: card bottom **778**, label
ink **781–789**, card **801** — **3 px** above, 12 below. Light and dark agree to the pixel.
Correcting ink to line box (11.5 / 1 caps, ~1.5 px of leading each side) makes the gap above
**≈1.5 px**.

**Baseline.** In the committed pre-X-1 frame the same label had **12 px** above it (verb box bottom
758 → label ink 770) and 12 below — symmetric. The reorder took 9 px off the top gap and left the
bottom alone, so a label that used to belong equally to both now visually belongs to the card
**above** it. On a card where a section label is the only thing telling you a new section has
started, that is a grouping error, not a rounding error.

**Pack line it breaks.** README Spacing: *"Between cards in a column: 8. Between a section label and
its card: 8. Between sections: 8 + margin-top 8 on the next label (16 visual)."* The spec is 16
visual between sections; this is 3.

**Root cause.** The rhythm was being supplied by the verb row's bottom margin. Moving the Files
section between the verbs and ACTIVITY put a card there instead, and the Files section carries no
bottom margin of its own.

**Fix in source.** Put the between-sections margin on the section wrapper rather than on the verb
row — `marginTop: space[4]` (16) on every section label in the task-detail composition, ACTIVITY
included — so the rhythm survives any future reorder. One change, and it also removes the ad-hoc
19 px the FILES heading currently gets.

**X1-11 · At 1366 the card no longer fits, and the fold cuts ACTIVITY's meta mid-glyph — MEDIUM;
X-1's as a whole, not the round-2 reorder's.**

**Measured.** The dialog's visible content edge is **y 832**. The ACTIVITY card opens at 801, its
title ink runs 818–825 and its meta line (`EA · Yesterday 9:00am`) is sliced at 832 with about its
top 3 px showing — a row of half-letters along the dialog's bottom edge. The nominal stack ends at
852, so the card overflows by **20 px**. The committed pre-X-1 frame at 1366 fits entirely: no
scroll thumb, dialog ends at 767, ACTIVITY card 700–751 whole. X-1 added ~101 px at this width and
tipped it over.

**Pack line it breaks.** This review's text rule — *"No clipped or ellipsised label"* — and hard
rule 24, *"nothing is cut mid-word"*. A scroll fold is allowed to cut; landing it through the
x-height of a line so that only ascender tips show is the worst possible place for it.

**Fix in source.** 20 px is the whole gap. Closing X1-10 (−9) and X1-05's overhang (−9 to −12)
recovers it without touching `Dialog`; the card fits at 1366 again. That is the cheapest argument
for fixing the two spacing findings.

**X1-12 · Brain's FILES section now truncates and nothing says how many — LOW, caused by the cap.**
All eight Brain frames. FILES is the only section on the tab carrying **neither a count badge nor a
hint**: MEMORY `4`, REPLIES `2`, RULES FOR MY EA `4` all carry Marker badges, LATEST IN carries the
hint *"what came in, where it went"*. Before the cap this was cosmetic — the list was complete.
Now four rows of ten are shown and the only signal that six are missing is a word, `all`, that
reads the same whether it means "see them again" or "see the other six". I raised this in round 1
under Q1 and declined to call it a defect; the cap is what makes it one.

**Pack line.** README Type: *"Badge: 10 white on Marker"*, and this review's colour rule — Marker is
*"only on count badges and the live mic"*, which is what every sibling section here uses it for.
This also extends carried **K1-11**.

**Fix in source.** Give the section the real total in a Marker badge, as its four siblings do.

#### On the e2e measurement in place of a frame

**Fair for half of what I asked, and I still want the frame for the other half.**

What `e2e/core/files.spec.ts` settles, it settles better than a screenshot would: a box-containment
assertion on the longest meta at 393 is exact where my round-1 pixel estimate (~320 px against a
331 px content box) was arithmetic, and it runs on every commit instead of once. 393 is also the
right width to pick — that is where the meta is widest relative to its container. Accept it as the
answer to *does it overflow*.

What it does not answer:

- **Whether a wrapped meta reads.** "Inside the row's box, no ellipsis" is satisfied by a meta that
  wraps to three lines. Round 1's question was whether the fifth part leaves the line legible, and
  a wrap is precisely where hard rule 24 bites — *"a separator never leads a line"* — which no box
  assertion can see. A wrapped meta is also exactly where carried **B2-02** lives.
- **A long file name.** The test drives the longest *meta*; the name is a separate line and a
  separate overflow.
- **The empty state.** "Nothing here yet" is still uncaptured on both surfaces.
- **The EA's report card and its file chips.** Still absent from every frame at every width — the
  1920 dialog shows the complete card and there is no report in it — so round 1's question, whether
  the report's chips and the Files section read as one repeated list, is unanswered a second time.

Under hard rule 22 those four remain a coverage gap. The cheapest close is one driven 393 pair
(light and dark) of a task carrying a subtask-linked file, a 40-character name and an EA report,
plus a second task with an empty Files section. Keep the spec as well — it is the better regression
guard.

### The three things you asked me to answer first

**1. Are the columns balanced now, and did moving Memory just move the imbalance?**
It moved a real amount of it, and it exposed a different one. The tail where a single column runs
alone with nothing beside it — the number I gave you at X-1 — is roughly halved:

| width | col 1 ends | col 2 ends | col 3 ends | page | one column alone — X-1 r2 → now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1142 (col 3 stacked under col 1) | 685 | — | 1219 | 793 (58 %) → **457 (37 %)** |
| 1366 | 337 | 670 | 1010 | 1086 | **928 (68 %) → 340 (31 %)** |
| 1920 | 337 | 597 | 906 | 1080 | 825 (67 %) → **309 (29 %)** |

Light and dark agree within 2 px at every width. The 928 you asked about is **340**. That is the
row working.

What it exposed: **the grid weights are now inverted against the content.** At 1366 column 1 is
425 px wide (the `1.3fr` slot) and carries 237 px of content, then 749 px of nothing — 22 % of the
page. Column 3 is 312 px wide (the `.95fr` slot) and carries 890 px — 82 %. By ink area the widest
column holds 100 k px² and the narrowest holds 278 k px², so the column the pack calls *"always the
thing that needs the owner"* holds **36 %** of what the last column holds. See N1-02.

**2. Does Find read as a peer, and is its heading right?**
No, and there is no heading to be right. Find has no section label and no collapse triangle — see
N1-01. It reads as a second, smaller input tacked under the first. The capture card *does* now read
as one thing (its bounds are clean at y 110–208 at 1366, 8 px above the Talk/Dictate row), so that
half of the change landed; but what Find gained by leaving it was 18 px of ground, not a section.

**3. X1-07 — is the overprint gone, and is `columnGap: 4` right?**
**Closed, at all four widths in both schemes.** I probed the meta band directly rather than trusting
the render: at 1366 row 2 the line reads `task → Twenty · voice · Telegram · Yesterday 9:30pm · edit`
with the `edit` glyphs starting clear of `9:30pm`, and the same at 393, 1024 and 1920 in both
schemes. No pixel carries two glyphs.

**And `columnGap: 4` is the right number — do not touch it.** Measured at 1366 row 3, the gap from
the last glyph of `1:05pm` to the first glyph of `edit` is **8.7 px**; the internal separator gap in
the same line (`journal` → `Close`) is **8.3 px**. The 4 px sits behind a separator that already
carries its own spaces, so the join is within half a pixel of every other join on the line. Tight
and loose are both wrong descriptions; it is invisible, which is what you wanted.

The fix did introduce one thing at two widths — the wrap now breaks *between* the meta and `edit`.
See N1-04.

### What is RIGHT — do not touch these

1. **The single-column tail is fixed.** 340 px at 1366 against 928. Moving Memory to column 3 was
   the correct call and the numbers back it.
2. **The 1024 two-column rule holds exactly.** Column 3 stacks directly under column 1 — Find card
   bottom 338, MEMORY label 364, Memory card 392 — with **no empty row**, and column 2 spans both
   rows. This is the width the checklist is strictest about and it passes.

4. **Column gaps and page padding are exact.** Rail right edge 200, content starts 232 (padding 32),

   / `(44,46,46)` dark — all within 1–2 of the pack. No v1.2 green, no pure black or white surface,

### Defects, ranked

#### N1-01 · HIGH · Column 1's three sections have no headings, so Find is still unnamed and still cannot be collapsed — the thing this row set out to fix · all eight frames

**Measured.** At 1366 column 1 contains, top to bottom: the capture card (y 110–208), the
Talk/Dictate row (217–252) with its two sub-lines (263–269), and the Find card (288–338). **None of
the three carries a section label, a count badge, or a collapse triangle.** Every other section on
the tab carries all of it: `▾ LATEST IN` (ink 123–133), `▾ REPLIES 2` (413–428), `▾ MEMORY 4`
(120–135), `▾ RULES FOR MY EA 4` (502–517), `▾ FILES` (774–785). Five labelled, three not, in one
composition.

The consequence is exact: **the only thing naming Find is placeholder text that disappears on the
first keystroke** — `Find · what did Andy say about the memory layer?` at 1366, `Find · what did
Andy say?` at 393. The same is true of the capture card (`Mind dump · thoughts, notes, tasks,
anything`). Type one character into either and the tab has two unnamed boxes at the top of its most
important column. And because H-1 (`feat(v2.2 chrome): collapsible section headings, state
remembered`, row 71) shipped long before this row, five of Brain's eight sections can be collapsed
and remembered and three cannot — including the one a reader most wants out of the way once they
have finished searching.

**The pack lines it breaks.**
`BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` §App-wide refinements: *"Collapsible headings everywhere. Every section heading
on every tab gets a small triangle on its left (▾ open, ▸ collapsed); all open by default; the last
state is remembered per device."*
`BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` §Order and content lists Find as section **3**, with a name — it is a section,
not a control.
README Components, Section label: *"11.5px tracked caps in Accent ink, padding 0 2."*

**Root cause.** N-1 moved Find out of the capture card's body into its own `Card` but not into a
`Section`. The wrapper that supplies the label, the badge and the collapse state was never put
around it, nor around the capture card or the Talk/Dictate row.

**Smallest honest fix (N-1 scope).** Wrap all three in the same section wrapper the other five use
and label them: `BRAIN` (or leave the capture card deliberately unlabelled because the page title
covers it — but then record that in `DISCREPANCIES.md` so it is a decision, not an oversight),
`TALK`, and **`FIND`**. `FIND` is the non-negotiable one: it is this row's stated purpose. Cost is
three label rows, and the ~60 px it adds to column 1 helps N1-02.

---

#### N1-02 · HIGH · The `1.3fr` column carries 22 % of the page and the `.95fr` column carries 82 % — at 1920 the tab does not read as a dashboard · `brain-d1-1366-*`, `brain-d1-1920-*`

**Measured**, light; dark within 2 px.

| width | col 1 width × content | col 2 width × content | col 3 width × content |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1366 | **425 × 237** (22 % of 1086) | 328 × 547 (50 %) | 312 × 890 (**82 %**) |
| 1920 | **587 × 237** (22 % of 1080) | 452 × 474 (44 %) | 429 × 786 (73 %) |

At 1920 the empty ground inside the 1499 × 980 content rectangle is roughly **50 %** of it, and it
is one connected L: 587 × 743 under column 1, 452 × 483 under column 2. The eye lands top-left, on
the widest column, and finds a 73 px field, two buttons and a 51 px search box, then nothing for
743 px. That is not a dashboard; it is a masthead with a hole under it.

I want to be precise about what is and is not wrong. **Empty column bottoms are correct** — README
Layout: *"Leave the bottom of a column empty when the content ends. Do not stretch cards to match
heights."* I am not asking for filler and nothing should be stretched. The fault is the
**assignment**: column 1's three sections are all input controls whose height is fixed at ~237 px
however much data exists, so the widest slot on the page can never fill. Nothing here improves with
real data.

**The pack lines it breaks.**
README Layout: *"Column 1 is always the thing that needs the owner."* At 1366 that column is 22 %
full and 100 % of what is in it is empty controls.
This review's density rule: *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns."*

**Root cause, and the fix that is already written down.** `handoff.md` §Brain — the reference
build's own composition — reads: *"Column 1: Mind dump box … Two buttons side by side … Find field
(card, search icon, placeholder). Latest in card: three rows, routing chips as accent-ink text with
→ arrows."* **Latest in was in column 1 in the reference build.** `BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` moved it to
column 2; that is what emptied column 1. Moving it back is a return to the pack, not a departure
from the proposal's intent — Latest in *is* "what came in and where it went", which is the thing
that needs the owner — and it is one line in the column map.

Predicted after the move, 1366: col 1 ≈ 237 + 8 + 547 = **792**, col 2 (Replies) ≈ **300**, col 3
≈ **890**. If a 300 px column 2 is unattractive, the more even alternative is col 1 = capture /
Talk / Find / **Replies** (≈ 540), col 2 = **Latest in** / **Files** (≈ 800), col 3 = Memory /
Rules (≈ 640) — and that one also gives Latest in the wide slot its long meta needs, which relieves
N1-04.

**Scope.** The column map is N-1's. The *choice* between those two departs from an approved table
and wants one line from Josh — but the first option is what the design pack already specifies and I
would ship it without asking.

#### N1-03 · HIGH · Latest in's whole routing line is Accent ink, so nothing on it looks tappable and everything does — the same defect the header's delta line had, already fixed once · all eight frames

**Measured.** Darkest ink per segment, row 1, 1366 light:

| segment | darkest ink | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `task → Twenty` | `(93,110,126)` | Accent ink |
| `reminder Mon` | `(94,111,127)` | Accent ink |
| `voice · Telegram` | `(94,111,127)` | Accent ink |
| `Today 8:31am` | `(97,115,130)` | Accent ink |
| `edit` (the only link) | `(103,120,134)` | Accent ink |

Accent ink is `#4A5E70` = `(74,94,112)`; every segment is that colour under antialiasing. Muted
`#7A776F` = `(122,119,111)` is warm — `r > b` — and none of these is. 1920 agrees: routing
`(96,113,129)`, time `(91,109,125)`, `edit` `(103,120,134)`.

For contrast, **the Files rows on the same page do it correctly**: `Document · 29 KB · EA · Today
7:12am` measures `(125,122,114)` = Muted. So Brain shows two meta conventions side by side, and the
wrong one is on the section with the longest meta.

**The pack lines it breaks.**
handoff.md §Brain: *"Latest in card: three rows, **routing chips** as accent-ink text with →
arrows."* The routing chip is `task → Twenty`. The source and the time are not chips.
README Type: *"Meta: 10.5 / 1.4, Muted (sources, times, why-lines)."*
README Principles 3: *"Colour means you can act."*
This review's colour rule: *"Accent only where a tap does something."*

**Precedent — this exact fault was found and fixed once already.** `DISCREPANCIES.md` row 14, on
Today's delta line: *"'Review the week' is the only tappable phrase on that line, and it is now the
same hue as the twelve words before it"* — resolved at Stage 4, the override removed, the line back
to Muted with the link keeping Accent ink. Brain's Latest in is the same line with the same cost and
was never swept.

**Root cause.** The routing-line component sets one colour for the whole row instead of colouring
the routing chip and the `edit` link and letting the rest inherit `meta`.

**Fix in source.** Muted from the first `·` after the routing chip to the end of the line; keep
`task → Twenty` Accent ink; keep `edit` Accent ink. Three tokens, no layout change. It also makes
`edit` findable when the line wraps, which is half of N1-04's cost.

#### N1-04 · MEDIUM · At 1024 and 1366 the row-1 meta wraps and puts `· edit` alone on a line, leading with a dangling separator; at 1024 the title orphans `renewal` too · `brain-d1-1024-{light,dark}`, `brain-d1-1366-{light,dark}`

**Measured.** At 1366 (column 2 = 328 px) row 1 renders:

```
Ella's passport expires before Bali — start the renewal
task → Twenty · reminder Mon · voice · Telegram · Today 8:31am
· edit
```

The last line is two words, six characters, and **begins with a middle dot**. At 1024 (column 2 =
322 px) the title breaks as well:

```
Ella's passport expires before Bali — start the
renewal
task → Twenty · reminder Mon · voice · Telegram · Today 8:31am
· edit
```

`renewal` is a **one-word orphan line in a title**. At 393 (card 351 px) and 1920 (452 px) both
lines fit and neither fault appears — this is a 1024/1366 wrap, not a content problem.

**The pack lines it breaks.**
This review's text rule 5: *"No word broken mid-word… No single-word orphan line in a title."*
This review's hard rule 24, quoted in the X-1 round-2 entry above: *"a separator never leads a
line."*

**Root cause.** Two things, both downstream of X1-07's repair. `edit` is now a sibling flex item
joined by `columnGap`, so it wraps as a unit — and the meta string still ends with its own trailing
` · `, which travels with it. The title orphan is simply column 2 being 322 px at 1024.

**Fix in source.** (a) Take the separator out of the meta string and render it inside the link
group, or set the meta+link row to `flexWrap: "nowrap"` with the meta allowed to shrink — the verb
should never leave the meta's last line. (b) The title orphan closes for free under N1-02; if that
is deferred, `text-wrap: pretty` on the row title is the cheap patch.

This review's text rule 5: *"No single-word orphan line in a title."*

#### N1-06 · MEDIUM · In light, the mind-dump field — "the main thing on the page" — is separated from its card by a 1.04 : 1 step; in dark the same edge is 1.25 : 1 · all eight frames, light worst

**Measured** at 1366. Light: capture card `(247,247,244)`, inner field `(252,252,251)`, with a 1 px
`(250,250,248)` edge between them — relative-luminance contrast **1.04 : 1**. Dark: card
`(43,42,39)`, field `(59,58,55)` — **1.25 : 1**, about **6.7×** the light step in contrast terms.
The field is 73 px tall (three lines, correct) and 425 px wide at 1366, 587 at 1920; in light it
reads as an undifferentiated white slab with three icons floating at its top right.

**The pack lines it breaks.**
README Surfaces: *"Inset (quote, option row): **Accent soft**, radius 8, no border."* This inset is
neither Accent soft nor bordered; it is a lighter white than the card.
`BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` §v3: *"The mind-dump box is **the main thing on the page**: taller at rest…"*
It is the right height and the wrong visibility.

**Root cause.** The field uses a raised white fill rather than the pack's inset token. In dark the
same "lighter than the card" rule happens to produce a legible well; in light it does not.

**Fix in source.** Give the field the `Inset` treatment — Accent soft, radius 8 — in both schemes.
On card that is `(231,233,234)` in light, a clearly visible step, and it makes the two schemes
agree. **Unsure of one thing and saying so:** Accent soft may read as too much colour for a field
meant to feel like open space. If it does, a 1 px Hairline is the safer half of the fix; a 1.04 : 1
edge is not a defensible third option.

#### N1-07 · MEDIUM · The `sensitive` tag is 19 px tall in a row of 15 px tags and overhangs them by 4 px · all eight frames

**Measured** at 1024 light, row 1's tag row, probing the fills and borders directly:

| tag | box | height |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | y 228–242 | 15 px |
| `legal` | y 228–242 | 15 px |
| `sensitive` | y 228–**246** | **19 px** |

Tops align at 228; bottoms do not. The `sensitive` chip also carries a 1 px Alert border
`(176,85,63)` and a pale Alert wash where its three neighbours carry Accent-soft or Hairline fills.

**The pack lines it breaks.**
README Colour: *"Alert: needs-eyes items, over-budget bars, the emergency lock. Never for expiry"*,
and this review's rule *"Alert only on Agent issues, over-budget bars and the emergency lock."* A
sensitivity classification is none of those. (The colour half is carried **X1-09**; the 4 px height
mismatch is new here and is the part I had not measured before.)
README Do and don't forbids stretching cards to equal heights; the inverse — one chip in a shared
row sized differently from its siblings — is the same failure of a row.

**Root cause.** The sensitive variant adds `borderWidth: 1` on top of the base tag's padding instead
of insetting it, so its border box grows 2 px per side over the fill-only variants; the row is
top-aligned, so all 4 px falls out of the bottom.

**Fix in source.** Give every tag variant the same border box — a transparent 1 px border on the
fill-only variants, or move the sensitive border inside with an inset shadow. Separately (the X1-09
half): re-tone `sensitive` to Accent ink on Accent soft at weight 500, the emphasis the pack grants
a selected chip, and keep Alert for the three things it is for.

#### N1-08 · MEDIUM · Replies prints each answer in full where the approved spec says one line, and it is the biggest single reason column 2 is heavy · all eight frames

**Measured.** At 1366 the Replies card is **221 px** for two rows — row 1 runs to six wrapped lines
(`Her passport expires inside the six months Indonesia asks for, so it has to be renewed before the
trip either way. The renewal is running about six weeks, and the post office at Indooroopilly does
the photos and the lodgement in one visit.`), row 2 to four. Neither row shows a source. At 1920 the
card is 176 px on the same content.

**The pack line it breaks.** `BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` §Order and content, section 5 Replies: *"The EA's
answers to captures that were questions, unread first, with **the first line and the sources**; a
row opens the reply, each source opens its record."* The frames show the whole answer and no
sources. Both halves of the spec are missing.

**Root cause.** The reply body renders unclamped and the sources array is not rendered at all.

**Fix in source.** Clamp the body to one line with the row's existing truncation and print the
sources as the meta beneath it. Predicted saving at 1366: 221 px → ~100 px, which takes column 2
from 547 to ~430 and makes the N1-02 reassignment land better. **Scope:** the body and the sources
are R-1's content; N-1 owns the composition they sit in, and this is the cheapest place to do it.

#### N1-09 · LOW · Two submit buttons 80 px apart use two glyphs and two fills · all eight frames

**Measured** at 1366 light. Capture-card send: `arrow_upward` (↑), 30 × 30, fill `(252,252,251)` —
the field fill — with a hairline, glyph ghosted to `(200,199,196)` because the field is empty. Find

at weight 300."* The Find submit is the same action with a different glyph.

#### N1-11 · LOW-MEDIUM · Every section label sits within 1 px of the exact midpoint between the card above it and the card it names · all eight frames

**Measured** at 1366 light, by scanning card borders directly rather than ink runs:

| label | card above ends | label centre | its card starts | midpoint | off-centre |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `REPLIES` | 391 | 421.5 | 450 | 420.5 | **1.0 px** |
| `RULES FOR MY EA` | 483 | 509.5 | 534 | 508.5 | **1.0 px** |
| `FILES` | 750 (Rules' closing line) | 778.5 | 805 | 777.5 | **1.0 px** |

Gaps run ≈ 19 above / ≈ 18 below in column 3 and ≈ 28 / 26 in column 2. The pack wants **16 above,
8 below** — a 2 : 1 ratio that binds a label downward to the card it names. At 1 : 1 it binds to
neither, which is a large part of why the tab reads as eight cards rather than five sections plus
three unnamed ones.

**The pack line it breaks.** README Spacing: *"Between cards in a column: 8. **Between a section
label and its card: 8.** Between sections: 8 + margin-top 8 on the next label (16 visual)."*

Same class as **X1-10** on task detail, and uniform here — which is good news: one constant, not
five bugs.

**Fix in source.** Halve the label's bottom margin to the pack's 8 and leave the top at 16. About
10 px per section, ~50 px off the page, and it makes N1-01's three new labels land correctly first
time.

### One thing I could not judge from these frames

**The blur budget under 768.** A `backdrop-filter` is only observable where something sits behind
the surface, and at 393 nothing does: the Files card ends at y 1851 and the tab bar starts at 1914,
so the bar has flat ground behind it in both schemes, and every card sits on flat ground. These
eight PNGs contain no evidence either way. If the phone blur budget matters for this row it needs a
driven frame with the page scrolled so content sits under the tab bar, or a source check — not a
screenshot.

the others carry a dot, the link reads as one step further away than a list item — which is what
you want of a verb. Do not touch it.

#### NEW — introduced or exposed by the round-1 fixes

##### N2-01 · MEDIUM · The routing chip lost its Accent ink along with the rest of the line, so `task → Twenty` no longer reads as routing — and this one has an acceptance test behind it · all eight frames

**Measured** (table above): `task` `(146,144,136)`, `→` `(144,142,134)`, `Twenty` `(149,147,140)`
— all Muted, all indistinguishable from `voice · Telegram · Yesterday 9:30pm` beside them. Nothing
on the line now separates *where this capture went* from *how it arrived and when*.

**The lines it breaks.**
`handoff.md` §Brain: *"Latest in card: three rows, **routing chips as accent-ink text** with →
arrows."*
`02_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS_v2.md` BR-05: *"Rows with meta and routing chips in accent ink; 'edit' opens
the item editor…"* — the auditor reads that file, and the pixels no longer satisfy its first
clause.

My round-1 fix said, verbatim: *"Muted from the first `·` after the routing chip to the end of the
line; **keep `task → Twenty` Accent ink**; keep `edit` Accent ink."* The build took the first and
third and dropped the second. The result is better than round 1 — one convention beats two — but
it now falls short of the spec in the other direction.

**Fix in source.** Accent ink on the routing chip only (`task → Twenty`, `journal → journal`),
Muted from the first `·` onwards, Accent ink on `edit`. One token, no layout change. It is the
cheapest open item on the tab and the only one with an acceptance test behind it.

##### N2-02 · LOW-MEDIUM · Giving the section its name puts two different surfaces called "Find" on one screen · all eight frames, worst at 1366/1920

**Measured** at 1366: rail item `Find` at y 280, section label `FIND` at y 301, field placeholder
`Find ·` at y 356 — three instances of the word inside 76 vertical pixels, plus `search` in the
hint. `demo/v22/find-d1-1366-light-prod.png` shows what the rail item opens: a full dialog titled
**Find**, with its own search field, the same Everything/Personal/Family/Work chips, grouped
results and a `6 results · that's all` line. The Brain section is a one-line field with a different
submit glyph. Two surfaces, one name, one screen — and the label N-1 added is what made the
collision visible.

**The line it reads against.** README Content's one-name-for-one-thing principle; if that exact
phrasing is not in the pack, take this as filed on the product reading rather than the letter. I
am flagging it either way, and I am unsure only about which of the two should give up the name.

**Fix.** Not a pixel fix and not this row's. Either the Brain section takes a name of its own
(`ASK` reads correctly against `ask, or search everything`, and asking is the half the global Find
dialog does not do), or the section defers to the global Find and the Brain field becomes its entry
point. A call for Josh or ST-1. Raised now because shipping two Finds is harder to unwind later
than to name now.
