### The six things you asked me to answer, before the defect list

**1. Is a hit obvious at a glance against a miss, at 393, in both schemes?**
**Dark yes. Light no — and the guard that passed it is measuring the wrong thing.**

Measured off `trends-d1-393-*-prod.png`, cell centres, tokens confirmed exact:

| | light | dark |
|---|---|---|
| hit fill vs the surface it sits on | `#66798A` on `(220,220,219)` → **3.13 : 1** | `#9AAEC0` on `(38,36,33)` → 6.77 : 1 |
| the day number **inside** a hit cell | `(237,237,233)` on `#66798A` → **3.83 : 1** | `(37,37,37)` on `#9AAEC0` → 6.71 : 1 |
| the day number in a **missed** cell | `(133,131,124)` on surface → **2.64 : 1** | `(135,132,126)` → 4.15 : 1 |
| miss cell **border** vs surface | `(204,204,204)` on `(215,215,215)` → **1.12 : 1** | `(56,54,51)` on `(38,36,33)` → 1.29 : 1 |

Your guard checks the first row and clears 3:1 by 0.13. It does not check the second or third row,
and those are the ones Josh will read — his whole reference is cells that *carry their day number*.
3.83 : 1 and 2.64 : 1 are below every floor the pack states for itself:

> "Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, Muted on Card 4.6:1, Accent ink on Accent soft 5.2:1 (light)."

In dark the same component is comfortable everywhere except the missed number at 4.15. So the
answer is scheme-dependent, and the light frame is the one that fails. See LH1-03.

**2. Has Habits eaten the Life column?**
Not vertically — horizontally, and in the opposite direction from the one you feared.

| width | Habits card | col 1 ends | col 2 ends | col 3 ends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 393 | 388–772 (384 px) | single column | — | — |
| 1024 | 351–731 (380 px) | **993** | 543 | stacked under col 1 |
| 1366 | 351–731 (380 px) | **731** | 543 | 381 |
| 1920 | 351–731 (380 px) | **731** | 543 | 381 |

380 px is 2.5 × the Goals card above it and 63 % of column 1's card height, and at 1024 it pushes
Health and Learning down far enough that column 1 runs to 993 against column 2's 543. The pack
sanctions that shape outright — *"Leave the bottom of a column empty when the content ends. Do not
stretch cards to match heights."* — so I am not calling the height a defect.

What *is* a defect is the width. The strip is **24 px cells at 393 and 24 px cells at 1920** —
identical, measured; the whole strip is 203 px at every width. So the gap between the habit's name
and its marks runs 95 px at 393, **200 px at 1366, 330 px at 1920**, nine times over. At 1920 the
card is 587 px wide and reads as two disconnected halves: a list of words on the left, a floating
grid on the right. That is checklist 7 — *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns"* —
failed by a card that is literally the phone card at desktop width. See LH1-06.

**3. Nine month grids in one dialog — readable, or does the habit need choosing first?**
**Neither. It needs to use the width it already has.** It does not need a picker — Josh's reference
image 1 is explicitly a *list* of habits each with its own grid, so nine at once is right.

But the grid is 203 px wide (7 × 24 px cells + 5 px gaps, measured identical at 393, 1366 and 1920)
inside a dialog body of **861 px at 1366 and 1920** and 674 px at 1024. So:

- 77 % of the dialog width is empty at 1366 and 1920; 70 % at 1024.
- The scrollbar thumb measures 260 px in a 700 px track — the content is ~1890 px in an ~800 px
  viewport. **60 % of the content is below the fold in a dialog that is three-quarters empty
  sideways.** At 1366 you see 3.6 habits of 9.
- The Find dialog at the same width, from the same build, is the control: identical 900 px shell,
  and it fills it. Trends does not.

Lay the nine habit blocks as cards in a responsive grid inside the sheet — 1 up under 768, 2 up at
1024, 3 up at 1180+. Nine months become three rows, the 1890 px of scroll becomes ~700, and the
empty right two-thirds disappears. See LH1-04 and LH1-05.

**4. Does the year grid at 393 read as scrollable or as cut off?**
**Cannot be judged — no frame shows it.** Only the Month tab was captured.

**5. The twelve bars at 393 — collision, numbers that lost their bar?**
**Cannot be judged — no frame shows it.**

This row exists because Josh wrote *"Trend tabs are empty"*. It shipped four tabs and the device
pass photographed one. Three quarters of the row's own output is unreviewed, in both schemes, at
all four widths. The input list did name the Month tab only, so the capture did what it was told —
but I cannot sign a row on a quarter of it, and the two questions you most wanted answered are the
two the frames cannot answer. Re-capture `trends-week`, `trends-year` and `trends-alltime` at
393/1024/1366/1920 × light/dark before the auditor runs.

**6. Does a "future" cell read as a miss?**
**Worse than that — a future day is not drawn at all, and a missed day is a 1.12 : 1 hairline.**

Measured at 1366: Exercise's last painted row bottoms at y 333 and the next habit's name starts at
y 431. The gap is **98 px** — exactly the three unpainted week-rows of September (3 × 29 px pitch)
plus the section gap. The container reserves the whole month and paints days 1–9 only. So:

- The month has no frame. "SEPTEMBER 2026" sits above a shape that is two rows tall and then stops.
- 87 px of reserved void per habit × 9 = ~780 px of the 1890 px scroll is nothing.
- And the only thing separating *"I missed it"* from *"it hasn't happened"* is a hairline at
  **1.12 : 1 in light, 1.29 : 1 in dark** — invisible at arm's length. Josh's reference image 2
  draws a missed day as a *filled* light-grey cell with grey text. Ours draws it as air with an
  outline.

See LH1-01 and LH1-02. These two are the row's real failure against the brief Josh actually wrote.

---

### Defects

#### LH1-01 · The month grid reserves the whole month and paints only the elapsed days
**Severity: high.** **Root cause:** future days render as no element (or an element with neither
border nor fill) inside a container laid out for all five week-rows of the month.

`trends-d1-*` at every width and both schemes. Measured at 1366: Exercise's grid ends at y 333,
"Burn" begins at y 431 — a 98 px void = three unpainted week-rows at the 29 px row pitch + 11 px
section gap. Same at 393 (106 px), 1024 and 1920 (106 px between Meditate and Audiobook). Nine
habits, ~780 px of reserved nothing.

Breaks — the pack's only calendar keeps its grid drawn when there is nothing in it:

> "Calendar grid: 24px per hour, 6:00 to 20:00, hour lines every two hours. Events sit at their
> real time; unbooked time stays visibly empty."

*Visibly* empty is the operative word: the grid survives, the content does not. Here the grid
itself vanishes for two thirds of the month.

**Fix in source:** paint every day of the displayed month. Three states, three fills, so the void
becomes a frame and future stops being ambiguous with missed:
`hit` = solid fill + light number (see LH1-03 for which fill);
`miss` = Accent-soft fill (`rgba(102,121,138,.14)` / `rgba(154,174,192,.16)`) + Muted number —
this is Josh's "light grey cell with grey text";
`future` = hairline box, number at Muted with the pack's existing `Disabled: opacity .45`.

#### LH1-02 · A missed day is separated from a blank one by a hairline at 1.12 : 1
**Severity: high.** **Root cause:** `miss` is styled as border-only with no fill, so it carries no
positive mark; the hairline token is a 4 % step by design and was never meant to be a data mark.

Trends month grid — miss border vs sheet: **1.12 : 1** light, **1.29 : 1** dark.
Life habit strip — miss border vs card: **1.16 : 1** light, **1.26 : 1** dark.

Josh's line, verbatim, is the specification this fails:

> "Current 'week' view is not great, doesn't show hits and misses clearly."

The hits now show. The misses still do not — they are the same 1.1 : 1 as blank card. **Fix:** as
LH1-01 — give `miss` an Accent-soft fill so it is a mark rather than the absence of one. Keeps the
pack's "no per-category hue" rule (still Accent) and gives ~1.9 : 1 of positive step, which at 24 px
is the difference between a cell and a gap.

#### LH1-03 · The day number is 3.83 : 1 in a done cell and 2.64 : 1 in a missed one, in light
**Severity: high.** **Root cause:** white ink on `Accent #66798A` — a mid tone — and Muted ink on a
sheet that is 30 levels darker than a card. The 3:1 guard measures fill-vs-ground and never touches
either number.

Numbers in the table under question 1. Every contrast floor the pack sets for itself is >= 4.6 : 1:

> "Text contrast: Ink on Ground 11:1, Muted on Card 4.6:1, Accent ink on Accent soft 5.2:1 (light)."

**Fix in source:** in **light** only, make the `hit` fill `Accent ink #4A5E70` rather than
`Accent #66798A`. White on it is **6.9 : 1** and the fill-vs-surface step goes from 3.13 to 6.4.
This is not an invention — it is the pack's own habit-done treatment:

> "Habit chip: … Done: Accent-soft fill, no border, Accent-ink text at 500, mark filled Accent ink
> with a white check."

Dark already clears (6.77 / 6.71); leave `#9AAEC0` alone there. Then extend the guard to assert the
*number* against its own cell, not just the cell against the sheet — that is the check that would
have caught this.

#### LH1-04 · The nine grids sit on the bare dialog sheet; every other dialog in the app uses cards
**Severity: medium-high.** **Root cause:** the Trends body renders habit blocks directly into the
sheet's scroll container with no card wrapper.

Measured at 1366, light: scrim `(173,172,167)`, sheet `(221,221,220)` — identical in Trends and in
Find. But Find's results sit on cards at `(251,251,251)`; Trends' grids sit on the bare `221`.
Dark: sheet `(39,37,34)` in Trends, cards at `(56,55,51)` in Find. Three consequences, all
measurable: the accent step drops from ~3.9 : 1 (on a card) to 3.13 : 1 (on the sheet); nothing
bounds a habit block, so its count caption floats free (LH1-05); and LH1-01's void has no container
to sit inside, which is why it reads as a rendering fault rather than as space.

Breaks:

> "Settings sheet: scrim + one frosted sheet, section label above each card."

**Fix:** wrap each habit block in `.js-card` (radius 10, hairline, blur 20) with the habit name as
its title and the count as its right-hand hint. That alone fixes LH1-05 and half of LH1-03.

#### LH1-05 · Caption and paging arrows are laid out across 861 px while the content is 203 px
**Severity: high at 1024 and above; mild at 393.** **Root cause:** the habit header row and the
month-paging row are full-width `space-between` while the grid below them is intrinsically sized.

At 1366: grid x 249–450 (203 px); "7 of 9" at x 1085 — **635 px from the grid it counts**. `‹` at
x 250 and `›` at x 1078 — **828 px apart**, with "SEPTEMBER 2026" centred between them. Identical
at 1920 (the dialog does not grow past 898 px). At 1024, 470 px of empty.

Breaks checklist 7 and the pack's standing rule against centring on desktop:

> "Don't: … centred layouts on desktop"

**Fix:** with LH1-04's cards in place, the caption sits inside its own card and the arrows flank the
month label in a content-width group (`‹  SEPTEMBER 2026  ›`, centred as a unit, not spread). Then
lay the cards 1/2/3-up at <768 / 1024 / 1180+.

#### LH1-06 · The Life strip is fixed at 24 px cells and 203 px at every width
**Severity: medium.** **Root cause:** the strip is a fixed 7-day component; the card's extra width
is absorbed by the flex gap between the name and the strip, not by the strip.

Measured: hit cells are 24 px wide at 393 *and* at 1920 (`life-d1-393-light` x 158–181;
`life-d1-1920-light` x 603–626). Name-to-strip gap: 95 px at 393, 200 px at 1366, 330 px at 1920,
in each of nine rows.

Breaks checklist 7 — *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns"* — and misses what Josh
actually asked for:

> "a dense grid of small rounded squares" (planner's note on reference image 1)

**Fix:** make the day count responsive — 7 days under 768, 14 at 768–1179, 28 (four clean weeks) at
1180+. The card fills, the density rises with the screen instead of falling, and it lands Josh's
image 1 without a new component.

#### LH1-07 · Today's mark is a different shape and a quarter of the area of a history mark
**Severity: medium.** You asked whether the size difference reads as deliberate. **It reads as an
accident, but not for the reason you expected.** The *box* grows (24 → 34 px) while the *mark*
shrinks and changes shape (24 px square → 14 px circle). **Root cause:** the today cell is the
pack's `Habit chip` with its label removed, dropped into a row of data cells that speak a different
language.

Measured, `life-d1-393-light`: history hit = 24 × 24 solid `#66798A`, 4.19 : 1 against the card,
area 576 px². Today done = a 34 × 34 plate at `(227,229,229)` — exactly `Accent soft` — holding a
14 px `#4A5E70` circle with a white check, area 154 px². The plate is **1.18 : 1** against the card
(1.33 : 1 dark). So the most important cell in the row carries the *weakest* plate and the
*smallest* mark: four days ago reads louder than today.

The chip itself is faithful to the pack —

> "Habit chip: min-height 34, padding 0 11 0 9, radius 8, 11.5px label … Done: Accent-soft fill, no
> border, Accent-ink text at 500, mark filled Accent ink with a white check."

— which is the point: a chip is a labelled control, and this is an unlabelled cell in a strip.
**Fix:** draw today as a 24 px square in the same language as the other six (solid fill when done,
Accent-soft when not), keep the 34 px pressable box as transparent padding around it, and mark
"today" with a 1 px Accent-ink underline beneath the cell. Never change mark size to signal
pressability.

*Unsure, and saying so:* the painted today box is 34 px wide. The pack asks for
*"Tap targets 36px minimum on phone"*. The row pitch is 40 px, so the hit box may already exceed the
paint — I cannot measure a hit box from a screenshot. Worth a source check either way.

#### LH1-08 · Today's ring in Trends is a 2 px border, and it is the focus affordance
**Severity: medium.** **Root cause:** `today` uses a 2 px `accentInk` ring.

Measured at 1366, Burn's day 9: `#4A5E70` at x 308–309 and x 332–333 — exactly 2 px each side.

Breaks two lines at once:

> "Borders: hairlines only. No 2px borders except none."

> "Focus: 2px Accent ring, offset 2, radius matching the element."

A keyboard user tabbing through the grid cannot tell focus from today, because they are the same
mark. **Fix:** today = 1 px Accent-ink border + Accent-soft fill (which also distinguishes it from
LH1-01's future cells). Keep 2 px rings for focus, exclusively.

#### LH1-09 · The Habits card has no row hairlines; every other card in the same column does
**Severity: low.** **Root cause:** the habit rows are laid out without the card's row separator.

Measured, `life-d1-393-light`, column x = 100: the People card carries hairlines at y 880, 929, 978
(`(231,230,228)`); the Habits card runs y 393 → 772 with none between its nine rows.

Breaks:

> "Card: … Rows inside separated by 1px Hairline, 9px vertical padding, horizontal padding 12 on the
> card and 0 on the row."

**Fix:** add the hairline. **Or**, if the intent is a dense grid where rules would fight the marks,
that is a legitimate argument — but then it needs a `DISCREPANCIES.md` row, not a silent second row
idiom sitting between Goals and People, which both keep theirs. This is a decision, not a patch;
see the ownership note below.

#### LH1-10 · In dark, a habit with no hits reads as an empty row
**Severity: medium.** **Root cause:** LH1-02 — the miss cell has no fill, and at 1.26 : 1 the
hairline does not survive the dark ground.

`life-d1-*-dark`, the "Nap" row (0 of 7) and "Burn" (1 of 7): the six day cells disappear and the
row shows a name and a lone circle at the far right. A person cannot see that there are seven days
there at all, so "I have missed every day" is indistinguishable from "this habit has no data".
Closes with LH1-02's fill.

#### LH1-11 · The habit name in Trends is neither a card title nor a section label
**Severity: low.** **Root cause:** the name renders as plain 12.5 px body Ink.

Measured cap span 9 px at 393 and 1366 — the same as "Exercise" in the Life card body, i.e. Body
12.5 / Instrument Sans 400 / Ink `(65,64,60)`. It is the only thing separating one habit's month
from the next, and it carries no more weight than a meta line.

Breaks the type scale, which has a slot for exactly this and it is not body:

> "Card title: 15 / 1.3, Source Serif 4 500." · "Section label: 11.5 / 1, uppercase, letter-spacing
> .08em, Accent ink."

**Fix:** with LH1-04's card, the name becomes the card title in Source Serif 4 500 at 15 and the
"7 of 9" becomes the right-hand hint at 11 Muted.

### Which of these are this row's, and which are app-wide decisions

**This row's to fix, all inside the habit visuals:** LH1-01, LH1-02, LH1-03, LH1-05, LH1-06,
LH1-07, LH1-08, LH1-10, LH1-11. None of them touches another tab. LH1-01/02/03 are one edit to the
cell's state table; LH1-04/05/11 are one edit to the block wrapper; LH1-06/07 are the Life strip.

**LH1-04 is this row's to *follow*, not to decide.** The convention already exists — Find and task
detail both put dialog content in cards on the sheet. Trends is the only dialog that does not.
Adopting it is a patch; changing it would be an app-wide decision.

**App-wide, not this row's:**

- **LH1-09's row-hairline idiom.** Wants a `DISCREPANCIES.md` row and Josh's eye, not a unilateral
  change by whoever holds the habit card.
- **The full-width segmented control.** I nearly raised the four 215 px segments in an 861 px
  dialog as a density defect and then checked the control: `task-detail-d1-1366-light` (Low /
  Medium / High) and `find-d1-1366-light` (All / Not sensitive / Sensitive only) do exactly the
  same. It is the house pattern. **Do not change it in Trends alone.**
- **Right-hand section hints in Accent ink rather than Muted.** `trends` measures `(119,133,145)`
  and `configure` `(121,135,146)` — identical, and both blue-tinted where the pack says
  *"Right-hand hint on the same line: 11, Muted"*. App-wide, off this row, and consistent, so
  recorded rather than raised.

**Carried, still standing, not re-raised:**

- **K1-03** — at 1024 every tall dialog's bottom edge sits under the demo watermark chip. Visible
  in both `trends-d1-1024-*` frames: dialog bottom y 708, watermark chip y 703–719. Unchanged.
- **N1-11** — section labels at 20/20 where the pack wants 16/8. Stage 6's job.

### Measured and found NOT to be defects — recorded so the auditor does not re-litigate them

1. **Bleed-through of the Life page inside the Trends dialog.** It looks worse than it is and I
   nearly wrote it up. Isolated on a caption-free band (x 700–1010, y 455–620): peak deviation from
   the sheet median is 12 levels, **1.11 : 1** in light and **1.07 : 1** in dark. That is at or
   under the pack's own visibility floor (*"gradients above 3.5% alpha"*). The dialog reads
   unfinished because of LH1-01's voids and LH1-05's empty right two-thirds, not because the scrim
   is thin. Fixing those fixes the impression.
2. **One Accent for all nine habits.** Josh's three reference images are per-habit colour — magenta
   in image 2. The build refused, correctly: *"Never: … per-category colours (habits, calendars,
   budgets all use Accent)."* Every hit cell in all 16 frames is the one Accent token. Do not let a
   later round "improve" this.
3. **Tokens are exact, not approximate.** Hit `(102,121,138)` = `#66798A` light, `(154,174,192)` =
   `#9AAEC0` dark. Today plate `(227,229,229)` = `rgba(102,121,138,.14)` over the card, to the
   level. Today mark `#4A5E70` / `#B7C8D8`. Grounds `#EDEBE5` / `#191815` at all four corners. Light
   card `(247,247,244)` — not pure white.
4. **Radii are right.** 24 px cell, corner inset 3 px ≈ radius 5 (*"5 tags and checkboxes"*); 34 px
   today plate, inset 4 px ≈ radius 8 (*"8 buttons, chips, rows-as-buttons, insets"*).
5. **The scrollbar is correct and honest.** Thumb 5 px wide at `(187,186,184)` = the pack's
   `rgba(122,119,111,.3)` over the sheet, to the level; no visible track. Thumb 260 px in a 700 px
   track, which is a truthful report of ~1890 px of content.
6. **The calendar arithmetic is right.** 1 September 2026 is a Tuesday and day 1 sits under the
   second column of a Monday-first M T W T F S S header; day 7 sits under M. Captions check out on
   every habit read: Exercise 7 hits / "7 of 9", Burn 2 / "2 of 9", Meditate 6 / "6 of 9",
   Audiobook 6 / "6 of 9".
7. **Two-column rules at 1024.** Column 3 stacks directly under column 1, column 2 spans both rows,
   no empty row between sections. Content max-width holds at 1920 — content runs x 231 → 1731 and is
   left-aligned, not centred.
8. **Text.** No word broken mid-word, no clipped or ellipsised label in a button, chip or segment,
   no orphan line, no two-line button label, in any of the 16 frames. "Audiobook", "Solo time",
   "Meditate" and "All time" all fit unwrapped at 393.
9. **Marker discipline.** The only Marker in these frames is the LEARNING count badge. Not on a
   habit cell anywhere.
10. **The watermark.** Bottom-left on all 16, legible, clear of the rail health line by 22 px at
    1366 and 1920 (B-32 has not returned).
11. **The closing line vs the mic orb at 393.** The Life closing line ends at x 331 (light) / 334
    (dark) and the orb's painted circle begins at x 336 at that height — 2–5 px of clearance, not an
    overlap. It is also not judgeable from a full-page capture, since the orb is viewport-fixed and
    the line scrolls past it. App-wide, recorded, not raised.

| LH1-09 no row hairlines in the Habits card | **carries to Stage 6** — confirmed, §4 | |

**LH1-02, the caveat you asked for.** Yes, the `hairline`-as-fill reads as a mark, and your reason
for rejecting Accent-soft was right — it *is* the done-chip fill and it would have said the opposite
thing. But be clear about why it works, because the number is doing more of the lifting than you may
think. Measured: miss fill vs card is **1.16 : 1** in light and **1.27 : 1** in dark — the same
luminance step as the round-1 hairline you replaced. What changed is area (576 px² instead of a 1 px
outline) and the ink number sitting inside it. Both are load-bearing. If a later round shrinks the
cell or drops the number, the mark goes with them. Worth a comment in source saying so.

**LH1-03, the reasoning you asked me to challenge.** I agree with you, and I would go further: an ink
number on a missed day is *correct*, not merely tolerable. I looked for the "reads as all-numbers"
failure and it is not there, because you have three tiers of ink, not two — hit numbers are
light-on-dark, miss numbers are ink-on-pale, future numbers are at .45 (measured 2.1 : 1 light,
2.99 : 1 dark against the card). The eye sorts them into dark blocks / grey blocks / pale ghosts
before it reads a single digit. NAP at 0 of 9 is the test case and it passes: nine grey blocks, then
the rest of the month in ghost. The future number at 2.1 : 1 is effectively decorative, which is the
right call — it is a non-interactive, information-free cell and the pack's `Disabled: opacity .45` is
exactly the token for it. Do not let a later round "fix" that.

---

### 2 · The two tabs I had never seen

**Year — the sideways scroll does not read as scrollable. It reads as broken.** Two separate defects,
LH2-02 and LH2-03. The short version: the heat grid is a 53-week grid clipped to the card with no
affordance, it opens at the emptiest end, and it never reaches the current month at any width. At
1024 and 1920 it is clipped *mid-dot*, with the sixth month label truncated to a single character —
which is the specific thing a person reads as "this is broken", not as "scroll me".

**Year — the twelve bars survive 393, and fail at 1366 and 1920.** This is the opposite of what you
feared, and it is the same shape as LH1-06: the card gets narrower as the screen gets wider, because
3-up in a dialog capped at ~898 px gives each card ~250 px. At 393 the card is ~340 px, the pitch is
~28 px, and `16 19 19 27 17 25 7` reads cleanly. At 1366/1920 the pitch is ~21 px, a two-digit label
is ~17 px wide, and adjacent labels are separated by 1–2 px — `20` and `28` read as `2028`, `22` and
`17` as `2217`. See **LH2-04**.

**All time — the problem is not thinness, and more fixture will not fix it.** You asked whether one
bar row per habit is too thin to notice. It is worse than thin: **the bar is 100 % full in every
card, so it encodes nothing.** Measured on `trends-all-d1-393-light`, every fill runs x 71 → 316,
length 246 px, identical, for habits at 40 %, 55 %, 56 %, 73 %, 75 %, 81 % and 96 %. NAP at 35 % of
101 draws the same mark as MEDITATE at 96 % of 161. That is not an empty chart, it is a misleading
one, and at 393 where the cards stack it is the first thing you see. See **LH2-05**. Adding a second
year would only make the bars relative to each other, which is still not what a reader assumes a full
bar means — the fix is to make the bar length the rate you already print two words later.

### 3 · Defects

#### LH2-01 · The Life habit strip overflows its card and lies across two more columns
**Severity: blocker.** **Root cause:** LH1-06's fix made the day count responsive (7 / 14 / 28) but
did not make the cell size or the container responsive with it, so the strip is intrinsically sized
and the card does not clip it.

Measured, `life-d1-1366-light`: the Habits card is x 234 → 656 (422 px). Habit cells run to
**x 1088** — **432 px outside the card**, across column 2 and into column 3.
`life-d1-1920-light`: card x 234 → 816, cells to x 1084 — **268 px outside**.
`life-d1-1024-light`: card x 234 → 649, cells to x 692 — **43 px outside**.
Identical in dark at all three widths. Only 393 (7 cells) is clean.

The consequences are not subtle. At 1920 the MONEY section label is overprinted by habit cells and
truncated to "MON"; its collapse chevron sits between two habit squares; and the Burn, Meditate and
Audiobook rows disappear behind the Money card, which paints on top of them. A reader cannot tell
whether those habits have data at all.

Breaks, verbatim:

> "Columns flow top to bottom. Column 1 is always the thing that needs the owner. At two columns,
> column 3 sits directly under column 1 and column 2 spans both rows: sections stack tight, never
> separated by an empty row. **Never lay a single section across columns.**"

**Fix in source:** the strip must derive its cell size from the available width, not the other way
round. Give the strip row `min-width: 0` and lay the cells in `grid-template-columns: repeat(N,
minmax(0, 1fr))` with a 24 px max cell and a 14 px floor, so N days fit the card at any width; choose
N from the *card's* measured width, not the viewport's. Failing that, cap N at whatever fits (7 under
768, and 14 only where the card is wide enough for 14 × 28 px). Either way the strip must never be
able to paint outside its card — `overflow: hidden` on the card is a seatbelt, not a fix, but it
should be there too.

#### LH2-02 · "Dec" and "Jan" are printed on top of each other on every Year card
**Severity: high.** **Root cause:** the heat grid starts at the ISO week containing 1 January (which
begins on 29 Dec 2025 — the three hollow rings in column 0 are those out-of-range days), and both the
December and the January month labels resolve to column 0.

`trends-year-d1-*`, every card, every width, both schemes. The label row reads
`Dedan · Feb · Mar · Apr · May` — "Dedan" is not a word, it is two words in the same 34 px. Nine cards
per frame × 8 frames = 72 instances in this pass alone.

Breaks the Text checklist:

> "No word broken mid-word. No clipped or ellipsised label inside a button, chip or segment."

**Fix in source:** label the grid from the first *full* month it contains, or suppress any label whose
x position is within one label-width of the previous one. The leading partial week belongs to the
previous December and should carry no label at all.

#### LH2-03 · The Year heat grid is clipped, not scrollable, and never shows the current month
**Severity: high.** **Root cause:** a 53-column grid at a fixed 13 px pitch (measured: first column
x 263, last visible x 510, pitch 13) inside a card 250–340 px wide, with no scroll affordance and no
initial scroll offset.

- 1366 and 1920: **20 of 53 columns visible.** Visible span Dec → May. September, the month the user
  is standing in, is off the right edge.
- 1024: clipped **mid-dot** — a half-column of dots at the card's inner edge — and the sixth month
  label truncated to a single character after "May".
- 393: more of the year survives (Dec → Aug), so the *same card tells a different story at every
  width*, and still never reaches September.
- At every width the grid opens at the **empty** end: the first ten columns are entirely pale, because
  the fixture starts in March. The default view of the Year tab is a quarter of a year of blanks with
  today invisible.
- There is no scrollbar, no edge fade and no partial cell at 1366/1920 to say more exists. The pack's
  scrollbar is `5px, thumb rgba(122,119,111,.3)`; none is present here.

Breaks:

> "No clipped or ellipsised label inside a button, chip or segment."

and the row's own brief, which exists because Josh wrote *"Trend tabs are empty"* — a year view whose
default scroll position hides the current month has not answered it.

**Fix in source:** size the dot to the card (`minmax(0,1fr)` across 53 columns puts the cell at 4–6 px
at 250 px, the GitHub-graph idiom, and it is fine at 393 too), so the whole year is visible without
scrolling and the month labels have room. If you keep the fixed 13 px pitch, the container must be a
real horizontal scroller **scrolled to the right edge on mount**, with the pack's 5 px thumb visible —
and a clipped half-dot at the edge is still not an acceptable affordance.

#### LH2-04 · Year bar value labels collide at 1366 and 1920
**Severity: medium-high.** **Root cause:** the value label is wider than the column it labels
(measured: bar ~15 px, label "20" ~17 px), so at 3-up the labels overhang into their neighbours.

`trends-year-d1-1366-*` and `-1920-*`, all nine cards. BUILD at 1920 reads `20 24 18 22 17 29` with
1–2 px between adjacent labels, and because a taller bar's label sits higher the pairs interlock
diagonally — `20`/`24` and `18`/`22` read as four-digit numbers. EXERCISE reads `1619 19`, MEDITATE
`2028 21`. Clean at 393; acceptable at 1024.

Breaks the spirit of the whole Text checklist —

> "No clipped or ellipsised label inside a button, chip or segment. No single-word orphan line in a
> title."

— a label a person cannot attribute to its own mark is worse than a truncated one.

**Fix in source:** drop the per-bar value labels below ~24 px of pitch and put the value in the
`title`/tooltip; or label only the maximum bar and the current month. Keep the twelve initials on the
axis — they are one character and they fit everywhere.

#### LH2-05 · Every All-time bar is 100 % full, so the bar says nothing
**Severity: high.** **Root cause:** the bar is scaled to the row's own maximum, and with one year in
the fixture the row's maximum is the row itself.

Measured on `trends-all-d1-393-light`: seven visible cards, fills all x 71 → 316, length 246 px, zero
variance — for 130/160 (81 %), 53/133 (40 %), 154/161 (96 %), 89/122 (73 %), 108/144 (75 %), 53/97
(55 %), 71/126 (56 %). Same at all four widths and both schemes. No track is visible anywhere because
the fill covers it.

Breaks:

> "Progress bar: 8px tall, Hairline track, Accent fill. Over budget: Alert at .8."

A progress bar with no visible track is not a progress bar, and this one actively misinforms: NAP at
35 % draws the identical mark to MEDITATE at 96 %, side by side in the same grid.

**Fix in source:** set the fill to `done / possible` — the percentage the card already prints in its
meta line — not to `count / max(counts)`. That works with one year of fixture and with ten, and it
makes the card's graphic and its sentence agree. While you are there: `130` appears twice in the
EXERCISE card (the bar's right-hand value and "130 of 160"); drop one.

#### LH2-06 · At 1024 the ninth All-time card stretches across both columns
**Severity: medium.** **Root cause:** the odd card in a 2-up grid is allowed to span.

`trends-all-d1-1024-{light,dark}`: eight cards sit in two columns of ~316 px; BUILD sits alone at the
bottom at ~640 px, twice the width of every card above it. Its bar is consequently ~530 px against
everyone else's ~208 px — which, given LH2-05, reads as "BUILD is by far the best habit". It is not;
it is 91 % against MEDITATE's 96 %.

Breaks:

> "Leave the bottom of a column empty when the content ends. Do not stretch cards to match heights."

and the Don't list:

> "Don't: … stretch cards to equal heights."

**Fix in source:** the grid's last item keeps its column width and the bottom right stays empty. That
is the pack's stated preference and it is already how Life behaves one screen away.

#### LH2-07 · "This all time 70% · 831 of 1195" is not a sentence
**Severity: low-medium.** **Root cause:** the mock's `This week 61% · 33 of 54` template with the
period name substituted in.

`trends-all-d1-*`, all eight frames. The Month tab gets this right — `trends-d1-1920-dark` reads
"This month 52% · 42 of 81" — which is what makes the All-time line read as a bug rather than a style.

Breaks:

> "Voice: a capable assistant speaking to one person. Short sentences. Plain words. Present tense."

and:

> "End-of-list lines are calm statements."

**Fix in source:** make the leader a property of the period, not a prefix: `This week` / `This month`
/ `This year` / `All time`. Also note the mock's line ends `· shared with Today.` and the build's does
not — decide that deliberately rather than by omission.

#### LH2-08 · The today ring is invisible whenever today is a hit
**Severity: medium.** **Root cause:** LH1-08's fix made the today border 1 px `accentInk`, and the hit
fill is *also* `accentInk`. Same colour, same place.

Measured, `trends-d1-1366-light`, scanning y 331 across Exercise's day 9: `(74,94,112)` unbroken from
x 321 to x 346 — the border pixel *is* the fill. Burn's day 9, a miss, shows the ring correctly at
x 611 and x 636. Confirmed identical in dark at 1920 (Audiobook's miss-today ring at `(183,200,216)`
over a `(72,70,67)` interior; Exercise's hit-today cell all `(183,200,216)`).

I classified all nine cards at 1366: **4 of 9 show no today marker at all** — Exercise, Meditate, Solo
time, Build, the ones where today is a hit; 5 of 9 show one. Nine cards on one screen, two different
idioms, and which one you get depends on the data. This is precisely the class Josh named as *"some
buttons centred, some left-aligned"*.

Breaks the pack's assignment of accent ink, which is being asked to carry two meanings in the same
24 px:

> "Accent ink: section labels, primary-verb text, links, expiry text, recommended option number,
> active tab, provenance links."

**Fix in source:** use the idiom you already invented for the Life strip in LH1-07 — a 1 px accent-ink
**underline beneath the cell**, outside the fill. It survives all three cell states, it is one
treatment rather than two, and it keeps the 2 px ring exclusively for focus. Do it in both surfaces so
the two habit views speak the same language.

#### LH2-09 · The habit name is a section label sitting inside a card
**Severity: medium.** LH1-11 is not closed; it moved from one wrong token to another.
**Root cause:** the fix used `Label` as the card's title.

Measured: "EXERCISE" in `trends-d1-1366-light` is `(85,104,121)`, uppercase and tracked — the same
token as "HABITS" `(84,103,120)` and "GOALS" `(79,98,119)` on the Life page behind it, which are
section labels sitting *above* their cards. Identical on the Year and All-time cards. The result is
that the entire Trends dialog contains no Source Serif 4 anywhere except its own "Habits · trends"
heading — 27 cards across three tabs with no card title in any of them.

Breaks two lines directly:

> "Settings sheet: scrim + one frosted sheet, section label above each card, rows 8px tall with
> hairlines, switches 26 × 15 (on = Accent track, white knob). **Never place a section label over a
> card.**"

> "Card title: 15 / 1.3, Source Serif 4 500."

**Fix in source:** the habit name is a `Card title` — 15 / 1.3, Source Serif 4 500, Ink. The count
stays where it is; `7 of 9` measured `(137,134,127)`, a neutral Muted, which is right and matches
*"Right-hand hint on the same line: 11, Muted"*. Only the title token is wrong. Sentence case follows
from the same change — *"Sentence case everywhere except section labels"*.

### 5 · Measured and found NOT to be defects — so the auditor does not re-litigate them

1. **Light/dark parity.** All sixteen pairs identical in size, 99.1–99.8 % edge agreement. No reflow,
   no column-count change, nothing appears or disappears. Grounds `#EDEBE5` / `#191815` edge to edge.
2. **The token pair inverting by itself.** Hit fill measures `(74,94,112)` = `#4A5E70` in light and
   `(183,200,216)` = `#B7C8D8` in dark, with the number inverting to match. No component branches on
   theme and the result clears in both. This was the right call; keep it.
3. **One Accent for all nine habits, still.** Every hit cell, every bar, every dot in all 32 frames is
   the one Accent token. *"Never: … per-category colours (habits, calendars, budgets all use
   Accent)."* Do not let a later round "improve" this.
4. **The right-hand hint is Muted.** `(137,134,127)` on the month card, `(125,122,114)` on the year
   card — neutral, not the blue-tinted hint I recorded app-wide in round 1. These new cards are on the
   right side of that.
5. **Card responsive break points.** 1-up under 768, 2-up at 1024, 3-up at 1180+, as specified, on all
   three tabs. Column 3 stacks under column 1 at 1024 on Life with no empty row.
6. **The hollow rings in the Year grid's column 0.** Three of them, top-left of every card: the 29–31
   Dec 2025 days of the ISO week containing 1 Jan, out of range, drawn as outlines. Correct, and not
   to be confused with LH2-02, which is the *label* fault sitting above them.
7. **Radii and borders.** 24 px cells with a 3 px corner inset ≈ radius 5 (*"5 tags and checkboxes"*);
   cards inset 5 px ≈ radius 10. Hairlines only; the one 2 px border found in round 1 is gone.
8. **Text.** No word broken mid-word, no ellipsis inside a button, chip or segment, no orphan title
   line, no two-line button label — with the two exceptions written up as LH2-02 and LH2-04, both of
   which are overlaps rather than truncations.
9. **The dialog capped at ~898 px at 1920.** Raised in round 1, checked again, still app-wide: the
   Find and task-detail dialogs do the same. Recorded, not this row's.
10. **The month grid's ~130 px of empty card to its right at 393.** The grid is 7 × 24 px = 203 px in
    a ~340 px card. I looked hard at this and it is the natural width of a square-celled week grid,
    not a layout fault; stretching the cells would break the 24 px square that the Life strip and the
    Trends grid now share. Recorded so it is not "fixed" later.

### The six things you asked me to look at

**1 · Does the Rules card read as belonging under Autonomy? I cannot tell you, because it is in
none of the sixteen frames.** See ST1-01. What I *can* say from the frames I have bears on the
question and you should hear it before the re-shoot: at 1366 and 1920 the sheet lays `APPEARANCE
AND ACCOUNT` and `AUTONOMY` as a **two-column band** (Appearance x 249-676, Autonomy x 684-1108 at
1366). "Directly under Autonomy" is therefore not a position that exists above 1024 unless the
Rules card is placed *inside the right-hand column*. If it is rendered full-width — as
`NOTIFICATIONS` is — it will sit under Appearance **and** Autonomy equally, which makes it a fourth
peer section, not a refinement of the third. That is the difference between your two outcomes, and
it is decided by which column it lands in, not by its content. Shoot 1366 and I will tell you which
one happened.

**2 · Does the rule meta line read as fact or as control? Not judgeable — no frame.** The thing to
photograph it against, measured on the frames I do have: on this sheet a fact is Muted 10.5
(`batched 8am, 4pm`, `10 min before, with prep` — measured `(140,138,131)`) and a control is Accent
ink (`manage`, `open`, `edit` — `(119,134,146)` on Brain's equivalent link). If `Everything · Ask me
first` renders at `(140,138,131)` it is a fact and you are fine. The risk I would look for in the
frame is the opposite of the one you named: if the whole **row** is pressable, then a line that
correctly looks like a fact is nevertheless inside a tappable target, and the person who taps the
words "Ask me first" expecting a three-way control gets an edit dialog instead. That is a
label-honesty question of the same family as DISCREPANCIES rows 9, 11 and 12, and it needs the
pixels plus one tap, not my guess.

**3 · Notifications at 393: endless, and here is the measurement.** Group pitch is **77 px** exactly
(title tops at 111, 188, 265, 342, 419, 496, 573, 650, 727, 804 — ten groups), plus the switch-less
`Push to this device` row at ~47 and 24 px of card padding. The card runs from y 87 to
**about 916 — roughly 830 px tall.** The sheet's scroll viewport at 393 runs y 84 to 807 =
**723 px**. So the first card of the sheet is **1.15x the height of the window it lives in**, and
taller than the 852-px screen itself. You cannot see the section whole on the device, at any scroll
position. (The 830 is derived from the measured 77-px pitch, because the frame is a viewport capture
and the card runs off the bottom — that is ST1-01.) Against the desktop sheet the same card measures
**577 px** of a 703-px sheet at 1024 (**91 % of the scroll body**), 825 at 1366 (**77 %**) and 991 at
1920 (**63 %**).

That is the arithmetic. The reason it *reads* endless rather than thorough is the repetition, not
the height: the four device names are printed **forty times**, every group is the identical 77-px
block in the identical weight, and nothing distinguishes the two settings a person actually changes
from the eight they never will. README Principles 2: *"Say when the list ends. 'That's all until
4pm.' Blank space after it is correct, not a gap to fill."* On a phone this section never visibly
ends.

**The fix is arithmetic too, and it is the same fix as ST1-02.** Use the desktop shape at 393 — one
header row of device names, bare switches beneath — at a 46-px column pitch (42-px switch + 4)
instead of the desktop's measured 61.5. Four columns = 184 px of the card's 348-px inner width,
leaving **164 px** for the title, which fits every string in the set (the longest, `Memory review
ready`, measures about 118 px at 12.5). Two-line rows (title over meta) with the switches centred at
the right make the group about 46-54 px, so the card becomes **roughly 560 px** — inside the 723-px
viewport, and the section ends where a person can see it end. It also removes 30 of the 40 repeated
device labels.

**4 · The six-segment speed control at 393: not judgeable — no frame.** Nothing in the pass reaches
the Voice section at any width. See ST1-01. For what it is worth, the segment metric that governs it
is visible: `Seg` at 393 renders `Auto / Light / Dark` — three segments in the ~348-px card, so
~110 px each. Six segments in the same box is ~55 px each less padding, and `1.75x` at 12.5/500 is
~34 px of glyph. It will fit; whether it is *legible* and whether the taps clear 36 px is exactly
what the frame would show, and the frame does not exist.

**5 · Brain's column balance: column 3 is not short — it is still the tallest column, and losing
Rules made the ratio better and the page emptier.** Ink extents, light (dark within 2 px):

| width | col 1 | col 2 | col 3 | tallest ends | viewport | col-1 ink / col-3 ink, before to now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1366 | 100-382 (282) | 123-680 (557) | 120-751 (**631**) | 751 | 900 | 36 % to **61 %** |
| 1920 | 100-382 (282) | 123-607 (484) | 120-675 (**555**) | 675 | 1080 | 50 % to **70 %** |
| 1024 | 100-956 (col 3 stacked under col 1) | 123-695 | — | 956 | 1022 | one-column tail 457 to **261 px** |

So: **it was overfull before and this fixed the proportion.** DISCREPANCIES 24's headline number —
"the widest column holds 36 % of what the narrowest one does" — is now 61 % at 1366 and 70 % at
1920. The Rules card was roughly 200 px of column 3 and taking it out did what you hoped.

What it also did is ST1-08: the tallest column now ends at 675 of 1080 at 1920, so the whole bottom
**405 px** of the content rectangle is empty across all three columns, on top of column 1's 698-px
tail. Removing content improved a ratio and worsened a density. Both are true and you should have
both.

**6 · What the new card did to the sheet's rhythm — the damage I can measure is at 1024, and it is
real.** The Notifications card grew from **516 px (v21) to 577 px (v22)** — one extra group (46) and
the wrapped heading (15). Everything below it moved 61 px down. In
`v21/settings-d1-1024-light-prod.png` the line `Quiet hours, 9:30pm to 7am, apply to all but
security.` sits at y 654, clear of everything. In this pass it sits at y 714 — **under the demo
watermark chip and on the scroll fold**. See ST1-05. That is one card's worth of growth landing a
sentence in the one 22-px band of the 1024 viewport where two other things already live. Anything
you add below Autonomy inherits that shift.

### Defects

#### ST1-01 · BLOCKING (evidence) · Three of this row's four changes are in no frame in the pass — the Rules card, the six-segment speed control and the silence options were never photographed · all eight `settings-d1-*` frames

**Measured.** All eight Settings frames are **viewport** captures at scroll position 0: 393 x 852,
1024 x 768, 1366 x 900, 1920 x 1080. The deepest any of them reaches is `AUTONOMY` row 6 (`Bills`)
at 1920, y 981, with the card still running past the sheet's bottom edge at 1035. `RULES FOR MY EA`
appears nowhere. Neither does `VOICE`, so neither the six speeds nor the Off/10s/60s silence options
are in the pass either.

The rig is already capable of the frame I need: `brain-d1-393-light-prod.png` is **393 x 1772** — a
full-page capture. `settings-d1-393-light-prod.png` is 393 x 852. Tabs are captured full-height and
dialogs are captured at the viewport, so a long scrolling dialog is only ever photographed down to
its first fold.

**The line it breaks.** My standing brief for this review: *"a frame missing for a screen the input
list names is itself a defect."* Your brief for this round names the Rules card first and asks two
questions about it; the pass cannot answer either.

**Fix in source.** In the device-pass rig, capture `screen`- and `dialog`-kind surfaces at their
scroll height rather than the viewport height (the same path that produces the 1772-px Brain frame),
or emit `settings-*-a/b/c` frames at successive scroll offsets. Either gives the missing frames and
closes questions 1, 2 and 4 in one pass.

#### ST1-02 · HIGH · `TELEGRAM` breaks mid-word to `TELEGRA / M` in the device column heading, at every desktop width, in both schemes · `settings-d1-{1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-prod.png`

**Measured** at 1366: heading glyph runs are `IPHONE` x 861-900, `IPAD` 931-954, `PC` 996-1011,
`TELEGRA` 1039-1091 with `M` alone on a second line at y 162-173. Switch-column pitch is **61.5 px**
(switch boxes at 858-900, 920-962, 981-1023, 1043-1085), and the header cell is being wrapped to
roughly the 42-px switch width, not the 61.5-px column. Identical at 1024 and 1920 — the sheet is
897 px wide at all three, so the geometry never changes. Identical in dark.

**The lines it breaks.** This review's rule 5, verbatim: *"No word broken mid-word."* And *"No
single-word orphan line in a title."* The heading row is also the only place in the sheet where a
label is not allowed to fail, because it is the key to forty controls.

**Fix in source.** Let the header cell take the column's full pitch rather than the switch's width
(`minWidth` on the header cell to match the column, or `numberOfLines={1}` with the cell sized to
the wider of switch and label). There is nowhere for it to collide: see ST1-07 — the label column
carries about 475 px of empty at 1920. Doing ST1-03 as well makes `Telegram` narrower again and
gives the fix headroom.

#### ST1-03 · MEDIUM-HIGH · The same four labels are proper-cased at 393 and upper-cased at every desktop width, and the caps are what causes ST1-02 · all eight `settings-d1-*` frames

**Measured.** At 393 the labels render `iPhone`, `iPad`, `PC`, `Telegram` — correct proper-noun
casing, legible, all four fitting the 348-px card. At 1024/1366/1920 the same four render `IPHONE`,
`IPAD`, `PC`, `TELEGRAM`. One control, two casings, decided by a breakpoint.

**The line it breaks.** README Content: *"Sentence case everywhere except section labels (tracked
caps) and proper nouns."* `iPhone`, `iPad` and `Telegram` are proper nouns whose casing is part of
the name; a column heading is not a section label. The v2.1 abbreviations (`IPH`, `IPAD`, `PC`,
`TG`) had the excuse that they were abbreviations. Full names do not.

**Fix in source.** Drop `textTransform: "uppercase"` from the header cell and render the same
strings the 393 layout already renders. `Telegram` at 10.5/400 measures about 48 px against
`TELEGRAM`'s ~60, which fits the 61.5-px pitch on its own and closes ST1-02 as a side effect.

#### ST1-04 · MEDIUM · The device headings are drawn in Accent ink at section-label size and tracking, so a row of four things that cannot be tapped is the same colour as the four things on the screen that can · all eight `settings-d1-*` frames

**Measured** at 1366 light, darkest 4 % of glyph pixels: heading ink `(89,107,124)`; the
`NOTIFICATIONS` section label 40 px above it `(88,106,122)`. One part in 255. Against them, the
group titles are `(65,64,60)` (Ink) and the group metas `(140,138,131)` (Muted). Dark agrees.

**The lines it breaks.** README Principles 3: *"Colour means you can act. The steel accent marks
verbs, labels, the recommended option and the current tab. Nothing decorative gets colour."* And
README Colour, Where colour goes: *"Accent ink: section labels, primary-verb text, links, expiry
text, recommended option number, active tab, provenance links."* A column heading is none of those.
There is a second cost this row created: `NOTIFICATIONS` and `IPHONE IPAD PC TELEGRAM` are now the
same size, the same tracking, the same colour and 40 px apart, so the sheet appears to have two
section labels for one section.

**Not this row's to fix.** `v21/settings-d1-1024-light-prod.png` measures the same ink at
`(94,111,127)`, so the styling predates ST-1. What ST-1 did was more than double the amount of it.
Muted (`(140,138,131)`) is the correct token for a heading that only describes, and it would put the
row in the same voice as the group metas beneath it.

#### ST1-05 · HIGH · At 1024 the demo watermark covers the first half of the quiet-hours sentence and the scroll fold cuts the other half through its descenders — and this is new, caused by this row's extra card height · `settings-d1-1024-{light,dark}-prod.png`

**Measured.** The watermark chip occupies x 8-190, y about 700-722. The line `Quiet hours, 9:30pm to
7am, apply to all but security.` begins at x 64 (the sheet's left edge) at y 707-720. Everything up
to and including `to ` is behind the chip; the reader sees `7am, apply to all but security.`
beginning mid-sentence, and the scroll viewport ends at y about 722, slicing the descenders of
`apply` and `security`. Identical in dark.

**It is new.** `v21/settings-d1-1024-light-prod.png`: Notifications card y 125-641 (**516 px**), the
quiet-hours line at y **654**, clear of the chip in both axes. This pass: card y 125-702
(**577 px**, +61 for the tenth group and the wrapped heading), the line at y **714**. The card's
growth put it there.

**The line it breaks.** The V2.1 A-1 watermark rule: the watermark *"must be legible and must not sit
over a control or another line."* It sits over a line. Also README Principles 7, *"Show the work"* —
a sentence stating when notifications are suppressed is not optional detail.

**Fix in source.** Two halves, and only the first is yours. **Yours:** move the quiet-hours line
inside the Notifications card as its footer meta (it is a fact about that card, and it would stop
drifting the next time a group is added), which takes it off the fold and out of the chip's band at
1024. **K-1's:** the chip should not overlap a dialog at all — this is the material half of K1-03
landing somewhere new for the third time.

#### ST1-06 · MEDIUM-HIGH · At 393 the Notifications card is about 830 px against a 723-px scroll viewport, so the first of six sections cannot be seen whole on the device · `settings-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod.png`

Measurements and the proposed fix are in answer 3 above and are not repeated here.

**The lines it breaks.** README Principles 2: *"Say when the list ends. 'That's all until 4pm.' Blank
space after it is correct, not a gap to fill."* And this review's rule 7: *"393 reads as a phone, not
a squeezed desktop"* — this reads as a settings form ported to a phone by stacking, which is the same
class of read as Josh's *"squished"*.

**I am partly unsure and will say so.** The labelled-row layout is unambiguously *clearer per row*
than the four unlabelled 40-px switches were at 393 in v2.1 — that half of your change is right and
I would not undo it. What I am confident about is the total: ten identical blocks, forty repeated
device names, and a card taller than the screen. The measured alternative in answer 3 keeps the
clarity and buys back roughly 270 px.

#### ST1-07 · LOW-MEDIUM · At desktop the label column carries about 475 px of empty while the four switch columns are ~20 px too narrow to hold their own headings · `settings-d1-{1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-prod.png`

**Measured** at 1920: the longest group title, `Replies from your EA`, ends at x 660; the first
switch column begins at x 1135. **475 px** of empty between the two halves of every row, 1920 and
1366 alike (the sheet is 897 px at both), and more than 500 on the shorter rows. Meanwhile
`TELEGRAM` cannot fit a 61.5-px column.

**The line it reads against.** This review's rule 7: *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone
columns"* — the row is a dashboard row with a 475-px hole in it. There is no pack line that forbids
the void as such, so I file this as low-medium and mainly as the reason ST1-02 has an easy fix
rather than a hard one: the space the headings need is sitting immediately to their left.

**Fix in source.** Cap the label column (`maxWidth` about 360, or flex the switch block wider) so the
grid closes up, and give the freed width to the four device columns. One change closes ST1-02,
ST1-07 and part of ST1-04's crowding.

#### ST1-08 · MEDIUM · At 1920 Brain's content now ends 405 px above the fold, so the tab reads as three short stacks on a large screen · `brain-d1-1920-{light,dark}-prod.png`

**Measured.** Column ink ends at y 382 / 607 / 675 against a 1080-px viewport. The bottom **405 px**
of the 1499-px-wide content rectangle is empty across all three columns; column 1 (the 584-px
`1.3fr` slot) has a **698-px** tail. Occupied ink area is about 620 k px² of a 1.47 M px² content
rectangle — **42 %**. The N-1 round-2 numbers for the same frame were 271 / 432 / 747 with the page
filling 1080; removing the Rules section took about 190 px off the only column that reached the
bottom.

**The line it breaks.** This review's rule 7: *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns."*
Note what it does **not** break: README Layout, *"Leave the bottom of a column empty when the content
ends. Do not stretch cards to match heights."* Empty column feet are correct. What is not correct is
that all three feet are empty for 405 px at once.

**Not this row's to fix, and I would not have you fix it.** The cause is the column assignment
recorded in DISCREPANCIES 24 — a column holding only the capture card and Find is 282 px tall
however much data the tab holds — and moving `Latest in` back to column 1 is Josh's call, not ST-1's.
Removing Rules was right and it improved the ratio; it simply also removed the one thing that was
hiding the shape. Worth adding to row 24 as the new measurement.

### Recorded, not raised as this row's defects

- **The Settings sheet's card-to-ground step is three times the app's.** Sheet fill `(220,220,219)`,
  card fill `(251,251,251)` — a step of **31**. Everywhere else the step is ground `(237,235,229)` to
  card `(247,247,244)` = **10**. README Surfaces: *"The card-to-ground step is deliberately small:
  one visible layer, no float."* Identical in `demo/v21`, so app-wide and older than ST-1 — but it is
  why the Notifications card reads as a slab rather than a frosted surface.
- **The light Settings sheet is the only neutral surface in the app.** `(251,251,251)` and
  `(220,220,219)` have R = G = B; every other light surface is warm by 8-10 between red and blue. The
  dark sheet is correctly warm (`(56,55,52)` on `(38,36,33)`). Identical in v21, so app-wide.
- **The off switch's knob is 1.14 : 1 against its own track in light and 1.56 : 1 in dark.** Light
  off: track `(234,234,234)`, knob `(250,250,250)`. Dark off: track `(72,70,67)`, knob `(42,40,37)`.
  On measures 5.27 : 1 in dark and is unmistakable. So "off" reads as *absence of a dark dot*, not as
  *knob on the left*. DISCREPANCIES row 8 already ruled that the mock's geometry and colours win, so
  this is a decision, not a defect — but ST-1 put **forty** of them in one card at 393 and the ruling
  now governs the densest control in the app. Worth Josh's eye, not a fix.
- **The breakpoint behaves as you described.** 393 gives labelled rows, 1024 gives the four-column
  grid. There is no frame at 768 itself, so I cannot confirm exactly where it flips.
- **Blur budget under 768: still not judgeable.** Nothing in either 393 frame sits behind a blurred
  surface — the sheet covers the viewport and there is no bar over content. Same answer as N-1.

Brain losing Rules is a good change and I would keep it: the section belongs with the autonomy
defaults it qualifies, column 3 was overfull, and the ratio moved 25 points in the right direction.
The Settings half is where the work is, and the first thing it needs is frames.

### 1 · Are ST1-02, ST1-03 and ST1-04 closed? Yes. All three, all eight frames, both schemes.

One token was the whole of it, exactly as you diagnosed.

| | round 1 | this pass |
|---|---|---|
| casing | `IPHONE IPAD PC TELEGRAM` at 1024/1366/1920, `iPhone iPad PC Telegram` at 393 | `iPhone iPad PC Telegram` at **all four widths** |
| `TELEGRAM` | broken to `TELEGRA` / `M`, second line at y 162–173 | one line, glyph run x 1039–1083 = **44 px** in a **68 px** column, 12 px clear each side |
| heading ink (1366 light) | `(89,107,124)` — one part in 255 from the `NOTIFICATIONS` section label `(88,106,122)` | `(151,149,142)` — one part in 5 from the group metas `(146,144,137)`, 62 parts from the section label `(98,114,129)` |

So `ST1-02` **CLOSED**, `ST1-03` **CLOSED**, `ST1-04` **CLOSED**. The sheet no longer appears to have
two section labels for one section, and the row of four things you cannot tap is no longer the same
colour as the four things you can. The 68 px column was the right call and not only for `Telegram`:
`iPhone` is 33 px, `iPad` 19, `PC` 13, so 68 leaves the shortest column 55 px of slack and the
longest 24 — the next device name has somewhere to go.

**ST1-01 is closed too, and your reading of it was better than mine.** I asked for a rig change;
two declared states were the right answer and I would not now take the rig change instead. On the
question you put to me — *is a scrolled dialog frame honest evidence?* — **yes, with one stated
limit.** A scrolled frame is honest about what it shows and silent about what it does not, so it
buys evidence at the price of coverage, and the price is visible in this pass in two places:

- **It cannot photograph a section taller than the body it lives in.** The Rules card at 1366 is
  455 px in a 750 px scroll body, so one offset shows it with its label and both neighbours — that
  is a complete piece of evidence. The Notifications card at 393 is 830 px in a 723 px body, so
  **no offset can ever show it whole**, which is why ST1-06 has to be argued from a number and not
  from a picture. That is a property of the screen, not a fault of the rig.
- **Three offsets is not a sheet.** Between `settings-d1`'s last row at 1366 (`Time zone`) and
  `settings-rules`'s first (`Sync`) sits `Devices · Josh's iPhone, Josh's iPad, This PC · manage`,
  which in this pass is photographed **only at 1920**. If that row breaks at 1366 no frame here
  says so.

Neither is a reason to touch the overlay branch of `shot()` — your K1-01 / B3R1-01 reasoning holds
and growing the viewport behind a dialog would trade a real defect for a worse one. Both are
reasons to keep naming declared states after the panel they exist to show, which is what these two
do. No further action.

### 2 · ST1-05: measured, and it is **NOT cleared**. It moved 14 px and needed about 20.

You asked me to measure rather than assume, and to say so plainly if it had not cleared. It has not.

**What the fix bought.** Un-wrapping the heading took 14 px out of the Notifications card and
everything below it moved up by exactly that much: at 1024 the card's fourth hairline sits at y 628
in this pass against y 642 in `demo/v21`, and the quiet-hours line moved from y 714 (round 1) to
**y 696–707** (glyph band; x-height 698–703, descenders to 707). Your arithmetic was right.

**Why it still lands.** The watermark chip's pill fill begins at **y 702** and runs to x 192. The
line begins at x 84. So the pill covers **x 84–192 × y 702–707** — the baseline and the descenders
of `Quiet hours, 9:30pm to`, 22 of the sentence's 53 characters. The rendering is worse to read
than round 1's, not better: in round 1 the words were *hidden* and the reader started at `7am`; now
they are *sheared*, so the reader sees half-height letterforms and has to decide whether they are
words. The fold half of round 1's finding **is** fixed — the line is no longer sliced by the scroll
edge, and `security.` at the right renders whole.

**And it is not a Notifications problem at all.** The two new states prove it. At 1024 the chip cuts
whatever line lands in that band, in every state:

| frame | the line the chip cuts |
|---|---|
| `settings-d1-1024-{light,dark}` | `Quiet hours, 9:30pm to 7am, apply to all but security.` |
| `settings-voice-d1-1024-{light,dark}` | `Everything` — the first row of the Focus filters card |
| `settings-rules-d1-1024-{light,dark}` | `How long JSTACK waits with no interaction before asking for your passkey again.` |

Three different cards, three different heights, same band. Chip x 7–192, pill top y 702; the sheet
at 1024 spans x 63–960 and its body runs to y ≈ 722. **The chip is inside the dialog's content
rectangle at 1024 in every state there is.**

**The line it breaks.** The V2.1 A-1 watermark rule: the watermark *"must be legible and must not
sit over a control or another line."* It sits over a line in six of this pass's eight 1024 frames.

**Fix in source.** Round 1 gave you half and you were right not to take it — moving the quiet-hours
line inside the Notifications card would have moved one sentence out of the band and left the other
two in it. **The whole fix is K-1's**: the demo chip must be placed against the topmost surface, not
the page, so that an open dialog either pushes it below the dialog's bottom edge or suppresses it.
Nothing ST-1 can do to a card changes where the chip is. Report ST1-05 as **open and reassigned to
K-1**, with the three-state evidence above attached to K1-03.

### 3 · The two new panels

#### The Rules card · it does belong under Autonomy, and its meta line is a fact

**Position: the good outcome of the two I named in round 1.** At 1366 and 1920 the sheet lays
`APPEARANCE AND ACCOUNT` and `AUTONOMY` as a two-column band, and the Rules block is rendered
**inside the right-hand column** — 1366: label and card at x 684–1108, directly under the Autonomy
card and directly above `SECURITY AND BEHAVIOUR`; 1920: x 962–1385, the same. It is not full-width,
so it does not become a fourth peer sitting under Appearance and Autonomy equally. At 1024 and 393
the sheet is one column and the block falls immediately after Autonomy in the flow. **Four widths,
both schemes, the right column.** That question is answered and answered well.

**Meta line: a fact, measured.** `Filing things that arrive · Do it — tell me after` renders at
`(149,147,140)` — the Muted token, one part in 4 from the Notifications group metas `(146,144,137)`
and from `the EA can ask; only you can change` `(140,138,131)`. Against it the same sheet's links
measure Accent: `open` on the Sync row `(118,133,147)`, `continue` `(124,138,151)`. So the meta is
**not** coloured like a control. The residual risk I named in round 1 — a fact-looking line inside a
pressable row — is answered by the card itself: there is no chevron, no row affordance, and an
explicit `Edit rules` button below the list. The control is named and separate. Good.

Two things are wrong with the card and one of them is bad. See ST1-09, ST1-10, ST1-14, ST1-15.

Also worth recording, not raised: the block is clean where it matters. Badge `7` measures
`(79,127,168)` = `#4F7FA8`, Marker exactly, on a count badge — the allowed use. Section label
`(91,108,124)` Accent ink. Rule text `(74,73,70)` Ink. Row hairlines only. The card has no nested
scrollbar (the thumb at x 1109–1113 is the sheet's own, outside the card at x 1108). `Edit rules`,
`Export`, `Hold to lock` and `Add a focus` are all consistently placed — Josh's *"some buttons
centred, some left-aligned"* does not reproduce anywhere in these eight frames.

#### The Voice panel · the six speeds fit and are legible; the control is too small on a phone and never grows

**Legibility at 393: pass, measured.** All six render in full — `0.8x 1x 1.2x 1.5x 1.75x 2x` — no
ellipsis, no clip, no wrap, in both schemes. The longest label `1.75x` has a glyph run of **25 px**
inside a **33.3 px** cell, 4 px clear each side. Digit height is **9 px**, identical to `Warm` in
the Style control directly above it (9 px) and one under `Off` (10 px), so they are the same type
size as their neighbours and nowhere near the 10.5 px floor. `1x` is set heavier than its
neighbours, which is the selected-chip weight the pack grants. On the question you asked —
*do they fit and are they legible* — **yes to both.**

`Off / 10s / 60s` is present, correct, three segments at 68.7 px, and carries no timer anywhere on

What is wrong is the tap target and the fact that the control is the same 200 px at 1920 as at 393.
See ST1-11. And see ST1-12 for a word inside the End phrases field that exists at two widths and not
the other two, and ST1-13 for what the Voice offset shows about the sheet's two columns.

### 4 · Did the fixes break anything? No. One thing they very slightly improved.

I looked for regressions specifically and found none. The heading fix is a strict improvement: the
14 px it recovered went into moving the whole sheet up 14 px, and the 62 → 68 px column widening
took its 24 px out of the label column's dead space, so ST1-07's gap fell from **475 px to 455 px**
rather than colliding with anything. At 1920 the longest group title `Replies from your EA` ends at
x 660 and the first switch column now begins at x 1115 — still 455 px of nothing, still no
collision. Brain is the same page it was: columns end at y 382 / 594 / 662 against a 1080 viewport
at 1920, the `MEMORY 4` and `REPLIES 2` Marker badges are the only Marker on the tab, and the
watermark (y 836–850) still clears the rail health line (y 874–887), so B-32 stays clear.

Everything new below is a thing the **new frames revealed**, not a thing the fixes broke. That
distinction matters for who owns them and I have kept it.

#### ST1-09 · HIGH · **NEW** · The Rules card is two stacked surfaces, and in dark its inner panel is 30 levels lighter than every other card on the same sheet · all eight `settings-rules-d1-*`, worst in the four dark frames

**Measured, dark, 1366** (identical at 1024 and 1920; 393 carries the same inner value):

| surface | fill | step from the one behind it |
|---|---|---|
| sheet ground | `(39,36,33)` | — |
| Schedules / Autonomy / Security card (every other card) | `(56,55,52)` | +17 |
| Rules card, outer frame (x 686–697 and 1096–1107, 12 px wide) | `(48,46,44)` | **+9** |
| Rules card, inner list panel (x 699–1095) | `(86,84,82)` | **+38 from the frame, +47 from the ground** |

Three visible layers, and the middle one is *darker* than a card while the top one is **30 levels
lighter** than every other card on the same surface. In light the same structure measures ground
`(217,216,216)` → frame `(247,247,247)` → inner `(254,254,254)` against a normal card `(251,251,251)`
— a card-to-inner step of **3**. So the light frames get away with it and the dark frames do not:
**the same construction is a 3-step in light and a 30-step in dark, ten times the contrast**, which
is the signature of an inner fill that has a light token and no dark one.

**The lines it breaks.** README Surfaces: *"The card-to-ground step is deliberately small: one
visible layer, no float."* This is three. And this review's rule 6: *"Dark tokens applied
throughout"* — the inner panel is the one surface in these frames that does not have one.

**And the sheet already contains the correct answer.** `SCHEDULES` is the same object — a card
holding a list of rows — and it draws **one** surface with 1 px hairlines between rows. So do
`NOTIFICATIONS` and `FOCUS FILTERS`. Rules is the only list card on the sheet that wraps its rows in
a second surface, so it is inconsistent within one scroll of itself.

**Fix in source.** Delete the inner panel. Let the rule rows sit directly on the Rules card with the
hairline separators they already have, exactly as `Schedules` does, and keep the hint line and
`Edit rules` where they are. If the inset must stay for a reason I cannot see from a still, give it
a dark token that lands a few levels off the card fill (≈ `(60,59,56)` against the `(56,55,52)`
card), not `(86,84,82)`.

#### ST1-10 · MEDIUM-HIGH · **NEW** · A raw silo identifier, `family1`, is printed in a rule the owner reads · all eight `settings-rules-d1-*`

**Measured.** Rule 3 reads, at every width and in both schemes: `Anything naming a child goes to
family1 and stays sensitive`. `family1` is an internal silo id — `jstack-app/data/labels.ts:11`
declares the union `"personal:josh" | "personal:joce" | "family1" | "family2" | "work"`, and line 40
gives that id a display name: `family1: { shortName: "family", who: "JO and Joce" }`.

**It is provably wrong here because the app itself does it right elsewhere.** On
`brain-d1-1366-light-prod.png` the same silo renders as the tag `family` on the Latest-in row, beside
`kids`, `legal`, `personal`, `money` and `journal` — display names throughout. Two surfaces, one
value, two spellings, and the one that leaks the id is the one whose whole job is to state a rule in
words the owner can check.

**The line it breaks.** README Content: *"Sentence case everywhere except section labels (tracked
caps) and proper nouns."* `family1` is neither, and it is not a word. It also breaks the card's own
promise: this is the record of what the EA has been taught, so its text is the one place where the
app must speak the owner's vocabulary rather than its own.

**Fix in source.** Render the rule's scope through `shortName` (or `who`) rather than the raw `Silo`
key when composing the rule string, so it reads `…goes to family and stays sensitive`. The same
lookup is presumably already in the path that draws Brain's tags.

#### ST1-11 · MEDIUM · **NEW** · The six speed segments are 33.3 px wide against the pack's 36 px phone minimum, and the segment track is the same 200 px at 1920 as it is at 393 · `settings-voice-d1-*`, the tap-target half at 393 only

**Measured at 393.** Speed track x **163–362 = 200 px**, height 38 px, six segments → **33.3 px per
segment**; the selected pill measures 198–231 = 33 px wide. In the same card the Style control is the
same 200 px track with three segments = **66.7 px**, and `Off / 10s / 60s` is a 206 px track =
**68.7 px**.

**The line it breaks.** README Interaction, verbatim: *"Tap targets 36px minimum on phone."*
33.3 < 36. Six of them in a row, each 3 px under, on the control that decides how fast a voice you
are listening to speaks — a thing a person changes while walking.

**The second half, at desktop.** The track is a fixed ~200 px at every width: 393 = 200, 1024 = 198,
1366 = 198, 1920 = 200. At 1920 that leaves the `Speed` label ending at x 1010 and its control
starting at x 1172 — the same class of hole as ST1-07 — while the segments stay at 33 px on a screen
with room for 100. Rule 7 again: *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns."*

**Fix in source.** Let the segmented control fill the row's control column rather than sit at a fixed
width, and floor the per-segment width at 36 px below 768. At 393 the card's inner width is 348 px,
so six segments have room for 46 px each with the label above rather than beside — which also
removes the orphan noted next. If six will not fit a phone row at 36 px, the honest alternative is
the pack's Options 1-3-1 pattern, not a shrunken segment.

*Recorded with it, not filed separately:* at 393 the `End my turn after a silence` meta wraps to
`off by default · a pause is not an` / `answer` — a single-word orphan on a meta line, caused by the
segment claiming 206 px of a 348 px row. Widening the label column fixes both.

#### ST1-12 · MEDIUM · **NEW · and I am unsure what it is, which is why I am naming it** · A word in Accent ink, `continue`, renders inside the End phrases field at 393 and 1024 and is absent at 1366 and 1920 · `settings-voice-d1-{393,1024}-{light,dark}`

**Measured.** At 1024 the End phrases field spans x 94–924; its scroll thumb sits at x 858–862 and
the word `continue` at **x 871–913, y 433–449 — outside the thumb, between the scrollbar and the

1366 (field x 697–1095) and 1920 (x 973–1372) the field shows the thumb and **nothing else**, in both
schemes.

**Why I cannot close it either way.** If `continue` is a control, a control exists on the phone and
the tablet and vanishes on the two widths with the most room for it. If it is a third end phrase,
it is being drawn on the first line's baseline, to the right of the field's own scrollbar, in Accent
instead of body ink — and the field claims to hold `that's all` and `thanks, that's it` when it holds

**The lines it is measured against.** README Colour, *"Accent ink: section labels, primary-verb text,
links, expiry text, recommended option number, active tab, provenance links"* — a phrase inside a
text field is none of those. And this review's rule 6's principle applied across widths: nothing
should appear or disappear that is not a deliberate density decision.

**Fix in source.** Find what renders to the right of the End phrases textarea's scrollbar and either
give it a label and a place at all four widths, or stop rendering it. Inspecting the component at
393 with the field focused will say which reading is true in about a minute.

#### ST1-13 · MEDIUM-HIGH · **NEW** · At the Voice scroll offset the Settings sheet's entire left column is empty — zero ink across the full height of the viewport at 1366 and 1920 · `settings-voice-d1-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}`

**Measured.** Ink-mask pixel counts inside the sheet's left column, over the whole visible body:

| frame | left column | ink px | of |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings-voice-d1-1366-light` | x 249–676, y 105–855 | **0** | 320,250 |
| `settings-voice-d1-1920-light` | x 528–950, y 110–1010 | **0** | 379,800 |
| `settings-rules-d1-1366-light` (same sheet, another offset) | same box | 54,977 | 320,250 (17.2 %) |
| `settings-d1-1366-light` | same box | 55,776 | 320,250 (17.4 %) |

Zero. Not sparse — **nothing at all**, for 750 px at 1366 and 900 px at 1920, in both schemes. Half
the dialog is a blank slab with the Today page ghosting through it, and because the sheet is frosted
you can read `Talk with EA` and card outlines through the hole. At 1920 that is **422 × 900 px =
47 % of the dialog's content rectangle** showing nothing.

**Why it happens and how much is this row's.** The sheet's left column holds Appearance-and-account
plus Schedules and ends at about y 705 at 1920; the right column holds Autonomy, Rules,
Security-and-behaviour, the file and voice numbers, Voice and Focus filters and runs past 2,000 px.
ST-1 added the Rules block to the **right** column and nothing to the left — at 1366 the block spans
y 241 (label) to 715 (card foot), **about 475 px** — so this row deepened an existing imbalance by
roughly half a viewport. The imbalance predates ST-1; the frame that shows it does not.

**The line it reads against.** README Layout permits an empty column foot — *"Leave the bottom of a
column empty when the content ends. Do not stretch cards to match heights"* — and that is a rule for
a page you can see whole. It does not license a scrolling two-column dialog in which the reader can
scroll into a viewport that is 100 % one column. This review's rule 7, *"1024 reads as a tablet, not
a stretched phone"* and *"1920 reads as a dashboard"*, is what it fails: at the Voice offset a 1920
desktop is showing a 420 px phone column and a grey field.

**Fix in source, and I would not have ST-1 take it alone.** The sheet's sections need balancing
across the two columns rather than being dealt in declaration order — Voice and Focus filters are the
