is a Settings-sheet layout decision, not a Rules-card decision, so if this row does not want it,
record it with the two zero measurements above and hand it on. It should not be closed silently:
until this pass no frame in the project had ever been taken at that offset.

#### ST1-14 · MEDIUM · **NEW** · The `RULES FOR MY EA` label sits 3–5 px under the Autonomy card and 12–15 px above its own — the inverse of the pack's spacing, at every width · all eight `settings-rules-d1-*`

**Measured**, card-fill edges and glyph rows, light (dark identical):

| width | Autonomy card fill ends | label glyph ink | Rules card fill starts | gap above | gap below |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1366 | y 237 | 241–249 | 262 | **3** | 12 |
| 1920 | 327 | 332–339 | 352 | **4** | 12 |
| 1024 | 186 | 191–195 | 211 | **4** | 15 |
| 393 | 174 | 180–186 | 199 | **5** | 12 |

Against it, the next label down on the same sheet, `SECURITY AND BEHAVIOUR` at 1366: Rules card ends
y 714, label 728–733, Security card starts 746 — **14 above, 13 below**. So the RULES label is about
11 px tighter above than its own peer, and four times closer to the card it does not label than to
the card it does.

**The line it breaks.** The pack's spacing scale, as quoted in N1-11: *"Between a section label and
its card: 8."* Here it is 12–15 below and 3–5 above — the relationship reversed.

**Why it matters more than 11 px normally would.** This is the label that has to say *these are the
rules that qualify the autonomy defaults above*. Position is doing that job correctly — see answer 3
— but it is doing it with a 3 px gap that welds the label to the Autonomy card, which is a spacing
bug that happens to read the way the design wants. That is not a stable way to communicate a
relationship: set it to 16 above / 8 below and the block reads as its own section, which is what its
typography already says it is. If the intent really is subordination, the honest form is to put the
rules **inside** the Autonomy card under a hairline, not to rely on a squeezed margin.

**Fix in source.** Give the Rules section the sheet's standard section-label margins (16 above,
8 below, matching `SECURITY AND BEHAVIOUR`'s neighbours), or move the block inside the Autonomy card.

#### ST1-15 · LOW · **NEW** · A rule line orphans `first` on a line of its own at 1366 and 1920 · `settings-rules-d1-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}`

Rule 2 sets as `Never send anything on my behalf without showing me the words` / `first`. At 1024 the
same string fits one line; at 393 it breaks as `…without showing` / `me the words first`, which is
fine. So it is the two desktop widths only, both schemes.
**The line it breaks.** This review's rule 5: *"No single-word orphan line in a title."* The rule
text is the row's title — the primary line, with a Muted meta beneath it.
**I am partly unsure and say so:** these are user-authored strings, so the app cannot guarantee a
good break for arbitrary text, and `text-wrap: pretty` is the general answer rather than anything
content-specific. Low severity for that reason. **Fix in source:** `textWrap: "pretty"` on the rule
title, which costs nothing and removes the class.

#### How this round was done

**Programmatic, over all 892 frames.**

1. **Inventory against the file-name grammar.** Every file parsed as
   `<screen>-d<day>-<width>-<scheme>-<flavour>.png`; 892 parsed, 4 unparsed (the
   `brain-proposal-*` set, correctly outside the pass). Forty families. Thirty-one hold the
   full 24 (4 widths × 2 schemes × 3 passes); `arrange` and `arrange-life` hold 18 (no 393);
   `decision-section`, `life-config`, `offline`, `talk`, `mic-listening`, `sync-queued`,
   `sync-conflict` hold 16 (test only, both days). **Nothing missing, nothing extra, no
   `-prod` frame of a rig-only state.**
2. **Blank / wrong-screen / below-the-fold sweep.** For every frame, the first row of ink
   more than 10 levels off the frame's own corner colour, compared with that width's
   viewport height. **No blank frame and no wrong screen. Twenty-four frames flagged: all of
   them `locked` — see S6-01.**
3. **Dark-ground sweep.** Corner pixel of all 446 dark frames against `#191815` = (25,24,21).
   Every non-matching frame is a scrimmed modal or an element frame; **no dark frame paints a
   ground that is not the warm token.**
4. **Light/dark parity sweep.** Contrast-normalised edge maps, column-occupancy profiles
   compared per light/dark pair. Column differences are 0–7 px of the frame width on every
   pair. **No dark reflow anywhere in the pass.**
5. **LV-09 (1) — prod vs test on day 1.** Full RGB diff of all 260 `-d1-…-prod` frames
   against their `-d1-…-test` twins (33 families hold both). Method and result below.
6. **LV-09 (2) — day 1 vs day 2.** Full RGB diff of all 316 `-d1-…-test` frames against
   `-d2-…-test`. Method and result below.

**By eye.** I opened and read, at full or near-full resolution, these 84 frames (crops of

#### LV-09 (1) · prod and test on the same screen and day

**Method.** For each of the 260 `-d1-…-prod` frames I loaded the `-d1-…-test` twin, checked
the size, then took the per-pixel max-channel absolute difference. I report three thresholds
(> 8, > 32, > 64) so that anti-aliasing noise can be told from a content change, and the
bounding box of the > 64 set.

**Result.** No size mismatch anywhere. 118 of the 260 pairs are bit-identical. Of the 142
that differ, **every one differs only in wall-clock-driven ink**, and only 36 pairs carry any
difference above 64 levels:

| what differs | families | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| the calendar grid's 1 px **now-rule**, 4–6 px of vertical travel | `today`, `triage`, `decision-bill`, `undo-toast` | `today-d1-1366-light-*`: the whole diff is x 720–989, **y 493–497** — a 5-row band; nothing else on a 1366 × 1141 page differs |
| the agent feed's **relative times**, "9 h ago" → "10 h ago", which rewraps the row | `agents` | `agents-d1-1366-light-*`: prod "9 h ago · Calendar write-back rejected" on one line, test "10 h ago · Calendar write-back / rejected" on two; diff bbox x 689–944, y 398–481 |
| the **mic orb's** pulse phase, ≤ 250 px at ≤ 42 levels | most tab pages | `life-d1-1920-light-*`: 45 px, bbox x 1865–1879 y 1011–1057 — the orb's own rectangle |
| **backdrop-blur resampling** behind a scrim, max amplitude 42 | `find` at 1366 and 1920 | `find-d1-1920-light-*`: 65,449 px above 8, **452 above 32, 0 above 64** — a whole-page haze, not a content change; I cropped both at 1.5× at the one place the page differs in height and they are the same page |

**Verdict on LV-09 (1): PASS on content, with one evidence finding.** I could not find a
single pixel where the production build shows different *content* from the test build on the
same screen and day. What I did find is that the pass is not reproducible, because two things
in it are driven by the machine clock rather than the fixture: the calendar's now-rule and
the agent feed's "N h ago". That is **S6-37** below, low, and it is worth fixing because the
audit's own A-1 line ("prod and test frames identical on the same screen and day") cannot be
met by pixel equality while it stands.

#### LV-09 (2) · day 2 must differ where it claims to

**Method.** All 316 `-d1-…-test` frames diffed against `-d2-…-test`; a size change counts as
a difference; otherwise the count of pixels differing by more than 32 levels.

**Families that change on day 2 — correct.** `today` (page height 2561 → 2527 at 393, 1141 →
1062 at 1366: the "since" line and the Needs-you list), `agents` (page 2272 → 2321 at 393:
the EA report card), `task-detail` (267,314 px at 1920: the delegation on t1), `brain`,
`offline`, `mic-listening` (~3,000 px each: Latest in), `trends`, `trends-week`,
`trends-year`, `trends-all` (837–4,332 px: habit logs), `life` (~3,600 px), `decision-bill`,
`decision-section`, `triage` (~10,000 px), `undo-toast` (26,000–68,000 px),
`decision-history`, `files-archive`, `tasks-list` (page height 1550 → 1537), `tasks-gantt`,
`tasks-board`, `board-drag`, `collapsed`, `talk`, `reply`, `find`, `arrange`, `settings*`,
`emergency-confirm`, `life-config`, `sync-queued`, `sync-conflict`, `toast-over-sheet`.

**Families where day 2 equals day 1.**

| family | day 1 vs day 2 | is that right? |
|---|---|---|
| `locked` | **0 px at all eight width/scheme pairs** | Yes. The gate carries no dated content. (It carries S6-01 on both days instead.) |
| `gantt-unscheduled` | 0 px at 1024/1366/1920, 8 px at 393 dark | Yes — the Unscheduled lane holds the same seven undated tasks on both days. |
| `tasks-done` | **69–98 px, and the whole of it is the rail's health line and the mic orb.** The Done LIST is identical: at 1366 the only differing bands are x 120–140 / y 840–890 (rail) and x 1300–1330 (orb) | **No.** D2-02/D2-03 name the Done tab as a day-2 change. Both days show the same two rows, "Notion export reconciled" and "Book dentist", in the same order with the same meta. Nothing the EA or Josh finished on day 2 reaches the Done tab. Filed as **S6-38**. |
| `arrange-life` at 1024 and 1920, `find` at 393 and 1024, `sync`, `settings-*` at 1366, `reply` at 393/1024 | 0 px | Yes — none of them claims a day-2 change. |

**Verdict on LV-09 (2): one family fails.** `tasks-done` is the same on both days except for
chrome.

height as its neighbours) but the **Alert tone** half of N1-07 is neither fixed nor carried
nor declined. It is still on the tree and it is not on any list. That is a hole in the

all four widths and both schemes carry **no toast**. `undo-toast` and `toast-over-sheet` carry

#### Defects

Every row names the frame and the pixel. Severity is mine. "New to V2.2" means the surface or
the behaviour is V2.2's; "carried" means it existed in V2 or V2.1 and is on a disclosure list;
"carried, undisclosed" means it existed before and is on no list.

##### S6-01 · HIGH · NEW to V2.2's evidence, the behaviour is older · The locked screen has nothing above the fold at 393 and at 1024 — sixteen frames

**Frames.** `locked-d1-393-{light,dark}-{prod,test}`, `locked-d2-393-{light,dark}-test`,
`locked-d1-1024-{light,dark}-{prod,test}`, `locked-d2-1024-{light,dark}-test`. Sixteen frames,
both days, both flavours, both schemes.

**Measured.** The lock block is one wordmark, one line and one button. Its ink occupies:

| frame | page height | wordmark top | button bottom | viewport | first ink below the fold by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `locked-d1-393-light-prod` | 2561 | **y 1226** | y 1346 | 852 | **374 px** |
| `locked-d1-1024-light-prod` | 1744 | **y 817** | y 937 | 768 | **49 px** |
| `locked-d1-1366-light-prod` | 1141 | y 516 | y 636 | 900 | — (visible) |
| `locked-d1-1920-light-prod` | 1126 | y 508 | y 628 | 1080 | — (visible) |

A whole-frame ink sweep (any pixel more than 10 levels off the corner colour) finds **no ink
at all** between y 0 and y 1225 at 393 and between y 0 and y 816 at 1024. The demo watermark
is at y 2464–2474 at 393 — also below the fold. At scroll 0 on an iPhone or an iPad, this
screen is an empty stone rectangle with no wordmark, no message and no way in.

The cause is visible in the page heights: 2561 at 393 and 1744 at 1024 are **the Today page's
heights at those widths** (`today-d1-393-*` is 2561, `today-d1-1024-*` is 1744). The gate is
centred in a document that is still the length of the page behind it, rather than in the
viewport. At 1366 and 1920 the Today page is shorter than twice the viewport, so the centre
happens to land on screen and the defect hides.

**The line it breaks.** README Accessibility, and before that README Principles 1, *"One thing
at a time. The first decision is open"* — but the flat rule is the pack's Layout: *"Page
padding: … `calc(env(safe-area-inset-top,0px) + 22px)` top, 20 sides, 120 bottom (phone,
clears the bar)."* A screen whose only content starts 1,226 px down is not obeying any page
padding. And this review's rule 7: *"393 reads as a phone, not a squeezed desktop"* — it reads
as nothing at all.

**Fix in source.** Give the gate its own height rather than inheriting the page's: the locked
surface should be `minHeight: 100dvh` / `100%` of the viewport with `justifyContent: "center"`
and the page behind it unmounted (or `display:none`) while the gate is up, so the document
height is the viewport height. The `screen`-kind surface in `layout/dialogs.tsx` that Talk
already uses is the shape that works — `talk-d1-393-light-test` is 852 tall and its header is
at y 30.

##### S6-02 · HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · At 393 the demo watermark covers the entire message of the mic-on banner

**Frames.** `mic-listening-d1-393-{light,dark}-test`, `mic-listening-d2-393-{light,dark}-test`.
All four 393 frames of the state.

**Measured** on `mic-listening-d1-393-light-test` (page 1940):

- the banner: x **9.2–383.3**, y **1830.0–1865.4** (a bar inset from the screen edges, sitting
  8 px above the tab bar)
- the watermark chip: x **9.2–192.5**, y **1837.5–1856.3** — an opaque `(237,235,229)` pill
- `Stop`: x 352–374

The banner's message — `Mic on · listening for Brain`, per `BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` row 1 — starts
at the banner's left padding, which is inside x 9–192. **Not one character of it is visible.**
The dark frames are the same: the chip is `(38,36,33)` over the bar and only `Stop` survives.
So on the phone the live-microphone warning is a bar with a lone word `Stop` on the right of
it and nothing that says what will stop.

**The line it breaks.** The V2.1 A-1 watermark rule, verbatim: the watermark *"must be
legible and must not sit over a control or another line."* This is B-32's exact class,
recurring on a surface B-32 never saw. And it defeats the thing the banner exists for —
`JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 11, verbatim: *"the mic stays on (good), but there is no visual warning
that I haven't turned it off..? Needs to be noticeable. Mic staying on and I don't know how to
turn it off – this must never happen."*

**Fix in source.** The watermark already knows how to step out of the way — `TOAST_BOTTOM.phone
+ WATERMARK_CLEARANCE` in DISCREPANCIES 22 is the same problem solved for the toast. Do the
inverse here: while `MicBanner` renders at 393, lift the watermark above it by the banner's
height + 8 (the same constant the toast uses), or hide the mark while a banner is up — which is
what `BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md` already says for a different case (*"the demo watermark and any banner
hide while a field is expanded"*).

##### S6-03 · HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · The board card's `···` button is drawn on top of the card's meta line, at 1024, 1366 and 1920, in both schemes

**Frames.** `tasks-board-d1-{1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` and the same twelve on
`-d2-`, plus every `board-drag` frame at those widths. Twenty-four `tasks-board` frames and
eighteen `board-drag` frames — every desktop board frame in the pass. Reproduced at 393 only
where the card is wide enough, which it is not.

**Measured** on `tasks-board-d1-1366-light-prod`, the `Waiting-on digest` card:

- the `···` icon button's box: x **587.8–623.8**, y **321.0–350.6** (36 × 30)
- the meta line's first row, `EA · low priority · recurring ·`: glyphs x **566–614.4**,
  y **334.8–343.1**
- the button's three dots: x **600–611**, y **331.9–335.0**

So 26.6 px of the meta line — the letters `ring` and the trailing `·` — sit **inside** the
button's rectangle, the button's left border runs vertically through the word `recurring`
between `recur` and `ring`, and the three dots land on the tops of `ri`. The second meta row,
`every Mon 8am · $0.05`, runs under the button's lower half.

At 1920 it is worse because the lane is 209 px: the dots at x 607.1–617.1, y 330.7–335.0 sit
squarely on `recurrin|g`, and **both** meta rows pass under the button. At 1024, x 595–625 over
`recurring ·` at x 570–614. Identical in dark at every width
(`tasks-board-d1-1366-dark-prod`, same coordinates).

**The line it breaks.** README Surfaces and Components give the icon button its own box —
*"Icon button `.js-iconbtn`: 32 or 36 square, radius 8 or 10, Card fill with Card border
(header) or Hairline border (in cards)"* — and this review's rule 5, *"No clipped or
ellipsised label inside a button, chip or segment,"* whose point is that a control and a line
do not share pixels. The automated overlap sweep (B-85's `theme.spec.ts` RL-11) tests tab
pages; a board card's meta is not in it.

**Fix in source.** `components/tasks/BoardCard.tsx`: the `···` sits in the card's top-right as
an absolutely positioned or floated child, so the meta line lays out under it. Put the title
and the `···` in a flex row (`justifyContent: "space-between"`) and let the meta line be a
sibling *below* that row, as `TaskRow` already does — or reserve the button's width on the meta
row with a `paddingRight` of 36 + gap. The list row is the model: on
`tasks-list-d1-1366-light-prod` no meta touches its chevron.

##### S6-04 · HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · The Gantt's leftmost axis label reads "7 Sep" and stands on the column the grid says is 10 September

**Frames.** `tasks-gantt-d1-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` and the `-d2-`
twelve — all 24. Measured at 393, 1366 and 1920.

**Measured** on `tasks-gantt-d1-1366-light-prod`:

| thing | x |
|---|---|
| tick under `7 Sep` | **430.5** |
| tick under `14 Sep` | 542.5 |
| tick under `21 Sep` | 738.0 |
| tick under `28 Sep` | 934.0 |
| day ticks | every **28.0 px** |
| weekend band before 14 Sep | 486.5 → 542.5 (**56 px = exactly 2 days**) |
| weekend band before 28 Sep | 878 → 934 (56 px) |
| the now-rule | 449.5 |

The grid is internally exact: 28 px/day, weekends two days wide landing on 12–13 and 26–27
September, and 14 → 21 → 28 Sep spaced 196 px = 7 days. Only the **first** label is out. Its
gap to `14 Sep` is **112 px = 4 days**, not 196. At 28 px/day, x 430.5 is **10 September**, and
the now-rule at 449.5 confirms it (0.7 of a day past 10 Sep, and today is Thursday 10
September). The label `7 Sep` is drawn **84 px = three days** to the right of the date it
names, on top of today's column, and 19 px to the *left* of the now-rule — so the axis says
today is the 8th.

Identical at 1920 (`tasks-gantt-d1-1920-light-prod`: `7 Sep` tick x 445.1, `14 Sep` 557.8,
gap 112.7, day ticks 28 px, now-rule 464.4) and at 393 (`7 Sep` 135.5, `14 Sep` 250.3, gap
114.8 against a 29.5 px day). The chart is **not** scrolled — its own scrollbar thumb on
`tasks-gantt-d1-1366-light-prod` runs x 430–550 with the track starting at the plot's left
edge x 430.

**Two things ride on it.** The now-rule at x 449.5 is drawn **through the glyphs of the
`7 Sep` label** (label ink y 266.7–275.6 at 1920, rule from y 264 down), so a 1 px Accent-ink
line crosses the only date on that end of the axis. And the two bars that begin at the plot's
left edge — `Bali deposit to Steve` x 430–542 and `Recruitment risk memo, Bundaberg` x 430–542
— are clipped there with nothing saying so.

**The lines it breaks.** README Principles 7, verbatim: *"Show the work. Every card states the
source, the expiry and what happens on silence."* An axis whose first label is three days out
is not showing the work, it is misreporting it. `DISCREPANCIES.md` 7 built this axis on that
principle — *"the full view gains a minimal axis — window start, 'today', window end, and a
1px accent-ink now-rule"* — and the window-start label is the half that is wrong. And
`JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 7, verbatim: *"The time horizon is no good. I see 31st Aug, today and
28th sept with no increments in between, or gauge of days or weeks. Do better here."* The
increments are now right; the first label is not.

**Fix in source.** `components/tasks/Gantt.tsx`: the week labels are the Mondays of the window,
and the first one is being clamped to the plot's left edge (x = 0 of the scroller) while
keeping its own date. Either draw it at its true offset and let it clip — the reader loses a
label they cannot use anyway — or, better, label the window start with the window start's own
date (`10 Sep`) and keep the Mondays after it. Whichever, do not print a date at a pixel that
is not that date. Second edit: give the now-rule a 2 px vertical gap under the axis-label row,
or draw the label with a background chip, so the rule does not cross the glyphs.

##### S6-05 · HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · Settings › Sync opens a second sheet over the Settings sheet — two scrims, and the app behind goes 45 levels darker than its own ground

**Frames.** `sync-d1-*` (24), `sync-queued-*` (16), `sync-conflict-*` (16). Fifty-six frames.
Measured at 1366 and 393, both schemes.

**Measured**, light, 1366, at four points, against `settings-d1-1366-light-prod` (one modal)
as the control:

| point | one modal (`settings`) | two modals (`sync-conflict`) | step |
|---|---|---|---|
| the page behind, x 150 y 500 | `(173,172,167)` | **`(128,128,123)`** | 45 levels darker |
| the page behind, x 1250 y 300 | `(173,173,169)` | `(131,131,128)` | 42 |
| the Settings sheet's own card, x 300 y 150 | `(251,251,251)` | **`(181,181,180)`** | **70 levels darker** |
| the Settings sheet's card, x 700 y 200 | `(251,251,251)` | `(182,182,181)` | 69 |

The Settings sheet, whose card fill is the app's lightest surface, is rendered at
`(181,181,180)` — **darker than the app's own light ground** `#EDEBE5` = `(237,235,229)` — and
only 8 levels lighter than the once-scrimmed page. And the two surfaces are geometrically
identical: on `sync-queued-d1-1366-light-test` the Settings sheet spans **x 233–1133** and the
Sync dialog spans **x 233–1133**, so the second sheet reads as a horizontal band cut out of the
first rather than a surface on top of it.

**The line it breaks.** README Components, Settings sheet, verbatim: *"scrim + **one** frosted
sheet."* And README Surfaces: *"The card-to-ground step is deliberately small: one visible
layer, no float."* This is scrim + sheet + scrim + sheet — four layers, and the middle one is
darker than the ground.

**Fix in source.** Settings › Sync is a sub-screen of Settings, not a dialog over it. Make it
replace the sheet's body (a push/back within the sheet, with `Sync` as the sheet's own heading
and a back control) — which is the shape `DISCREPANCIES.md` 28 already proposes for
Notifications under 768, so it is not a new layout language. If it must stay a dialog, at
minimum it must not paint its own scrim over an existing one, and it must not be the same
width as the sheet beneath it.

##### S6-06 · HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · The sync status is missing from the desktop rail at every width, and at 393 it is an unlabelled dot with no separator

**Frames.** Every desktop frame in the pass — all 1024, 1366 and 1920 frames of every tab
family, in every state including offline. Measured on `today-d1-1920-light-prod`,
`life-d1-1024-light-prod`, `brain-d1-1366-light-prod`, `offline-d1-1366-light-test`.

**Measured, desktop.** The rail's foot on every one of those frames carries exactly two lines:
the demo watermark, then the health line. On `today-d1-1920-light-prod` the health line is
`● needs attention · $0.40` with a `(176,85,63)` Alert dot at x 10–17, y 1075–1082, and there
is **nothing below or above it**. On `offline-d1-1366-light-test` — the state in which the
sync status is amber by definition — the rail reads `● offline · captures queue` with a
`(122,119,111)` Muted dot, and again nothing else. There is no dot, no label, no `sync status`
anywhere in the rail at any width, in any state, on any tab.

**Measured, phone.** On `brain-d1-393-light-prod` the health line reads
`● needs attention · $0.40 ●`: the health dot at x 21–27 in Alert `(176,85,63)`, and a second
dot at x 154–160 in `(79,138,107)` = the `ok` token. On `offline-d1-393-light-test` the same
trailing dot is `(150,112,46)`-family amber = the `warn` token added by `DISCREPANCIES.md` 30.
The colours are right and the states are right. What is missing is everything else: **no
label, no title, and no separator** — it is appended after `$0.40` with a plain space, where
the line it sits on uses a middle dot between every other pair of values.

**The lines it breaks.** `BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md`, "App-wide refinements this proposal carries
(Josh, 7 Sep)", verbatim: *"**Sync status** lives at the bottom of the desktop rail, above the
health line, as a small dot with the label 'sync status' (green synced, amber waiting or
offline, red needs attention; tap opens Settings › Sync); on phone it sits in the header's
health line."* That is on the file's own "Decisions Josh has taken on this proposal" list —
*"Sync dot: rail bottom with the label (7 Sep)"* — so it is a decision, not a suggestion. And
README Content: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`."* A bare
glyph tacked on after a space is not on that line's grammar.

**Fix in source.** Add the row the proposal describes to the rail, under `components/chrome/
Rail.tsx`, above the health line: a 6 px dot in `ok` / `warn` / `alert` plus the words
`sync status` at 11 Muted, the whole row an `onPress` into Settings › Sync. On phone, put the
dot **before** its own middle dot separator and give it an accessible label, so the line reads
`needs attention · $0.40 · ● synced` rather than `$0.40 ●`.

##### S6-07 · MEDIUM-HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · Four raw internal identifiers are printed to the owner, on the three surfaces where she is asked to check what the EA did

**Frames and pixels.**

| what is printed | frame | where |
|---|---|---|
| **`/brain/dump`** as the *name* of the item waiting to sync, in card-title size | `sync-queued-d1-1366-light-test`, and all 32 `sync-queued` / `sync-conflict` frames | x **263–337**, y **476–487** |
| **`personal:josh`** twice — in the card title *and* as the first tag | `triage-d1-1366-light-test`, all 24 `triage` frames | title x 245–614 y 213–255; tag x 245–320 y 355–372 |
| **`/learning`**, and **`column 3`**, in the line that tells you what Approve will do | `decision-section-d1-1366-light-test`, all 16 frames | `goes on Life, column 3 · reads /learning`, x 245–430, y 372–382 |

**Why these are defects and not fixture noise.** The app already holds display names for two
of them and uses them elsewhere. `jstack-app/data/labels.ts` gives every silo a `shortName`,
and `brain-d1-1366-light-prod` renders the same silos as the tags `family`, `personal`,
`kids`, `legal`, `money`, `journal` on the Latest-in rows — display names throughout. So the
triage card, whose entire job is to let Josh verify the silo and labels the EA chose, is the
one surface that shows him the key instead of the word. This is **ST1-10 exactly** (`family1`,
still open from the ST-1 round), now in a second and third place.

`/brain/dump` is a route. The V2.1 brief's own framing of the queued line is *"the app telling
someone their words are safe"*; `/brain/dump — queued` tells them a URL is safe.

**The line it breaks.** README Content, verbatim: *"Sentence case everywhere except section
labels (tracked caps) and proper nouns."* `personal:josh`, `/brain/dump` and `/learning` are
none of those and are not words. And `02_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS_v22.md` SE-02's own standard, quoted
in the ST-1 round: *"The abbreviations saved four characters and cost the reader the answer to
'which of my things is this?'"*

**Fix in source.** One lookup, three call sites. Compose the triage card's title and tags
through the same silo-display path `LatestIn` uses. Give the sync queue entry the capture's own
first line (or `Mind dump · 8:44am`) as its title and keep the route in the row's `testID`, not
its text. In the section card, replace `reads /learning` with the section's display name
(`reads Learning`) and `column 3` with something a reader can see — `on the right` or,
better, nothing: the card already shows the preview.

##### S6-08 · MEDIUM-HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · You can tell a configured section from a component by looking, because only the configured ones carry `configure`

**Frames.** `life-d1-*` (24), `collapsed-d1-*` (24), `life-config-*` (16), `brain-d1-*` (24),
`offline-*` (16), `mic-listening-*` (16). Measured at 1366 light, reproduced at 393, 1024 and
1920 and in dark.

**Measured** on `life-d1-1366-light-prod`, the right slot of each section label:

| section | what it is | right slot |
|---|---|---|
| GOALS | component | `edit`  `all` |
| HABITS | component | `edit`  `trends` |
| PEOPLE | config record | **`configure`** |
| MONEY | config record | **`configure`** |
| HEALTH | config record | **`configure`** |
| LEARNING | config record | **`configure`** |

Four for four, both ways, with no exception. `collapsed-d1-1366-light-prod` shows it survives
collapsing: `PEOPLE ▸ … configure` and `HABITS ▸ … edit trends`. The same tell is on Brain:
`brain-d1-1366-light-prod` has `REPLIES 2 … configure` and `FILES 10 … all  configure`, while
`MEMORY 4 … all` and `LATEST IN` and `FIND` have none.

**The line it breaks.** The V2.1 A-1 brief, verbatim, and it is the whole reason the check
exists: *"A dynamic Life section beside a static one — People, Money, Learning and Health are
config records; Goals and Habits are components. **If you can tell which is which from a frame,
that is a defect.**"* The `configure` link is a perfect discriminator.

**I am not saying `configure` should go.** It is a real control and rule 20's logic (a
tappable phrase gets Accent ink) applies. What is wrong is that it is only on half the
sections, so it stops being "configure this section" and becomes "this section is one of the
configured ones". **Fix in source:** give every section the same right-slot vocabulary. Goals
and Habits are configurable too — their `edit` is the same job under another name — so either
rename all six to `configure`, or move the affordance off the label entirely and into Arrange
(which already lists every section, `arrange-life-d1-1366-light-prod`), which is where a
reader would look for "how is this tab put together".

##### S6-09 · MEDIUM-HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · Talk with EA shows "listening" and "Mic unavailable here" at the same time, and the idle mic orb floats over the panel

**Frames.** `talk-d1-{393,1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-test` and the `-d2-` eight — all 16.

**Measured** on `talk-d1-1366-light-test`:

- the orb: x 636–729, y 145–238 — **93 px**, filled `(79,127,168)` = Marker `#4F7FA8`, white
  glyph. That is the pack's *Listening* orb exactly.
- directly under it, the state line `listening` at y 254–265, Muted.
- directly under **that**, at y 275–285, x 542–823:
  `Mic unavailable here · type instead · you can still type below`, in Alert
  `(176,85,63)`.

So the surface says, in three consecutive lines, that the microphone is live and that the
microphone is not available. `JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 11, verbatim, is the report this surface was
built to answer: *"Problem 1: I couldn't visually differentiate when I'd clicked it or if it's
working or not?"* A reader here is worse off than before, because now there are two claims and
they disagree.

**Second half, same frames.** The idle mic orb is still rendered at
x **1296.7–1343.3**, y **830.8–876.7** on `talk-d1-1366-light-test` — over the panel's scrim,
below the panel's own foot at y 820, in the same corner it always occupies. It is a live
control that starts a second capture session on top of a running conversation.

**The lines it breaks.** The A-1 rule, verbatim: *"no floating element over content or a
control with a toast up **or a sheet open**"* — the Talk panel is a sheet and the orb is a
floating control on top of it. And README Colour: *"Alert: needs-eyes items, over-budget bars,
the emergency lock. Never for expiry."* A capability notice is not on that list — and putting
it in Alert under a Marker orb is what makes the contradiction shout.

**I am partly unsure and say so.** The capture rig is headless, so `Mic unavailable here` may
be an artefact of the machine rather than a state Josh will meet. That does not clear the
frame: whatever the reason for the state, the orb should not be in its *Listening* dress while
the app is saying the mic is unavailable, and A-2 chose this frame as the evidence for Talk.

**Fix in source.** One state, one dress. When `micState === "unavailable"`, the orb takes the
resting Card surface with an Accent-ink glyph (README Mic, *Idle*), the state line reads
`type instead` and the Alert sentence becomes one Muted line under the field, not two
sentences saying the same thing. And hide `Orb` whenever a `screen`- or `modal`-kind surface is
open — the same predicate `TalkBanner` already uses.

##### S6-10 · MEDIUM-HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · A finished task shows neither when it was finished nor what it cost to finish

**Frames.** `tasks-done-d1-*` and `-d2-*` (24), `task-detail-*` (24), and the DONE lane on
every `tasks-board` / `board-drag` frame.

**Measured** on `tasks-done-d1-1920-light-prod`, the Done tab's only two rows:

```
☑ [EA]  Notion export reconciled
        EA · medium priority · 1,387 rows · report attached · $0.03
☑       Book dentist
        you · low priority
```

No date, no time, no model, no token count, on either row, on either day, at any width. On
`task-detail-d1-1366-light-test` the ACTIVITY card carries one line —
`2 of 3 subtasks done` / `EA · Yesterday 9:00am` — with no model and no in/out counts, and the
two completed subtasks carry nothing at all.

**The lines it breaks.** `JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 2, verbatim, twice: *"When tasks are done
either by EA or human checking the box, add in date & time completed"* and *"Ensure each
completed task and subtask shows the models used and number of tokens used to complete it. Part
of the activity section. I want to be able to use this info to analyse how to improve the
system."* And the build's own claims: `02_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS_v22.md` **TK-12**, *"Done rows carry
'Completed · formatWhen(completedAt)'"*, and **US-01**, *"Each agent run shows 'EA · <model> ·
<in> in · <out> out · $<cost> · <when>'"*. Neither string is on any frame in the pass.

**I am unsure of one half and say so.** US-01 says *each agent run*, and the fixture may
simply hold no run record for these two tasks — in which case the missing model and tokens are
the fixture's gap, not the component's. TK-12's `Completed · …` is not conditional and is
missing outright.

**Fix in source.** `components/tasks/TaskRow.tsx` / `lib/taskMeta.ts`: when `completedAt` is
set, append `Completed · formatWhen(completedAt)` to the row's meta (and `· EA` / `· Josh` from
`completedBy`), for the Done tab, the Done lane and the card header. Separately, check that the
fixture carries a usage record for `t9`; if it does not, the Activity section is asserting a
capability no frame can show.

##### S6-11 · MEDIUM-HIGH · NEW to V2.2 · The habit trends dialog: the default tab is two-thirds empty and unlabelled, the Year card's two charts never show the same months, and the control you press moves 180 px

**Frames.** `trends-week-*`, `trends-*` (Month), `trends-year-*`, `trends-all-*` — 96 frames.
Measured at 1366 light; reproduced at 1024, 1920 and 393 and in dark.

**(a) The Week segment — the dialog's default — leaves 68 % of it empty and drops the day
labels.** On `trends-week-d1-1366-light-prod` the dialog spans x **233–1133** (900 px) and the
content stops at x **522**: nine habit rows, each a name at x 248–290 and seven 24 px cells
running x 316–522. **611 px — 68 % of the dialog's width — is empty frosted ground with the
Life page ghosting through it.** And every cell is bare: no weekday letter, no date, only an
underline on the seventh. The Month segment beside it puts the day number in every cell.

`JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 12, verbatim: *"Current 'week' view is not great, doesn't show hits and
misses clearly."* Seven unlabelled squares in a 900 px slab is the same view, moved into a
dialog.

**(b) The Year card's two charts default to opposite ends of the year and never overlap.** On
`trends-year-d1-1366-light-prod`, the `Exercise` card:

| chart | its own scrollbar thumb | track | window shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| the day grid | x **421–507** (35 % of the track, at the **right** end) | x 263–509 | **Sep · Oct · Nov · Dec** |
| the month bars | x **263–421** (64 % of the track, at the **left** end) | x 263–509 | **J F M A M J J A** (Jan–Aug) |

The card says `130 of 253`. The grid shows about 15 filled dots, because it is showing the
three-and-a-half months that have not happened yet; the 122 marked days of January to August
are off-screen to the left. The bar chart shows those eight months and hides September. **The
two halves of one card never show the same period, and neither shows the month you are in.**
The grid's leftmost column is also clipped in half — the first column of dots is a row of
half-circles at x 263.

**(c) The segmented control moves under your finger.** Measured, the y of the Week/Month/Year/
All time control at 1366:

| segment selected | control y | dialog y |
|---|---|---|
| Week | **259–293** | 172–728 |
| Month | 135–164 | 45–845 |
| Year | 135–164 | 43–810 |
| All time | **314–346** | 227–673 |

Tapping `Month` from `Week` moves the control **126 px up**; tapping `All time` from `Year`
moves it **181 px down**. Four taps in a row and the control is never twice in the same place.

**The lines these break.** This review's rule 7 — *"1366 and 1920 read as a dashboard, not
three phone columns"* — for (a); README Principles 7, *"Show the work"*, for (b), because a
card that prints `130 of 253` over a picture of 15 is not showing the work; and README Motion,
*"Nothing animates on load. Nothing bounces"*, whose spirit (c) breaks by a fifth of a screen.

**Fix in source.** (a) Give the Week segment the Month segment's card grid: one card per habit
in the same 3 × 3, seven day-labelled cells each, and it fills the dialog. (b) Open the year
grid at the current month, not the end of the window, and drive both charts from one scroll
position — or drop the grid's scroller and fit 52 weeks at 5 px a column, which is what Josh's
reference image does. (c) Give the dialog a fixed height (the tallest of the four, or a
`maxHeight` with the body scrolling inside it) so the header and the segments never move.

##### S6-12 · MEDIUM · NEW to V2.2 · The Latest-in meta line prints a leading middle dot when there is no routing, and a dangling accent-ink dot with a doubled space when there is

**Frames.** `brain-d1-*`, `offline-*`, `mic-listening-*`, `triage-*` — every frame that shows a
Latest-in row. Measured on `mic-listening-d1-1366-light-test` and `brain-d1-393-light-prod`.

**(a) A leading middle dot.** On `mic-listening-d1-1366-light-test`, the row
`What's most urgent?` — a capture the EA has not routed yet — has a meta line whose **first
glyph is a middle dot**: the `·` at x **690.0–692.5**, y 258.7–261.2, then a gap, then `voice`
starting at x **702**. The line reads `·  voice · Today 4:36pm   edit`.

**(b) A dangling separator at the run join.** On the row above it,
`Ring the school about the Term 4 dates`, the routing run ends `→ filing · Librarian ·` in
Accent ink and the source run begins `typed · Today 4:36pm` in Muted. Measured:

| separator | gap to the next word |
|---|---|
| between `filing` and `Librarian` (inside one run) | **3.0 px** |
| after `Librarian ·` (between the two runs) | **8.3 px** |

So the join carries a middle dot painted in the *left* run's colour, followed by 2.8× the
normal separator gap — the dot reads as a full stop on the routing phrase rather than a
separator between two. Every Latest-in row does it, at every width: on
`brain-d1-393-light-prod` the same shape is `task → Twenty · reminder Tue ·   voice · Telegram`
and `journal → journal ·   Close the day`.

**The line it breaks.** README Content, verbatim: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces:
`JSTACK · today · high`."* One dot, one space each side, and never in front of the first word.
The A-1 sweep asks for it in as many words: *"no leading middle dot"*.

**Fix in source.** `layout/sourcesBrain.ts` / `components/brain/LatestIn.tsx` compose the meta
from two run arrays and join them with `" · "` while the first array already ends with its own
separator and the second begins with a leading space. Build one array of non-empty parts and
join once — `parts.filter(Boolean).join(" · ")` — so an empty routing run produces no dot at
all and a present one produces exactly one.

##### S6-15 · MEDIUM · CARRIED from V2.1's N1-07, and **undisclosed** · The `sensitive` tag is painted in Alert, which the pack reserves for three things and this is none of them

**Frames.** `brain-d1-*`, `offline-*`, `mic-listening-*`, `find-*`, `triage-*` — every frame
that shows a tag row. Measured at 393 and 1366, light and dark.

expires before Bali`:

| tag | ink | token |
|---|---|---|
| `family` | `(127,141,153)` / `(118,133,146)` | Accent-ish |
| `kids`, `legal` | `(155,154,147)` | Muted |
| **`sensitive`** | **`(176,85,63)`** border and text | **Alert `#B0553F`** |

On `find-d1-393-light-prod` three of the six results carry it, so an Alert-red pill is the only

**The line it breaks.** README Colour, "Where colour goes", verbatim: *"Alert: needs-eyes items,
over-budget bars, the emergency lock. Never for expiry."* A sensitivity label is a *property* of
a record, not something that needs eyes. And README Colour again: *"Everything else is Ink,
Muted, Card, Hairline."*

**Why this is a disclosure finding as much as a design one.** V2.1's ux round raised N1-07 as

ink on Accent soft, which is what `family` and `personal` already use and which still reads as

##### S6-18 · MEDIUM · NEW to V2.2 · While the mic is live, the app says so in three different ways at three widths, and the one that means "listening" is dressed as a selected filter

**Frames.** `mic-listening-*` — all 16.

**Measured.**

| what | 1366 / 1920 (`mic-listening-d1-1366-light-test`) | 393 (`mic-listening-d1-393-light-test`) |
|---|---|---|
| the banner | a bar x **209–1358**, y **853–887** (1149 × 34, ~8 px insets, square corners), reading `Mic on · listening for Brain` … `Stop` | a bar x 9–383, y 1830–1865, message covered — see **S6-02** |
| the rail / header health line | `● mic on` — the health state and the spend **disappear** | `● needs attention · $0.40 ●` — **unchanged**; it does not say `mic on` at all |
| the in-field mic control | a pill, fill `(231,233,234)` = Accent soft, glyph `(126,159,189)` = Marker, label `Listening` | identical |

Three problems in one state.

**(a) The desktop bar is not the pack's.** README Components, Mic, verbatim: *"On desktop a
360px bar appears bottom right,"* and `handoff.md`: *"Desktop: a 360 × 60 bar bottom right with
the same content."* The shipped bar is 1149 × 34 edge to edge. I accept the intent — Josh asked
for noticeable — but a 34 px bar is under the pack's own Bar height of 60 and it is inset 8
where the pack says 14, so it is neither the pack's bar nor a deliberate new one.

**(b) The health line loses its content at desktop and gains nothing at phone.** On desktop
`needs attention · $0.40` is replaced outright, so while the mic is on you cannot see that an
agent needs attention. On phone the proposal's own line — *"the health line says 'mic on'"* —
is not implemented at all. The same state reads three different ways at three widths.

**(c) The "Listening" chip wears the selected-chip dress.** Its fill `(231,233,234)` is Accent
soft, which on the same screen, 60 px above it, is the fill of the selected focus chip
`Everything`. README Colour: *"Marker `#4F7FA8` (count badges, **mic while listening**; the
only saturated colour),"* and Components, Mic: *"Listening: 42px circle, **Marker fill**, white
filled glyph, pulse ring 1.4s."* Nothing on this screen is Marker-filled; only the 17 px glyph
inside the chip is Marker. `JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 11: *"I couldn't visually differentiate when
I'd clicked it or if it's working or not?"*

**Fix in source.** Make the in-field control take the pack's Listening dress — Marker fill,
white glyph, the pulse ring — so the live mic is the only saturated thing on the page. Append
`· mic on` to the health line rather than replacing it, at every width. And either bring the
desktop bar to 360 × 60 bottom-right, or record the full-width bar in DISCREPANCIES with
Josh's line as the reason and give it the Bar's own height, radius and 14 px inset.

**Why it matters.** `02_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS_v22.md` TF-08's claim, quoted in the changes table, is
*"a focus and a slicer show the same task set on every view"*, and F-1 was written because
*"a filter you cannot see is a filter you forget is on"*. A range that silently changes when
you tap a segment is the same failure in the other direction: you set `This week` on List, you
tap `Done`, and you are looking at all time without being told.

I can see why: a future-facing range would empty a list of finished work. That is a sound
product reason and it should be *said*, not hidden in the chip.

**Fix in source.** Either make the range one value across the four views and have Done invert
it (`This week` → tasks *completed* this week), which is what a reader will assume it already
does; or keep the override and say it — `All time · edit` with the hint `Done ignores the range`
in the slicer row's right slot, where `Slicers` already lives.

##### S6-24 · MEDIUM · NEW to V2.2 · The compact Gantt card's bars are 3 px on a 308 px track, so four tasks are four identical dots

**Frames.** `tasks-board-*`, `board-drag-*`, `tasks-list-*`, `tasks-done-*` — every Tasks frame
that shows column 3. Measured at 1024, 1366 and 1920.

**Measured** on `tasks-board-d1-1920-light-prod`, the `GANTT` card:

| row | track | bar |
|---|---|---|
| Send Moz the sample pack | x 1410–1718 (**308 px**) | x **1410–1413 (3 px)** |
| Redact the 200 sample emails | 1410–1718 | a 3 px dashed ring at x 1410 |
| Book the Term 4 holiday flights | 1410–1718 | x **1420–1423 (3 px)** |
| Passport renewal forms | 1410–1718 | x **1430–1433 (3 px)** |

At 1024 the track is ~310 px and the bars are the same 3–8 px. The arithmetic is honest — the
active range is 90 days, so a one-day task is 308 / 90 = 3.4 px — but the result carries no
information: there is no axis, no start, no end, and four one-day tasks in different weeks are
four indistinguishable specks. The wider the screen, the smaller the bar is relative to its
track, which is the inverse of what more width should buy.

**The line it breaks.** README Principles 7, *"Show the work"*, and this review's rule 7,
*"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three phone columns."* `DISCREPANCIES.md` 7 protects the
compact card's *shape* (*"The `compact` sidebar card keeps the mock's shape exactly"*) — it does
not protect a shape that has become unreadable now that the window is 90 days rather than the
mock's four weeks.

**Fix in source.** Give the compact card the full view's own window rule but a floor: clamp the
track to the *union of the bars' dates* plus a margin (so four September tasks fill a September
track), and give every bar a minimum width of 6 px so a one-day task is visible. Add the two
end dates as 9 px Muted labels under the card, which is the smallest honest axis and the same
one `DISCREPANCIES.md` 7 sanctioned for the full view.

##### S6-25 · MEDIUM · NEW to V2.2 · The Section card's preview is painted in the same Accent soft as the button that approves it, so it reads as a live section rather than a picture of one

**This is the judgement the V2.1 brief asked for**, so I answer it plainly first: **it reads as
a section that has escaped into a card.**

**Frames.** `decision-section-*` — all 16.

**Measured** on `decision-section-d1-1366-light-test`:

| surface | fill |
|---|---|
| the card | `(247,247,244)` |
| **the preview block** | **`(227,229,229)`** |
| **the `Approve` primary button** | **`(227,229,229)`** |

Identical. And the preview's rows are typographically identical to the real thing: on
`life-d1-1366-light-prod` the Learning card renders
`Multi-agent orchestration patterns` / `summary ready · resurfaces in the review` at the same
sizes, with the same hairline between the two rows. The only differences between the picture
and the section are the ground and the absence of the `open` buttons — neither of which reads
as "this is a preview". Nothing labels it, nothing scales it down, nothing dims it.

**The line it breaks.** README Colour, "Where colour goes", verbatim: *"Accent soft: primary-verb
fill, selected focus chip, recommended option row, owner tags (EA, J)."* A section preview is
not on that list, and on this one card the same fill now means three things at once — "this is
the preview", "this is the recommended option" (on a Clash card) and "this is the button that
says yes".

**Fix in source.** Give the preview its own dress: the Ghost treatment the pack already has for
a section without a feed (*"Ghost: 1px dashed Hairline, radius 10, Muted text"*) says "not real
yet" in the pack's own vocabulary, costs no new token, and leaves Accent soft to mean "act".
Add a 10.5 Muted line above it — `a preview` — and the card reads as a proposal.

##### S6-29 · LOW-MEDIUM · NEW to V2.2 · The Unscheduled lane is seven full-width dashed boxes with a doubled dashed rule between them, two of which are finished tasks

**Frames.** `gantt-unscheduled-*` (24), and the same lane at the foot of every `tasks-gantt-*`
frame (24).

**Measured** on `gantt-unscheduled-d1-1366-light-prod`:

- seven rows, pitch **38 px**, each row 35 px tall with its own 1 px dashed border on all four
  sides.
- between rows, at x 400: a dashed rule at **y 51** and another at **y 54** — two dashed lines
  3 px apart, because each row draws its own top and bottom.
- each row carries a title and nothing else, in a box **1,180 px wide** at 1366 (1,700 at
  1920). `Book dentist` is 88 px of it.
- two of the seven — **`Notion export reconciled`** and **`Book dentist`** — are the two rows
  the Done tab shows struck through as completed (`tasks-done-d1-1366-light-test`). Here they
  are presented as work waiting for dates, with no strikethrough and no done mark.

**The lines it breaks.** README Surfaces, verbatim: *"Borders: hairlines only. No 2px borders
except none"* — two dashed rules 3 px apart read as one thick one. README Components: *"Rows
inside separated by 1px Hairline"* — one line, not two. And README Principles 7, *"Show the
work"*, for the two completed tasks: a lane called Unscheduled that contains finished work is
telling the reader something untrue.

**Fix in source.** Make the lane one dashed container with 1 px Hairline separators between its
rows (the `ListCard`/`Row` pair B-80 introduced for Habits is the shape). Exclude
`completedAt`-bearing tasks from the Unscheduled bucket, or render them with the Done row's
strikethrough and check so the lane is honest. And give each row the meta line every other task
surface carries, so the box has something in it.

##### S6-32 · LOW · CARRIED in shape from V2, sharper in V2.2 · One Needs-you stack carries two expiry forms

**Frames.** `today-*`, `triage-*`, `decision-bill-*`, `decision-section-*`, `undo-toast-*`.

`expires Sun 5pm` · `expires Sun 5pm` · `expires Fri 5pm` · **`expires 22 Sep`** ·
`expires Mon 7am`

Four weekday-plus-time and one bare date, in one card stack, 300 px apart.

**The line it reads against.** The A-1 sweep, verbatim: *"one expiry and time form per
surface,"* and README Content: *"Expiry is stated as a time and a consequence: `expires Wed 5pm
· then proposes 1`."* The bill's line is `expires 22 Sep · then reminds you` — a date and a
consequence, no time.

**I am unsure this is fixable as stated and say so.** A bill twelve days out cannot use a
weekday without ambiguity, so a single form across the stack means either dates everywhere
(which loses the "this week" reading the near ones give you) or a hybrid. The honest fix is a
stated rule rather than one form: within seven days use `Wed 5pm`, beyond it use `Tue 22 Sep,
5pm` — one grammar, two lengths, and the time never disappears.

**Frames.** `board-drag-*` — all 18. Measured on `board-drag-d1-1366-light-prod` against

|---|---|---|

else changes: no lane is highlighted, no gap opens where the card would land, no insertion rule
is drawn. A still cannot prove the absence of a drop indicator when the card is held over its
own lane, which is what A-122 says this frame captures, so **I mark this unsure**. What the
frame does show is that a 9-level dim is the entire visual difference between "dragging" and

##### S6-36 · LOW, and I am unsure · NEW to V2.2's frames · The bill card puts the app's meta separator inside a number you are meant to type, and its `copy` is 380 px from its value

**Frames.** `decision-bill-*` — all 24. Measured on `decision-bill-d1-1366-light-prod`.

- the BSB row: label `BSB` at x 244–256, value **`084 004 · 5510 8822`** at x 300–414,
  `copy` at x **614–636**.
- the ref row: `POL 4471 9920` at x 300–386, `copy` at x 614–636.

The middle dot between the BSB and the account number is the same glyph the app uses to
separate `JSTACK · today · high`, so a reader who is about to key this into a banking app has
to decide whether the dot is part of the string. And the `copy` link sits **228 px** to the
right of the value it copies, with nothing between them.

**The line it reads against.** README Content, verbatim: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with
spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`"* — the dot is the app's separator, and using it inside a value
overloads it. **I mark this unsure** because the pack does not say how to set a BSB and the
handoff's grid (`44px 1fr auto`) puts the link at the right by design.

**Fix in source.** Split the BSB and the account number into their own labelled rows
(`BSB` / `084 004`, `account` / `5510 8822`), each with its own `copy` — which is what the grid
already supports and what `DISCREPANCIES.md` 12 reasons about ("a bill card exists to hand the
owner the strings they paste into a banking app"). Failing that, use a hyphen (`084-004`), which
is how a BSB is written.

#### How this round was done

**Programmatic, over all 1,060 frames.**

1. **Inventory against the file-name grammar.** Every file parsed as
   `<screen>-d<day>-<width>-<scheme>-<flavour>.png`. 1,060 parsed, 4 unparsed (the
   `brain-proposal-*` set, correctly outside the pass). **Forty-seven** families. Thirty-eight
   hold the full 24 (4 widths × 2 schemes × 3 passes); `arrange` and `arrange-life` hold 18
   (no 393); `decision-section`, `life-config`, `offline`, `talk`, `mic-listening`,
   `sync-queued`, `sync-conflict` hold 16 (test only, both days). Expected total from the
   grammar: 1,060. Actual: 1,060. **Nothing missing, nothing extra, no `-prod` frame of a
   rig-only state, and all seven of the S6-40 families present with both flavours.**
2. **Blank / wrong-screen / below-the-fold sweep.** For every frame, the first row of ink more
   than 10 levels off the frame's own corner colour, against that width's viewport height.
   **No blank frame, no wrong screen, and — this is S6-01 — not one frame in the pass whose
   first ink falls below the fold.** Round 1 flagged 24; this round flags 0.
3. **Frame-size sweep.** Every frame's pixel width equals its file-name width except the 24
   `gantt-unscheduled` element frames (327 / 394 / 742 / 1023 wide, 258 tall), which is what an
   element frame should be. Page heights are identical between `-prod` and `-test` on every
   screen and day; the only height variation inside a family+width is day 1 against day 2.
4. **Dark-ground sweep.** Corner pixel of all 530 dark frames against `#191815` = (25,24,21).
   461 match exactly. The 69 that do not are the scrimmed-dialog families and the
   `gantt-unscheduled` element frames, whose corner is a scrim or a card, not the ground. **No
   dark frame paints a ground that is not the warm token; no frame in the pass has a pure black
   or pure white corner.**
5. **Light/dark parity.** Column-occupancy profiles per light/dark pair; differences 0–7 px of
   frame width on every pair, as in round 1. **No dark reflow anywhere.**
6. **LV-09 (1) — prod vs test on day 1.** Full RGB diff of all 316 `-d1-…-prod` frames against
   their `-d1-…-test` twins. Method and result below.
7. **LV-09 (2) — day 1 vs day 2.** Full RGB diff of all 372 `-d1-…-test` frames against
   `-d2-…-test`. Method and result below.

#### LV-09 (1) · prod and test on the same screen and day

**Method.** For each of the 316 `-d1-…-prod` frames I loaded the `-d1-…-test` twin, checked the
size, then took the per-pixel max-channel absolute difference, reporting counts above 8, 32 and
64 levels and the bounding box of the >64 set.

**Result.** No size mismatch anywhere. **141 of the 316 pairs are bit-identical** — including
`today-d1-1366-light`, which round 1 could not make identical because the calendar's now-rule
moved between runs. A-124's fixed instant works: the now-rule and the agent feed's relative
times are gone from the diff entirely.

Of the 175 that differ:

| what differs | pairs | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **the mic orb's own box**, ≤ 44 levels over 4–107 px | 170 | `agents-d1-1024-dark`: the whole >8 set is x 955–1000, y 1537–1571 — the orb's rectangle. `agents-d1-1920-light`: x 1868–1879, y 1025–1038. `brain-d1-393-light`: x 345–356, y 1664–1680. Nothing above 32 anywhere in this group. Not a content change. |
| **the undo ring's digit** | 2 | `toast-over-sheet-d1-1366-light-prod` reads `Undo (10)`, `-test` reads `Undo (9)`; the >64 set is x 886–896, y 844–851, maxd **201**. Same at 1920 dark, x 1164–1173, y 1025–1031, maxd 203. **A content difference — S6-46.** |
| **the Today page behind the Find dialog** | 4 | `find-d1-1920-dark`: 72,647 px >8, **8,281 >32**, 25 >64; the >32 set is x 245–707, y 888–1035. At (264,972) prod is (25,24,21) — bare ground — and test is (77,82,86) — a ghosted card. **A content difference — S6-45.** |

**Verdict on LV-09 (1): FAIL on six pairs, PASS on 310.** Round 1's clock defect is closed;
two new content differences stand (S6-45, S6-46) and are named below.

comparison.

(`today` 1141→1062 at 1366, `today-collapsed` 1141→1062, `tasks-list` 952→939,
`tasks-collapsed` 952→939, `agents` 1072→1121, `decision-bill` 2487→2500 at 393,

`bundaberg-memo.docx` and `THE EA'S REPORT`), `files-archive` 108,915, `decision-history`
70,825, `undo-toast` 47,982, `tasks-list`/`tasks-collapsed` 30,217, `settings*` 22,203.

The 28 identical pairs are all correct and I name every one:

- `locked` (8) — the gate has no day-2 content.
- `gantt-unscheduled` (8) — an element frame of a bucket none of whose five rows changes on
  day 2 (what day 2 finishes is t1's last **subtask**, per A-127).
- `talk` (4, at 393 and 1024), `find` (2, 393), `reply` (2, 393), `sync-conflict` (2, 393),
  `sync-queued` (2, 393) — full-bleed or panel surfaces that cover the page behind, so no

**Verdict on LV-09 (2): PASS.** No family that claims a day-2 change is identical, and every
identical pair has a reason on the frame.

##### S6-41 · HIGH · NEW · The delegate picker paints a second scrim, taking the task card 99 levels darker than its own fill and 111 levels below the app's ground

**Frames.** `delegate-picker-d1-{1024,1366,1920}-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` and the `-d2-` six —
**eighteen desktop frames**. The nine light ones carry the signature in their corner pixel; the
dark ones are the same surface but a dark scrim over a dark ground is within a level of itself,
so the measurement is made in light.

**Measured** on `delegate-picker-d1-1366-light-prod`, against `task-detail-d1-1366-light-test`
(the same task card with **one** modal) as the control:

| point | one modal (`task-detail`) | two modals (`delegate-picker`) | step |
|---|---|---|---|
| the frame's corner, (2,2) | `(173,172,167)` | **`(128,128,123)`** | 45 levels |
| the page behind, (150,500) | `(173,172,167)` | **`(128,128,123)`** | 45 |
| the task card's own fill, (300,150) | `(219,219,218)` | **`(126,125,121)`** | **93** |
| the task card's fill, (700,120) | `(217,217,216)` | **`(118,117,113)`** | **99** |

The app's light ground is `(237,235,229)`. The task card underneath the picker is rendered at
`(118,117,113)` — **111 levels below the ground**, a mid-grey slab on which the card's title
`Passport renewal forms` and its whole body are barely legible. `delegate-picker` is the **only**
family in the 1,060 whose corner reads `(128,128,123)`; every other dialog family reads
`(173,172,167)` (one scrim) or a sheet fill.

**The line it breaks.** README Components, Settings sheet, verbatim: *"scrim + **one** frosted
sheet."* And README Surfaces, verbatim: *"The card-to-ground step is deliberately small: one
visible layer, no float."* This is scrim + card + scrim + panel — four layers, and the middle
one is 111 levels darker than the ground it is supposed to float one step above. It is S6-05's
exact class on a surface B-152 did not reach: that fix exempts a `Dialog` rendered while
`settingsOpen`, and the delegate picker opens from inside the **task** dialog.

**Fix in source.** `layout/dialogKit.tsx` / `components/chrome/Dialog.tsx`: make
`overlayBackdrop`'s `scrim = false` branch fire whenever **any** overlay is already open, not
only the settings sheet — the predicate `useOverlayOpen` already exists (B-154 uses it to stand
the orb down). One scrim, the outermost.

##### S6-42 · HIGH · NEW · JQ-06 is not fixed: collapsing "Waiting on" removes the Gantt section outright, and the Gantt heading has no collapse triangle

**Frames.** All 24 `tasks-collapsed`, measured against all 24 `tasks-list`; the missing triangle
is on every `tasks-list`, `tasks-board`, `tasks-gantt`, `tasks-done`, `tasks-filtered` and
`board-drag` frame, and on `CALENDAR` on every `today` and `today-collapsed` frame.

**Measured.** Ink bands in column 3 (x 1010–1360) at 1366:

| frame | bands |
|---|---|
| `tasks-list-d1-1366-light-prod` | 120–135 (`WAITING ON ②`), **154–258** (the card), **275–283** (`GANTT`), **295–501** (the Gantt card), 883–928 (the orb) |
| `tasks-collapsed-d1-1366-light-prod` | 120–135 (`WAITING ON ②`, collapsed), **nothing**, 883–928 (the orb) |

Identical at 1920 (list 154–258 and 295–501 in x 1420–1900; collapsed neither) and at 393, where
the page shortens from **1586 to 1232** and the last three bands — 1223–1429 (the Gantt card),
1453–1499, 1512–1573 — vanish with it. The GANTT **label** is gone too, so this is not a
collapsed section: a collapsed section keeps its heading, as `WAITING ON ▸`, `ALL CALENDARS ▸`
and `AT A GLANCE ▸` all do on the same pass.

**And the cause is visible.** On `tasks-list-d1-1366-light-prod` the `WAITING ON` label carries
a `∨` at x **1027**; `GANTT` at x **1017** carries **none**. The same on Today:
`today-collapsed-d1-1366-light-prod` has `▸ ALL CALENDARS` with a triangle at x ~558 and
`CALENDAR` at x 546 with none. Two section headings in the app are not collapsible sections,
and one of them is the one Josh reported.

**The lines it breaks.** `JOSH_QA_v22.md`, build-time line JQ-06, verbatim: *"When I collapse
the 'Waiting on' subheading, it hides Gantt."* And `BRAIN_PROPOSAL.md`, "App-wide refinements
this proposal carries (Josh, 7 Sep)", verbatim: *"**Collapsible headings everywhere.** Every
section heading on every tab gets a small triangle on its left (▾ open, ▸ collapsed); all open by
default; the last state is remembered per device; a collapsed heading keeps its badge and its
'all' link. One implementation in the section label, so static and configured sections behave the
same."* GANTT and CALENDAR have neither the triangle nor the behaviour.

**Fix in source.** Register the Gantt card and the Calendar card as their own sections in the
Tasks and Today column definitions (`layout/registry.tsx`) so each gets its own `Label` with a
collapse state, instead of rendering inside the section above it. That closes the missing
triangle and JQ-06 in one edit. Re-take `tasks-collapsed` afterwards.

##### S6-43 · LOW-MEDIUM · NEW, introduced by B-156 · Arrange's ↑↓ pair has no column, so it ripples 26 px down the list

**Frames.** All 36 `arrange` and `arrange-life` frames, 1024 / 1366 / 1920, both schemes.

**Measured** on `arrange-d1-1366-light-prod`, the x of the `↑` glyph on each row:

| row | ↑ glyph x | ↓ glyph x |
|---|---|---|
| Needs you | (disabled, pale) | 403–411 |
| From your EA | **358–367** | 397–405 |
| All calendars | 353–362 | 392–400 |
| Calendar | **332–341** | 371–379 |
| Your tasks | 338–347 | 377–385 |
| At a glance | 343–352 | 382–390 |
| Close the day | 357–366 | (disabled) |

**26 px of travel on the ↑ and 34 px on the ↓**, four times down one card, because the pair sits
immediately after a name of variable length. Same in the `APP` group and on `arrange-life`.

**The line it breaks.** README Components, Waiting row, verbatim: *"Type label at 48px fixed
width so titles align."* It is the rule round 1 quoted against the task list (S6-14) and that
B-134 fixed with `OWNER_COL = 30`; B-156 then reintroduced the same ragged-column shape one
surface away. And this review's rule 7, for a dialog that is meant to read as an ordered list.

**Fix in source.** `components/chrome/ArrangeDialog.tsx`: give the name a fixed-width column
(the widest name in either group plus the gap) so the ↑↓ pair starts at one x on every row —
the same one-number change `lib/labelColumn.ts` already holds for the task row and the waiting
row.

**Frames.** All 24 `trends-year` frames. Measured at 1366 light; reproduced at 393, 1024, 1920
and in dark.

**Measured** on `trends-year-d1-1366-light-prod`. Every one of the nine cards opens with today's
column at the right edge, which leaves the left edge in the middle of a month:

| card | month captions as printed | bar values as printed |
|---|---|---|
| Exercise | **`y`** · Jun · Jul · Aug · Sep | **`l9`** · 27 · 18 · 24 · 8 |
| Audiobook | **`y`** · Jun · Jul · Aug · Sep | **`l4`** · 16 · 14 · 13 · 7 |
| Solo time | **`y`** · Jun · Jul · Aug · Sep | **`l7`** · 18 · 12 · 24 · 6 |
| Meditate | **`y`** · Jun · Jul · Aug · Sep | **`21`** (partly) · 30 · 21 · 29 · 6 |

`y` is a clipped `May`; `l9`, `l4` and `l7` are clipped `19`, `14` and `17` — and they read as
letters, not as numbers.

**The lines it breaks.** This review's rule 5, verbatim: *"No word broken mid-word."* And README
Principles 7, verbatim: *"Show the work."* Round 1's own standard against the Gantt axis (S6-04)
was *"do not print a date at a pixel that is not that date"*; printing `l9` where the value is 19
is the same failure. The card's whole job is that hits and misses are readable at a glance
(`JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 12).

**Fix in source.** `components/life/HabitYear.tsx` / `YearScroller`: snap the opening scroll to a
whole month boundary as well as a whole column (`weekColumnOf` already ceils to a column), or
give the scroller a left inset equal to one caption's width so a partial column is never
captioned. Whichever — a caption or a value that cannot be fully drawn should not be drawn.

##### S6-45 · MEDIUM · NEW · evidence · The Find frames are not the same frame on prod and test

**Frames.** `find-d1-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` — four pairs. The 1024 and 393 pairs
match (at 393 the dialog is full-bleed and covers the page).

**Measured** on `find-d1-1920-dark`:

| threshold | pixels differing | bounding box |
|---|---|---|
| > 8 | **72,647** | x 232–1919, y 0–1046 |
| > 32 | **8,281** | **x 245–707, y 888–1035** |
| > 64 | 25 | x 264–273, y 971–974 |

At (264,972) the prod frame is `(25,24,21)` — the bare dark ground — and the test frame is
`(77,82,86)`. Cropping both at x 200–900, y 820–1080: the **prod** frame's Today column 1 ends
after the `Sunday's dev call still overlaps school pickup` card; the **test** frame carries, below
it, the `Her passport expires inside the six months Indonesia asks for…` card with `Open` /
`Dismiss`, and a `Talk with EA` / `Dictate to EA` pair beneath that. Ink coverage differs by
2.6 % of the frame (prod 0.4133, test 0.4396).

**And the prod frame contradicts its own tab frame.** `today-d1-1920-dark-prod` (page 1126)
carries that card at y ~900–1080 and the button pair at ~1090. So the page behind the Find
dialog on the production capture is missing content the production Today capture proves is
there. At 1366 the same difference is small (3,701 px > 8, 0 > 32) because the card sits below a
900 px viewport; at 1920 the viewport reaches it.

**The line it breaks.** The A-1 sweep, verbatim: *"prod and test frames identical on the same
screen and day."*

**I am unsure of the cause and say so.** It is either the build rendering the tab differently
under a modal on the two flavours, or a paint race in the rig — the frames are pixel-identical
from y 0 to ~880 and diverge only in the last card, which is what a race looks like. Either way
the pass carries two different pictures under one name.

**Fix (rig first).** `tools/capture-v2.mjs`: before an overlay frame, wait for the page behind to
reach its settled height (the value `shot()` already reads for a page frame) rather than for the
overlay alone. If the frames still differ after that, it is a build row.

##### S6-46 · LOW · NEW · evidence · The undo ring's digit still races the shutter

**Frames.** `toast-over-sheet-d1-1366-light-{prod,test}` and
`toast-over-sheet-d1-1920-dark-{prod,test}` — two of the eight pairs in the family; the other six
and all eight `undo-toast` pairs match.

**Measured.** `toast-over-sheet-d1-1366-light-prod` reads **`Undo (10)`** and `-test` reads
**`Undo (9)`**. The >64 set is x **886–896**, y **844–851** — 62 px, maxd **201** — the ring's
glyph and nothing else. At 1920 dark: x 1164–1173, y 1025–1031, 51 px, maxd 203.

**The line it breaks.** The same A-1 line: *"prod and test frames identical on the same screen
and day."* A-124 deliberately let app timers run at the real rate while pinning "now"; the
ten-second undo countdown is the one visible consequence, and it makes two of the pass's frames
non-reproducible.

**Fix (in the rig).** `tools/capture-v2.mjs`: for the toast frames, drive the toast and then
advance Playwright's clock to a fixed elapsed offset before the shot (or stub the ring's value),
so the digit is the same number in every run.

##### S6-48 · MEDIUM-LOW · NEW · Marker is used as a text colour in two places, where the pack allows it in two places and neither is text

**Frames.** All 16 `mic-listening` frames, at every width, both schemes, both days.

**Measured** on `mic-listening-d1-393-light-test`, darkest-decile of each glyph run:

| run | measured | token |
|---|---|---|

| the field control's `Listening`, x 275–320, y 196–214 | **(102,143,179)** | Marker |
| *control:* the selected `Everything` chip (Accent ink), x 52–150, y 140–160 | (80,95,116) | Accent ink `#4A5E70` = (74,94,112) |
| *control:* the page title `Brain` (Ink), x 20–90, y 20–50 | (43,42,38) | Ink `#2B2A26` |

At 1366 the rail's `mic on` measures **(97,141,182)** — the same. Anti-aliasing at 10.5 px lifts
a run a little off its token, and the Accent-ink control shows how little: (80,95,116) against
(74,94,112). These two runs are 60–70 levels away in blue from Accent ink and sit on Marker.

**The line it breaks.** README Colour, "Where colour goes", verbatim: *"Marker: count badge next

#### How this round was done

**Programmatic, over all 1,060 frames.**

1. **Inventory against the file-name grammar.** 1,064 PNGs; 1,060 parse as
   `<screen>-d<day>-<width>-<scheme>-<flavour>.png`, 4 do not (the `brain-proposal-*` set,
   correctly outside the pass). **Forty-seven** families. Thirty-eight hold the full 24
   (4 widths × 2 schemes × 3 passes); `arrange` and `arrange-life` hold 18 (no 393);
   `decision-section`, `life-config`, `mic-listening`, `offline`, `sync-conflict`, `sync-queued`
   and `talk` hold 16 (test only, both days). By pass: **316 / 372 / 372**. Expected from the
   grammar: 1,060. Actual: 1,060. **Nothing missing, nothing extra, no `-prod` frame of a
   rig-only state.**
2. **Blank / wrong-screen / below-the-fold sweep.** For every frame, the first row of ink more
   than 10 levels off the frame's own corner colour, against that width's viewport height.
   **No blank frame, no wrong screen, no frame whose first ink falls below the fold, and no
   frame still showing the gate that should be unlocked.**
3. **Frame-size sweep.** Every frame's pixel width equals its file-name width except the 24
   `gantt-unscheduled` element frames (327 / 394 / 742 / 1023 wide × 258 tall). Page heights are
   identical between `-prod` and `-test` on every screen and day; the only height variation
   inside a family and width is day 1 against day 2, on ten families (`agents`, `decision-bill`,
   `decision-section`, `tasks-collapsed`, `tasks-list`, `today`, `today-collapsed`, `triage` and
   their widths) — which is the point.
4. **Dark-ground sweep.** Corner pixel of all 530 dark frames against `#191815` = (25,24,21).
   **458 match exactly.** The 72 that do not are the scrimmed-dialog families (corner
   (38,36,33) / (41,38,35) — a dialog card at 393, or a sheet), the 12 `gantt-unscheduled`
   element frames ((44,43,42) — a card, not the ground), and 3 `emergency-cancelled` 393-dark
   frames at **(23,22,20)** — two levels, measured below and not a defect. **No dark frame paints
   a ground that is not the warm token; no frame in the pass has a pure black or pure white
   corner.**
5. **Light/dark parity.** Column-occupancy profiles per light/dark pair. **No dark reflow
   anywhere**, no section appearing or disappearing between schemes on any family.
6. **LV-09 (1) — prod vs test on day 1.** Full RGB diff of all 316 `-d1-…-prod` frames against
   their `-d1-…-test` twins. Method and result below.
7. **LV-09 (2) — day 1 vs day 2.** Full RGB diff of all 372 `-d1-…-test` frames against
   `-d2-…-test`, plus a page-height comparison. Method and result below.

#### LV-09 (1) · prod and test on the same screen and day

**Method.** For each of the 316 `-d1-…-prod` frames I loaded the `-d1-…-test` twin, checked the
size, then took the per-pixel max-channel absolute difference, reporting counts above 8, 32 and
64 levels and the bounding box of each set.

**Result.** No size mismatch anywhere. **178 of the 316 pairs are now bit-identical** — up from
round 2's 141. Of the 138 that differ:

| what differs | pairs | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **the mic orb's own box**, ≤ 53 levels over 1–107 px | 132 | `today-d1-1366-dark`: the whole >8 set is x 1307–1342, y 1072–1115 — a 36 × 44 rectangle, the orb. `brain-d1-393-light`, `agents-d1-1920-light` and the rest are the same box at their own coordinates. Not a content change. |
| **scattered sub-threshold pixels** (15–86 px, n32 ≤ 6) | 6 | `tasks-list-d1-{393,1366}-*`, `tasks-collapsed-d1-{1024,1366,1920}-*`: isolated single pixels spread over the page, never a run. Anti-aliasing, not content. |
| **the Today page behind the Find dialog** | **4** | `find-d1-1920-dark`: 72,647 px >8, **8,281 >32**, 25 >64, maxd 66; the >32 set is x **245–707, y 888–1035**. `find-d1-1920-light`: 65,449 >8, **452 >32**, box x 262–670, y 971–1033. `find-d1-1366-light` 6,957 >8 / 6 >32; `find-d1-1366-dark` 3,701 >8 / 0 >32, both in the band y 709–899. **A content difference — S6-45, still open.** |

**The undo ring is fixed.** All eight `toast-over-sheet` prod/test pairs are now bit-identical
(maxd 0 at seven, 1 at `1366-dark`); all eight `undo-toast` pairs differ only in the orb's box.
Round 2's `Undo (10)` / `Undo (9)` split is gone.

**Verdict on LV-09 (1): FAIL on four pairs, PASS on 312.** One content difference stands
(S6-45), and it now reproduces *to the pixel* across a full re-take — see below.

#### LV-09 (2) · day 2 must differ where it claims to

**Method.** Full RGB diff of all 372 `-d1-…-test` frames against `-d2-…-test`, plus a page-height
comparison. A pair whose page heights differ cannot be pixel-diffed and is counted as differing
by construction.

**Result.** Of 372 pairs: **40 differ in page height** (proof of a day-2 change on its own),
**285 differ pixel-wise**, and **47 are bit-identical**. Ten families carry a day-2 height change:
`today` (1366 1141→1062, 1920 1126→1080, 1024 1744→1665, 393 2583→2549), `today-collapsed`
(1141→1062 / 1126→1080 / 1630→1551 / 1998→1964), `tasks-list` and `tasks-collapsed`
(952→939 / 1001→988 / 1600→1587 and 1489→1476), `agents` (1072→1121 / 1595→1644 / 2296→2345),
`decision-bill` (393 2509→2522), `decision-section` (2501→2514), `triage` (2525→2538). Amplitude
on the rest is large where it should be: `task-detail-d1-1920-light` **267,408 px >32**,
`files-archive-d1-1920-light` 108,915, `decision-history-d1-1920-light` 70,825,
`undo-toast-d1-1920-dark` 47,984, `tasks-list`/`tasks-collapsed` at 1920 30,219.

The 47 identical pairs are all correct and I name every one:

- `locked` (8) and `gantt-unscheduled` (8) — the gate has no day-2 content, and the element frame
  is a bucket none of whose five rows changes on day 2 (what day 2 finishes is t1's last
  **subtask**, per A-127).
- Full-bleed or panel surfaces that cover the page behind, so no day-2 content is on the frame:
  `talk` (4, at 393 and 1024 — at those widths Talk is a `screen`, not a centred panel),
  `sync-conflict` (4, 393 and 1024), `sync-queued` (4), `settings` (2, 393), `sync` (2, 393),
  `reply` (2, 393), `find` (2, 393), `emergency-confirm` (2, 393), `toast-over-sheet` (2, 393),
  `settings-rules` (1, 393-dark), `settings-voice` (1, 393-dark), `task-complete` (1, 393-dark),
  `delegate-picker` (1, 393-dark), `life-config` (1, 393-dark).
- `arrange-life` (2, 1024-dark and 1920-dark). Arrange has no day-2 content of its own; the
  **light** twins of those two frames differ by 370 and 473 px, all of it below 32 levels in a
  26 × 16 box, and cropping it shows the Life page's own habit strip **frosting through the
  dialog's empty lower band** — the page behind changed, the dialog did not. In dark that
  show-through falls below the 8-level threshold, so the dark pair reads identical. Correct in
  both.

**Verdict on LV-09 (2): PASS.** No family that claims a day-2 change is identical, and every
identical pair has a reason on the frame.

- **The Calendar list's label row on every `today*` frame.** It is a `Section` now, with a

- **The Waiting-on column on every Tasks frame.** Two sections where there was one, on
  `tasks-list`, `tasks-board`, `tasks-gantt`, `tasks-done`, `tasks-filtered`, `tasks-collapsed`
  and `board-drag`, at all four widths and both schemes. The Gantt card's own content
  (four bars, `5 Sep` / `17 Sep`) is byte-for-byte where S6-24 left it. No regression.
- **Every dialog and sheet over another overlay.** The corner sweep over all 1,060: every light
  dialog family reads **(173,172,167)** (one scrim) or a card/sheet fill; **no family reads
  (128,128,123)**. Checked by eye on the three stacked cases: `delegate-picker` over the task
  dialog, `sync`/`sync-conflict`/`sync-queued` over the Settings sheet (the sheet's own card at
  (300,150) reads 251 behind the panel — undimmed), and `toast-over-sheet`.
- **The Arrange rows.** One column at every width and scheme, measured above. The rows read as an
  ordered list. *Named, not raised:* the pair now starts 200 px into a 900 px dialog with the
  switch flush right, so each row is two clusters with ~620 px between them — that is S6-26's
  shape, carried, not a new finding.
- **The Year cards' opening position at every width.** The left edge is clean. **The right edge
  is not, and it is a defect: S6-55.** My answer to the question the round put: no, a partial
  next month at a scroll edge is not automatically acceptable here. The board strip's clip
  (S6-28) was declined because what is clipped there is a *card* — a whole object partly seen.
  What is clipped here is a *caption and a value*: `Oc` where the month is `Oct`, and a left
