##### S6-54 · HIGH · NEW · A segmented control lets a label overrun its segment and print on top of its neighbour — glyphs share pixels on two surfaces, and one of them is a regression from 200 px to 119 px

**Frames.** All 24 `settings-voice` frames (393, 1024, 1366, 1920, both schemes, both flavours,
both days) and the eight `files-archive` **393** frames.

**Measured — Settings › Voice, `Speed`.** On `settings-voice-d1-1366-light-prod` the three
controls in the Voice card, taken as the non-card run along their own row:

| control | options | track | per segment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Style (`Warm / Clear / Brisk`) | 3 | x **896–1095 = 200 px** | 66.7 px |
| **Speed** (`0.8x / 1x / 1.2x / 1.5x / 1.75x / 2x`) | **6** | x **977–1095 = 119 px** | **19.8 px** |
| End my turn (`Off / 10s / 60s`) | 3 | ~180 px | 60 px |

The same 119 px at 393 (x 244–362, against Style's 200 px at x 163–362), at 1024 and at 1920 —
**the control does not grow with the screen and does not grow with its option count.** The glyph
runs across the whole track are 1 px apart at four of the five joins (x 1024–1029 / 1031–1039,
1044–1048 / 1050–1055, 1059–1070 / 1072–1082, 1072–1082 / 1084–1088).

**And they do not merely touch — they overprint.** Cropping x 1040–1095, y 328–346 at 16× shows
the `1` of `1.75x` drawn **through** the `x` of `1.5x` (the x's diagonal crosses the 1's stem) and
the `2` of `2x` drawn **through** the `x` of `1.75x`. It reads as `.5x⟨X⟩.75x⟨X⟩2x`. The selected
`1x` pill's left edge (x ~999) also cuts the tail of `0.8x`. Identical in dark
(`settings-voice-d1-393-dark-prod`, same crop) and at every width.

**Measured — Files › kind, at 393.** `files-archive-d1-393-light-prod`: the "kind" row holds
**seven** segments (`Any kind / PDF / Document / Spreadsheet / Image / Text / Link`) in a 354 px
track = **50.6 px each**. At 9× (x 110–270, y 190–212) the `nt` of `Document` and the `Sp` of
`Spreadsheet` occupy the same pixels, and the final `t` of `Spreadsheet` is overprinted by the `I`
of `Image`. It reads as `Documeǹŝpreadsheetlmage`. The same row is clean at 1024, 1366 and 1920.

**The lines it breaks.** This review's rule 5, verbatim: *"No clipped or ellipsised label inside a
button, chip or segment."* Overprinting is worse than clipping: a clipped label is short, an
overprinted one is wrong. README Accessibility, verbatim: *"Tap targets 36px minimum on phone."*
19.8 px is **55%** of that, six times in a row, on the control that sets how fast a voice speaks
— a thing changed while walking. And `DISCREPANCIES.md` 9's own stated reason for keeping the
`Seg` where the pack and the mock both wanted a value button: *"The segmented control shows every
option at once."* At 19.8 px per segment it does not.

**This is a regression, and I name the number.** The ST-1 round-2 review measured this exact
control at **200 px / 33.3 px per segment** and wrote, verbatim: *"All six render in full —
`0.8x 1x 1.2x 1.5x 1.75x 2x` — no ellipsis, no clip, no wrap, in both schemes. The longest label
`1.75x` has a glyph run of 25 px."* The track has lost **81 px** since, and 25 px of glyph is now
being asked to sit in 19.8 px of segment. ST1-11 is on round 1's "still open from ST-1" list and
has no carried row; whatever moved the control between then and now made an open MEDIUM into a
HIGH.

**Fix in source.** `theme/ui/*` `Seg`: give the segment row `flex: 1` per option against the row's
control column rather than sizing the track to a constant, and floor the per-segment width at the
widest label's measured width plus the 3 px padding the pack gives the control (and at 36 px under
768, per README Accessibility). If six options will not fit a phone row at 36 px, the honest
alternative is the pack's own 1-3-1 option rows or a value button with a picker behind it — not a
segment narrower than its own text. The Files "kind" row wants the same change or a second line at
393.

##### S6-55 · MEDIUM-LOW · NEW, introduced by B-165 · The Year card's clipped caption and value moved from the left edge to the right, and at 393 the column it cuts is the current month

**Frames.** All 24 `trends-year` frames. Measured at 1366 and 393 light; reproduced at 1024, 1920
and in dark.

**Measured** on `trends-year-d1-1366-light-prod`, the right edge of every one of the nine cards
(crop x 420–520, y 240–450, at 6×):

| what | printed | should be |
|---|---|---|
| the fifth month caption | **`O`** plus a sliver | `Oct` |
| the fifth bar's value | **`(`** — the left curve of a zero | `0` |

At **393** the same cut lands one column earlier, on **September**: `trends-year-d1-393-light-prod`
prints `Feb · Mar · Apr · May · Jun · Jul · Aug · **`Se`**` and the values
`0 · 15 · 19 · 19 · 27 · 18 · 24 · **a half `8`**`. The month the owner is standing in is the one
whose caption and count are cut. At 1920 it is `Oc` and the half zero again.

**The lines it breaks.** This review's rule 5, verbatim: *"No word broken mid-word."* And README
Principles 7, verbatim: *"Show the work."* Round 2's own standard against this card, which B-165's
note accepted — *"a caption or a value that cannot be fully drawn should not be drawn"* — is
satisfied at the left edge and broken at the right.

**Why this is not S6-28's declined clip.** S6-28 was declined because what the board strip cuts is
a **card** — a whole object partly visible, which reads as "there is more". What this cuts is a
caption and a numeral, which read as a different word and a different number. `Oc` is not a month
and `(` is not a count.

**Fix in source.** `components/life/HabitYear.tsx` / `YearScroller`: apply at the trailing edge the
rule B-165 applied at the leading one — clip the scroller's viewport to a whole month boundary at
both ends, or give the content a right inset of one caption's width so a partial column is never
captioned or valued. At 393, where the trailing month is today's, the snap must round **out** so
the current month stays whole.

**Frames.** All 24 `trends-week` and all 24 `trends-all` frames at 1024, 1366 and 1920 (the 393
frames are fine).

**Measured** — the dialog's own vertical extent against its last row of real ink (ink taken as
> 120 levels off the dialog fill (247,247,244), so the show-through is excluded):

| tab | 393 | 1024 | 1366 | 1920 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Week | 0% | 4% | **41%** (336 of 810 px) | **51%** (498 of 972) |
| All time | 2% | 10% | **47%** (383 of 810) | **56%** (545 of 972) |
| Month | 3% | 0% | 8% | 23% |
| Year | 0% | 0% | 0% | 6% |

On `trends-all-d1-1366-light-prod` the nine cards end at y **471** and the dialog runs to y
**854**. In that band the Life page reads through the frosted surface at up to **50 levels** of
contrast (min (197,200,202) against the fill's (247,247,244)) — the habit strip's rows and the
Money card are distinguishable as shapes.

**The lines it breaks.** This review's rule 7, verbatim: *"1920 reads as a dashboard, not three
phone columns"* — a modal that is more than half bare surface on a 34-inch monitor is the "amateur"
read Josh gave the v1.1 frames. And it is the surface `JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 12 asks for by name;
the A-1 list puts "the three habit views" on my desk.

**I name the cause, because the obvious fix would undo a fix.** B-150(c) gave the body
`minHeight: trendsBodyHeight(height, phone)` — a constant 90% of the viewport — precisely so the
header and the segmented control stop moving between tabs, which was S6-11(c). Letting the dialog

number rather than to what it holds.

**Fix in source.** `components/life/TrendsDialog.tsx`: keep the header and the segmented control
pinned (a fixed-height header block above a body that is free), and let the **body** size to its
content with the 90% figure as a `maxHeight` rather than a `minHeight`. The segment's y stays
constant — which is all S6-11(c) asked for — and the Week and All-time tabs stop printing half a
dialog of nothing. If the dialog must keep one height, the honest use of the space is a fourth
card column at 1366+ rather than empty surface.

**Measured** on `talk-d1-1366-light-test`, the rail foot (x 10–195): one ink band **y 862–884, 23
px tall — two lines** where every other frame's health line is one 11 px line. At 5× it reads

```
● needs attention · $0.40 · in
  conversation
```

Identical at 1920 (band y 1042–1064) and in dark at both. Every other suffix the line takes fits:

`offline-d1-1366-light-test` reads `● offline · captures queue` on one line.

**The lines it breaks.** This review's rule 5, verbatim: *"No single-word orphan line in a title"*
— and the substance of B-83's own rule, which bound the header's subtitle and the Latest-in titles

##### S6-61 · LOW · NEW · Rules for my EA punctuates seven sentences of the same kind two different ways

**Frames.** All 24 `settings-rules` frames; the same card at 1366 in both schemes.

**Measured** on `settings-rules-d1-1366-light-prod`, the RULES FOR MY EA card at 3× (x 690–1120,
y 290–620):

| # | rule | terminator |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `File anything from a supplier under Work · money and tell me at the daily wrap rather than at the time` | **none** |
| 2 | `Never send anything on my behalf without showing me the words first` | **none** |
| 3 | `Anything naming a child goes to the family silo and stays sensitive` | **none** |
| 4 | `School pickup days are fixed; move the meeting or ask Joce first.` | full stop |
| 5 | `Never book anything before 7:30am.` | full stop |
| 6 | `Deal documents never appear in a "summarise my week" answer.` | full stop |
| 7 | `Replies to Andy: short, first names, no bullet points.` | full stop |

Three without, four with, in one card, on the surface `ST-01` and `JOSH_QA_v22.md` exist for.
*Named with it, not filed separately:* rule 6 uses straight double quotes where the same card's
meta lines use a proper em dash (`Do it — tell me after`), so the card is typographically careful
in one line and not in the next.

**The line it breaks.** README Content, verbatim: *"Voice: a capable assistant speaking to one
person. Short sentences. Plain words."* — and the consistency standard S6-49 was fixed on one round
ago, which was that a line either is a sentence and carries a terminator or is a fragment and does
not. This card is the record of what the EA has been taught; it is read as a list, and a list that
punctuates itself two ways reads as two lists.

**Fix in source.** `data/mock/fixtures/rules.json` (or wherever `settings-rules` sources its seven
strings): one form for all seven — full stops, since four of the seven are complete sentences with
a subject and a verb and the pack's voice is sentences. Straighten the quotes in rule 6 to the
typographic pair the em dash implies.

#### Measured and found NOT to be defects this round

Recorded so the auditor does not re-litigate them. Rounds 1 and 2's lists still stand where the
fixes did not touch the thing measured; these are the ones a round-2 fix **did** touch, or that I
looked at fresh.

- **The frame set.** 1,060 frames, forty-seven families, the grammar exact, `arrange` /
  `arrange-life` correctly without 393, the seven rig-only states correctly test-only, no blank
  frame, no wrong screen, no frame with its first ink below the fold, no frame showing the gate
  that should be unlocked. `demo/v22` is a complete pass.
- **Dark.** 458 of 530 dark frames carry the exact warm (25,24,21) corner; 69 of the other 72 are
  scrimmed dialogs and element frames whose corner is a scrim or a card. The remaining three —
  `emergency-cancelled-d1-393-dark-{prod,test}` and its `-d2-` twin — read **(23,22,20)**: a
  gradual 3-level falloff over the leftmost ~14 px, which the light twin shows too (237 → 233), so
  it is the emergency card's own soft shadow reaching the page edge, under the pack's 3.5% ceiling.
  No pure black or white corner anywhere. No reflow between any light/dark pair.
- **The drop target's fill.** On `board-drag-d1-1366-light-prod` the NEXT lane's Accent-soft fill
  is 4 levels above the other lanes' (217,218,215 against 221,219,214), not the ~17 a .14-alpha
  tint gives at full opacity. That is the drag's own dimming acting on both, and the dashed
  Accent-ink border carries the state unmistakably. Recorded, not raised.
- **The dashed border doing two jobs on one frame.** On `board-drag-d1-1366-light-prod` the
  drop-target lane is dashed and so are the two EA-owned cards (`Waiting-on digest`, `Redact the
  200 sample emails` — dashed on `tasks-board` too, where nothing is being dragged). Two meanings,
  one dress. I looked hard at this and did **not** raise it: during a drag the whole board is
  dimmed except the held card, so the lane's dash is at full Accent ink while the cards' are
  washed, and the two are at different scales (a lane outline against a card outline). Named so
  nobody thinks it was missed.

#### A6-01 · HIGH · The phone page now ends 112 px above the foot of the frame, but the rig still grows the viewport to the page height — so **every** grown 393 frame is missing the last 112 px of its page, and 74 of them are cut through a card

**What I measured.** On every 393 frame taller than the viewport the page's content stops dead at
row **h−113**, and rows h−112 … h−1 hold only the watermark chip and the tab bar. That is
`WATERMARK_BAND` exactly. The capture rig grows the viewport to the page's `scrollHeight`
(`jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs`, `shot()`: `max = el.getBoundingClientRect().top +
window.scrollY + el.scrollHeight`) and that number does not know about the scroll box's new 112 px
bottom **margin**, so the grown viewport is 112 px too short and the scroller silently swallows the
page's own 24 px bottom padding plus **88 px of real content**.

**Named, with the pixel.**

| frame | h | what is cut at y = h−113 |
|---|---|---|
| `today-d1-393-light-prod` | 2487 | the third habit-chip row — `Learning`, `Nap`, `Build` sliced horizontally through the glyphs at y 2374; the card has no bottom edge; **the whole "How was today?" reflection field is absent from the frame.** The V2.1 frame of the same screen (`demo/v21/today-d1-393-light-prod.png`, h 2325) shows the chips complete, the field beneath them, and the card's rounded bottom |
| `agents-d1-393-light-prod` | 2200 | the Emergency-lock card cut mid-sentence — `token, freezes the vault, pauses the agents, wipes this device's` and nothing after it |
| `collapsed-d1-393-light-prod` | 960 | the Learning row `Multi-agent orchestration patterns` cut through its second line, its `open` button sliced in half |
| `tasks-list-d1-393-light-prod` | 1504 | the Gantt row `Book the Term 4` cut, its bar half-drawn |
| `brain-d1-393-light-prod` | 1687 | the Files card runs into the clip with no bottom edge and no 10 px bottom radius |
| `triage-d2-393-dark-test` | 2442 | the same chip row, the same cut, dark |

**Tally.** 86 grown 393 frames. **74 are cut through content** — `agents` 6, `brain` 6, `collapsed`
6, `decision-bill` 6, `decision-section` 4, `life` 6, `tasks-board` 6, `tasks-gantt` 6,
`tasks-list` 6, `today` 6, `triage` 6, `offline` 4, `mic-listening` 4, `brain-proposal` 2. Only
`tasks-collapsed` and `today-collapsed` (12 frames) happen to carry 112 px of slack and end
cleanly.

**The lines it breaks.** README Surfaces, verbatim: *"Radii: 10 cards, bars, icon buttons"* — 74
frames show a card with a square cut where its bottom should be. README Layout, verbatim: *"Leave
the bottom of a column empty when the content ends."* — this round's own question is whether that
now reads right at the foot of a phone, and **the evidence cannot answer it**, because on 74 of 86
grown frames the foot of the page is not in the frame. And my standing remit: *"a frame that is
obviously the wrong screen, blank, or still showing the gate when it should be unlocked"* is itself
a defect — a frame missing the last 112 px of the page it claims to photograph is the same family.

**What I *can* say about the change itself, from the two frames that do show the foot.** On
`today-collapsed-d1-393-light-prod` and `tasks-collapsed-d1-393-light-prod` the last card's bottom
edge sits at **y = h−137** (24 px page padding + the 112 band), the watermark chip at h−100 … h−84,
the tab bar at h−74 … h−15, the mic orb at h−132 … h−88. In V2.1 the last card ended at h−120, so
the foot has moved **17 px up** — "roughly where it always did", as the brief says. The mark is
clear of content by 37 px of ground; the bar and the orb have not moved a pixel (`demo/v21` bar
h−74 … h−15, `demo/v22` bar h−74 … h−15); and there is **no dead strip** — the band reads as the
step the floating bar always wanted. **On those two frames the change is right.** I cannot extend
that to the other forty-three phone screens from these pixels, and I will not.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/tools/capture-v2.mjs`, in `shot()`: `needed` must add whatever the
box model puts *below* the scroll box, not only its `scrollHeight` — measure
`window.innerHeight − el.getBoundingClientRect().bottom` on the same element and add it, so the
grown viewport becomes `contentHeight + 112` on a phone and is unchanged everywhere else. Then
re-take the 393 pass. Nothing in `layout/TabScreen.tsx` or `components/chrome/watermarkText.ts`
needs to change for this.

#### A6-02 · MEDIUM · `files-archive` at 393 — the `who` control wraps for no reason and strands `Dev`, one 21 px word, centred across a 355 px row

**Frames.** `files-archive-d1-393-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` and the day-2 twins — **6 frames**.

**Measured** on `files-archive-d1-393-light-prod`. The `who` track spans **x 16–371 (355 px)**,
y 128–208. It holds five options. Five segments would be **71 px each**; the longest label,
`Anyone`, measures **x 42–83 = 42 px**. Every label fits one row with 29 px to spare. It wraps
anyway: `Anyone | Josh | Joce | EA` at quarters on row 1, and **`Dev` alone on row 2, x 184–204,
centred on 355 px** — one word with 167 px of empty track either side.

**The lines it breaks.** README Components, verbatim: *"Segmented control `.js-seg` (Tasks views):
Hairline fill, 3px padding, radius 9; selected segment Card fill, Ink, 500, shadow `0 1px 3px
rgba(60,55,45,.14)`"* — the pack describes one track of equal segments and nothing else; a 355 px
segment holding a 21 px word is not one of them. And Josh's standing complaint, quoted in my brief:
*"some buttons centred, some left-aligned"* — this is exactly that, inside a single control.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/theme/ui/chips.tsx`, `Seg`: wrap on **fit**, not on count. Measure
the widest label against `width / options.length` and take a second row only when a label does not
fit its share. Five 42 px labels in 355 px never needed one.

#### A6-03 · MEDIUM · `files-archive` at 393 — the `kind` control's second row divides in thirds under a first row divided in quarters: one control, two grids

**Frames.** The same 6.

**Measured** on `files-archive-d1-393-light-prod`. Track x 16–371 (355 px), y 216–296. Row 1 is
four segments at 88 px — `Any kind | PDF | Document | Spreadsheet`, centres at x 63 / 150 / 237 /
324. Row 2 is three segments at 118 px — `Image | Text | Link`, centres at x **77 / 194 / 310**.
Not one centre lines up with a centre or a divider above it. The selected pill (`Any kind`, Card
fill + shadow) is 88 px wide; select `Link` instead and the same pill becomes 118 px.

The overprinting B-255 set out to fix **is** fixed — `Spreadsheet` measures x 291–359 = 69 px
inside its 88 px segment, clean at 393 in both schemes, and 1024 / 1366 / 1920 keep one row of
seven, which is right. What is left is the shape of the wrap, not the width.

**The lines it breaks.** The same `.js-seg` line as A6-02: a selected segment whose width depends
on which row it lands in is not equal segments. Checklist 7, density — two rows at two divisions
read as two controls sharing a track rather than one control.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/theme/ui/chips.tsx`: hold one division for the whole control —
`Math.ceil(n / rows)` cells per row with the short row's trailing cells left as empty track, so
every segment is 88 px and the selected pill is one size — or fall back to the pack's chip row for
a control this long on a phone. Growing the last row to fill is what produces both A6-02 and
A6-03.

**Frames.** `settings-voice-d1-393-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` and the day-2 twins — **6 frames**.

y 258–338 — **80 px tall, two rows**. Row 1: `0.8x | 1x | 1.2x | 1.5x` at 75 px each. Row 2:
`1.75x | 2x` at 150 px each, their labels at x 133–156 and x 282–293 — both sitting over the

#### A6-06 · LOW · B-173's bound phrase works, and leaves the rail's health line ending on a stranded middle dot

**Frames.** `talk-d1-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}-test` and the four day-2 twins — **8 frames**.

**Measured** on `talk-d1-1366-light-test`, rail foot x 10–195: two lines, y 862–874 and y 875–887,
reading

```
● needs attention · $0.40 ·
  in conversation
```

`in conversation` is whole on one line — **B-173 is closed**, the break S6-59 named is gone. What it
left is line 1 ending on the separator with nothing after it. S6-59's own fix text named the
alternative and it was not taken: *"or the rail's 176 px of text width takes it on one line if the
`$0.40` is dropped while a conversation is up."*

**The line it breaks.** README Content, verbatim: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces:
`JSTACK · today · high`."* A dot separates two things on a line; a line that ends on one has
nothing left to separate, and a reader who scans line 1 now gets `needs attention · $0.40 ·`.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/components/chrome/HealthLine.tsx`: bind the separator to the word
that follows it, so the dot travels with `in conversation` to line 2 — or drop the `$0.40` while a
conversation is live so the whole line fits the rail's 176 px on one row.

#### A6-07 · LOW, and unsure it is this round's · the mic orb paints out two thirds of a live `open` control at 393 — the same defect the watermark band was added to fix

**Frames.** `collapsed-d1-393-{light,dark}-prod` and twins, `life-d1-393-*`, `brain-d1-393-dark-*`,
`offline-d1-393-*`.

**Measured** on `collapsed-d1-393-light-prod`: the Learning row's `open` button spans **x 308–367,
y 836–866**; the idle mic orb's disc spans **x 329–373, y 828–872**. The orb covers the right
**39 px of a 59 px button** — at 4× the word reads `op`, then the disc. Identical in dark and on
`life-d1-393-dark-prod`.

**Why I raise it now.** `WATERMARK_BAND`'s own derivation is that the mark *"sat over a Needs-you
card's `Open` and `Dismiss`: opaque ground over two live controls, invisible but still tappable."*
The new band ends the page above the **mark** (112 px). The orb reaches **132 px** up, so the page
still runs under it, and on these frames it lands on a control. The pack sanctions a floating orb
(*"Idle: 44px circle, Card surface, Accent ink glyph, opacity .8. Phone: fixed right 20, bottom
88"*) and content has always scrolled beneath it, so this is **not new** and may be by design —
which is why I mark it unsure rather than a straight defect.

**What I would need to decide it.** One line from Josh or the pack: does the phone page end above
the *mark's* band, or above the *bottom-right chrome's* band? If the latter, the band is 132 and
`TabScreen.tsx` takes the larger of the two. If the former, this is closed and belongs in
`watermarkText.ts` so the next reviewer does not re-find it.

#### Defects

##### A62-01 · MEDIUM · A6-06's fix moved the stranded middle dot from the end of line 1 to the **start of line 2**, which is a thing row A-1 forbids by name

**Frames.** `talk-d{1,2}-{1366,1920}-{light,dark}-test` — **8 frames**.

**Measured** on `talk-d1-1366-light-test`, rail x 10–195, health line y 862–887:

```
● needs attention · $0.40
  · in conversation
```

and on `talk-d1-1920-light-test` and `talk-d2-1366-dark-test` (`$0.88`) identically. The separator
did travel with the phrase — that half is done, line 1 no longer ends on a dot. But it now **opens
line 2**, and line 2's first ink is a middle dot with nothing to its left.

**The lines it breaks.** Row A-1 of `19_CC_V22_AUDIT_PROMPT.md`, on every frame, verbatim: *"no raw
instant, no 'in N days', **no leading middle dot**, no orphaned emphasised value"*. And README
Content, verbatim: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`"* — a dot
separates two things **on a line**; a line that begins with one has nothing to its left to separate
from, exactly as a line that ends on one has nothing to its right.

This is the second attempt at S6-59 and the second thing it has produced. Round 1 named the fix that
works and it is still not taken.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/components/chrome/HealthLine.tsx`: do not bind the separator to
either neighbour — **drop the `$0.40` while a conversation is live**, as S6-59's own fix text said
(*"the rail's 176 px of text width takes it on one line if the `$0.40` is dropped while a
conversation is up"*), so the line reads `needs attention · in conversation` on one row; or break
the line into two meta rows with no separator between them at all. Binding a dot to a word can only
choose which end it is stranded at.

##### A62-02 · MEDIUM · two phone screens carry **no demo watermark at all** — `dump-focused` and `mic-listening`, 10 frames

**Frames.** `dump-focused-d1-393-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` + the day-2 twins (**6**);
`mic-listening-d1-393-{light,dark}-test` + the day-2 twins (**4**).

**What I measured.** I swept the bottom 210 rows of all 258 frames at 393 for the mark's box (a run
of ≥ 40 non-ground pixels in x 12–210 with x 240–320 empty, which separates the mark from the tab
bar and the orb). It resolves on **248 of 258**. On these ten it resolves on nothing, and the pixels
agree: on `dump-focused-d1-393-light-prod` rows **752–768**, where every other Brain frame puts
`Demo · fixture data · nothing sends` at x 14–185, are flat ground `(237,235,229)`; the next ink
below y 711 is the tab bar at y 778. On `mic-listening-d1-393-light-test` (H 2053) rows 1803–1934 are
flat ground and the next ink is the mic banner at y 1935. Both schemes, both days, prod and test.
The same two screens **do** carry the mark at 1024 / 1366 / 1920 — `dump-focused-d1-1366-light-prod`
has it in the rail at y 805–818, above `● Sync` and the health line — so this is the phone layout
only.

**The line it breaks.** My brief, on V2.1's additions, verbatim: *"**The demo watermark** — bottom-left,
on every screen INCLUDING the locked one."* `locked-d1-393-light-prod` obeys it (mark at y 752–768).
These two do not. A demo build that stops saying it is a demo on the two screens where someone is
mid-capture — a focused mind-dump, a live mic — is the wrong two screens to lose it on.

**What the two have in common** is that both replace or displace the bottom-right chrome: the mic
banner takes the orb's place on `mic-listening`, and the dump field is focused on `dump-focused`.
The mark looks to be mounted in the same slot as the thing that is being swapped out.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/layout/TabScreen.tsx` / `components/chrome/watermarkText.ts`: the mark
is page chrome, not part of the mic/composer group — mount it unconditionally at the page foot and
let the banner and the focused composer be laid out around it, so it survives both states.

##### A62-03 · LOW · at 393 the mark has **two placements**, and in the second one its opaque chip prints over the tab bar's bottom-left corner — 109 frames

**Frames.** Every 393 frame whose surface is a sheet or a dialog: `caps-edit`, `decision-history`,
`delegate-picker`, `emergency-confirm`, `files-archive`, `life-config`, `reply`, `settings`,
`settings-rules`, `settings-voice`, `sync`, `sync-conflict`, `sync-queued`, `task-complete`,
`task-detail`, `toast-over-sheet`, `trends`, `trends-all`, `trends-week`, `trends-year` — **109
frames** by the sweep. Of these, the ones over a scrimmed tab page carry the overprint; I confirmed
it on **63** in light by measurement and on the dark twins by eye.

**Measured** on `caps-edit-d1-393-light-prod`: the mark is an **opaque chip filled with the page
ground `(237,235,229)`, x 8–191, y 826–843** (H−26 … H−9). The floating tab bar, dimmed by the
dialog's scrim, runs **y 776–837** at x 320. The chip therefore covers the bar's bottom **12 rows,
826–837**, across its left 183 px — the corner under `Today` and `Tasks`. Identical boxes on
`decision-history-d1-393-light-prod`, `task-complete-d1-393-light-prod` and, in dark,
`task-complete-d1-393-dark-prod` (chip fill `(25,24,21)`). On the tab pages the same mark sits at
**H−100 … H−84**, 10 px clear above the bar (`today-d1-393-light-prod`, text y 2530–2540, bar
2553–2612) — so one mark, two positions, 74 px apart.

**The line it breaks.** My brief, verbatim: *"It must be legible and must not sit over a control or
another line (it printed over the rail's health line for eight rows before anyone looked: B-32)."*
This is B-32's shape again — *"opaque ground over two live controls, invisible but still tappable"* —
with the mitigation that the bar is behind a modal scrim and so is not live while the sheet is up.
That is why I file it LOW and not higher. It is **not** a regression from this round's fixes: nothing
in 1–7 touched sheet chrome, and round 1 measured the same y 826–843 on `files-archive` and read it
as clear because it only checked the card above, not the bar below. I am correcting my own round-1
"the watermark clears every one of the 45 phone screens": it does not.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/components/chrome/watermarkText.ts`: give the sheet/dialog placement
the same `bottom` the tab-page placement uses (above the bar's 88 px) whenever a tab bar is mounted
behind the surface, so the mark has one resting height on a phone instead of two.

##### A62-04 · MEDIUM · `tasks-filtered` at 393 — `Clear` and `Slicers` are two separate live controls painted identically 6 px apart, and read as one phrase

**Frames.** `tasks-filtered-d1-393-{light,dark}-{prod,test}` + day-2 twins (**6**); `Slicers` alone
appears the same way on every Tasks view at 393 (`tasks-list`, `tasks-board`, `tasks-gantt`,
`tasks-done`, `tasks-collapsed`, `board-drag` — another 36 frames), but only `tasks-filtered` shows
the pair.

**Measured** on `tasks-filtered-d1-393-light-prod`, slicer row y 242–255: `Clear` occupies
**x 261–287**, `Slicers` **x 293–330** — a **6 px** gap, no separator, no chip, no underline, same
10.5 px meta size, same Accent ink (both sample as blue-cast antialias against the `In progress`
chip's exact `(74,94,112)`). At 8× the two read as one run: **`Clear Slicers`**, which parses as a
verb and its object. They are not: on `board-drag-d1-393-light-prod`, with no slicer active, only
`Slicers` is there — `Clear` appears only when something is on. Two independent taps, one of which
clears every filter, look like one phrase. At 1366 the same row has 500 px of air and the two are
far apart, so this is the phone only.

**The lines it breaks.** README Principles 3, verbatim: *"Colour means you can act."* — true of both
words, and that is the problem: nothing distinguishes them, so the reader cannot tell there are two
things to act on. And Josh's standing complaint quoted in my brief — *"some buttons centred, some
left-aligned"* — is this family: controls that do not announce their own edges.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/components/tasks/SlicerRow.tsx`: the two `Txt` links at lines 87 and 91
need a visible boundary at 393 — put the pack's middle dot with spaces between them
(`Clear · Slicers`), or give `Clear` the chip dress the active-filter chip already has, or drop
`Slicers` to the icon button's accessible label and let the icon stand alone, as it already must
when nothing is narrowed.

##### A62-05 · LOW · `mic-listening` at 393 leaves a 132 px band of dead ground between the last card and the mic banner

**Frames.** `mic-listening-d{1,2}-393-{light,dark}-test` — **4 frames**.

**Measured** on `mic-listening-d1-393-light-test` (H 2053): the Files card's last ink is at **y 1802**
(H−251); the mic banner `Mic on · listening for Brain   Stop` starts at **y 1935** (H−118), x 20–372;
the tab bar follows at **y 1978**. Between the card and the banner are **132 px of unbroken ground**
(y 1803–1934) with
nothing in them — and, because of A62-02, not even the watermark. The same page with the orb idle
(`brain-d1-393-light-prod`) closes its last card at H−170 and fills the band with the orb and the
mark. The page is reserving for a 132 px orb that is not on screen and for a banner that is 35 px
tall, and the two reserves stack.

**The line it breaks.** Checklist 4, verbatim: *"Empty column bottoms are left empty — that is
correct, not a gap."* — that licenses an empty **column**, not 127 px of reserved page foot under a
full-width card; and this round's own question, whether anything at the foot reads as dead. On
these four frames it does. It is the only place in 90 grown frames where it does.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/layout/TabScreen.tsx`: the bottom reserve already takes the larger of
the two chrome heights *"only while each is actually on screen"* — extend the same rule to the mic
banner, which **replaces** the orb rather than adding to it, so the reserve is `max(band, banner +
step)` and not the sum.

**The lines it breaks.** Row A-1 of `19_CC_V22_AUDIT_PROMPT.md`, on every frame, verbatim: *"no raw
instant, no 'in N days', **no leading middle dot**, no orphaned emphasised value"* — and *"nothing cut
mid-word at 1024"*. The 1366 rows are the trailing half of the same rule: a middle dot with nothing
to its right is the defect this build has already spent B-259, A6-06, A62-01 and a carried row on,
on the rail, and here it is on a card seven rows deep in the production build with nobody's name on
it. And README Content, verbatim: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today ·
high`"* and *"Dates: `4 September`, `19 Sep` in tight spaces"* — `Sat 5` / `Sep,` is not a date the
pack writes.

**Why it is here.** B-145 fixed S6-22 by routing every status through `formatWhen`, which replaced
short strings (`passed 3 September`) with longer ones (`passed · Thu 3 Sep, 9:41am`). The forms are
right now — that half of S6-22 genuinely closed — but nothing checked whether the card's right-hand
column could still hold them. **I am not calling this a regression from this round's changes**; it
predates them, and earlier rounds, mine included, read this card for its *forms* and never read its
*wraps*. It is in the shipping frames and it is unfiled, which is what matters two hours before a
tag.

**Fix in source.** `jstack-app/components/agents/Checks.tsx`: bind the separator-and-value as one
unbreakable unit the way `HealthLine.tsx` binds `in conversation` for B-173 — wrap each
`· <formatWhen(lastRun)>` fragment so the dot and its date travel together and a break falls between
fragments, never inside one and never after a dot. If the column still cannot hold seven rows at
393, drop the instant to a second line deliberately (`status` on line 1, `Thu 3 Sep, 9:41am` on line
2, no separator between them) rather than letting the wrap choose.

them to expect a 132 px dead strip, on a frame that is not in the pass, for a defect the constant
band has already taken out. A carried row that overstates a live defect by 2.6× is a defect in the
carried list.

**Fix.** Close A62-05 in `CARRIED_DEFECTS_v22.md` §12 and remove it from `KNOWN_GAPS.md`, citing the
measurement above and `TabScreen.tsx:88`'s constant band as the cause; or, if the 51 px is still
thought worth carrying, restate the row with the real number and an evidence frame that exists
(`mic-listening-d1-393-light-test`, y 1802–1852).

#### Verdict for this round's scope

**These are the frames of source `6d35de554aad40be02ea0737e836e307500cf569463e7056e7bab7a0b8b4fffc`
(352 files)** — recomputed from the tree, matched against the mock's stamp and against both exports'
`.jstack-source.json`, with every frame written after every source edit. The auditor's D-1 is
answered: this round judged the pass that ships, and it is the first round that has.

All three of the changes I was sent to judge land. The band is a constant and it cost nothing —
no overlay moved, nothing reads cramped, and it closed A62-05 on the way past. `Clear · Slicers` is
two controls again. The Talk rail is back to the trailing form, `in conversation` is whole, and the
carried row says what the frames show.

What I found that was not on the list is two things the frames have been carrying all along and
nobody had read: a security card that breaks four of its seven dates in half at the phone width and
ends two lines on a stranded middle dot at 1366, and a bill the app truncates to `$1,1…` at 1024.
Neither is this round's doing; both ship if nobody moves.

#### The four things I was sent to judge

##### 1 · A63-01 — the fix LANDS on the claim it was made for, and does NOT land on the rest of the line

**What I was asked to verify.** *"no line may end or begin on a separator, and no date may break
mid-value."* Both hold, at 1366 and 393, light and dark. Measured on
`agents-d1-1366-light-prod`, status column right-aligned to x1320:

| row | y | what the two lines read |
|---|---|---|
| Watchdog heartbeat | 126–136 | `every 5 min · Today 9:41am` — one line |

##### 2 · A63-02 — the reasoning is right on the arithmetic, and wrong on two of the three constraints it cites

**The measurement reproduces exactly.** On `today-d1-1920-light-prod`, title band y531–545: the
whole string runs **x307–563 = 257 px**, `RACQ home insurance` runs x307–437 = **131 px** and the
tail from the separator at x439–441 runs to x563 = **125 px**. You said 257 / 130 / 126. That is
right to a pixel. And the slots: 1366 title ink x307–476 with the expiry column starting x490;
393 title ink x95–271 with the next ink at x284; 1024 title ink x307–469 with the next ink at x483.
The cuts are `RACQ home insurance · $1,184…` at 393, `· $1,1…` at 1024, `· $1,18…` at 1366, whole at
1920. **Carried correctly, and MEDIUM is the right severity.**

**Three things in the disclosure are wrong or thin, and you asked me to say so plainly.**

(a) **The string is misquoted.** §14 and your brief both give the tail as `· $1,184.20 · due 27 Sep`.
The frames say **`due 24 Sep`** (`today-d1-1920-light-prod` x307–563; the undo toast on
`undo-toast-d1-393-light-prod` prints it too: `Later · returns Mon 8am · RACQ home insurance ·
$1,184.20 · due 24 Sep`). The fixture is
`"title": "RACQ home insurance · $1,184.20 · due {{DATESHORT+14}}"` and DATESHORT+14 from 10 Sep is
24 Sep. This is the second carried row in two rounds whose evidence cell does not match the pass
(A63-03 was the first). Fix the string.

(b) **"a second line contradicts UX-H's one-line rail row" cites a rule that does not exist in that
form.** UX-H is the DEFECT, not the rule — `02_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS_v22.md:339` reads *"CD-05 | UX-H
phone waiting-row titles truncate to about twelve characters | Today waiting rows at 393 | e2e at
393: every fixture row shows at least twenty characters of its title **(the two-line row)**"*. The
two-line row is CD-05's own remedy, named in its own check. And this is not a rail row: README
Components, Waiting row `.js-row`, says only *"Title truncates with ellipsis"* — nothing about one
line. The row at 393 is already two lines (title over `expires 22 Sep`).

(c) **The CD-05 objection to truncating at the separator is arithmetically true and reads badly.**
`RACQ home insurance` is 19 characters, so it does fall one short of twenty. But the head needs
131 px in a 175 px slot — it fits with 44 px to spare — and a row that reads `RACQ home insurance…`
identifies the bill perfectly, where `RACQ home insurance · $1,1…` states a sum that is not the sum.
Satisfying a twenty-character floor by printing a wrong-looking number is the check winning over the
reader. If the floor is the blocker, `RACQ home insurance · due 24 Sep` is 32 characters, fits the
tail's date instead of its amount, and breaks nothing — the amount is on the card the row opens
(`decision-bill-d1-1024-light-prod`).

(d) **The disclosure understates the worst width.** It measures 393 and 1366 and says "three of four
widths". The width where the cut is worst is **1024**, whose slot is ~7 px narrower still
(next ink at x483 against 1366's x490) and which prints `$1,1…`. 1024 is not measured in §14 and the
evidence cell names no frame that SHOWS the defect — only `decision-bill-d1-1024-light-prod` "for
the intended form". A reader of the carried list cannot find the defect from the row.

**My answer: the reasoning holds, the carry is right, and the row needs an edit** — the date, 1024's
number, a frame that shows it, and either drop the UX-H clause or restate it as CD-05's
twenty-character floor, which is the only real constraint of the three.

##### 4 · The Gantt axis — it reads correctly, and **no frame in this pass exercises the change you asked me to judge**

**What the frames show.** At every width, both schemes, both days, the axis is: a month row (`SEP`,
and `OCT` at 1920), a week-caption row, a day-tick row at 28 px per day, and weekend shading. On
`tasks-gantt-d1-1366-light-prod` I measured the week hairlines directly — 1 px at `231,230,228` at
**x430, x542, x738, x934**, with day ticks at x430, 458, 486 … 962 (28 px apart) and the now-rule a
13-px-tall mark at x449. x430 = Thu 10 Sep, so:

- the **lead band is 10–13 Sep, four days, 112 px**;
- **the Monday hairline at 14 Sep IS drawn**, at x542, with its caption `14 Sep` at x551–577;
- captions `10 Sep` / `14 Sep` / `21 Sep` / `28 Sep` each sit on **one line**, 8–9 px of ink
  (`y268–276` at 1366), inside the band, clear of the day ticks and the now-rule.

The same geometry at the other widths, read off the weekend bands (28 px/day, Sat 12 Sep = day 2):
1920 day 0 at x445, weekends x501–556 / 697–752 / 893–948 / 1089–1144, Monday hairlines at 557, 753,
949, 1145, chart edge ≈1289 → end band **144 px**; 1024 day 0 at x349, Monday at x461, chart edge
≈638 → end band **177 px**; 393 day 0 at x138, Monday at x250, chart edge ≈373 → end band **123 px**.
Caption-row ink is 8–9 px tall on all 24 `tasks-gantt` frames and 12 px at 393 — **no caption wraps
anywhere**, and nothing hangs out of the band.

**So the axis reads correctly — but it is not the axis you described.** You told me "the lead band is
8 days wide today and the Monday hairline at 14 Sep is not drawn". Neither is true of any frame in
the pass. `lib/ganttAxis.ts:236-238` absorbs a band only when its width is under `MIN_CAPTION_WIDTH`
(44); the lead band here is 112 px and the narrowest end band is 123 px, so `absorbNarrowEnds` is a
no-op on every one of the 24 frames. The 8-day band and the missing hairline appear only when
"today" is a Sunday — which is the real clock the certifying board ran on (13 Sep 2026 is a Sunday),
not the rig's installed clock (Thu 10 Sep 2026 16:20, confirmed independently: the calendar now-rule
on `today-d1-1366-light-prod` is a 1 px `74,94,112` line at y491 against a grid top of y243 at
24 px/hour = **10.33 h after 06:00 = 16:20**).

**This is an evidence gap, and I am recording it as one rather than signing off a rendering I cannot
see.** The S6-04 failure the board caught has no frame in this pass, and neither does its fix. I can
tell you that the unabsorbed path is clean at four widths and two schemes. I cannot tell you whether
an 8-day band captioned `13 Sep` with no hairline at 14 Sep reads correctly, because no frame shows
it. If you want that judged before the tag, the rig needs one Sunday-clock capture of `tasks-gantt`
at 1366 light; without it the cost you describe ships unreviewed.

**Frames.** All 24 `agents-*` — every width, both schemes, both days, prod and test. Behind the
scrim on `emergency-confirm`, `emergency-cancelled` and `caps-edit`, where it is dimmed and I am not
counting it.

|---|---|---|---|

| Backup and restore drill | `Singapore · restored in 14` (322–332) | `min · Sat 5 Sep, 2:00am` (335–344) | **`14 min` split** — a number orphaned from its unit |

`agents-d1-393-light-prod`, right edge x359: the same three rows, Canaries y1809–1819 / 1822–1832,

y1239–1249 / 1252–1262 and Sessions y1284–1291 / 1297–1306 (Canaries fits on one line at 1024).
`agents-d2-1920-dark-test`: Sessions only, y ≈345 / 358. Dark is pixel-identical in wrapping to
light at every width.

**The lines it breaks.** Row A-1 of `19_CC_V22_AUDIT_PROMPT.md`, on every frame, verbatim: *"no raw
instant, no 'in N days', no leading middle dot, **no orphaned emphasised value**"*. `14` with its
`min` on the next line is an orphaned value by any reading. And README Principles 7, verbatim:
*"Show the work. Every card states the source, the expiry and what happens on silence."* — a
security card whose second line reads `tripped · Yesterday 6:00am` under a green dot does the
opposite of showing the work; it shows the inverse of it. This is the same S6-22 class the card was
already fixed for once: the status is composed into a display string and the layout is left to
choose where it breaks.

**Why it is here.** A63-01's fix bound the SEPARATORS to both neighbours. It did not bind the
values. `lib/richText.tsx` now exports a sibling called `unbroken` — exactly the tool this needs —
and `components/agents/Checks.tsx` composes the separators through it but not the phrases between
them.

**Fix in source.** In `jstack-app/components/agents/Checks.tsx`, wrap each status SEGMENT in
`unbroken`, not only the separators, so `none tripped`, `restored in 14 min` and `vault brokered`
travel as units and a break can only fall between segments. If the column still cannot hold seven
rows at 393 and 1366, take A63-01's own second proposal and drop the instant to its own line
deliberately (`status` on line 1, `Yesterday 6:00am` on line 2, no separator between them) rather
than letting the wrap choose.

##### A64-02 · MEDIUM · NEW · The Needs-you Section card ends its why-line on a stranded middle dot at 393 and 1024 — the exact defect A63-01 was fixed for, on a card that opens the app

**Frames.** Eight of `decision-section`'s sixteen: `decision-section-d{1,2}-393-{light,dark}-test`
and `decision-section-d{1,2}-1024-{light,dark}-test`. 1366 and 1920 wrap clear.

**Measured.** The why-line is `You open Learning most mornings; this puts it where you look first ·
your EA · silence leaves the tab as it is · undo 10s`.

- `decision-section-d1-393-light-test`: line 1 is y461–471, x33–351; **its last ink is a 3 px middle
  dot at x349–351, present on y464 alone**, with the preceding glyph ending at x347. Line 2 is
  y475–485 and begins at x33 on `your`. Identical on the dark twin and on both d2 twins.
- `decision-section-d1-1024-light-test`: line 1 is y419–425; **its last ink is a 3 px middle dot at
  x604–606, on y421 alone**. Line 2 begins on `silence`.
- `decision-section-d1-1366-light-test`: line 1 ends on `silence`, line 2 begins on `leaves` — clear.
- `decision-section-d1-1920-light-test`: one line — clear.

**The line it breaks.** Row A-1, verbatim: *"no raw instant, no 'in N days', **no leading middle
dot**, no orphaned emphasised value"*. This is the trailing half of the same rule, and it is the
defect this build has already spent B-259, A6-06, A62-01 and a carried row on — every one of those
on the 200 px rail, where the pack's own words genuinely do not fit. Here it is in a card body with
340 px of line and a wrap point two words earlier that would have avoided it. README Content,
verbatim: *"Meta lines use a middle dot with spaces: `JSTACK · today · high`"* — a dot with nothing
to its right is not that form.

**Why it is here.** A63-01 exported `bindDots` from `lib/richText.tsx` and applied it in
`components/agents/Checks.tsx`. The decision card's why-line does not go through it, so whether a
dot strands is left to the wrap. `today`'s CLASH why-line and `triage`'s both happen to break on a
word; this one happens not to. That is luck, not a rule.

**Fix in source.** Route the decision card's why-line through the same exported `bindDots` /
`unbroken` in `lib/richText.tsx` that `Checks.tsx` now uses, so every `· <fragment>` travels as a
unit and a break can only fall between fragments. One call site; the helper already exists and is
already exported.

##### A64-03 · MEDIUM · NEW · The Habits "Year" view draws eighteen weeks under a year label, a year selector and year-to-date denominators

**Frames.** All 24 `trends-year-*`.

**Measured** on `trends-year-d1-1366-light-prod`, Exercise card:

- header: `2026` between `‹` and `›` year chevrons;
- the card's right-hand count: **`130 of 253`** — 253 days is 1 January to 10 September;
- the dialog footer: **`This year 38% · 831 of 2277`** — 2277 = 9 habits × 253;
- the grid: **18 columns × 7 rows = 126 cells**, columns are weeks and rows weekdays; the only month
  labels are `Jun`, `Jul`, `Aug`, `Sep`; today's underline sits in **column 13**, so columns 14–17
  are future and columns 0–13 reach back only to about 4 June.

Identical at 1920 (same 18 columns in a 900 px-capped dialog with ~500 px of unused width beside it)
and at 393. The grid physically cannot hold the 253 days its own number counts.

**The lines it breaks.** README Content, verbatim: *"Numbers over adjectives: '3 of 5 today', not 'a
few items'."* — a denominator the chart cannot contain is not a number a reader can check. And the
reference intent A-1 sends me to, `JOSH_QA_v22.md` item 12 and the planner's note on it: *"monthly,
**yearly** and all-time views in the JSTACK design language … with hits and misses obvious at a
glance"*, against *"Image 2, 'Calendar': a GitHub-contribution-style **year** grid. Columns are
weeks, grouped under month labels"*. A tab labelled Year with a year selector on it shows a third of
a year.

**Uncertain, and saying so.** I am certain of the measurement. I am not certain the 18-week window
was an accident rather than a density choice — the reference screenshot Josh sent also showed only
about five months. But the label, the year chevrons and the `of 253` / `of 2277` denominators are
this app's own promises, and they do not describe the grid underneath them. Whichever way it is
resolved, the two halves have to agree.

**Fix in source.** Either draw the whole selected year — 52–53 week columns with month labels across
the top, which is what the reference does and what the year chevrons imply — or, if 18 weeks is
deliberate, rename the tab and the denominators to the window actually drawn (`Last 18 weeks`,
`130 of 126`-style counts recomputed over the window) and drop the year selector.

##### A64-04 · LOW-MEDIUM · NEW · `tasks-filtered` prints two counts that contradict each other and an empty line that blames the wrong control

**Frames.** All 24 `tasks-filtered-*`.

**Measured** on `tasks-filtered-d1-1366-light-prod`:

- header, title ink y27–51: **`Tasks` · `5 open · 1 waiting`**;
- active filters, y150–240: the `Waiting` slicer selected, plus an `In progress ×` chip on its own
  row, with `Clear · Slicers` and a `tune` button badged `1`;
- the list card: **`Nothing here for this focus.`**;
- the Gantt card in column 3: `Nothing on the timeline for this focus.`

The subtitle counts the FOCUS (Work has five open). The slicers emptied the list. So the screen says
five are open and then says there is nothing, and the sentence that explains the nothing names the
one control that is not responsible — and does not offer the way out, which is the `Clear` link at
the far right of another row.

**The lines it breaks.** README States, verbatim: *"Empty: a single Muted sentence that says what
happens next. No illustration."* This sentence says what is not there and misattributes why.
README Content, verbatim: *"Numbers over adjectives: '3 of 5 today', not 'a few items'."* Two
numbers on one screen that cannot both be true is worse than an adjective.

**Fix in source.** Make the empty line name the filters that actually emptied the list and carry the
escape — `Nothing matches Waiting + In progress. Clear filters.` with `Clear filters` as the link —
or make the header subtitle count what is shown, so `0 open` sits above `Nothing here`. The Gantt
card's line needs the same treatment; they are the same sentence.

  other under one title.
- **`find-d1-393-light-prod` ellipsises inside a word** — `…he asked for the dates in writin…` on the
  REPLIES row. Card body, not a control label, so checklist 5 does not bite; it still reads badly.
- **`sync-queued` / `sync-conflict` at 393 are ~65 % empty**, the same shape as the carried S6-58 on
  `sync`. Not re-opened.
- **`tasks-filtered`'s list is still empty by fixture choice**, recorded in rounds 2 and 3. A64-04 is
  about the copy on top of that emptiness, not about the emptiness.
- **A warning for whoever measures next**, repeated from round 3 because it nearly caught me too:
  these frames are rendered with sub-pixel (RGB) antialiasing, so a naive sample of a glyph returns
  oranges and blues that are not in the palette. Sample the darkest pixel of a run, or the uniform
  interior of a filled shape. The `warn` amber above is real — it is a 4 × 4 uniform core at
  `150,112,46` with a symmetric rim — and it is the only off-README hue in the pass, sanctioned by
  DISCREPANCIES 30.

---

#### Verdict for this round's scope

**These are the frames of source `58dd97cae5d521ac942b10a0794edf0e82b688c7dcc167f36b57e0eaa9d8b949`
(352 files)** — recomputed from the tree, matched against the mock's stamp, gated by the rig's own
refusal to photograph a stale bundle, and written 00:45–01:25, after every source edit.

Of the four things I was sent to judge: **A63-01 is fixed as stated** — no line ends or begins on a
separator and no date breaks mid-value, at 1366 and 393 in both schemes — but the same seven rows
now break three two-word values instead, and one of them prints `tripped · Yesterday 6:00am` as a
line of its own on a security card. **A63-02's reasoning holds and its arithmetic is exact to the
pixel**, but the row misquotes its own string (`due 24 Sep`, not 27), cites a one-line rail rule that
does not exist in that form, and omits 1024, which is the width where the cut is worst. **A63-03 is
accurate and not overstated.** **The Gantt axis reads correctly at every width and scheme — and no
frame in this pass exercises the absorb path you asked me to judge**, because the rig's clock is a
Thursday and the rule only fires on a Sunday; that cost ships unreviewed unless one Sunday-clock
frame is taken.

Beyond the four, the pass is in good order — columns, cap, type scale, dark tokens, floating chrome,
time forms, 1024 stacking and the phone's density all hold, on every frame I opened. What it is
still carrying that nobody has filed is a decision card that ends a line on a middle dot at two of
four widths, a Year tab that draws a third of a year under its own denominators, and a filtered
Tasks screen that states five and shows none.
